title: [Enhancement]: Feedback should be sent through the backend to avoid CORS issues
body:
We recently added the ability of the frontend to send some feedback to the backend, but because the frontend is sending the feedback directly we need to enable `no-cors`, the frontend is not able to receive the response from the server.

Instead, the frontend should probably send feedback to the backend, and then the backend hits the storage service.

The technical implementation is probably just:

1. Create a function "submit_feedback" to the API server: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/cfae6821fae4259974cfaf6cf249abf9192ea412/opendevin/server/listen.py
2. Port the code that hits the storage server from the frontend to the backend: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/cfae6821fae4259974cfaf6cf249abf9192ea412/frontend/src/api/index.ts#L8
3. Change the request code in the frontend to hit the backend instead of hitting the storage server directly
author: neubig

title: [Enhancement]: Allow user to specify their email for feedback sharing purposes
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

We now allow people to share feedback about when an OpenDevin session goes well or poorly, but this is all shared anonymously so we can't track contributions (e.g. to thank/reward the largest contributors), or follow up (e.g. to help debug issues).

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

We should allow people to specify their email address, and also describe how feedback is used the first time they give feedback through OpenDevin.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

My preferred implementation would be that it is a configuration option, just like any of the other configuration options. It can be set via the config file, and if it isn't set a dialog box pops up and tells them to enter their email and also describes how the data will be used.

Once this email is able to be specified, it should be set in the feedback sharing code:
https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/ae105c2fafc64ad3eeb7a8bea09119fcb5865bc4/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx#L61

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

We also could possibly add authentication, but that seems complex to manage when the server is run locally. We are also planning a hosted demo (#1086), and that will probably have authentication, but that will be a little bit farther in the future.

**Additional context**

This is mainly useful for #1802

title: Add a mechanism to stop the agent execution by setting a max budget per task
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

It can very expensive to run one instance of swe-bench, especially when the agent got stucked.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

Add an additional configurable config `max_budget_per_task` (default to None). When it is set (e.g., 4 USD), controller will keep track with cost using the implemented LLM metrics (https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/opendevin/controller/agent_controller.py#L93), and STOP the task when the cost exceed that budget.
author: xingyaoww

title: Integrate SWE-Bench-docker to our existing SWE-Bench Evaluation framework for more accurate eval
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Our existing `swe_bench` eval logic (https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/evaluation/swe_bench/scripts/eval_infer.sh) is a bit shaky (and is the results of agile development) :(

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

We have a better solution out there: https://github.com/aorwall/SWE-bench-docker

It has been shown that it can produce more accurate solve rate of patches, without actually re-generating patches from models.

TODO: We need to replace our existing eval logic with this SWE-Bench Docker

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Replace the content of `evaluation/swe_bench/scripts/eval_infer.sh` and maybe other scripts to use https://github.com/aorwall/SWE-bench-docker

From `run_infer.sh`, we get a JSONL output file `output.jsonl` (example: https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenDevin/evaluation/blob/main/outputs/swe_bench_lite/CodeActAgent/gpt-4o-2024-05-13_maxiter_50_N_v1.3/output.jsonl) where each line that looks like this:

```json
{
    "instance_id": "sympy__sympy-14774",
    ...
    "git_patch": "diff XXX"
}
```

The idea is to convert this `output.jsonl` to a `output.merged.jsonl`, by evaluating on `git_patch` using SWE-bench-docker and then add an additional field that contains the success / resolve information obtained from the SWE-bench-docker.

For more info on how we do this now, check https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/evaluation/swe_bench/EVAL_PATCH.md

title: Lazy launching BrowseEnv / making BrowseEnv optional
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently BrowseEnv is always launched but it is only used by some agents at some time. One idea is to make it optional and only those agents who need it shall launch it (globally), similar to how AgentSkills are installed on demand.

One minor obstacle is, an agent may or may not need browsing capability. BrowsingAgent needs it for sure, but other agents might only need it for some tasks. One solution is to make them always delegate to BrowsingAgent for browsing tasks: see https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2103, with which CodeActAgent doesn't need to declare need of BrowseEnv / install BrowseEnv by itself.

It doesn't mean #2103 is a blocker; we could of course declare dependency of BrowsingEnv for both CodeActAgent and BrowsingAgent.

title: New config: GLOBAL_MAX_ITERATIONS
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

We now have MAX_ITERATIONS config, which limits the number of turns/steps/iterations an agent could interact with LLM. This is very useful as a safe guard for user's wallet.

With https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/1910, an agent could delegate to another agent - every time a delegate agent is instantiated, it would have MAX_ITERATIONS as limit. I have seen a case where my parent agent (due to a bug in prompt engineering) keeps delegating a task to a child agent, who exhausts MAX_ITERATIONS and then gets invoked again in the next turn of parent agent. This means we effectively have MAX_ITERATIONS * MAX_ITERATIONS as the global limit, in the worst case.

We should have another config, e.g. GLOBAL_MAX_ITERATIONS (or maybe FULL_TASK_MAX_ITERATIONS) to control the total number of steps to finish a task.

title: Prettify diff in case of integration test failure
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently, when an integration test fails due to prompt mismatch, we display something like:

```
Mismatched Prompt File path /Users/liboxuan/workspace/OpenDevin/tests/integration/mock/CodeActAgent/test_edits/prompt_002.log
------------------------------
...FULL PROMPT, omitted...
------------------------------
Mismatch at index 16278:  vs
Mock response for prompt is not found
```

This is not helpful enough to visually see the mismatch.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

A `diff` style of mismatch visualization. E.g.

```
Mismatched Prompt File path /Users/liboxuan/workspace/OpenDevin/tests/integration/mock/CodeActAgent/test_edits/prompt_002.log
< original prompt
---
>updated prompts
```

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

The code shall be implemented in `tests/integration/conftest.py::get_mock_response` method. Our current implementation is as follows:

```python
            # print the mismatched lines
            print('Mismatched Prompt File path', prompt_file_path)
            print('---' * 10)
            print(messages)
            print('---' * 10)
            for i, (c1, c2) in enumerate(zip(file_content, prompt)):
                if c1 != c2:
                    print(
                        f'Mismatch at index {i}: {c1[max(0,i-100):i+100]} vs {c2[max(0,i-100):i+100]}'
                    )
                    break
```

As you could see, we are comparing `file_content: str` and `prompt: str`. Note: they are not original files, with all special symbols and newline characters removed, and thus not readable. We should compare original files, i.e. `messages: str` and `prompt_file_path`.

We could dump `messages` into a temporary file, and use `diff`  shell command to compare it with `prompt_file_path` and generate a diff.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**

I would appreciate it if someone could try using OpenDevin's help to solve this.

title: [Feedback]: Allow people to consent to public sharing of conversation histories
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently we have the ability to share OpenDevin conversation histories by pressing "thumbs-up" and "thumbs-down". But it's not clear a-priori that these will be shared, and there's also no way to decide whether this will be public or not.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

After the thumbs-up/thumbs-down button is pressed, we can pop up a dialog box that says

"Your conversation and positive/negative feedback will be shared with the OpenDevin developers to improve the OpenDevin experience. In addition, you can opt-in to contribute to a shared repository of data that can be used for improving open-source coding models."

Followed by a checkbox that says "Make my feedback public." (off by default) and a "Share" button that results in the data being shared.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

We should modify these sections of the code:
https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/42c6b506b5418fd8de0fff371e5aac5232dd6e5c/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx#L145-L160

https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/42c6b506b5418fd8de0fff371e5aac5232dd6e5c/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx#L59

title: Should we add an option to disable storing SSH host keys
body: **Current Issue** SSH connections are storing host keys in the .ssh/known_hosts file, causing management difficulties and potential conflicts in dynamic environments. **Solution** As the title, should we add an option to disable storing SSH host keys like: ```python pxssh.pxssh(options={ "StrictHostKeyChecking": "no", "UserKnownHostsFile": "/dev/null" }) ``` BTW, We have the persistent container now, it can solve this problem to some extent. But we'll continue to use the non-persistent container in some situations.

title: [Feature]: Aider-inspired RepoMap
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Aider has a functionality to create a [RepoMap](https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider/blob/main/docs/repomap.md), which is a concise description of the repo in text format, with the most relevant/important parts highlighted.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

It would be nice to have a RepoMap class within OpenDevin that can be used by any agent to pull in a description of the repo.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

- [ ] copy the aider [repomap.py](https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider/blob/main/aider/repomap.py) into OpenDevin. This could probably be put in either a new `indexing` folder [here](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/tree/main/opendevin), or in the [memory](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/tree/main/opendevin/memory) folder.
- [ ] make it possible to import the repomap into one of our competitive agents, such as CodeAct. This functionality should be optional, like the github message ([details](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/f9c7c3a5205d294506a7b190b7621c0216239a3b/agenthub/codeact_agent/codeact_agent.py#L111-L114)).
- [ ] run experiments on SWE-Bench to see if this functionality improves accuracy

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

We could also implement this from scratch, or create improved code search functionality.

**Additional context**

* Parent issue #120

title: [Feature]: Aider-inspired linting functionality
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

[Aider](https://aider.chat/) has functionality for linting code in multiple languages that could be helpful for OpenDevin.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

It would be good if OpenDevin agents (optionally?) linted the code they generated so that they could create code that passes basic syntax and style checks.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Currently OpenDevin supports some [rudimentary linting](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/opendevin/runtime/plugins/agent_skills/agentskills.py).

In contrast, [Aider's linting](https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider/blob/main/aider/linter.py) has a number of good points that OpenDevin does not yet support:
- [ ] Multi-language support with treesitter
- [ ] The conversion of the output into a prompt seems more sophisticated

We may want to take some inspiration from their work, either by importing the library wholesale and replacing our current agentskills implementation with theirs, or more piecemeal.

**Additional context**

Aider [article](https://aider.chat/2024/05/22/swe-bench-lite.html) on swe-bench lite.
Aider super-issue https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/120
author: neubig

title: [Feature]: Retry on failure functionality
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Sometimes models fail to do their job correctly, and we would benefit from starting all over from the beginning. There are a few examples of this in the agent literature:
- Aider recently introduced a [harness](https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider-swe-bench) for testing SWE-bench that allows for retries when tests and linting don't pass on swe-bench
- @Jiayi-Pan has work on [Evaluation and Refinement for web agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.06474) that use a reward model to judge when a web task has failed, a reset mechanism to return to the beginning, and a method for improving the prompts based on reflexion.
- @niansong1996 has a method [LEVER](https://github.com/niansong1996/lever) that uses a learned verifier to rerank code generation execution results.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

Ideally, this would be something that could be implemented in a general way, so that we could implement different strategies with a shared interface. For instance:

```
class ResetStrategy:

   @abstractmethod
   def initialize_state():
       """Take note of the initial state that should be reset too."""
       ...

   @abstractmethod
   def verify(...):
      """This verifies whether the agent has reached a failure state."""
      ...
   
   @abstractmethod
   def reset(...):
      """This performs some sort of reset."""
      ...

   @abstractmethod
   def message_on_reset(...):
      """This creates a message to the agent upon reset (e.g. a task with a prompt based on reflexion)."""
      ...   
```

Then, when using OpenDevin, we could choose an option that says "retry N times when you get stuck", and select the strategy that is used to do so.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

The actual reset strategies would vary based on the task. For instance:

- AiderResetStrategy ([code reference](https://github.com/paul-gauthier/aider-swe-bench/blob/1ae32650e44707c1aa67bbe0a7bf090edd1358c6/harness.py#L229-L339)):
  - `initialize`: save the current git commit of the repository `commit_id`
  - `verify`: tests+linting pass
  - `reset`: `git checkout commit_id`
  - `message_on_failure`: no-op
- EvalRefineResetStrategy ([code reference](https://github.com/Berkeley-NLP/Agent-Eval-Refine)):
  - `initialize`: save the current web page `initial_page`
  - `verify`: the reward model is positive
  - `reset`: `goto(initial_page)`
  - `message_on_failure`: reflexion prompt

This could either be integrated into OpenDevin, allowing for retries in the main app as well

**Additional context:**

* [Aider superissue](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/120)
* Thanks to @xingyaoww and @frankxu2004 for offline discussion

### If you find this feature request or enhancement useful, make sure to add a 👍 to the issue

Context: https://opendevin.slack.com/archives/C06P5NCGSFP/p1717733829670139

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

Add a confirmation mode for OpenDevin: A checkbox on the frontend; when enabled (checked), the frontend will prompt for the user's approval for **every** action the agent wants to execute.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

When confirmation mode is on, we probably need to add a check in the agent controller for every "executable" action -- the action can only be sent off for execution when it receives user confirmation from the front end.

title: Feat: add Vulture for detection of dead/deprecated code
body:
## What problem or use case are you trying to solve?

[Vulture](https://github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture) helps maintain a clean and efficient codebase by identifying and removing unused code, which reduces technical debt and improves code readability. This is particularly beneficial in collaborative projects on GitHub, as it ensures that all contributors work with a streamlined and maintainable codebase, enhancing overall productivity and code quality.

Should work in combination with flake8 and also as pre-commit (per repo description).

## Vulture can be installed using Poetry:

### Step-by-Step Guide

1. **Navigate to Your Project Directory**:
   ```sh
   cd your_project_directory
   ```

2. **Add Vulture as a Development Dependency**:
   Use the following command to add Vulture to your `pyproject.toml` file under the `[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]` section:
   ```sh
   poetry add --dev vulture
   ```

3. **Install Dependencies**:
   If you haven't already installed your project's dependencies, you can do so with:
   ```sh
   poetry install
   ```

4. **Run Vulture**:
   You can now run Vulture using Poetry's run command:
   ```sh
   poetry run vulture your_codebase/
   ```

### Example `pyproject.toml` Snippet
After adding Vulture, your `pyproject.toml` might look something like this:
```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "your_project"
version = "0.1.0"
description = ""
authors = ["Your Name <you@example.com>"]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"

[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]
vulture = "^2.3"
```

### Running Vulture
To run Vulture on your codebase:
```sh
poetry run vulture your_codebase/
```

This setup ensures that Vulture is installed and managed as part of your project's development dependencies, making it easy to maintain and use across different environments.

title: Agent Config
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
We need some way to configure the agent more in detail and easier than we do today.
For example [on slack](https://opendevin.slack.com/archives/C06U8UTKSAD/p1717779430449069?thread_ts=1717778692.412489&channel=C06U8UTKSAD&message_ts=1717779430.449069)
Also: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/1996#pullrequestreview-2104227581
- config to prefer command line for working on github (presumably enabling/disabling some part of the prompt)
- eval_mode

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
An AgentConfig modeled after LLMConfig, as described in this comment: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/1552#issuecomment-2093998935
In practice, it would be like:
```
[agent]
name=CodeActAgent
memory_enabled=true
prefer_browsing_on_github=false
prefer_browsing=true
max_history=20
summarize_delegates=true

[browse]
name=BrowsingAgent
memory_enabled=false
prefer_browsing_on_github=true

[mono]
name=MonologueAgent
memory_enabled=true
prefer_browsing_on_github=true
max_history=50
```

In this setup, the generic `agent` config is the default, the others have user-defined names: preconfigured agents for various experiments. When starting main.py, we can include it on the command line, like `main.py -l 'gpt-4o' --agentconfig 'browse'`. This will override any attribute from the generic 'agent' (or default in config.py) with attributes in 'browse'.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
Similar to LLMConfig.

**Alternatives**
I'm not sure if the memory-related vars as exemplified above are more of "an agent thing" or a general "memory thing", e.g. max_history, summarize_delegates. I suppose an alternative is to split `memory` from `llm` for memory configs. Does it make sense to make those per agent, will they really differ per agent?

**Additional context**
What other things do we want to test for an agent setup or per agent?

title: Voice input capability (speech to text)
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
For some people, typing is difficult. But because AI tools accept natural language input, it should be easy for those people to give instructions by speaking.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
There will be two ways of triggering the speech input function. One will be a button and the other one will be a keyboard shortcut. My preference is a shortcut like in Microsoft Teams where you can press Ctrl + Space and for as long as you are holding it down, the program is listening. And then when you release those keys, the program will convert the recording into text. To reduce confusion, maybe the button could work the same way (hold down to record), and it could be next to the text input box. I don't think there's any need to show transcribed text while the user is speaking, but rather the transcription could all happen after the user has finished recording. The transcription should happen immediately and automatically after the user releases the record button.

I suggest that the speech input function should not depend on which widget the user has focused. I suggest that the keyboard shortcut to start the recording should work from any program state. It should not matter whether the user has clicked inside the text input box.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
There is something similar in the Aider software, though its interface is a bit different. I find that it makes Aider a lot easier to use compare to text-only input.

The Aider implementation of this uses Whisper, which has the advantage that the API key will be the same one that the user provided in order to use the GPT models. However, it looks to me like the latest AssemblyAI model may have surpassed Whisper in accuracy, so it would also be good to have that as an option for users who have an API key for AssemblyAI.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative for users who don't want to type very much is to use some kind of external speech to text function, such as Nuance Dragon, or maybe some kind of plugin in their browser. My experience has been that Whisper and AssemblyAI provide far more reliable transcription in terms of accuracy compared with tools external to the application such as Dragon, Google speech to text or Microsoft speech to text. I don't find that those tools (external to the application) are reliable enough to give clear and comprehensive instructions to the AI on your first try.

This is a good reason to implement this function in the OpenDevin interface using a highly accurate transcription engine.

**Additional context**
I wrote this entry using the AssemblyAI speech-to-text engine and a modest amount of editing.

title: Lightweight 'OmniscientAgent' which the head agent can query for a broader view of the codebase
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
For example: 'Hey AI, what is the least mature module in this codebase?', or 'Where is the documentation lacking? Fill in some gaps.'

SWE-Agent and CodeAct offer interfaces to the AI which deliberately show only a small amount of code at a time when searching or when reading files. However my experience when using AIs to understand unfamiliar code bases is that when the AI can only see a small amount of code, it will often give misleading or unhelpful answers. 

On one hand, the SWE-Agent paper found that showing only 100 lines of code at a time to the AI was optimal. However it looks like they were using GPT-4 in that experiment. It may be that the reason why showing 100 lines at a time to the AI was optimal for the solve rate is simply that GPT-4 makes very poor use of large context. (Poor score on Needle In A Haystack.) 

In contrast, I have found that when I feed an entire code base into Haiku, it tends to give really useful answers to questions about the code. (Maybe not surprising, given that unlike GPT-4, Haiku gets a very strong score on Needle In A Hay Stack.) I would not be surprised if offering a tool for this as a sub-agent to be called upon by a larger model improves the solve rate for problems which require a broader understanding of the code base: The head agent (e.g. GPT-4o) could ask the sub-agent (e.g. Haiku) a question which requires a full view of the codebase when it suspects that its narrow searches are not going to yield the right information reliably.

Another reason why the size of the context matters is that it affect the cost of each message (in AI credits). It is not economical to feed large contexts into large models such as GPT-4o. However because Haiku is a fairly small model, asking a question about the code base tends to cost on the order of US 5c / message (for large context and ~1 paragraph of output). (Maybe Gemini 1.5 Flash is similar.)

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
This will require two additional items of user input:
1. Enable this sub-agent.
2. Provide the API key for the provider of the smaller model.
(e.g. Maybe the head agent uses GPT-4o and the subagent uses Haiku. That means that two API keys are required instead of one.)
The output to the user will show when this subagent is called by the head agent, and will show the instructions to the subagent, the size of the context that it loads, and the response from the subagent.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
I gather that there is already some kind of framework in the works for subagents.
The functionality of feeding a whole codebase into the AI has been implemented in a non-agentic way in the ClaudeCLI tool under the MIT license, in Python. (https://github.com/edwardbrazier/claudecli)
The code could simply be copied from ClaudeCLI and integrated into a new agent.
Maybe the most complex change will be to allow the user to supply multiple API keys for multiple models.
Implementation would also require feeding the head agent some examples of when and how to call the sub-agent.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The Aider algorithm for selecting files to load in the context is pretty good at this. However I think there are cases when feeding as much of the codebase as possible into the model still yields more reliable answers than Aider's approach.

**Additional context**
Here is an example conversation:


USER: 
Hey AI agent, in this web app for document management, most of the pages require similar functionality because it's all about viewing and editing tables. Can you tell me which page of the web app is missing the most functionality, on the assumption that it needs similar functionality to the other pages? 

HEAD AGENT [e.g. CodeAct w/ GPT-4o]:
This is a question which I can't readily answer by looking at small chunks of source files at a time. I will need some help.
<execute_ipython>
```
ask_omniscience (codebase_location='./src',
                 file_extensions=['ts','cs'],
                 question="Assuming that each page of this webapp requires a similar interface, which one is missing the most functionality relative to the others?")
```
</execute_ipython>

OMNISCIENCE [Haiku]: 
[Log message: Loaded 400 kB of source code.]
For the file view page, the file view module lacks a lot of functionality which the other modules, for example the edit users module, do have. In the file view module, there isn't yet a way to edit cells in the table that lists the file, or to reorder the entries by sorting.

HEAD AGENT: 
That seems to address the question adequately. The module with the most room for improvement is the file view page.

USER:
You've listed there some of the functions that the file view page needs. List for me the new files, classes and methods that we'll need in order to add that functionality.

title: Feat: Agentskills - enhancement suggestions for  command descriptions from LLM itself
body:
### What problem or use case are you trying to solve?

As title says, I kindly asked ChatGPT4o:
"_Any recommendations on the commands descriptions that would make it easier for YOU to instantly know what they do? we want to improve the interactions with you._"

The answers themselves indicate that with little tweaks we could prevent misconceptions on side of the LLM's.

### Answer:

_Thank you for considering improvements to the command descriptions! Here are some suggestions to make the descriptions even clearer and more intuitive for me:_

1. **create_file**
   - **Current Description:** Creates and opens a new file with the given name.
   - **Suggested Description:** Creates and opens a new file with the specified name. Useful for starting new projects or adding new files.

2. **edit_file**
   - **Current Description:** Edit a file. It replaces lines `start` through `end` (inclusive) with the given text `content` in the open file.
   - **Suggested Description:** Replaces lines `start` through `end` (inclusive) with the specified `content` in the open file. Ideal for modifying existing code or text.

3. **open_file**
   - **Current Description:** Opens the file at the given path in the editor. If line_number is provided, the window will be moved to include that line.
   - **Suggested Description:** Opens the specified file in the editor. Optionally, move to a specific line number for quick access.

4. **goto_line**
   - **Current Description:** Moves the window to show the specified line number.
   - **Suggested Description:** Jumps to the specified line number in the open file. Useful for quick navigation.

5. **scroll_down**
   - **Current Description:** Moves the window down by 100 lines.
   - **Suggested Description:** Scrolls down by 100 lines in the open file. Useful for viewing more content without editing.

6. **scroll_up**
   - **Current Description:** Moves the window up by 100 lines.
   - **Suggested Description:** Scrolls up by 100 lines in the open file. Useful for reviewing previous content without editing.

7. **search_dir**
   - **Current Description:** Searches for search_term in all files in dir. If dir is not provided, searches in the current directory.
   - **Suggested Description:** Searches for the specified term in all files within the given directory. Defaults to the current directory if none is provided.

8. **search_file**
   - **Current Description:** Searches for search_term in file. If file is not provided, searches in the current open file.
   - **Suggested Description:** Searches for the specified term in the given file. Defaults to the current open file if none is provided.

9. **find_file**
   - **Current Description:** Finds all files with the given name in the specified directory.
   - **Suggested Description:** Locates all files with the specified name within the given directory. Useful for quickly finding specific files.

10. **parse_pdf**
    - **Current Description:** Parses the content of a PDF file and prints it.
    - **Suggested Description:** Extracts and prints the content of the specified PDF file. Useful for reading and analyzing PDF documents.

11. **parse_docx**
    - **Current Description:** Parses the content of a DOCX file and prints it.
    - **Suggested Description:** Extracts and prints the content of the specified DOCX file. Useful for reading and analyzing Word documents.

12. **parse_latex**
    - **Current Description:** Parses the content of a LaTex file and prints it.
    - **Suggested Description:** Extracts and prints the content of the specified LaTeX file. Useful for reading and analyzing LaTeX documents.

13. **parse_pptx**
    - **Current Description:** Parses the content of a pptx file and prints it.
    - **Suggested Description:** Extracts and prints the content of the specified PowerPoint file. Useful for reading and analyzing presentations.

_These suggestions aim to make the purpose and utility of each command immediately clear, enhancing the interaction experience._

title: [Enhancement]: Better handle observations for PIP install in two separate environment
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

See example here: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2377#pullrequestreview-2111168085

There are some issues with `test_ipython_module` we need to think about improving - basically, when `pip install` is run on bash, the jupyter kernel won't get automatically rebooted. Ideally, we can throw a reminder suggesting, "If you think the package is installed for your jupyter kernel env, please reboot your jupyter kernel, etc".

But in the long run, we will probably have two separate Python environments for OpenDevin:
1. Python environment used for IPython kernel, which is mainly used for `agentskills` tools
2. Bash terminal, where the agent can switch between different virtual environments - In SWE-Bench, the agent is `conda activate` into a different environment. We probably need to think of a way for agent to know this better (e.g., keep the `(base)` environment PS1 prefix for the agent).

_Originally posted by @xingyaoww in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2377#pullrequestreview-2111168085_

title: [Arch Refactor for Agent Runtime]: Deprecating SSH-based communication and use EventStream
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Right now, the backend mainly relies on `ssh` to communicate with `sandbox`, which does not fit too well with our current Event Stream-based communication. The requirement of the backend to know the existence of "ssh" makes thing much harder to support different runtimes/docker images (https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/1387, e.g., we need to automatically install `sshd` if user bring their own docker images without it - and it can get tricky very quickly since `sshd` may need to be installed differently across different linux distributions) and creating hosted version (https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/1086).

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

I imagine our next step in architecture will be able to support *arbitrary docker image* sandbox/runtime by creating one piece of software called `od-runtime-client` and automatically installing it into the user-provided sandbox (if it wasn't installed already - this is already partially done in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2101).

Then, at the entry point of each docker sandbox, `od-runtime-client` will be started:
  - [x] it will connect to backend's event stream (~via WebSocket~ well it is currently implemented as REST API), handle event stream communication to/from other sources. Resolved by https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2603
     - For example, `CmdRunAction` can be directly stream from the agent and received by `od-runtime-client`, and `od-runtime-client` can maintains a `pexcept` session that directly interact with `/bin/bash` to execute that command.
     - This will allows us to get rid of the SSH requirement altogether
  - [x] be docker-image agnostic to support arbitrary user-provided sandbox images
    - Partially done in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2101
    - Partially done in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2879, require further testing
    - [x] We need to shrink down the size of our dependency required to install in the `runtime-client` (now we need to install everything opendevin needed), so we can build any user-provide images faster (#690 is related): https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3195
  - [x] A browser can be maintained as a plugin for `od-runtime-client`, so we can get rid of the current browsing running on the backend (cc @frankxu2004). Done in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2899
     - It will also make it easier for (multimodal) agent to use the browser to browse some local multimedia file (e.g., goto url `file://image.jpg`)
     - [ ] It will also be more natural to integrate browser primitives (e.g., `goto_url`) into `agentskills` library when they are in the same container.
  - [x] maintain an IPython + `agentskills` library with the `od-runtime-client`. Done in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2879
  - [x] we might also consider merging all the existing plugins into `od-runtime-client`. https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2879
  - ~[ ] replace `<execute_bash>` with a `execute_bash` `agentskills`.~ (no plan for me)
  - [x] Extensively tests EventStream runtime to make sure it is in feature parity as our existing `ServerRuntime`: 
    - [x] Add tests for sandbox: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3128
    - [x] Add integration tests: #3184 
  - [x] Make sure `EventStreamRuntime` works across all the evaluation suite. Run SWE-Bench to ensure there's no performance degradation: #3230 
  - [x] Deprecate and remove `ServerRuntime`, and switch to `EventStreamRuntime` by default: #3271

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Due to the diversity of user-provided docker images we might need to support, I propose we use some package manager like [miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge) that is *already* multi-platform to maintain the environment (miniforge can install different python version, and even maintains [its own `glibc` version](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/glib/) to circumvent some system-level restriction, e.g., `glibc` version too old) and dependencies of `od-runtime-client`. So the workflow of user-bring docker sandbox would be (essentially what we implemented in https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2101):

1.  Detect if a user brings an image that comes with already installed `od-runtime-client`
2. If not, we create a temporary `Dockerfile`, `FROM user-provided-docker`, then build that image with a suffix `_od`
3. Then we use `${SANDBOX_CONTAINER_IMAGE}_od` to start the sandbox, and assume every dependencies is met.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

title: [Enhancement]: Present the user with a basic privacy notice that they can accept or decline when sharing feedback
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
Because we obtain the users personal data such as their name, email, and may indirectly retrieve other information via their chat with OpenDevin, we are required to display a privacy notice on how we store the data and what do we do with it. We can only send the feedback if the user accepts.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
When the user presses either feedback action for the first time, display a basic privacy notice such as ""To help us improve, we collect feedback from your interactions to improve our prompts. By submitting this form, you consent to us collecting this data. [Read Privacy Policy (if applicable)]"

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
Update the modal to display the privacy notice

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**
Unblocks #2419, #2420

title: Mechanism to Handle Post-Execution Editing
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

After Devin completes a task, I often manually adjust the results. However, Devin does not reload the file to check for differences when requesting additional tasks. Instead, Devin edits its latest response, which may have already been manually edited by me. This can result in inconsistencies and loss of manual changes.


**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

I want a mechanism that reloads the relevant files before Devin proceeds with new requests to check for differences. If there are changes, Devin should incorporate these updates to ensure they work with the latest data version. This mechanism should be seamless and efficient, minimizing any additional steps for the user.


**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Implement a file-checking system that triggers before Devin begins executing a new task. This system would compare the current file state with the last known state.
Devin should reload the files and update its internal data structures to reflect these changes if differences are detected.
Optionally, you can log these updates for transparency and debugging purposes.
Consider implementing a notification or prompt to inform the user when updates are detected and incorporated.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Currently I'm stating it as part of the next prompt but it doesn't work so well.

**Additional context**

This feature will enhance the reliability and accuracy of Devin's operations, ensuring that manual edits are always taken into account. It will help maintain consistency and trust in the automated processes, particularly in environments where manual adjustments are common.

title: Make the agent error message more informative
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

I have tried OpenDevin for a few tasks. I have encountered a few times the error message "Agent encountered an error."  or "Agent encountered an unexpected error." 

It took me a while to figure out how I could dig into docker logs to find out more. 

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

It would be helpful to directly display the error messages extracted from the relevant docker log. 

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

The user interface could have a new tab called agent error message to display docker log, after the tabs for Editor, Browser, Jupyter.

title: [Bug]: Unable to Execute Commands with execute_cli but echo and Pipe Worked perfectly

title: [Bug]: test_ipython integration test: error in skipif
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [X] I have checked the troubleshooting document at https://opendevin.github.io/OpenDevin/modules/usage/troubleshooting
- [X] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug

The run of integration test `test_ipython` is skipped due to a faulty condition in `test_agent.py`.
In below source, the `or` operator needs to be replaced by `and`.

For brevity sake, the shortened source  (around line 100) looks like this:
```py
@pytest.mark.skipif(
    os.getenv('AGENT') != 'CodeActAgent' or os.getenv('AGENT') != 'CodeActSWEAgent',
    reason='currently only CodeActAgent and CodeActSWEAgent have IPython (Jupyter) execution by default',
)
...
def test_ipython():
```
Must be:
```py
@pytest.mark.skipif(
    os.getenv('AGENT') != 'CodeActAgent' and os.getenv('AGENT') != 'CodeActSWEAgent',
    reason='currently only CodeActAgent and CodeActSWEAgent have IPython (Jupyter) execution by default',
)
...
def test_ipython():
```
A call of either of these 2 lines will cause `.skipif` to wrongly skip that specific test:
```sh
 ONLY_TEST_AGENT=CodeActAgent ./tests/integration/regenerate.sh
 ONLY_TEST_AGENT=CodeActSWEAgent ./tests/integration/regenerate.sh
```

title: feat: a FileChangeHandler service (for e.g. agentskills)
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

In order to let OpenDevin know that files have changed intermittently without its knowledge,
I'd like to implement a FileChangeHandler service.

When OpenDevin then acts to edit/append files, the agentskills could query that observer
and give a warning about the file already being changed to the LLM and cancel the operation.

Idea introduced in this issue: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/2443

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

The changes to the agentskills are comparably easy, but I'm looking for collaboration on below drafts, that I had gpt4o craft as I don't feel comfortable enough around Linux.

* The Makefile part could either be rewritten to become part of the agentskill's `setup.sh` or the main Makefile?
* How to fully integrate the rest or make it somehow optional from the beginning as `sudo` seems required?

----

A bash-style shell script to set up the `FileChangeHandler` as a systemd service, and a Makefile that calls this script.

### Shell Script (`setup_file_change_handler.sh`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Define variables
SCRIPT_PATH="/usr/local/bin/file_change_handler.py"
SERVICE_PATH="/etc/systemd/system/file_change_handler.service"
DIRECTORY_TO_WATCH="/path/to/directory"

# Create the Python script
cat <<EOL > $SCRIPT_PATH
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler
import time

class FileChangeHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_modified(self, event):
        print(f'File {event.src_path} has been modified')

    def on_created(self, event):
        print(f'File {event.src_path} has been created')

    def on_deleted(self, event):
        print(f'File {event.src_path} has been deleted')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    path = "$DIRECTORY_TO_WATCH"
    event_handler = FileChangeHandler()
    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(event_handler, path, recursive=True)
    observer.start()

    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()
EOL

# Make the script executable
chmod +x $SCRIPT_PATH

# Create the systemd service unit file
cat <<EOL > $SERVICE_PATH
[Unit]
Description=File Change Handler Service
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 $SCRIPT_PATH
Restart=always
User=nobody
Group=nogroup

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOL

# Reload systemd, start the service, and enable it to start on boot
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl start file_change_handler.service
systemctl enable file_change_handler.service

echo "FileChangeHandler service setup complete."
```

### Makefile:

```makefile
.PHONY: setup

setup:
    sudo bash setup_file_change_handler.sh
```

### Instructions:

1. **Save the Shell Script**:
   Save the shell script as `setup_file_change_handler.sh`.

2. **Make the Shell Script Executable**:
   ```sh
   chmod +x setup_file_change_handler.sh
   ```

3. **Create the Makefile**:
   Save the Makefile content in a file named `Makefile`.

4. **Run the Setup**:
   Execute the setup by running:
   ```sh
   make setup
   ```

### Explanation:
- **Shell Script**: This script creates the Python file change handler script, makes it executable, creates the systemd service unit file, and starts/enables the service.
- **Makefile**: The `setup` target in the Makefile calls the shell script with `sudo` to ensure it has the necessary permissions to create files in system directories and manage services.

By running `make setup`, the entire process of setting up the `FileChangeHandler` as a systemd service will be automated.

----

title: 1-click serverless cloud deployments
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
I'm exploring ways to easily deploy OpenDevin on my personal cloud (not locally), and automate the deployment process.
I'm using AWS, and prefer using the AWS Copilot CLI to deploy on a serverless stack – App Runner or ECS + Fargate.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
* Deploy OpenDevin into my personal cloud account (AWS/Azure/GCP) form a single click / command. This requires programmatically deploying both front and backend to a cloud compute, preferably serverless (like on AWS Fargate).
* [Optional] If I make local changes to the OpenDevin src code then I should be able 1-command redeploy (e.g., `copilot deploy`) it to my cloud, without pushing the code to the Github repo.

I tried deploying the Dockerfiles in [OpenDevin/containers](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/tree/main/containers) on AWS and ran into a bunch of errors like below:
```
06-19-2024 08:27:28 PM Starting OpenDevin...
06-19-2024 08:27:28 PM SANDBOX_USER_ID is not set
 ```

In [Getting Started](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin?tab=readme-ov-file#-getting-started) I see that the run command needs the local user Id, password, etc. but my local variables won't apply when the container is being run in a serverless environment. 

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
Ideally the Dockerfile could be self sufficient and not require environment variables to run. This will allow it to be easily deployed to any serverless compute.
We can modify the app to not require user Id / password. If I understand correctly the user/pass is needed for making file system changes in the host. Options:
* Have a fully isolated cloud workspace within the container, which is not linked to the host's file system (i.e., no Docker Volume). I'm okay if the workspace is deleted along with the container.
* Alternatively, for long term storage put the workspace in S3 and not on the host.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Ditch the Copilot CLI and write a custom script / CDK to build, deploy and run the docker containers on a self-managed EC2 instance. I will lose the serverless benefits. 
* Create a script that uses AWS Secrets Manager to get the ssh user/pass from a serverless host (Fargate), and run that script from Docker ENTRYPOINT. This seems complex and unstable.

title: Multi Agentic (We can select one agent at a time )
body:
@mroch @jeremi @penberg @ohhmm 
Feature Request: Waterfall Model Workflow for Agents and multi agent
What problem or use case are you trying to solve?

Currently, in OpenDevin, users can select and activate one agent at a time, such as the SWE agent, Codeac Agent, or Planning Agent. This process requires manual intervention to switch from one agent to another, which can be inefficient and time-consuming. The need is to automate the workflow in a waterfall model where agents work sequentially without requiring manual activation for each step. This approach ensures that tasks are handled in a structured manner, from planning to execution to testing, improving the overall efficiency and effectiveness of the workflow.

Describe the UX of the solution you'd like

The user experience should be streamlined and intuitive:

Single Workflow Selection: Users can select a "Waterfall Model Workflow" option that initiates a predefined sequence of agent activities.
Automated Sequence: Once initiated, the Planning Agent starts first. Upon completion, the system automatically transitions to the Codeac Agent, followed by the Testing Agent.
Progress Tracking: Users should be able to monitor the progress of each phase through a dashboard or progress bar, showing the current agent in operation and estimated time to completion.
Notifications and Updates: Users receive notifications upon the completion of each phase, with summaries of what was accomplished and what the next steps are.
Interruption and Resumption: Users can pause the workflow if needed and resume from where it left off.
Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?

The implementation could involve:

Workflow Controller: Develop a workflow controller that manages the sequence of agents. This controller handles the initiation, monitoring, and transition between different agents.
State Management: Implement a state management system to track the progress of each phase and manage transitions. This could be done using a state machine or workflow engine.
Inter-agent Communication: Ensure smooth communication between agents by defining clear interfaces and data exchange protocols.
UI/UX Enhancements: Update the user interface to include the workflow selection option, progress tracking dashboard, and notification system.
Error Handling: Implement robust error handling to manage and recover from failures at any stage in the workflow.
Configuration Files: Allow customization of the workflow sequence and parameters through configuration files or a user-friendly settings page.
Describe alternatives you've considered

Manual Sequential Execution: Users manually start each agent in sequence, but this approach lacks automation and can lead to inefficiencies and delays.
Parallel Execution: Running all agents in parallel could save time but may lead to resource conflicts and a less structured workflow, which might not be suitable for all projects.
Custom Workflows: Allow users to define custom workflows and sequences, offering flexibility but requiring more user input and configuration.
Additional context

Implementing a waterfall model workflow can significantly improve project management and execution efficiency in OpenDevin. By automating the transition between different phases, users can focus on higher-level tasks and decision-making. This feature aligns with best practices in software development and project management, ensuring a systematic approach to task execution.

title: Implement Cost Reduction Options for LLM Usage in OpenDevin
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

We are trying to reduce the costs associated with using Large Language Models (LLMs) in the OpenDevin project. This involves optimizing the usage of LLMs to ensure that we are not incurring unnecessary expenses while maintaining the quality and efficiency of the system.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

The solution should be seamless and transparent to the end-users. Users should have the option to select cost-saving modes or configurations when initiating tasks that involve LLMs. This could be presented as a simple toggle or dropdown menu in the user interface where users can choose between different cost-saving strategies, such as using a less expensive model, limiting the number of tokens, or adjusting the model parameters.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Yes, here are some thoughts on the technical implementation:

1. **Adjust Configuration Parameters**:
   - Modify the `config.py` file to set default values for parameters that affect cost, such as reducing the number of retries, lowering the maximum number of input and output tokens, and adjusting the temperature and top_p parameters.

2. **Optimize Token Usage**:
   - Implement a method in `llm.py` to truncate or summarize input text to reduce the number of tokens sent to the LLM.

3. **Use Cost-Efficient Models**:
   - Implement a dynamic model selection mechanism in `llm.py` that selects a model based on the task's complexity and cost constraints.

4. **Monitor and Log Costs**:
   - Continuously monitor the cost of LLM usage and log it for analysis. Implement alerts or thresholds to notify when the cost exceeds a certain limit.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

1. **Manual Cost Monitoring**:
   - Manually monitor the costs and adjust the usage patterns based on periodic reviews. This approach is less efficient and prone to human error.

2. **Fixed Model Usage**:
   - Always use a fixed, less expensive model regardless of the task complexity. This approach may compromise the quality of results for more complex tasks.

3. **Token Limitation Only**:
   - Only implement token limitation without adjusting other parameters or model selection. This approach may not be as effective in reducing costs comprehensively.

**Additional context**

For more details on configuring LLMs and troubleshooting, refer to the following documentation files:
- [LLM Backends Documentation](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/docs/modules/usage/llms/llms.md)
- [Troubleshooting Guide](https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/docs/modules/usage/troubleshooting/troubleshooting.md)

title: Enable human input in the right area of OpenDevin, like file edit and terminal command execution.
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
Right now, if OpenDevin write sth wrong in the file, like typo/grammar error, or provide some configuration content, I can't modify and provide it for OpenDevin.
And sometimes I'm pretty sure what to do, but OpenDevin just fails many times to solve some problem by executing some command, I want to execute the command for OpenDevin. 

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
I think we can make file area and terminal area inputable, when we pause OpenDevin. Then human do something for him, and resume to execute. 

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
We need to record what human do, like file content diff, terminal executed, and tell OpenDevin when resume him. Maybe just put the detail things human did to the chat message. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**
I found some discussion about integrating a webide inside, but I don't think we need it to accomplish this at the early stage.

title: Interactive Content Previews
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
The ability to preview and interact with various types of content directly within the OpenDevin interface, including code (with a focus on HTML, SVG, and React with Tailwind CSS), text, and diagrams. This enhancement would allow users to visualize and understand generated or referenced content without leaving the main conversation flow, particularly benefiting web developers and designers.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**
Similar to Claude.ai's artifacts, OpenDevin could have a feature where:
1. Generated content appears in a distinct, collapsible panel within the chat interface.
2. Users can expand these panels to view the full content.
3. For code (including HTML, SVG, and React with Tailwind), syntax highlighting and one-click copy functionality would be included.
4. For HTML and SVG, a live preview option would be available to render the code in real-time.
5. For React components with Tailwind, a sandbox-like environment could be provided to see the rendered component with applied styles.
6. Users could interact with rendered content (e.g., clicking buttons in HTML previews).
7. A download option for each artifact would be available.
8. For diagrams, users could zoom in/out and potentially interact with elements.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**
1. Implement a content rendering system that detects and appropriately displays different types of content.
2. Use libraries like Prism.js for code syntax highlighting, with support for HTML, SVG, JSX, and CSS (including Tailwind classes).
3. Integrate a lightweight HTML/SVG renderer for live previews.
4. Implement a sandboxed React environment with Tailwind CSS support for rendering React components safely.
5. Use SVG or Canvas-based rendering for diagrams.
6. Create a collapsible UI component for artifact display.
7. Ensure proper sanitization and security measures for rendered content.
8. Integrate seamlessly with the existing chat interface to include artifacts in the conversation flow.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Simply improving code block formatting within the existing chat interface.
2. Adding separate tabs or windows for different content types.
3. Implementing a split-screen view with content preview on one side.
4. Linking to external tools or IDEs for more complex interactions with code.

**Additional context**
This feature would significantly enhance OpenDevin's usability, especially for web developers and designers who frequently work with HTML, SVG, and React with Tailwind CSS. The ability to see live previews and interact with rendered content would streamline the development process and make OpenDevin a more powerful tool for web-related tasks. It would also align OpenDevin more closely with advanced AI assistants, potentially increasing its appeal to a wider user base in the web development community.

Additional context This feature would significantly boost OpenDevin’s appeal to web developers and designers, streamlining their workflow by providing immediate visual feedback and interaction with generated content. It would position OpenDevin as a more comprehensive development assistant in the AI-powered tool landscape.

title: Container-to-Host Communication Issue
body:
# Container-to-Host Communication Issue

## What problem or use case are you trying to solve?

The problem is enabling communication between a containerized application and a service running on the host machine.

## Describe the UX of the solution you'd like

The ideal solution would allow the containerized application to seamlessly access and interact with the service running on the host machine, as if they were on the same network.

## Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?

The current implementation involves running a web application on the host machine's localhost on a specific port. The application is started using a command that runs the server in the background and logs output to a file. Specifically, Docker networking needs to be configured to allow the container to communicate with the host's localhost.

1. **Network Configuration:**
   - Ensure that Docker is correctly configured to allow communication with the host machine using `--add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway`.

2. **Environment Variables:**
   - Set relevant environment variables to configure the frontend and backend components to communicate over the correct network paths.

3. **Docker Run Command:**
   - Utilize the following docker run command to ensure proper networking setup:

     ```bash
     docker run -it \
         --pull=always \
         -e SANDBOX_USER_ID=$(id -u) \
         -e WORKSPACE_MOUNT_PATH=$(pwd)/workspace \
         -v $(pwd)/workspace:/opt/workspace_base \
         -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
         -p 3000:3000 \
         --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
         --name opendevin-app-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S) \
         ghcr.io/opendevin/opendevin:0.6.2
     ```

4. **Sandbox Configuration:**
   - Ensure the `config.toml` file correctly specifies the sandbox type and settings, such as ssh or exec for Docker.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1. **Using Host Networking Mode:**
   - Explore Docker's `--network="host"` mode if applicable, though it might introduce security considerations and is not supported on all operating systems.

2. **Reverse Proxy Setup:**
   - Implementing a reverse proxy on the host machine to forward requests from the containerized application to the local service.

## Additional context

- The web application on the host is running in a development mode.
- The server is currently only accessible locally.
- The containerized application is running within a restricted environment, which adds layers of network isolation.
- The container includes additional security measures, which may further restrict network access.
- The `config.toml` file and environment variable settings should be verified for correct paths and network settings:

  ```toml
  [core]
  sandbox_type = "exec"
  ssh_hostname = "localhost"
  sandbox_timeout = 120
  max_iterations = 100
  cache_dir = "/tmp/cache"
  ```

title: [Documentation]: Custom docker image instructions should note that you can use a pre-existing docker image
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

In our custom sandbox guide: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/41ddba84bd0d62f8a4bc48d08addde4b4269a687/docs/modules/usage/custom_sandbox_guide.md?plain=1

We state that you can create a custom sandbox by creating your own docker image, then specifying it. But actually it's also easy to use an existing docker image from the docker hub, e.g. the following code if you want a sandbox with node installed:

title: Add Placeholder Docstrings To Reduce PyLint Messages
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Running PyLint on the OpenDevin codebase produces 713 messages. 234 of these messages are related to missing docstrings. It is possible, even easy, to configure PyLint to ignore these messages. However, doing so won't nudge the code base towards better documentation. Once all placeholder docstrings are in place, future code (pull requests) can be rejected if docstring are not present.

Having a large number of PyLint messages make it hard to find important messages. For example, this message might be important enough to fix since when check is True a CalledProcessError exception will be raised when the sub-process returns a non-zero exit code.

```
opendevin/runtime/docker/local_box.py:31:32: W1510: Using subprocess.run without explicitly set `check` is not recommended. (subprocess-run-check)
```

If the community is willing, I'd be happy to work on resolving the mundane PyLint messages. 

Does this seem valuable?

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

Run the attached python script. Spot check the changes. Push to GitHub. This set of changes should be isolated from other changes so that formatting and logic commits are separated.

Please consider running "isort ." to organize the python import into the suggested order.

Please consider running "black --target-version py310 ." afterwards so that the code conforms to a coding style.

After the above steps, there should be 471 PyLint messages, down from 713.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

I wrote a python script that uses the Abstract Syntax Tree of Python to add placeholder docstrings where they are missing.

```
"""Placeholder Module Docstring"""
import os
import ast
import astor
error_count = 0
errors = []


def find_classes_without_docstrings(tree):
    """Placeholder Function Docstring"""
    classes_without_docstrings = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
            if not node.body or not isinstance(node.body[0], ast.Expr
                ) or not isinstance(node.body[0].value, ast.Constant):
                classes_without_docstrings.append(node)
    return classes_without_docstrings


def find_functions_without_docstrings(tree):
    """Placeholder Function Docstring"""
    functions_without_docstrings = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            if not node.body or not isinstance(node.body[0], ast.Expr
                ) or not isinstance(node.body[0].value, ast.Constant):
                functions_without_docstrings.append(node)
    return functions_without_docstrings


def docstring(s):
    """Placeholder Class Docstring"""
    return ast.Expr(value=ast.Constant(s))


def add_placeholder_docstrings(file_path):
    """Placeholder Function Docstring"""
    global error_count
    needs_writing = False
    try:
        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            content = file.read()
            if not content.strip():
                with open(file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as empty_file:
                    empty_file.write('"""\nPlaceholder Module Docstring\n"""\n'
                        )
                return True
            tree = ast.parse(content, filename=file_path)
        if not tree.body or not isinstance(tree.body[0], ast.Expr
            ) or not isinstance(tree.body[0].value, ast.Constant):
            tree.body.insert(0, docstring('Placeholder Module Docstring'))
            needs_writing = True
        for func in find_classes_without_docstrings(tree):
            func.body.insert(0, docstring('Placeholder Class Docstring'))
            needs_writing = True
        for func in find_functions_without_docstrings(tree):
            func.body.insert(0, docstring('Placeholder Function Docstring'))
            needs_writing = True
        if needs_writing:
            with open(file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
                file.write(astor.to_source(tree))
    except Exception as e:
        errors.append(f'Error processing {file_path}: {e}')
        print(f'Error processing {file_path}: {e}')
        error_count += 1
        pass
    return needs_writing


def check_directory_for_missing_docstrings(root_dir):
    """Placeholder Function Docstring"""
    for subdir, _, files in os.walk(root_dir):
        for file in files:
            if file.endswith('.py'):
                file_path = os.path.join(subdir, file)
                if add_placeholder_docstrings(file_path):
                    print(f'Added placeholder docstrings in {file_path}')


check_directory_for_missing_docstrings('.')
print('---------------------------')
for error in errors:
    print(error)
print(f'Finished with {error_count} errors.')
```

title: Enhance code agent's search ability with ACR's context search API
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

The current search skills available to the agent is:
```python
- search_dir(search_term, dir_path='./'): # Searches for a term in all files in the specified directory.
- search_file(search_term, file_path=None): # Searches for a term in the specified file or the currently open file.
```
This is versatile but quite coarse-grained, and sometimes the agent doesn't use the skill at all but `grep` or `find` instead. (e.g. [1](https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenDevin/evaluation?filepaths=outputs%2Fswe_bench_lite%2FCodeActAgent%2Fgpt-4o-2024-05-13_maxiter_30_N_v1.6-no-hint%2Foutput.jsonl&row_idx=5), [2](https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenDevin/evaluation?filepaths=outputs%2Fswe_bench_lite%2FCodeActAgent%2Fgpt-4o-2024-05-13_maxiter_30_N_v1.6-no-hint%2Foutput.jsonl&row_idx=6))
 
**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

We could try to implement some more fine-grained search tools for the agent, which may help the agent to quickly locate the necessary code and possibly increase the possibility that the agent ends up use tools. [ACR](https://github.com/nus-apr/auto-code-rover) has defined some:

```python
- search_class(class_name: str): # Search for a class in the codebase
- search_method_in_file(method_name: str, file_path: str): # Search for a method in a given file
- search_method_in_class(method_name: str, class_name: str): # Search for a method in a given class
- search_method(method_name: str): # Search for a method in the entire codebase
- search_code(code_str: str): # Search for a code snippet in the entire codebase
- search_code_in_file(code_str: str, file_path: str): # Search for a code snippet in a given file file
```

*However, because these skills are for coding-oriented tasks, it may be more preferable to only use them in agents specific for coding, instead of generalist agents.*

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

The implementation from `ACR` is well-written and documented so we can reference from there. However, we will need to make some modifications to:

- Enable line number for these tools

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

None.

**Additional context**

- With this API as a baseline, we can try to improve further by implementing new tools if needed. (e.g. `tree` command to get the repository structure)
- Some works on `swe-bench-lite` that achieve good scores like [CodeR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01304) or [RepoUnderstander](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01422) also utilize this API, so implement this can be a prerequisite to support these agents if we would like to in the future.

---
P/s: I'm not 100% sure that this is needed, any thoughts are welcome!

title: [Agent]: Add functionality from the "Agentless" tool
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Recently, agentless tools has reported good accuracy and efficient cost on SWE-bench lite: https://github.com/OpenAutoCoder/Agentless

It would be good to incorporate this in to OpenDevin.

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

I think we could have a two-level technical implementation:

- [ ] Incorporate Agentless directly into OpenDevin

This could be done by creating a new `AgentlessAgent` that basically just runs their tool as-is. Agentless relies on code search and patching, so the overall framework for the code would look like this.

```python
class AgentlessAgent:
    def step(...):
        localizations = localize(user_message)
        patch = repair(localizations)
        apply_patch()
```

- [ ] Incorporate some components of Agentless into other agents like CodeAct

This would pull out individual components (such as Agentless's code search or patching functionality) and incorporate them into our "main" agents like CodeAct.

**Additional context**

- Twitter Thread: https://x.com/LingmingZhang/status/1808501612056629569

title: [Bug]: Wrong /workspace folder contents and cannot reset OpenDevin to a working state with a /workspace folder in sync with the computer /workspace folder
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [X] I have checked the troubleshooting document at https://opendevin.github.io/OpenDevin/modules/usage/troubleshooting
- [X] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug

I have a /workspace folder with my work,

On the OpenDevin UI I could see it and all its contents (many files)

I tried OpenDevin on it

OpenDevin tried to create everything from scratch instead of using the existing code

I attempted to stop it but it did not work so I stopped the docker and re started the docker

The docker restarted but now OpenDevin /workspace shows a completely different workspace folder, out of sync with the computer's /workspace folder, with a single and empty .svelte file, which is not at all the content of the /workspace file in my computer

(Clicking on the little "refresh" icon next to the workspace in UI does not solve the problem)

### Current OpenDevin version

```bash
0.7.1
```


### Installation and Configuration

```bash
WORKSPACE_BASE=(absolute path to /workspace folder)
docker run -it \
  --pull=always \
  -e SANDBOX_USER_ID="$(id -u)" \
  -e WORKSPACE_MOUNT_PATH=$WORKSPACE_BASE \
  -v $WORKSPACE_BASE:/opt/workspace_base \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  --name opendevin-app \
  ghcr.io/opendevin/opendevin
```


### Model and Agent

(Any)

### Operating System

Debian 12.5

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install OpenDevin
2. Make it work with a folder with contents in it
3. See that all files / folders inside the /workpace folders are same than the ones in the computer
3. Start a task to work on a projet, OpenDevin starts the task
4. Stop the container
5. Restart Devin
6. See that the workspace folder is now out of sync with the computer one
7. Delete all containers, volumes, image
8. Re install devin from scratch
9. Open OpenDevin
10. See that all files / folders inside the OpenDevin UI /workpace folder are out of sync with the ones in the computer's /workspace folder

### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

_No response_

title: [Feature Request] OpenDevin to read files/folders contents of Workspace before starting tasks, esp. to avoir restarting a project that is in progress

OpenDevin tries to create a project from scratch even when the project is started

Doing it manually each time, tell devin to manually list the fils before starting

This bug : https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/2837

Something in the Readme to help me reset OpenDevin to a working state

Yes this is a script I made but it did not work

#!/bin/bash

fi

docker builder prune -af

if [ -n "$VOLUMES" ]; then

fi

echo "Done"

I guess build from source ?

title: [Feature Request] Allow to provide a startup command (be able to run a command at the startup of OpenDevin for example to be able to install requirements for its shell context)
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Initially, OpenDevin generally has to install dependencies to run commands, in my case it was bun, but it could be python, poetry, node, rust...

Ideally, the user should be able to provide a command to setup the environment

A typical startup command could be "./setup_env.sh", basically running a bash command in the OpenDevin context. Here a script to setup a development environment and avoid paying / waiting for OpenDevin to try & find out all the things that are missing for him to setup 

Additionally, OpenDevin tends to use outdated versions, in my case it installed Node v16 (current LTS is v20) even when explicitly instructed to use Bun v1.1 in my given task

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

In the settings, allow to provide a "startup command"

If empty, do nothing

If provided, run it in the bash of OpenDevin

**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

- Allow a new setting in the settings page
- If the command is provided, at Devin startup, run it in the Devin bash context 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I guess tell devin to run a command before it starts developing ?

**Additional context**

title: [Feature] Pre-build a list of OpenDevin supported sandbox images
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Relavant discussion: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/2658#issuecomment-2212544525

User may have diverse environment needs (e.g., some need `python 3.10`, `3.11`, some need `nodejs`, etc). We already supported [custom sandbox images](https://docs.all-hands.dev/modules/usage/custom_sandbox_guide) that allow the user to specify a sandbox image they want to use in OpenDevin (e.g., `nodejs`), and OpenDevin can locally build it to be compatible with OpenDevin.

**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

- [ ] Instead of user need to build their custom image locally, maybe we can support a list of commonly used docker images (e.g., prevalent python/nodejs version, etc) as "officially build and supported" images. This will get re-build when a new version is released to save CI time.
- [ ] Select from a drop-down list on the frontend interface on which image you want to start the session with


**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Maybe we can create a `.txt` file, where each line is an upstream docker image, e.g., https://hub.docker.com/r/ubuntu/python.
And we add a Github workflow to read this file and build the corresponding images at time of each release.
