Multi-SWE-Bench makes this possible: https://multi-swe-bench.github.io/#/
We should incorporate it into our evaluation harness.
author: neubig

title: [Bug]: Sending consecutive tasks in headless mode results in "Let's get back on track"
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

If you setup headless mode from the docs using Docker then proceed to execute the command `python -m openhands.core.main -t "write a bash script that prints hi" -n "test_session"`, it works the first time, but any consecutive use referencing the same session (e.g. `python -m openhands.core.main -t "now modify the bash script to say hello" -n "test_session"`) results in just the message `CONTENT: Let's get back on track. If you experienced errors before, do NOT resume your task. Ask me about it.` being sent, and not the given task.

### OpenHands Installation

Docker command in README

### OpenHands Version

0.30

### Operating System

MacOS

### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

_No response_

title: [Feature]: Add links to documentation and usage instructions in the UI
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
Users have reported difficulty in finding documentation or usage instructions for connecting and activating the GitHub resolver in OpenHands. Specifically, some users do not see instructions on how to use the resolver effectively after connecting a GitHub repository.

**Desired UX of the solution**
The frontend UI should have visible links to the documentation and clear explanations for how to use the resolver, including how to activate it via messages to OpenHands on a connected repository.

**Technical implementation**
Include a prominent section or banner in the OpenHands UI with links to the relevant documentation pages. Provide a step-by-step guide or tooltip explaining how users can activate the resolver after connecting a GitHub repository.

**Alternatives considered**
- Using proactive conversation starters to guide users on resolver activation (already in progress).

The feedback button should be highly accessible and intuitively placed within the app interface. Once clicked, it should open a text input modal where users can type feedback and submit.

Potentially leveraging a feedback collection library or creating a custom feedback submission module in React. This would involve:

title: Turn openhands App into a PWA (Progressive Web App)
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

When I develop with openhands, it is effectively my IDE. So I often use that particular chrome-tab. But from windows perspective it is just one chrome tab, in one chrome window. So sometimes when I want to switch back to it, i have to spent some time to find it. Especially if I by mistake opened another tab in the window with openhands that now has focus.

This can be improved a lot by turning it into a PWA Progressive Web App. 
Then you get this:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/089a2d96-6bfc-4847-a84b-e4530c799c8a)

You can try it right now. 
ChatGPT:

> Step-by-step fix: make Chrome treat your app like a standalone app
> Find the shortcut Chrome created (on your Desktop or in the Start Menu).
> 
> Right-click → Properties.
> 
> In the Target field, you'll see something like:
> 
> "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome_proxy.exe" --profile-directory="Default" --ignore-profile-directory-if-not-exists http://127.0.0.1:12000/
> Change it to launch Chrome directly with app mode, like this:
> 
> "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --app=http://127.0.0.1:12000/
> (Note: chrome.exe, not chrome_proxy.exe.)
> 
> Click Apply, then OK.

I did that, works pretty good. 
* own spot in taskbar with own icon
* own spot in the Alt+Tab window
* more space because the browser bars are gone


**Describe the UX of the solution you'd like**

Would be nice to give everyone that experience with one click. 


**Do you have thoughts on the technical implementation?**

Apparently that is possible by editing like 3 files. I think @openhands-agent will one shot this.  

Then we would get this in the address bar: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1581321b-3c2c-482c-91e8-21a9ec17e04a)

Hi there,

title: Task-Oriented Memory System: A Hierarchical Approach for Complex Task Execution
body: **Summary** I propose a task-oriented memory system that extends the current architecture to improve performance on complex, long-running tasks. This hierarchical memory approach addresses the context length limitations of LLMs by compartmentalizing memory and focusing attention on relevant information at each execution stage. **Problem Statement** The current single-memory architecture faces efficiency challenges when handling complex, multi-stage tasks: * Context window limitations lead to information loss as conversations grow * Important details may be condensed or dropped during memory management * Delegation mechanisms exist but are underutilized * Performance degrades as task complexity increases **Proposed Solution** A hierarchical task-oriented memory system that: * Separates planning from execution * Maintains isolated memory contexts for individual subtasks * Preserves only task-relevant information at each level * Optimizes attention to critical information **System Architecture** Planning Layer: * Planning Controller: Manages the overall task lifecycle * Planning Memory: Stores user requests, the task plan, and subtask results * Planning Agent: Creates structured execution plans, potentially utilizing tools—such as browsing or knowledge search—to acquire information before planning. Execution Layer: * Agent Controller: Handles individual subtask execution * Task Memory: Stores only the current task context and essential prior results * Task Solving Agent: Performs the actual work with focused attention Execution Flow * Planning Controller receives user request * Planning Agent creates structured execution plan * Planning Controller assigns subtasks sequentially to Agent Controller instances * Each Agent Controller focuses only on its specific subtask with minimal context * Task results flow back to Planning Controller * Planning Controller tracks progress and returns final results when complete **Advantages** * Improved performance through focused attention on relevant information * Reduced context pollution and memory constraints * Better handling of complex, multi-stage tasks * More efficient resource utilization **Implementation Status** I have a working prototype implementation of this system. If there's interest, I can submit a pull request with the necessary changes and documentation. ### If you find this feature request or enhancement useful, make sure to add a 👍 to the issue

body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

We need to verify in unit tests if Gemini 2.5 Pro models ("preview" and "exp", see below) have tool use enabled by default.

Look carefully at llm.py and specifically, at the check:

```
# Check if model name is in our supported list
        model_name_supported = (
            self.config.model in FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS
            or self.config.model.split('/')[-1] in FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS
            or any(m in self.config.model for m in FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS)
        )
```

In particular, the last one. Make a unit test to verify that Gemini 2.5 Pro models pass the check and eventually self._function_calling_active is True in the LLM instance after initialization.

The test should verify multiple variations: "gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25", "gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25" , and in both cases both alone and with prefixes like "gemini/" (so "gemini/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25", and "gemini/gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25" when we apply the prefix), same for the prefixes "litellm_proxy/", "openrouter/gemini/", "litellm_proxy/gemini/".

Find test_llm.py where other LLM class tests are, and add this new test there.

title: Fix failures in Circle CI
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
After pushing a branch to github, we should be able to monitor circle ci jobs to see if there are failures. If there are failures, we should try to fix them.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**
Use the MCP provided by circleci to fetch build failures: https://circleci.com/blog/circleci-mcp-server/

I have tested an alternate approach of just instructing openhands to use the api and it's worked great. Here's an example prompt:
```
There are failures in circle CI. Can you pull those down and fix them?

We have a circle ci token in the environment variable CIRCLE_CI_TOKEN . https://circleci.com/docs/api/v2/index.html#tag/Job/operation/getJobDetails has instructions for using the api to pull down job details. Use the api to find the failures and then fix them.
```

**Additional context**
We may benefit a lot from this PR https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/7725 which will allow us to wait before trying to fetch the failures instead of polling.
Management of mcp secrets is also a gap we might need a solution for. Right now I provide the token via `runtime_startup_env_vars` but there may be a better way.

author: tawago

title: Support for condensation pipelines
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

There are situations where it's handy to have multiple condensers simultaneously: the `BrowserOutputCondenser` is great for reducing costs when the agent is browsing, and the `LLMSummarizingCondenser` is great at reducing costs for long-running tasks.

But there's no condenser that's great for long-running tasks when the agent is also browsing.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

We could write a new condenser that combines the behavior of the `BrowserOutputCondenser` and the `LLMSummarizingCondenser`. That's likely to lead to all condenser behavior centralizing to a single, difficult-to-maintain implementation. **The alternative proposed here** is to make it so that individual condensers can be "composed" by the agent.

The central task in developing a condenser pipeline is handling the composition. Condensers act via the function:

```
condense: View -> View | CondensationAction
```

Some condensers, like `BrowserOutputCondenser`, will _never_ emit a `CondensationAction`, which makes their inclusion trivial: given two functions `View -> View` I can always make a new function `View -> View` by composing them. 

(This might warrant a new base class for them to inherit from to make that behavior clear.)

When we have a condenser that can emit either a `View` or a `CondensationAction`, we don't have any other way to handle the `CondensationAction` except for passing it back to the agent -- no downstream condenser can do anything with that information.

So the proposal: add a new `Condenser` implementation called `CondenserPipeline` that is parameterized by a _list_ of condensers and whose `condense` function acts something like:

```python
def condense(self, view: View) -> View | CondensationAction:
    result: View | CondensationAction = view
    for condenser in self.condensers:
        result = condenser.condense(result)
        if isinstance(result, CondensationAction):
            break
    return result
```

Configuration might be tricky (as evidenced by #7793), and we'll want to be careful about tuning a condenser pipeline -- intersectional effects likely mean we'll want to re-run experiments to identify the appropriate parameterization for the entire pipeline.

title: [Bug]: Resolver not using configured sandbox runtime image
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When I specify `base_container_image` it gets properly captured by the workflow but the image launched is still the default `ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.32.0-nikolaik`

I _think_ this is because the `SANDBOX_ENV_` prefix means the env var will get added to the sandbox environment, whereas just `SANDBOX_<setting name>` ends up modifying the setting. So `SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE` is what should be set here, not `SANDBOX_ENV_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE`.

title: [Bug]: Resolver fails using GitHub Actions token in `send_pull_request.py`
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When using the default GITHUB_TOKEN in github actions, we get the following error in step Create draft PR or push branch:

```
ERROR:root:<class 'ValueError'>: Token is invalid.
```

It looks like it's because we don't pass the repo into `identify_token` in https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py#L645 , which then ignores the possibility of a github actions token and only looks for a PAT. When it doesn't find a PAT it declares it invalid, even though the token has write access to PRs and can perform the action just fine.

Is this as simple as adding `--repository` as a argument and populating it with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`?

I'm new around here, but this seems ripe for the openhands resolver to take and open a PR. 😄

For setup.sh scripts that take some time to run, OpenHands will interrupt the execution of setup.sh instead of waiting for the shell script to finish.

Here is our setup.sh:
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e

echo "Starting BluMint development environment setup..."

# Function to check if a command exists
check_command() {
  if ! command -v "$1" &> /dev/null; then
    echo "$1 command not found. Installing..."
    return 1
  else
    echo "$1 is already installed."
    return 0
  fi
}

# Function to check if an npm package is installed globally
check_npm_global() {
  if ! npm list -g "$1" &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Global npm package $1 not found. Installing..."
    return 1
  else
    echo "Global npm package $1 is already installed."
    return 0
  fi
}

# Install required npm packages if they don't exist
check_npm_global "dotenv-cli" || npm install -g dotenv-cli -y
check_npm_global "dotenv-vault" || npm install -g dotenv-vault -y
check_npm_global "commitizen" || npm install -g commitizen -y

npm install || echo "Warning: npm install had some issues, but continuing setup. You may need to run npm install manually."

export PATH=$PYTHONUSERBASE/bin:$PATH
export PIP_USER=yes

# Install Foundry using the script

fi

  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do

  # Create empty file

  echo "# Add your OpenHands environment variables here" > .env.openhands
  echo "# Format: VARIABLE_NAME=value" >> .env.openhands
fi

# Create .env.me file with DOTENV_ME if it exists
if [ ! -z "$DOTENV_ME" ]; then
  echo "Creating .env.me file..."
  echo "DOTENV_ME=$DOTENV_ME" > .env.me
  echo ".env.me file created."
else
  echo "DOTENV_ME environment variable not found. Skipping .env.me file creation."
fi

# Pull environment configurations using dotenv-vault
echo "Pulling environment configurations..."
npx dotenv-vault pull -y || echo "Warning: dotenv-vault pull failed, but continuing setup"
npx dotenv-vault pull production -y || echo "Warning: dotenv-vault pull production failed, but continuing setup"
npx dotenv-vault pull emulators -y || echo "Warning: dotenv-vault pull emulators failed, but continuing setup"
npx dotenv-vault pull staging -y || echo "Warning: dotenv-vault pull staging failed, but continuing setup"
npx dotenv-vault pull ci -y || echo "Warning: dotenv-vault pull ci failed, but continuing setup"

# Extract JSON files from environment variables
echo "Extracting JSON files from environment variables..."
if [ -f "./.devcontainer/extract_json.sh" ]; then
  bash ./.devcontainer/extract_json.sh FB_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_DEVELOPMENT functions/src/config/development-key.json || echo "Warning: Failed to extract development service account key"
  bash ./.devcontainer/extract_json.sh FB_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_PROD functions/src/config/prod-key.json || echo "Warning: Failed to extract production service account key"
  bash ./.devcontainer/extract_json.sh FB_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_REMOTE_EMULATORS functions/src/config/remote-emulators-key.json || echo "Warning: Failed to extract remote emulators service account key"
else

fi

# Configure git
echo "Configuring git..."
if [ ! -z "$GIT_USER_NAME" ] && [ ! -z "$GIT_USER_EMAIL" ]; then

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

**It appears that there are **two** condensation llm-calls happening and neither are being tracked in the trajectory.json.** 



I discovered this when debugging the LLMSummarizingCondenser. 

I start a new conversation on my test-project: https://github.com/happyherp/openhands-test

I set a breakpoint in CodeActAgent._step and wait for it to be hit. When hit, I set `self.condenser.max_size` to 10 to more quickly reach a condensation. Then I disable the breakpoint.

I set a breakpoint in LLMSummarizingCondenser: get_condensation


I ask the agent to read all files. This triggers the breakpoint in LLMSummarizingCondenser: get_condensation.

I note the value of `self.llm.metrics.get()`

I note the value of summary

Immediately the breakpoint is hit **again**.

now the summary-event contains the event that was created from the previous call.

]
```

I let the program resume. because of the low value, of condenser.max_size, another condensation happens later on. I stop the agent and download the trajectory.json and compare it to what I saw when debugging. 

Before the condensation we have events 14(RunAction) and 15(RunObservation).

Event 14 has 

```
    "llm_metrics": {
        "accumulated_cost": 0.03647205,

            "model": "anthropic/claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219",
            "prompt_tokens": 17488,
            "completion_tokens": 410,

            "cache_write_tokens": 6671,

Then comes event 16 CondensationAction

  {

    "message": "Summary: <SUMMARY>\nUSER_CONTEXT: ....", //truncated

title: [Bug]: Line numbers are often included in `str_replace` commands
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

I'm not sure this qualifies as a bug. Might be an improvement request instead.

I have noticed a common pattern that leads to a failed command execution when OpenHands tries to edit a file via `str_replace`:
1. It checks the file content via `cat -n`. The output includes line numbers (due to `-n`).
2. It calls `str_replace` but it includes the line numbers in the argument strings.
This results in the `str_replace` command not finding a match in the file and therefore not replace anything.

I'm running OpenHands via GitHub Actions, if that makes a difference.

I tried to mitigate the issue by adding some instructions in a `.openhands_instructions` file but with little to no effect.

title: Allow disabling all tools in CodeActAgent
body:
From a discussion in [#7881](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/7881#issuecomment-2813125354)

>with MCP support, I think the CodeActAgent should not have default tools. Currently, the thinking, finish, and bash tools cannot be disabled since `get_tools` will always add them (see below). Many other MCP servers have similar tools, and this leads to collisions of semantics.  Should I open a separate issue on this?
> 
> ```python
> def get_tools(
>     codeact_enable_browsing: bool = False,
>     codeact_enable_llm_editor: bool = False,
>     codeact_enable_jupyter: bool = False,
>     llm: LLM | None = None,
> ) -> list[ChatCompletionToolParam]:
>     SIMPLIFIED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION_LLM_SUBSTRS = ['gpt-', 'o3', 'o1']
> 
>     use_simplified_tool_desc = False
>     if llm is not None:
>         use_simplified_tool_desc = any(
>             model_substr in llm.config.model
>             for model_substr in SIMPLIFIED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION_LLM_SUBSTRS
>         )
> 
>     tools = [
>         create_cmd_run_tool(use_simplified_description=use_simplified_tool_desc),
>         ThinkTool,
>         FinishTool,
>     ]
>     if codeact_enable_browsing:
>         tools.append(WebReadTool)
>         tools.append(BrowserTool)
>     if codeact_enable_jupyter:
>         tools.append(IPythonTool)
>     if codeact_enable_llm_editor:
>         tools.append(LLMBasedFileEditTool)
>     else:
>         tools.append(
>             create_str_replace_editor_tool(
>                 use_simplified_description=use_simplified_tool_desc
>             )
>         )
>     return tools
> ```

title: Search Conversation History
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

It would be very useful if there were a way to search through your local conversation history (also see related ask: [show more than 9 conversations in history](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/7928))

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

* Minimum: Search box at the top of the "Conversations" popout which filters, as you type, conversations that contain the typed term
* Bonus: When opening a conversation, the searched term is highlit

**Additional context**

My primary motivation for exploring alternatives to Claude Code was having access to past conversations. Often I find myself asking questions about the codebase or debugging issues that are useful to be able to come back & review later. Although OpenHands does persist sessions, it's not really feasible to find any of them given that 
1) it only shows the most recent 9, and 
2) Even when the desired conversation is within the most recent 9, a short title is often not enough to identify everything that was discussed.

Currently the only way to find prior conversations is to do a local document search of the JSON in the .openhands-state folder, get the conversation's id, & then directly visit its url.

title: MCP Server should be able to run inside the sandbox
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

At the moment, MCP Servers can only be connected through a service running on localhost outside the sandbox, even if such a server could in principle be started within the container. This completely bypasses any safety mechanisms - for example an MCP server with a shell tool can do arbitrary things outside the sandbox even if all openhands tools are operating within it.

This is a technically unnecessary restriction


**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

While connecting to a server via sse over localhost is a good feature, it should not be the only nor the default way to connect to MCP servers. Most clients connect via stdio, starting the MCP server by themselves. Openhands could run the server within the sandbox if a server-startup script (e.g., for installing necessary things) and a command to start it with stdio protocol is provided. This would greatly enhance both functionality and security


**Additional context**

title: [Bug]: Guardrails against infinite loops
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

The biggest "operational" issue I've noticed with OpenHands is that sometimes it gets stuck in a logical loop, and goes on infinitely, burning tokens until you notice & stop it. It seems like there should be some kind of guard rails against this. For example, I've seen it doing things like: Let me try to build the application; OK, first let's install (package X); Let me try to build the application; OK, first let's install (package X); and so on and so on, because one or the other didn't work.

Similar but not quite identical, I've seen it do things like "Let me fix the remaining indentation" many times in a row. I realized that it's actually continuing to go a few lines at a time changing the indentation, but this is a ton of back-and-forth / tokens, so it seems like it should be caught by a similar guardrail - i.e. at a certain point say "It looks like we might be stuck - would you like me to continue?" That way it won't just keep burning tokens on non-productive work.

Docker command in README

title: [Bug]: setup.sh is not executed by the GitHub Actions resolver
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When I ran the OpenHands issue resolver on my private repository, it seemed that ./openhands/setup.sh was not executed.
I use this workflow.
https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/.github/workflows/openhands-resolver.yml

According to the documentation, ./openhands/setup.sh should be executed:
https://docs.all-hands.dev/modules/usage/customization/repository

I conducted some investigation.

From the source code, it appears that setup.sh is called by the maybe_run_setup_script method of the Runtime class in runtime/base.py.

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/cd9d96766c3a46ecbdccdd33a08eb3b4c8b49ecb/openhands/runtime/base.py#L383

This method is called in run_controller within core/main.py.

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/core/main.py#L116

However, this only happens when runtime is None:

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/core/main.py#L104

The run_controller function is called in the process_issue function in resolve_issue.py:

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/resolver/resolve_issue.py#L242

But since the runtime is already created by create_runtime earlier in the process, runtime is not None, and as a result, setup.sh is not called.

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/resolver/resolve_issue.py#L226

body:
I am trying to use a custom sandbox and I have tried both, the CLI mode and also de dev method with the config.toml. 

With the CLI method I use SANDBOX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ENV_VARS to set the proxies for runtime following https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/6672

```
export SANDBOX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ENV_VARS= "{'HTTP_PROXY':'http://myproxy.com:912', 'HTTPS_PROXY':'https://myproxy:912', 'NO_PROXY':'localhost,127.0.0.1,host.docker.internal' }"

docker run -it \
  --privileged \
  --pull=always \
  --runtime=nvidia \
  --gpus all \
  -e SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE=nvidia/cuda:12.6.2-devel-ubuntu22.04 \
  -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ENV_VARS=$SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE \

  docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.33 \
  python -m openhands.core.cli
```

With this approach fails during image build because cannot reach pypi.org. I have verified from inside the app container I can pip install correctly, but this looks an issue in the runtime.

I also noticed the build command doesn't show the SANDBOX_RUNTIME_STARTUP_ENV_VARS

With the config.toml mehtod below the build also fails
```
python -m openhands.core.cli --config /home/me/OpenHands/config.toml  

[core]
workspace_base="/home/me/Openhands_workspace"

[llm]
model="anthropic/claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219"

Any ideas on how to make the runtime build work?

A side question to this is that I would also like to have additional mounting volumes mounted in the runtime contaner `(-v ${HF_HOME}/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub,  -v /dev/shm:/dev/shm)` how to do that with CLI mode or config.toml?

title: [Bug]: Certain MCP function names will fail to be called
body: ### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead). - [x] I have checked the existing issues. ### Describe the bug and reproduction steps When playing around with MCP, I noticed that certain MCP function names would get munged and then fail to be called, for example with this function called `get_model_info`: I traced this issue to CodeActAgent's function_calling.py, when it is constructing the MCPAction object: ```python elif tool_call.function.name.endswith(MCPClientTool.postfix()): action = McpAction( name=tool_call.function.name.rstrip(MCPClientTool.postfix()), arguments=tool_call.function.arguments, ) ``` it turns out this usage of `rstrip()` is misguided. It will strip ending characters matching ANY character from `MCPClientTool.postfix()`. In my test this postfix resolved to `_mcp_tool_call`, hence why the "o" was being dropped from my function name. I'll send a PR momentarily. ### OpenHands Installation Docker command in README ### OpenHands Version _No response_ ### Operating System None ### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context _No response_

title: [proposal] make response_to_actions() a classmethod
body:
I have an application where I've extended CodeActAgent with a subclass. However, I also need to modify the behavior of `response_to_actions`, which is currently defined as a [module-level function](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/5d749aeba795d026cc1eb14339955752ebd35346/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/function_calling.py#L56).

Is there a reason this could not be a classmethod of CodeActAgent, so that its behavior can be optionally overridden by a child class?

The only argument against it that I can think of is if you wanted to have the function calling capability be composable (rather than inheritable). For example, it could possibly be useful to expose only the MCP function calling ability via a Mixin class, or something like that.

I'd be interested in the maintainers thoughts on this, and thanks for your time!

title: [Bug]: PAT with SSO results in 'invalid github token'
body:
**Describe the bug and reproduction steps**  
Users with PATs configured with SSO encounter an 'Invalid GitHub Token' error when using organizational tokens. This error occurs as soon as users attempt to save their token in OpenHands settings. The issue started after upgrading from version 0.21 to version 0.22, presumably due to changes in GitHub token logic. The problem persists across recent versions up to 0.30 but works in version 0.21. Attempts to regenerate tokens, clear cached settings, and use incognito mode have failed to resolve the issue.  
Steps:
1. Open OpenHands version >= 0.22.
2. Navigate to 'Settings' and enter a token configured with SSO.
3. Save the settings.
4. Observe the error notification: 'Invalid GitHub Token'.

**Describe any potential solutions to the bug**  
One suggestion is to verify changes made to GitHub authentication logic between versions 0.21 and 0.22. The commit history for this update can be found here: <https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/commit/36c2abadc2c2e2b9bece59a88fbe34acdf0267d5>. Ensure compatibility for organizational tokens that rely on SSO-based policies.

**Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context**  
Message thread confirms that users with personal tokens (non-organizational) do not face this issue. Relevant organizational tokens are confirmed to have the necessary permissions and expiration dates validated. 
Attached screenshot: <https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T06P212QSEA-F08L2GZP8JD/download/screenshot_2025-03-28_at_09.29.54.png>

author: enyst

title: larger code file editing/viewing improvements
body:
I've been using Open Hands for a couple months now and I find `str_replace_editor` causes a lot of problems when working with code files longer than a few hundred lines.

Here are a few suggested improvements:

1. It would be nice if the view truncation limit was configurable on an advanced configuration level. I personally run DeepSeek-V3-0324 locally and I have a fair degree of control over how long the context length is and how long the max output per response is through `ktransformers`. It wastes time when `str_replace_editor` truncates a 900 line file. I'd much prefer that it just spit out the file in its entirety. I realize not everyone wants this functionality when deal with pay per million token APIs, but it makes sense for me because I'm only paying for the cost of electricity.

2. When writing unit tests for code of more than trivial complexity, it is common to have duplicate lines in the unit test file. This makes it extremely difficult to edit the file with `str_replace_editor` due to the uniqueness constraint. Has anyone tried adding a line number option to `str_replace_editor` so that the uniqueness constraint can be bypassed when a line number is also provided? My mind keeps coming back to the `diff` and `patch` tools in unix systems as they appear to have solved this problem a long time ago.

Similar to https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/6889

title: [Bug]: Missing path parameter `conversation_id` in OpenAPI spec
body: ### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead). - [x] I have checked the existing issues. ### Describe the bug and reproduction steps OpenAPI spec of endpoints containing `conversation_id`, such as `/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/config`, should have a path parameter for `conversation_id`, but currently it does not. As a result, debugging APIs via Swagger UI does not work properly, and code generation based on the spec may fail. As shown in the screenshot, conversation_id is not in the parameter. Including conversation_id as a path parameter in the endpoints will fix Swagger UI debugging issues and improve code generation compatibility. ### OpenHands Installation Docker command in README ### OpenHands Version v0.34 ### Operating System MacOS ### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context This issue occurs because `conversation_id` is not included in the handler’s arguments: https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/5fa01ed278fea17acf38f0b6092b13cd3e466ad5/openhands/server/routes/conversation.py#L11 `conversation` is set to `state` in `AttachConversationMiddleware` However, I think that using `Depends` is more typical way in FastAPI, for example: ```python @app.get('/config') async def get_remote_runtime_config(conversation=Depends(get_conversation)): ... ``` ```python async def get_conversation(request: Request, conversation_id: str): user_id = await get_user_id(request) conversation = await shared.conversation_manager.attach_to_conversation( conversation_id, user_id ) if not conversation: raise HTTPException( status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="Conversation not found", ) try: yield conversation finally: await shared.conversation_manager.detach_from_conversation(conversation) ``` In this way, conversation is attached/detached before/after the handler, and `conversation_id` is declared in the path parameter. If this approach looks good, I would be willing to submit a PR.

title: Fix empty string content handling in ConversationMemory
body:
## Issue Description

When `ConversationMemory` processes observations into messages, it checks if `assistant_msg.content is not None` to determine whether to include content in the message. However, if `assistant_msg.content` is an empty string (''), this check passes, but then causes validation errors with the Anthropic API because it requires a valid text field.

### Error
```
litellm.BadRequestError: AzureException - -4316: messages.3.content.0.text.text: Field required
```

### Root Cause
The current check `if assistant_msg.content is not None` allows empty strings to be included in the content array. When using the Anthropic API, this causes validation errors as it expects the text field to be valid.

### Solution
Change the condition from `if assistant_msg.content is not None` to `if assistant_msg.content` so that both None and empty strings result in an empty content list, avoiding the validation error.

This is a small but crucial fix for ensuring compatibility with the Anthropic API.

### Images

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/baf47cdd-fb71-4d46-909a-7db452237003)

title: [Bug]: Agent delegation seems to be broken
body: ### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead). - [x] I have checked the existing issues. ### Describe the bug and reproduction steps As of at least 0.33 (and I believe much earlier), agent delegation seem to be broken. As a minimal test to reproduce the error, I checked out v0.35 and added the following lines to CodeActAgent, right after the `/exit` message handling in `step()`: ```python if latest_user_message and latest_user_message.content.strip() == '/exit': return AgentFinishAction() elif latest_user_message and latest_user_message.content.strip().startswith( '/delegate' ): print("Trying to delegate to ReadOnlyAgent") return AgentDelegateAction( agent='ReadOnlyAgent', inputs=latest_user_message.content.strip().removeprefix('/delegate'), ) ``` When I use this "slash command" to try to ask the agent to delegate the task, the agent gets stuck indefinitely in the state "Agent is running task": Here are the contents of the backend server logs when I send the /delegate command: ``` 18:59:39 - openhands:INFO: agent_controller.py:586 - [Agent Controller e64e57d44bad40939019532394bdc00a] Setting agent(CodeActAgent) state from AgentState.AWAITING_USER_INPUT to AgentState.RUNNING 18:59:39 - openhands:INFO: agent_controller.py:774 - [Agent Controller e64e57d44bad40939019532394bdc00a] Agent not stepping because of pending action: RecallAction (id=11) Trying to delegate to ReadOnlyAgent 19:00:33 - openhands:INFO: standalone_conversation_manager.py:106 - Conversation e64e57d44bad40939019532394bdc00a connected in 0.01733994483947754 seconds ``` ### OpenHands Installation Docker command in README ### OpenHands Version _No response_ ### Operating System None ### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context _No response_

title: [Bug]: Fix the resolver to comment / finish without code changes
body:
### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

The resolver should account for the possibility that a run doesn't end with code changes. They should not be a requirement. 

I think we should fix this to allow the resolver to comment / finish without code changes. Display the explanation in a comment in the issue or PR, like we do for runs with code changes.

You can find the resolver in openhands/resolver.

You do not need to run it, I took care of it in CI. You do need to write unit tests to verify the behavior, please find the suitable place for tests in the same resolver tests file as other tests of this part of the code.

GitHub resolver

main

title: Enhance Workflow Flexibility with Support for User-Defined Runners
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Right now, the OpenHands resolver workflow have the runs-on locked to ubuntu-latest.

In my setup, for example, I’m running gh runners inside a Kubernetes cluster. These runners are already configured with access to private container registries and the necessary secrets to pull customized runtime images. That setup just works but only if the workflow actually runs on those runners.

Since the OpenHands workflow doesn’t let you set the runs-on, there’s no way to point it to your own runners. So if you need to use pre-configured ones (like I do), your only option is to fork the whole workflow or hack around it (which kinda defeats the whole point of reusing it cleanly)

Adding a runner input fixes this by letting you tell the workflow which runner to use. 


### If you find this feature request or enhancement useful, make sure to add a 👍 to the issue

title: [Feature]: Fix CLI Display for Agent Messages
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
The CLI mode does not display the agent's query or confirmation when requesting user input. This results in confusion for the user, as they only see a `>` prompt to type their next instruction without knowing what the agent is asking for or if the agent has completed execution.

**Desired UX of the solution**
To solve this, the CLI mode should display the agent's message at each instance where user input is requested. This would improve the interaction flow and provide clarity on what the agent expects.

**Technical implementation**
The CLI implementation must include a feature to print the agent's message preceding the user input prompt. This could be done by appending the agent's context directly before rendering the `>` prompt.

**Alternatives considered**
<N/A>

**Additional context**
<N/A>

title: [Bug]: Cost-Termination Flag Not Triggering Due to Incorrect Metrics Reference
body:
**Describe the bug and reproduction steps**
While reviewing the codebase, in agent_controller.py, line 803 (https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/de175dcc8757d377cb6a8aa45eba4ae835e87c44/openhands/controller/agent_controller.py#L803), it was noted that `self.state.metrics.accumulated_cost` is being checked instead of `self.agent.llm.metrics.accumulated_cost`. As per the understanding, `self.state.metrics` should represent the total cost; however, this value does not update after each LLM call. This behavior results in the cost-termination flag not being triggered when expected, even after setting `max_budget_per_task` in AppConfig.

**Potential solutions**
The code could be updated to use `self.agent.llm.metrics.accumulated_cost`, as initial tests have shown this resolves the issue.

title: Add support for custom volume mounts in DockerRuntime
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
Currently, the DockerRuntime only supports mounting the workspace directory into the container. However, there are use cases where users need to mount additional directories from the host machine into the container, such as:

- Mounting read-only model directories (like pre-trained ML models)
- Accessing shared data directories
- Mounting temporary storage for downloads or generated content
- Using host machine's cached dependencies to improve performance

This is particularly useful when working with large datasets or models that already exist on the host machine and should be accessible from within the runtime environment.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**
I suggest implementing a new environment variable CUSTOM_VOLUMES that allows users to specify additional volume mounts in the following format:
```
CUSTOM_VOLUMES=/host/path1:/container/path1:rw,/host/path2:/container/path2:ro
```

Each mount specification consists of three parts:

- Host path: The path on the host machine
- Container path: Where to mount it inside the container
- Access mode: rw for read-write or ro for read-only

Multiple mounts would be separated by commas. The DockerRuntime would parse this environment variable and add these additional mounts when creating the container.

For example, users could run:
```shell
docker run -it -d \
    -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik \
    -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
    -e CUSTOM_VOLUMES="/opt/openhands/workspace:/workspace:rw,/mnt/data1:/data1:ro" \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    -v ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state \
    -p 3000:3000 \
    --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
    --name openhands-app \
    docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.36
```

body:

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

Hi all,

I’m seeing a consistent “Forbidden” error in the VS Code introduced by [PR #8033](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/8033)  whenever I connect to OpenHands via my machine’s LAN IP, although everything works perfectly when I connect via localhost.

## Description
When running OpenHands with the officially‑recommended Docker deployment, the embedded VS Code editor loads correctly at http://localhost:3000 but shows only a white page with the word:

Forbidden



if I connect instead to http://local IP:3000. All other parts of the UI (chat, settings, file browser, etc.) work fine over both URLs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. **Pull and run OpenHands** using the exact command below:
    

bash
    docker run -it --rm --pull=always \
        -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik \
        -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
        -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
        -v ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state \
        -p 3000:3000 \
        --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
        --name openhands-app \
        docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.36


2. **Open in browser via localhost**  
   Navigate to http://localhost:3000 → click the **VS Code** tab → the in‑browser editor appears as expected.
3. **Open in browser via LAN IP**  
   Navigate to http://local IP:3000 (on the same machine or a different machine on the network) → click the **VS Code** tab → the tab shows only Forbidden.

## Expected Behavior
The VS Code tab should embed the headless code‑server editor identically, regardless of whether I connect via localhost or the host’s LAN IP.

## Actual Behavior
Only localhost connections succeed. Any non‑localhost origin yields a 403 “Forbidden” in the VS Code iframe.

## Environment
- **OpenHands image**: docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.36  
- **Runtime image**: docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik  
- **OS**: Linux Mint 21.3 (Ubuntu 22.04 “Jammy”), kernel 5.15.0-139-generic

It would be a pity, if it stayed this way. Not being able to access OpenHands from a different machine on my local network severely limits its utility for me.

title: [Feature]: Move enable/disable prompt extensions to app config
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**  
The user wants to disable specific microagents such as `gitlab`. Current behavior suggests that a config option to disable prompt extensions exists for agents, but this isn't properly accounted for in the front-end. 

One alternative is moving the option to app config, instead of per agent. In that case, when it's disabled, memory.py will not create these observations at all, so they will not be in the event stream.

**Desired UX of the solution**  
The configuration option for enable/disable prompts should function without introducing dependencies from system components to agent configuration. The user should see only applicable events based on the app's configuration settings.

**Technical implementation**  
To correctly implement this, the enable/disable prompt extensions should be moved to app config. This ensures that agent runtime or memory components adhere to the configuration without needing agent-specific information nor lead to inconsistencies in the stream.

IMPORTANT:
This implies that when the user has it disabled, and runs the agent for a while, the RecallObs, both types, are not in the stream. But when the session is restored, with it enabled, then:
- the RecallObs with type WORKSPACE_CONTEXT is created and inserted in the stream
- the FE receives it when it reads the stream (listen_socket.py)
- the condenser finds it in history and skips it (it shouldn't be summarized)
- agent LLM will eventually receive it from conversation_memory `process_events` *in the right order*

title: [Bug]: OpenHands 0.36 Fails Agent Initialization due to `/update_mcp_server` 404 Error
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

# Bug Report: OpenHands 0.36 Fails Agent Initialization due to `/update_mcp_server` 404 Error

## Affected Versions & Environment

* **OpenHands Application:** `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.36`
* **Runtime Image:** `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik`
* **Host Operating System:** macOS
* **Docker Environment:** Docker Desktop (installed via Homebrew)

## Problem Description

OpenHands version 0.36, when used with the `runtime:0.36-nikolaik` image, fails to initialize agent sessions. The `openhands-app` container logs a `404 Not Found` error. This error occurs because the application cannot reach the required `/update_mcp_server` endpoint at `http://host.docker.internal:35078/update_mcp_server` on the runtime container.

## Steps to Reproduce

1.  Execute the following Docker command. This command reflects the exact setup used when this issue was originally encountered:

    ```bash
    docker run -it --rm --pull=always \
      -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik \
      -e SANDBOX_ADD_HOSTS="host.docker.internal:host-gateway" \
      -e LLM_API_KEY="ollama" \
      -e LLM_BASE_URL="[http://127.0.0.1:11434](http://127.0.0.1:11434)" \
      -e LLM_OLLAMA_BASE_URL="[http://127.0.0.1:11434](http://127.0.0.1:11434)" \
      -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
      -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
      -v ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state \
      -p 3000:3000 \
      --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
      --name openhands-app \
      docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.36
    ```

2.  Observe the `openhands-app` container's logs for errors during agent session initialization. To view these logs while the container attempts to run or after it exits, use the command:
    `docker logs openhands-app` (if the container is still named `openhands-app`) or `docker logs <container_id_if_renamed_or_exited>`.

3.  Identify the dynamically created runtime container. While OpenHands attempts to start (or immediately after an error), execute `docker ps` in a separate terminal to list running containers. The runtime container's name often appears similar to `openhands-runtime-[SESSION_ID_EXAMPLE]` (where the session ID is a long unique string), or you can use its shorter Container ID from the `docker ps` output. If the container has already stopped, use `docker ps -a` to find it.
    Then, inspect its logs using:
    `docker logs <actual_runtime_container_name_or_id>`
    These logs will reveal how it handles requests to `/update_mcp_server`.

## Observed Behavior

* The `openhands-app` log clearly displays the 404 error:
    ```log
    [TIMESTAMP] - openhands:ERROR: session.py:[LINE_NO] - Error creating agent_session: Client error '404 Not Found' for url '[http://host.docker.internal:35078/update_mcp_server](http://host.docker.internal:35078/update_mcp_server)'
    ```

* The `openhands-runtime-[SESSION_ID_EXAMPLE]` container's log (using image `runtime:0.36-nikolaik`) confirms its internal Uvicorn server receives the request for `/update_mcp_server` and directly returns a 404 status:
    ```log
    INFO:     [HOST_IP_IN_LOGS]:[CLIENT_PORT] - "POST /update_mcp_server HTTP/1.1" 404 Not Found
    ```

## Expected Behavior

The OpenHands agent session should initialize without errors. The runtime container (`runtime:0.36-nikolaik`) should correctly provide and handle requests to the `/update_mcp_server` endpoint at `http://host.docker.internal:35078/update_mcp_server`.

## Impact

This bug makes OpenHands version 0.36 unusable with the specified `runtime:0.36-nikolaik` image combination because the agent cannot start.

## Recommendations for Developers

1.  **Investigate Endpoint:** Please determine why the `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.36-nikolaik` image lacks a functional `/update_mcp_server` endpoint.
2.  **Rectify or Update:** Correct the runtime image to provide this essential endpoint. Alternatively, if the `openhands:0.36` application's requirements for this endpoint have changed (e.g., different path, or it is no longer necessary), update the application accordingly.

MacOS

title: [Bug]: LLM Connection Fails for Dockerized OpenHands to Host Ollama - UI Settings Override `host.docker.internal`
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

# Bug Report: LLM Connection Fails for Dockerized OpenHands to Host Ollama - UI Settings Override `host.docker.internal`

## Affected Versions & Environment (for diagnosis of this specific issue)

* **OpenHands Application:** `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.34`
* **Runtime Image:** `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.34-nikolaik`
* **Host Operating System:** macOS
* **Docker Environment:** Docker Desktop (installed via Homebrew)
* **LLM:** Ollama (running on the host machine)

Note: The 0.36 documentation has the same issue as I only changed the value 0.36 to 0.34 to get around issue https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/8317 and then proceed here.

## Problem Description

OpenHands, when running in a Docker container, fails to connect to an Ollama instance that operates on the host machine. I experienced `litellm.APIConnectionError: OllamaException - [Errno 111] Connection refused`. This problem persisted even when I correctly set `LLM_OLLAMA_BASE_URL` or `LLM_BASE_URL` environment variables in the Docker command to `http://host.docker.internal:11434`.


## Final Working Configuration Steps for Users (Example for OpenHands 0.34 & Local Ollama on Host)

To successfully use OpenHands 0.34 in Docker with a local Ollama instance on your host, I found the following steps effective:

1.  **Set UI Configuration First (Most Reliable Approach):**
    * Start OpenHands using the Docker command detailed in the next step.
    * Immediately open your browser and navigate to `http://localhost:3000/settings`.
    * Locate the LLM settings, specifically the field for "Ollama Base URL" or the general "LLM Base URL".
    * Set this value to **`http://host.docker.internal:11434`**.
        *(Note: For Ollama with LiteLLM, usually only the base address `http://host.docker.internal:11434` is needed. The specific model, e.g., `ollama/granite3.3`, is typically selected elsewhere in the UI or relies on a default if the `LLM_MODEL_NAME` environment variable is not used.)*
    * Save the settings in the UI. This action ensures the correct URL is persisted in the `~/.openhands-state` volume.

2.  **Use the Following Docker Command:**
    *(This command was provided by the user in the problem description and represents a working setup once the UI settings are correct. Environment variables for LLM URLs serve as defaults if UI is not set, but UI settings will take precedence.)*

```bash
docker run -it --rm --pull=always \
  -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.34-nikolaik \
  -e SANDBOX_ADD_HOSTS="host.docker.internal:host-gateway" \
  -e LLM_API_KEY="ollama" \
  -e LLM_BASE_URL="http://host.docker.internal:11434" \
  -e LLM_OLLAMA_BASE_URL="http://host.docker.internal:11434" \
  -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -v ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  --name openhands-app \
  docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.34
```

3.  **Verify Host Setup:**
    * Ensure Ollama runs on your host and is accessible (e.g., `curl http://localhost:11434` from your host terminal should return "Ollama is running%").
    * Confirm your host firewall (e.g., macOS firewall) allows incoming connections from Docker to port `11434`.
    * As a definitive test of container-to-host connectivity, once `openhands-app` is running, execute `docker exec -it openhands-app curl http://host.docker.internal:11434` from another terminal; it should also confirm Ollama is running.


## Recommendations for OpenHands Users Troubleshooting Similar Issues:

* **Inspect Container Logs:** When troubleshooting, always check the logs:
    * For the main application: `docker logs openhands-app` (if named so, or use the container ID if it has exited or been renamed).
    * For runtime issues: First, identify the runtime container. Use `docker ps` (for running containers) or `docker ps -a` (for all containers) to find its name (often like `openhands-runtime-[SESSION_ID_EXAMPLE]`) or its Container ID. Then, view its logs with `docker logs <runtime_container_name_or_id>`.
* If using OpenHands in Docker to connect to a service (like Ollama) on your host machine, **always use `host.docker.internal:[PORT_NUMBER]`** for the URL, not `localhost:[PORT_NUMBER]`.
* **Crucially, check and update the OpenHands Web UI settings (via `http://localhost:3000/settings` on your host browser)** for LLM configurations. If you have run OpenHands before, these UI settings can contain outdated `localhost` URLs which will override your environment variables. Ensure the URL in the UI is set to `http://host.docker.internal:[PORT_NUMBER]`.
* Temporarily disabling your host machine's firewall can help diagnose whether it is blocking network connectivity between the container and the host.


## Root Causes Identified

1.  **Persisted UI Configuration with Incorrect `localhost` URL:** I had previously run OpenHands (likely in a non-Docker or different Docker network setup) and had manually configured the LLM Base URL in the Web UI to `http://localhost:11434/v1`. When I later ran OpenHands 0.34 in the current Docker setup, this persisted UI setting (loaded via the `~/.openhands-state` volume) took precedence over the environment variables, as is expected behavior for UI configurations. However, the stored `http://localhost:11434/v1` value is incorrect for a Docker container attempting to reach a service on the Docker host, leading to the connection failure.

2.  **Lack of Clear Guidance for Docker Host Networking in UI/Docs:** When I encountered the connection issue, the system did not provide clear feedback or guidance that my persisted UI setting (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) would be problematic in the new Dockerized context, nor did it clearly direct me to update this UI setting to `http://host.docker.internal:11434`. The log snippet from `LLMSummarizingCondenserConfig` showing `base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1'` alongside `ollama_base_url='http://host.docker.internal:11434'` further highlighted that a `localhost`-based URL was active in the configuration, likely propagated from this primary UI setting.

## Steps to Reproduce (Illustrates UI Override with OpenHands v0.34)

1.  Ensure your Ollama service runs on the host machine and is accessible (e.g., at `http://localhost:11434`).

2.  (Pre-condition for reproduction): Have a pre-existing `~/.openhands-state` where the LLM base URL was previously saved as `http://localhost:11434/v1` through the UI. Or, as part of this test:
    a.  Run OpenHands once with any Docker command that mounts `~/.openhands-state`.
    b.  Access the OpenHands UI (`http://localhost:3000/settings`). Navigate to LLM settings. Explicitly set the Ollama base URL to `http://localhost:11434/v1`. Save settings. Stop the container.

3.  Now, run OpenHands 0.34 using the Docker command with environment variables pointing to `host.docker.internal` (as I did during debugging, though the user's *initial* failing command for this scenario as provided in their text below uses `127.0.0.1` which would also fail, but for a different primary reason if UI wasn't overriding):

```bash
docker run -it --rm --pull=always \
  -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.34-nikolaik \
  -e SANDBOX_ADD_HOSTS="host.docker.internal:host-gateway" \
  -e LLM_API_KEY="ollama" \
  -e LLM_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:11434" \
  -e LLM_OLLAMA_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:11434" \
  -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -v ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  --name openhands-app \
  docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.34
```

4.  Attempt to use the LLM agent by submitting a prompt (e.g., "make a python script to add two numbers together"). Check the `openhands-app` logs for errors. I viewed these logs by running `docker logs openhands-app` (when the container was named `openhands-app`).

## Observed Behavior

The agent fails to connect to Ollama. The `openhands-app` logs show:
    ```log
    [TIMESTAMP] - openhands:ERROR: agent_controller.py:[LINE_NO] - ... litellm.APIConnectionError: OllamaException - [Errno 111] Connection refused
    ```
This happens because OpenHands attempts to connect to `http://localhost:11434/v1` (the value from the previously saved UI settings) from within the container. Inside the container, `localhost` refers to the container itself, not the host where Ollama actually runs.

## Expected Behavior

When running in Docker and connecting to a host service, OpenHands should ideally make it straightforward for users to configure the correct address (`http://host.docker.internal:11434`) or `localhost`, `0.0.0.0`, and/or 127.0.0.1 should work as in the instructions. If UI settings take precedence (which is normal), users need clear guidance on how to manage these settings for different environments (Dockerized vs. non-Dockerized).

## Impact

Users with pre-existing configurations who switch to a Dockerized setup can face significant difficulty and confusion in getting OpenHands to connect to local LLMs. This requires extensive troubleshooting if the impact of persisted UI settings and the need for `host.docker.internal` are not clear.

## Recommendations for Developers

1.  **Clarify Configuration Precedence and Persistence:**
    * While UI settings overriding environment variables is standard, please explicitly document this behavior and the role of `~/.openhands-state`.
    * Consider logging the source of critical configuration values (e.g., "LLM Base URL loaded from UI settings") at startup or when an agent session begins. This would greatly aid user debugging.

2.  **Improve Guidance for Docker Networking & UI Configuration:**
    To help users correctly configure connections from Dockerized OpenHands to host services like Ollama:
    * **Option A (Enhance System Design for `localhost` Usability):** Explore ways for OpenHands (when running in Docker) to intelligently handle `http://localhost:[PORT]` entries in its configuration (whether from UI or defaults). For example, it could attempt to resolve `localhost` to `host.docker.internal` internally, or provide a clear in-app mechanism to switch context. This would simplify the experience for users who previously used `localhost` in non-Docker setups.
    * **Option B (Explicit `host.docker.internal` Documentation & UI Assistance):** If direct user configuration of `host.docker.internal` remains the primary method:
        * **Documentation:** Provide clear, prominent documentation. Stress that `host.docker.internal:[PORT]` must be used for host services in **both** environment variables AND **Web UI settings** when OpenHands is Dockerized.
        * **Web UI Enhancements:** Add tooltips or help text in the UI settings near URL input fields, explaining `host.docker.internal`. Consider a UI warning if `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` is detected in such a field when OpenHands knows it's running in Docker.

3.  **Review Default Fallbacks:**
    * If no UI setting is present and environment variables are also not set for an LLM URL, ensure any internal default values are sensible and clearly documented. Avoid `localhost` defaults for external services if OpenHands is in Docker.

Thanks for giving this a look!

title: [enhancement] [medium severity] [small effort] Allow overriding `file_viewer_server.py` bind address and public URL via environment variables
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

When running OpenHands on Synology Docker (or any platform where containers must use `bridge` network mode), the runtime’s file viewer server binds to `127.0.0.1` and generates public URLs using `localhost:<port>`. This causes iframe features like the embedded VSCode and file viewer to be unreachable from the host or frontend, even when ports are exposed with `-p`.

This makes OpenHands runtime partially unusable in any production-like environment where `--network host` is not available.

---

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

Make the host binding and generated public URL for `file_viewer_server.py` configurable via environment variables, like this:

```python
host = os.environ.get('FILE_VIEWER_HOST', '127.0.0.1')
public_url_host = os.environ.get('FILE_VIEWER_PUBLIC_HOST', 'localhost')

config = Config(app=app, host=host, port=port, log_level='error')
server_url = f'http://{public_url_host}:{port}'
```

Then users can run the runtime container with:

```bash
-e FILE_VIEWER_HOST=0.0.0.0
-e FILE_VIEWER_PUBLIC_HOST=192.168.1.200
```

This change would preserve current behavior by default, while allowing flexibility for real-world deployments.

---

**Additional context**

This limitation affects platforms like Synology DSM, Rancher Desktop, and many Kubernetes environments where `host` networking mode is not available. Enabling control over the bind address and public URL makes OpenHands runtime more compatible with containerized deployments.

---

title: [Bug]: Resolver PR Review Trigger Not Working in Private Repos
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

In private repos, `github.event.comment.author_association` and `github.event.review.author_association` [are set to](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/18690) `NONE` instead of `MEMBER` if the user has their organizational membership set to private (which appears to be the default. This cause the issue comment and pull request review triggers to fail to fire as defined [here](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/.github/workflows/openhands-resolver.yml#L83C10-L83C48).

I believe the fix should be to add `NONE` to the above linked or clause, or to add a new input variable that can be used to override this requirement in some way.

### OpenHands Installation

GitHub resolver

0.37.0

title: [Bug]: max_output_tokens in openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet doesn't work correctly
body: ### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead). - [x] I have checked the existing issues. ### Describe the bug and reproduction steps #### Bug Description When using llm of `openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet`, the value of `max_output_tokens` works incorrectly, which will result loop stuck when the Agent tries to generate long response (> 4096 tokens). #### Bug Result Loop stuck: `file_text` error: #### Bug Logs for ModelInfo ``` LLMSummarizingCondenserConfig(type='llm', llm_config=LLMConfig(model='openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet', api_key='******'('**********'), base_url='', api_version=None, aws_access_key_id='******', aws_secret_access_key='******', aws_region_name=None, openrouter_site_url='https://docs.all-hands.dev/', openrouter_app_name='OpenHands', num_retries=4, retry_multiplier=2, retry_min_wait=5, retry_max_wait=30, timeout=None, max_message_chars=30000, temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, custom_llm_provider=None, max_input_tokens=200000, max_output_tokens=8192, input_cost_per_token=None, output_cost_per_token=None, ollama_base_url=None, drop_params=True, modify_params=True, disable_vision=None, caching_prompt=True, log_completions=False, log_completions_folder='/app/logs/completions', custom_tokenizer=None, native_tool_calling=None, reasoning_effort='high', seed=None), keep_first=4, max_size=80, max_event_length=10000) ``` #### Root Cause Analysis: In `llm.py` (line 406-421), it has a check and configuration for `max_output_tokens`: ```python if self.config.max_output_tokens is None: # Safe default for any potentially viable model self.config.max_output_tokens = 4096 if self.model_info is not None: # max_output_tokens has precedence over max_tokens, if either exists. # litellm has models with both, one or none of these 2 parameters! if 'max_output_tokens' in self.model_info and isinstance( self.model_info['max_output_tokens'], int ): self.config.max_output_tokens = self.model_info['max_output_tokens'] elif 'max_tokens' in self.model_info and isinstance( self.model_info['max_tokens'], int ): self.config.max_output_tokens = self.model_info['max_tokens'] if 'claude-3-7-sonnet' in self.config.model: self.config.max_output_tokens = 64000 # litellm set max to 128k, but that requires a header to be set ``` It only handles `claude-3-7-sonnet` (official provider), which can't handle `claude-3.7-sonnet` (openrouter provider) #### Fix Suggestion Add `claude-3.7-sonnet` to current check. ### OpenHands Installation Development workflow ### OpenHands Version 0.37.0 ### Operating System MacOS ### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context _No response_

title: Document `get_impl` and `import_from`
body:
The `get_impl` function in `openhands.utils.import_utils` is one of the extensibility mechanisms in the project. It allows applications built on openhands to customize behavior by redefining and substituting at runtime their own implementations of the classes that this function is used for.

Look up its uses in the project.

For example, you can find the conversation manager implemented as a `StandaloneConversationManager`, which is single server. Since it's instantiated via `get_impl` and `import_from`, an application can substitute a clustered conversation manager and use it where their superclass is used.

Add clear docstrings to them, and to each class that uses them.

Also, find an appropriate place for a readme or add to an existing readme a simple, concise explanation of how it works. Maybe the `server` readme, but only if all uses are in `server` module, if they're elsewhere then it's not a good place. Maybe near where it's defined. Choose wisely, I count on you. :)

title: [proposal] modify LLMConfig.native_tool_calling semantics
body:
I'm often using openhands with LLMs that I self-host with vLLM. Unfortunately, vLLM and litellm together don't do a great job of determining the model's capability, which is actually kind of tricky. For example, a model like llama3 or qwen may or may not support native tool calling, depending on whether the `--enable-auto-tool-choice` flag and an appropriate tool calling parser are provided to the vLLM server.

There is already a `native_tool_calling` config option in `LLMConfig`; however, its current semantics are not intuitive:

* `native_tool_calling == None`: (default) Openhands will check against its own hard-coded list of `FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS`, and enable it if the model is listed
* `native_tool_calling == False`: Tool calling is disabled
* `native_tool_calling == True`: OH does not check against its own list of supported models. Instead, it uses `litellm.supports_function_calling(model_name)` and if that returns true, then it is enabled, otherwise, it's disabled.

The problem is if I have my own custom model provider, which I specify as e.g. `vllm_hosted/llama3.3`, that neither passes the check for OH supported models, nor does litellm correctly determine it is capable. Therefore, because of the above semantics, I cannot enable tool calling even if I set `native_tool_calling = True` in the config, which is confusing and does not seem like the expected result.

I propose redefining `native_tool_calling = ['auto', 'true', 'false']` with the following semantics:
* `native_tool_calling = false`: Native tool calling will be disabled.
* `native_tool_calling = true`: Native tool calling will be enabled and attempted, even if litellm doesn't think it's supported. (this does not cause errors in litellm, as far as I can tell).
* `native_tool_calling = auto`: OH will check if EITHER: the model is in `FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS` or if `litellm.supports_function_calling(model_name) == True`. This should be the default config value.

Please let me know what you think! I would be happy to send a PR. The biggest downside is that this could break backwards compatibility if people are counting on Mock function calling to happen by default for models that are not in `FUNCTION_CALLING_SUPPORTED_MODELS`, but I think it's worth that corner case in service of the "principle of least surprise".

OpenHands should use the provided API key for authentication when using Gemini models, similar to how it works with other API-key based models like Claude.

Instead of using the API key, OpenHands/LiteLLM is attempting to use Google Cloud's Application Default Credentials (ADC), which results in authentication failures.

Provided API key through LLM_API_KEY secret

Update LiteLLM integration to use the API key authentication method for Gemini models when no ADC credentials are available
Add support for passing Vertex AI credentials through the GitHub Actions workflow
Document the correct way to use Gemini models with OpenHands

Additional Information
Based on examining the codebase, it seems that LiteLLM is defaulting to the Vertex AI authentication method rather than using the Google AI Studio API key method for Gemini models. This makes it difficult to use Gemini through the API key method, which is simpler for many users.

title: [Feature Request]: Make git username and email configurable
body:
**Problem Description**
Currently, OpenHands hardcodes the git user configuration to `user.name "openhands"` and `user.email "openhands@all-hands.dev"` in multiple places throughout the codebase. This prevents users from customizing the git author information for commits made by the agent.

**Current Hardcoded Locations**
- `openhands/runtime/action_execution_server.py` (lines 353-374)
- `openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py` (lines 181-182)
- Various test files

**Proposed Solution**
Add configuration options to allow users to specify custom git username and email through:
1. Environment variables (e.g., `GIT_USER_NAME`, `GIT_USER_EMAIL`)
2. Configuration file options in `config.toml`
3. Fallback to current defaults if not specified

**Use Cases**
- Users want commits to be attributed to their actual identity
- Organizations want commits to use company email addresses
- Different projects may require different git configurations
- Compliance requirements for proper commit attribution

**Implementation Considerations**
- Should work across all runtime types (local, docker, remote)
- Should be consistent between resolver and runtime execution
- Should maintain backward compatibility with current defaults
- Should be documented in configuration documentation

**Related Code Paths**
- [Action Execution Server](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/runtime/action_execution_server.py#L353-374)
- [Pull Request Resolver](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py#L181-182)
- Configuration system in `openhands/core/config/`

**Original Issue Context**
This issue was originally about `setup.sh` not overriding hardcoded git config commands, but the core problem is that git configuration should be configurable through the standard OpenHands configuration system rather than being hardcoded.

title: Allow git treeless clone for faster launch in headless environments
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
Cloning large repos can take 30s+. In an automated environment (e.g. Github Actions) it is very unlikely that we will need the entire contents of the git repository.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**
Per https://github.blog/open-source/git/get-up-to-speed-with-partial-clone-and-shallow-clone/ they call out two approaches:

Blobless clones: `git clone --filter=blob:none <url>`
Treeless clones: `git clone --filter=tree:0 <url>`

They call out:
> In environments like GitHub Actions using public runners, you want to minimize your clone time so you can spend your machine time actually building your software! Treeless clones might be an excellent option for those environments.

Therefore, I think we should support treeless clones.

Pros:
* Much faster cloning
* All data is available, but some will be fetched lazily
Cons:
* Some odd behavior with submodules
* Unpredictable performance of lazy git commands

By making this an opt-in flag, we can provide a meaningful speedup for resolver actions and other headless workflows.
