title: Provide a GPU-enabled Docker default (CUDA support) for AI workloads
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Using the agent to build and run AI workloads often requires access to the machine's GPU. Currently, the Docker setup for the openhands agent does not provide GPU passthrough or CUDA support out of the box, which limits its usefulness for AI/ML development and deployment.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

It would be helpful to provide a default Dockerfile or Docker Compose configuration that supports GPU usage, including:

Base image with CUDA, cuDNN, and other GPU dependencies installed (e.g., nvidia/cuda)

runtime: nvidia or equivalent settings for Docker Compose

Instructions or scripts to launch the container with `--gpus all` using the NVIDIA Container Toolkit

Validation that GPU access is correctly configured (e.g., via nvidia-smi in the container)

This would allow users to immediately utilize their GPU for AI tasks without requiring custom setup.

title: Why is the style different between function call names?
body: Some functions are named like `CmdRunAction` and some are named like `str_replace_editor`. Devstral seems to have awareness of both of these baked into the model, without any external information being provided. Why were these two styles used, and is there some distinction between them? It seems like the model can decide to output `execute_bash`, `CmdRunAction`, or hallucinate `execute_code`. This leads to errors such as: https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/8805

title: Upgrade Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
body:
Large language model (LLM)-powered multi-agent systems (MAS) have demonstrated cognitive and execution capabilities that far exceed those of single LLM agents, yet their capacity for self-evolution remains hampered by underdeveloped memory architectures. Upon close inspection, we are alarmed to discover that prevailing MAS memory mechanisms (1) are overly simplistic, completely disregarding the nuanced inter-agent collaboration trajectories, and (2) lack cross-trial and agent-specific customization, in stark contrast to the expressive memory developed for single agents. To bridge this gap, we introduce G-Memory, a hierarchical, agentic memory system for MAS inspired by organizational memory theory, which manages the lengthy MAS interaction via a three-tier graph hierarchy: insight, query, and interaction graphs. Upon receiving a new user query, G-Memory performs bi-directional memory traversal to retrieve both  that enable the system to leverage cross-trial knowledge, and  that compactly encode prior collaboration experiences. Upon task execution, the entire hierarchy evolves by assimilating new collaborative trajectories, nurturing the progressive evolution of agent teams. Extensive experiments across five benchmarks, three LLM backbones, and three popular MAS frameworks demonstrate that G-Memory improves success rates in embodied action and accuracy in knowledge QA by up to  and , respectively, without any modifications to the original frameworks. Our codes are available at [this https URL](https://github.com/bingreeky/GMemory).

title: Add User Directory Support for Microagents
body:
(openhands-agent, after it made a funny boo-boo and proved it uses `git reflog` better than me 😅)

## Problem
Currently, microagents are read from multiple locations but not from a user-specific directory. This leads to the problem of having uncommitted local microagents in the repository, which can be accidentally lost during git operations (as we experienced when `local.md` and `local-gem.md` were lost during a `git add .` and `git reset --hard`).

## Desired Behavior
The microagents system in OpenHands should read microagents from `~/.openhands/microagents/` in addition to its existing sources. This would allow users to:

1. Store personal/local microagents in their user directory (`~/.openhands/microagents/`)
2. Avoid keeping uncommitted microagent files in repository working directories
3. Have persistent personal microagents across all OpenHands projects

## Current Microagent Sources
As of now, microagents are read from multiple locations, but the user directory is not included. We need to implement reading them from the user directory.

## Implementation Requirements
- Add `~/.openhands/microagents/` as a microagent source
- Ensure proper loading order and precedence
- Maintain compatibility with existing microagent sources
- Handle cases where the user directory doesn't exist (create it or gracefully skip)

## Best Practices for Users
- **Personal/local microagents**: Add them to `~/.openhands/microagents/` instead of keeping them uncommitted in repository directories
- **Shared microagents**: If microagents are intended to be shared with other users, commit them to the repository's `.openhands/microagents/` directory
- **Never keep microagents uncommitted** in repository working directories to avoid accidental loss during git operations

## Files Affected
- Need to identify where microagent loading logic is implemented
- Likely in the microagents system/loader code
- May need to update configuration or initialization code

## Testing
- Verify microagents are loaded from user directory
- Test precedence/priority of different microagent sources
- Ensure backward compatibility with existing microagent locations

title: str_replace_editor create command should require file_text parameter
body:
## Problem

The `str_replace_editor` tool's `create` command currently does not validate that the `file_text` parameter is provided, even though it's described as "Required parameter of `create` command" in the tool description. This leads to confusing behavior where a file is created with `None` content instead of failing with a clear validation error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call the `str_replace_editor` tool with:
   - `command`: "create"
   - `path`: "/some/file.py"
   - Missing `file_text` parameter

2. The tool call succeeds and creates a `FileEditAction` with `file_text=None`

## Expected Behavior

The function call should fail with a `FunctionCallValidationError` indicating that the `file_text` parameter is required for the `create` command.

## Actual Behavior

The function call succeeds and creates a `FileEditAction` with `file_text=None`, which will likely cause issues downstream when the action is executed.

## Impact

- **User Experience**: Users get confusing behavior instead of clear error messages
- **Debugging**: Makes it harder to identify missing parameters in tool calls
- **Data Integrity**: Files may be created with unexpected `None` content

## Root Cause

The issue is in `/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/function_calling.py` where the `str_replace_editor` tool handling (lines 148-199) doesn't validate command-specific required parameters. The JSON schema in `/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/tools/str_replace_editor.py` only lists `command` and `path` as required parameters, but doesn't handle conditional requirements based on the command type.

## Proposed Solution

Add validation logic in the `str_replace_editor` tool handling to check for command-specific required parameters:

- `create` command: require `file_text`
- `str_replace` command: require `old_str` and `new_str`
- `insert` command: require `new_str` and `insert_line`

## Test Case

A test case has been created to reproduce this issue and can be used to verify the fix.

## Environment

- OpenHands version: Latest (main branch)
- Affected component: CodeAct Agent function calling
- Related files:
  - `/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/function_calling.py`
  - `/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/tools/str_replace_editor.py`

title: Bug: "Parameter `file_text` is required for command: create" Error in OpenHands Cloud
body:
## Description
Users are encountering an error when using the file editor in OpenHands Cloud:
```
ERROR: Parameter `file_text` is required for command: create
```

This error occurs when attempting to create files through the file editor interface.

## Root Cause Analysis

The error originates from the `openhands-aci` package (version 0.3.0) which is used by OpenHands for file editing operations. Specifically:

1. **Location**: The error is thrown by the `OHEditor` class from `openhands-aci` when the `create` command is executed
2. **Trigger**: The error occurs when `FileEditAction` with `command='create'` is called but `file_text` parameter is `None`
3. **Code Path**: 
   - Frontend sends `FileEditAction` → 
   - `ActionExecutor.edit()` in `action_execution_server.py` → 
   - `_execute_file_editor()` → 
   - `OHEditor()` from `openhands-aci` → 
   - Error thrown when `file_text=None`

## Technical Details

### Expected Behavior
According to the test cases in `tests/runtime/test_aci_edit.py`:
- `file_text=None` → Should show error (current behavior is correct)
- `file_text=""` → Should create empty file successfully  
- `file_text="content"` → Should create file with content successfully

### Current Implementation
- **Python**: `FileEditAction.file_text: str | None = None` (in `openhands/events/action/files.py`)
- **TypeScript**: `file_text?: string | null` (in `frontend/src/types/core/actions.ts`)

### Problem
The issue suggests that somewhere in the system, a `create` command is being sent with `file_text=None` instead of `file_text=""` when the user intends to create an empty file.

## Potential Causes

1. **Frontend Issue**: The UI might not be properly handling empty file creation, sending `null` instead of empty string
2. **Serialization Issue**: JSON serialization/deserialization might be converting empty strings to `null`
3. **Agent Logic Issue**: The AI agent might be generating `FileEditAction` with `file_text=None` when it should use `file_text=""`
4. **Default Value Issue**: The default value of `None` might be problematic for the `create` command

## Reproduction
- **Environment**: OpenHands Cloud
- **Action**: Attempting to create a file using the file editor
- **Expected**: File should be created (empty or with content)
- **Actual**: Error message displayed

## Suggested Solutions

### Option 1: Frontend Validation
Add validation in the frontend to ensure `file_text` is never `null` for `create` commands:
```typescript
// In frontend file edit logic
if (command === 'create' && file_text === null) {
  file_text = '';
}
```

### Option 2: Backend Normalization
Modify `_execute_file_editor()` to normalize `None` to empty string for create commands:
```python
# In action_execution_server.py
if command == 'create' and file_text is None:
    file_text = ''
```

### Option 3: Agent Prompt Improvement
Update agent prompts/microagents to ensure they always provide `file_text` parameter for create commands.

### Option 4: Schema Validation
Add validation in `FileEditAction` to ensure required parameters are present for specific commands.

## Files Involved
- `openhands/runtime/action_execution_server.py` - Main execution logic
- `openhands/events/action/files.py` - FileEditAction definition
- `frontend/src/types/core/actions.ts` - Frontend type definitions
- `tests/runtime/test_aci_edit.py` - Test cases showing expected behavior

## Priority
**High** - This affects core file editing functionality in OpenHands Cloud and impacts user experience.

## Additional Context
- The error is coming from an external dependency (`openhands-aci` v0.3.0)
- The behavior is actually correct according to the API contract, but the user experience suggests this should be handled more gracefully
- This might be a regression if it was working previously, or a new edge case that wasn't properly handled during implementation

title: [Bug] UI Performance: Chat becomes laggy and unresponsive with extremely long user messages
body:
## Problem Description

When users send extremely long messages (more than 10 pages of text) to the chat interface, the UI becomes significantly laggy and unresponsive. Page render times increase to 2-3 seconds, making the chat difficult to use.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the OpenHands chat interface
2. Send an extremely long user message (10+ pages of text)
3. Observe the UI performance degradation
4. Try scrolling through the chat - it becomes slow and unresponsive

## Expected Behavior

The chat interface should remain responsive even with very long messages, maintaining smooth scrolling and reasonable render times.

## Actual Behavior

- Chat becomes laggy and unresponsive
- Page render times increase to 2-3 seconds
- Scrolling becomes slow and choppy
- Overall poor user experience during long conversations

## Technical Analysis

The performance issue likely stems from:

1. **React Markdown rendering**: The `ChatMessage` component uses `react-markdown` to render the entire message content at once, which can be expensive for very long messages
2. **No message virtualization**: All messages are rendered in the DOM simultaneously
3. **Lack of content truncation**: Long messages are displayed in full without any truncation or "show more" functionality
4. **Potential re-renders**: The entire message list may be re-rendering when new messages are added

## Affected Components

- `frontend/src/components/features/chat/chat-message.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/features/chat/messages.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/features/chat/chat-interface.tsx`

## Potential Solutions

### Short-term fixes:
1. **Message truncation**: Implement a "show more/less" toggle for messages exceeding a certain length
2. **Lazy rendering**: Only render the visible portion of very long messages
3. **Debounced rendering**: Delay rendering updates during rapid scrolling

### Long-term improvements:
1. **Virtual scrolling**: Implement virtualization for the message list to only render visible messages
2. **Message chunking**: Break very long messages into smaller, manageable chunks
3. **Progressive loading**: Load message content progressively as the user scrolls
4. **Memoization improvements**: Better memoization of message components to prevent unnecessary re-renders

## Environment

- Browser: All browsers affected
- OpenHands version: Latest
- Message length: 10+ pages of text

## Priority

This affects user experience significantly during long conversations and should be addressed to maintain a smooth, responsive interface.

## Labels

`frontend`, `performance`, `ui`, `chat`, `bug`

title: [Enhancement] Add User-Configurable LLM Parameters and Agent Settings to Frontend
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently, users who want to customize their AI agent's behavior have to manually edit configuration files. This includes adjusting LLM parameters like temperature and token limits, or enabling/disabling agent capabilities like web browsing and command execution. This creates several issues:

- **Technical barrier**: Not all users are comfortable editing config files
- **Error-prone**: Manual config editing can introduce syntax errors or invalid values  
- **Poor user experience**: No validation, help text, or immediate feedback
- **Inconsistent**: Different from how other settings are managed in the UI

Users should be able to configure their AI agent through an intuitive frontend interface, just like they can configure their API keys and model selection.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

Add comprehensive user-configurable settings for LLM parameters and agent capabilities directly in the OpenHands frontend:

**LLM Parameters** (integrated into existing advanced settings):
- `temperature` - Controls response creativity and randomness (0.0-2.0 slider)
- `top_p` - Nucleus sampling parameter (0.0-1.0 slider)
- `max_output_tokens` - Maximum tokens in responses (number input)
- `max_input_tokens` - Maximum tokens in prompts (number input)
- `max_message_chars` - Character limit per message (number input)
- `input_cost_per_token` - Cost tracking for inputs (decimal input)
- `output_cost_per_token` - Cost tracking for outputs (decimal input)

**Agent Capabilities** (new dedicated settings page):
- Tool toggles for web browsing, Jupyter notebooks, command execution
- Editor preference (LLM-based vs. standard string replacement)
- Agent behavior options (thinking steps, task completion, prompt extensions)
- Microagent management (ability to disable specific microagents)

Each setting should include helpful tooltips, proper validation, and immediate feedback. The implementation should extend the existing Settings model and maintain backward compatibility with config files.

**Additional context**

This would significantly improve the user experience by making OpenHands more accessible to non-technical users while providing power users with granular control over their AI agent's behavior. The settings should follow existing UI patterns and include proper internationalization support.

title: Improve VS Code extension auto-installation reliability
body:
## Problem

The current VS Code extension auto-installation mechanism uses a flag file approach that has reliability issues in real-world usage:

**Current Implementation:**
- Creates flag file at `~/.openhands/.{editor}_extension_install_attempted`
- Skips installation attempts if flag file exists
- No verification that extension was actually installed successfully

**Issues:**
1. **File system fragility**: Flag file creation can fail due to permissions, cleanup tools, or file system issues
2. **No recovery mechanism**: Once flag exists, no way to retry failed installations
3. **Multiple VS Code instances**: Doesn't handle different VS Code versions (stable/insiders)

## Proposed Solution

Replace flag file approach with extension status verification:

### 1. Check Actual Installation Status
```bash
# Verify extension is actually installed
code --list-extensions | grep -q "openhands.openhands-vscode"
```

### 2. Time-based Retry Logic
- Store timestamp instead of boolean flag
- Allow retries after reasonable intervals (e.g., 24 hours)
- Distinguish between permanent failures and transient issues

### 3. Improved Error Handling
- Detect different failure types (command not found, user cancelled, network issues)
- Only create persistent flags for permanent failures
- Provide clear user feedback and manual installation instructions

### 4. User Configuration
- Allow users to reset installation attempts

## Implementation Plan

1. Modify `attempt_vscode_extension_install()` in `openhands/cli/main.py`
2. Replace boolean flag with timestamped status tracking
3. Add extension verification before installation attempts
4. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff
5. Add user configuration options

## Benefits

- More reliable extension installation
- Better user experience with failed installations
- Reduced support burden from installation issues
- Maintains backward compatibility

body:
# 📦 Add essential tools to agent container image (Ubuntu 22.04)

## Description

Currently, the agent container image — based on **Ubuntu 22.04** — is a solid foundation. However, I’d like to propose adding a few key tools that would significantly improve the development experience and CI/CD automation capabilities.

These additions are especially useful for projects relying on Node.js, .NET SDKs, and coverage reporting via ReportGenerator.

---

## 🔧 Suggested tools to include

### 1. NVM (Node Version Manager)

Install via official script:

```bash
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
```

---

### 2. Node.js (versions 16, 18, 20, and 22)

Install and set default via NVM:

```bash
nvm install 16 && nvm install 18 && nvm install 20 && nvm install 22 && nvm use 16
```

---

### 3. .NET SDKs (versions 8 and 9)

Install via Microsoft backports repository:

```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:dotnet/backports -y \
&& apt update \
&& apt-get install -y curl zlib1g libc6 dotnet-sdk-8.0 dotnet-sdk-9.0
```

---

### 4. ReportGenerator (for .NET coverage reports)

Install globally as a .NET tool:

```bash
dotnet tool install --global dotnet-reportgenerator-globaltool
```

---

## ✅ Why this is useful

- **Environment consistency:** Tools are pre-installed and available across sessions and containers.
- **Productivity boost:** Developers and CI jobs won't need to manually install or configure these tools.
- **Reproducibility and stability:** Specific tool versions are pinned and predictable.

---

## 🧩 Suggested Dockerfile snippet

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Install dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    curl zlib1g libc6 software-properties-common \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install NVM and Node.js
ENV NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm
RUN curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash \
 && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" \
 && nvm install 16 && nvm install 18 && nvm install 20 && nvm install 22 \
 && nvm alias default 16

# Install .NET SDK 8 and 9

title: [CLI] Terminal requires reset after CLI usage
body:
## Problem
Every time users finish using the OpenHands CLI, they need to reset their terminal afterward. This is a significant UX issue that affects the terminal state.

## Current Behavior
- After exiting the CLI, the terminal is left in an altered state
- Users must manually reset their terminal to restore normal functionality
- This happens consistently across different terminal environments

## Expected Behavior
- CLI should properly restore terminal state on exit
- No manual terminal reset should be required
- Terminal should be left in the same state as before CLI was started

## Technical Context
The issue likely stems from the cleanup process in the `cleanup_session()` function in `openhands/cli/main.py`. The CLI may be using terminal control sequences or raw mode that isn't properly restored.

## Potential Solutions
- Ensure proper cleanup of terminal modes and control sequences
- Use context managers for terminal state changes
- Add proper signal handlers for graceful cleanup on unexpected exits

## Impact
- **Severity**: High - affects every CLI session
- **User Experience**: Poor - requires manual intervention after each use
- **Frequency**: Every CLI usage

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/main.py` (cleanup_session function)
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` (terminal interaction functions)
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Advanced settings modification requires replacing all settings one-by-one
body:
## Problem
When modifying advanced settings in the CLI, users cannot change individual settings. Instead, they must replace all settings one-by-one, even if they only want to change a single value.

## Current Behavior
- `/settings` → Advanced → User must input all settings again
- Cannot selectively modify just one setting (e.g., only the API key)
- Forces users to re-enter all configuration values

## Expected Behavior
- Allow selective modification of individual settings
- Show current values and allow users to keep existing values
- Provide options like "Keep current value" or show defaults

## User Experience Impact
- Frustrating when only wanting to change one setting
- Risk of introducing errors when re-entering all values
- Time-consuming for users with complex configurations

## Technical Context
The issue is in the settings modification flow in `openhands/cli/settings.py`, specifically in the `modify_llm_settings_advanced()` function.

## Proposed Solutions
1. **Interactive setting selection**: Allow users to choose which settings to modify
2. **Current value display**: Show existing values and allow keeping them
3. **Incremental updates**: Only prompt for settings the user wants to change

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/settings.py` (modify_llm_settings_advanced function)
- `openhands/cli/commands.py` (handle_settings_command function)
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Settings command should show config file location
body:
## Problem
The CLI settings interface doesn't tell users where the configuration file is located, making it difficult for users to manually edit settings if needed.

## Current Behavior
- `/settings` command shows current settings but not the file location
- Users don't know where to find the config file for manual editing
- No indication of where settings are stored

## Expected Behavior
- Display the config file path in the settings interface
- Allow users to easily locate and manually edit the configuration
- Provide clear information about where settings are persisted

## Technical Context
Settings are stored in `~/.openhands/settings.json` by default (configurable via `file_store_path`), but this information is not exposed to users.

## Proposed Solution
Add a line in the settings display showing:
```
Configuration file: ~/.openhands/settings.json
```

## User Benefits
- Users can manually edit settings when needed
- Better transparency about where configuration is stored
- Easier troubleshooting and backup of settings

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/settings.py` (display_settings function)
- `openhands/storage/settings/file_settings_store.py`
- `openhands/core/config/openhands_config.py` (file_store_path configuration)

title: [CLI] Settings changes require restart even when no session is active
body:
## Problem
Settings changes require a restart to take effect, even when no session has been started yet. This creates unnecessary friction in the setup process.

## Current Behavior
- User modifies settings via `/settings`
- CLI shows "They will take effect after restart"
- Restart is required even if no agent session is running

## Expected Behavior
- Settings should take effect immediately when no session is active
- Only require restart when an active session would be affected
- Provide immediate feedback when settings are successfully applied

## User Experience Impact
- Adds unnecessary steps to initial setup
- Confusing when no session is running
- Breaks the flow of configuration

## Technical Context
The settings are loaded at startup in `main_with_loop()` and not reloaded during runtime. The configuration could be reloaded when no session is active.

## Proposed Solution
1. **Immediate application**: Apply settings immediately when no session is running
2. **Smart restart detection**: Only require restart when an active session exists
3. **Clear messaging**: Different messages based on whether restart is actually needed

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/main.py` (settings loading in main_with_loop)
- `openhands/cli/settings.py` (save_settings_confirmation function)
- `openhands/storage/settings/file_settings_store.py`
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Diffs should display side-by-side on wider displays for better space usage
body:
## Problem
File diffs are currently displayed in unified format, which doesn't make optimal use of screen space on wider displays. Side-by-side diffs would be more readable and efficient.

## Current Behavior
- All diffs shown in unified format (+ and - lines)
- Doesn't utilize available horizontal space on wide terminals
- Can be harder to compare changes visually

## Expected Behavior
- Detect terminal width and use side-by-side diff when space allows
- Fall back to unified diff on narrow terminals
- Better visual comparison of before/after states

## User Experience Impact
- **Readability**: Side-by-side is often easier to understand
- **Space efficiency**: Better use of wide terminal windows
- **Visual clarity**: Clearer separation of old vs new content

## Proposed Solution
1. **Terminal width detection**: Check available columns
2. **Adaptive display**: Use side-by-side when width > threshold (e.g., 120 columns)
3. **Fallback**: Keep unified diff for narrow terminals

Example side-by-side format:
```
File Edit
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Before                    │ After                           │
│ ─────────────────────────│─────────────────────────────── │
│ def old_function():       │ def new_function():             │
│     return "old"          │     return "new"                │
│                           │     # Added comment             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Technical Context
The change would be in `display_file_edit()` function in `openhands/cli/tui.py`, utilizing the `CustomDiffLexer` and potentially extending it.

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` (display_file_edit function, CustomDiffLexer class)
- `openhands/events/observation.py` (FileEditObservation.visualize_diff method)
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Thoughts display after suggested action instead of before (confusing UX)
body:
## Problem
Agent thoughts are displayed after the suggested action rather than before, which creates a confusing user experience. Users see the action first and then the reasoning, which is backwards from natural thought flow.

## Current Behavior
```
Command
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ $ npm install                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

I need to install the dependencies first before running the tests.

Proceed with action? (y)es/(n)o/(a)lways >
```

## Expected Behavior
```
I need to install the dependencies first before running the tests.

Command
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ $ npm install                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

Proceed with action? (y)es/(n)o/(a)lways >
```

## User Experience Impact
- **Confusion**: Users see action before understanding the reasoning
- **Decision making**: Harder to make informed decisions about whether to proceed
- **Flow**: Breaks natural thought → action sequence

## Technical Context
In `display_event()` function in `openhands/cli/tui.py`, thoughts are displayed first but the action display logic may be interfering with the order.

The issue is in the event handling order:
1. Thoughts are displayed when the Action event is processed
2. Command is displayed when CmdRunAction is processed
3. But the confirmation prompt appears immediately after the command

## Proposed Solution
Ensure thoughts are displayed before any action confirmation prompts, maintaining the natural flow of reasoning → action → decision.

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` (display_event function)
- `openhands/cli/main.py` (event handling in on_event_async)
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Improve confirmation UX with better options (like Claude's arrow interface)
body:
## Problem
The current confirmation interface is limited and forces users into a cumbersome workflow when they want to provide alternative instructions instead of just yes/no.

## Current Behavior
```
Proceed with action? (y)es/(n)o/(a)lways >
```

When users want to give different instructions:
1. Type "N" + Enter
2. Wait for prompt
3. Type their alternative instructions

## Expected Behavior (inspired by Claude)
```
Proceed with action?
→ Yes, proceed
  No, let me give different instructions
  Always proceed (don't ask again)

Or type your alternative instructions directly:
> 
```

## User Experience Issues
- **Workflow interruption**: Must say no, then explain what to do instead
- **Inefficient**: Extra steps when user wants to provide guidance
- **Unclear options**: Limited to yes/no/always

## Proposed Enhanced UX
1. **Arrow navigation**: Use arrow keys to select options
2. **Direct input**: Allow typing instructions directly at confirmation prompt
3. **More options**: 
   - Yes, proceed
   - No, skip this action
   - Always proceed (don't ask again)
   - Let me provide different instructions
4. **Inline editing**: Type alternative instructions directly

## Example Enhanced Interface
```
Command
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ $ rm important_file.txt             │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

Choose an option:
→ Yes, proceed
  No, skip this action  
  Always proceed
  Give different instructions

Or type alternative instructions:
> Instead, move the file to backup/ folder
```

## Technical Context
This would require enhancing the `read_confirmation_input()` function in `openhands/cli/tui.py` to support:
- Arrow key navigation
- Multiple choice selection
- Direct text input as alternative

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` (read_confirmation_input function)
- `openhands/cli/main.py` (confirmation handling in on_event_async)
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Fix terminal compatibility warning: cursor position requests (CPR)
body:
## Problem
Users see a warning message: "WARNING: your terminal doesn't support cursor position requests (CPR)" when using the CLI, which indicates terminal compatibility issues.

## Current Behavior
- Warning appears during CLI usage
- May affect terminal functionality and user experience
- Suggests the CLI is trying to use terminal features not supported by all terminals

## Expected Behavior
- No warnings for standard terminal operations
- Graceful fallback for unsupported terminal features
- Better terminal compatibility detection

## Technical Context
Cursor Position Requests (CPR) are ANSI escape sequences used to query the terminal cursor position. The warning suggests the CLI is trying to use these sequences but the terminal doesn't support them or respond properly.

This is likely related to:
- Terminal detection and capability checking
- Prompt toolkit's terminal interaction
- Raw mode terminal operations

## Impact
- **User confusion**: Unclear what the warning means
- **Potential functionality loss**: Some features may not work properly
- **Professional appearance**: Warnings reduce confidence in the tool

## Proposed Solutions
1. **Better terminal detection**: Check terminal capabilities before using advanced features
2. **Graceful fallback**: Provide alternative implementations for unsupported terminals
3. **Suppress unnecessary warnings**: Only warn when functionality is actually impacted
4. **Terminal compatibility**: Test and improve support for common terminal types

## Investigation Needed
- Which specific terminal operations trigger this warning
- Whether functionality is actually impacted
- How to detect terminal capabilities reliably

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` (terminal interaction functions)
- Prompt toolkit configuration and usage
- Terminal mode management in CLI
author: neubig

title: [CLI] Remove confusing error message when user intentionally exits session
body:
## Problem
When users intentionally exit a session, they see a red error message: "The action has not been executed. This may have occurred because the user pressed the stop button..." which is confusing since the exit was intentional.

## Current Behavior
- User exits session on purpose (via `/exit` or other means)
- Red error message appears suggesting something went wrong
- Message implies unintended interruption when exit was deliberate

## Expected Behavior
- No error message for intentional exits
- Clear, positive confirmation of successful session termination
- Distinguish between intentional exits and actual errors

## User Experience Impact
- **Confusion**: Users think something went wrong when it didn't
- **Anxiety**: Red error messages suggest problems
- **Unprofessional**: Makes the tool seem buggy

## Current Error Message
```
❌ The action has not been executed. This may have occurred because the user pressed the stop button...
```

## Proposed Behavior
For intentional exits:
```
✅ Session terminated successfully
```

For actual errors/interruptions:
```
⚠️ Session was interrupted: [specific reason]
```

## Technical Context
The error message likely comes from the cleanup process or event handling when the session is terminated. The system should distinguish between:

1. **Intentional termination**: User commands like `/exit`, `/new`
2. **User interruption**: Ctrl-C, Ctrl-P pause, etc.
3. **System errors**: Actual failures or exceptions

## Investigation Needed
- Where this error message originates
- How to detect intentional vs unintentional termination
- Proper cleanup messaging for different exit scenarios

## Related Files
- `openhands/cli/main.py` (cleanup_session, exit handling)
- `openhands/cli/commands.py` (handle_exit_command)
- Event handling and session termination logic

title: [PRD] Personal Conversation Dashboard
body: As a software engineer who is embracing AI agents, I want the ability to manage multiple agents and get an "at a glance" view at what conversations and PRs are in progress or needs my attention. ### Use cases * **See Active Conversations:** I want a quick way to see which conversations are currently running * **See Conversations grouped by Repo / PR (branches):** I want a quick way to see which conversation(s) are associated with Repos and/or PRs (branches) I am working on. For example, I may have two conversations working on the same repo, and want to easily see that grouped. * **See PRs and Issues created or assigned to me:** I want to see PRs assigned to me or that I created, even if they don't have OpenHands convos associated with them. This is because there may be opportunities for me to initiate an OpenHands conversation to help 1) implement the Issue, or 2) resolve outstanding items in the PR * **See PRs grouped by status:** Sometimes I am working on multiple PRs and need to be attentive to those that require me to intervene. For example: * a PR with "Failing Tests" will require me to investigate and maybe kickoff an OpenHands conversation to help resolve * a PR with "Waiting for Feedback" may require me to give feedback, or may require me to bug someone to give feedback ### Requirements * The dashboard should show offer the following filters over conversations: * Filter by Repo name * Filter by active vs. inactive conversations (where runtime is still active) * Filter on conversations with PRs associated with them * Open PRs created or assigned to me from my Git provider (may or may not have a conversation associated with it yet) * Open Issues created or assigned to me from my Git provider (may or may not have a conversation associated with it yet) * The dashboard should allow for groupings * Group conversations by Repo and PR * Group conversations by Open PRs or Issues I created, or have been assigned to me * Group by Open PR status (Waiting for Feedback, Unresolved Comments, Failed Tests) * Conversation Details: * Display runtime status for each conversation (running, paused, stopped, etc.) * Display PR status for conversations with a PR associated with it (Waiting for Feedback, Unresolved Comments, Failed Tests) * Ability to dismiss a conversation from the dashboard Figma designs: [https://www.figma.com/design/iM5UBG1lnpg2sgE3cFnF1P/OpenHands-Product-Designs--Paul-Bloch-?node-id=12406-22825&t=PmuQz8GAR7lFMz4x-0](https://www.figma.com/design/iM5UBG1lnpg2sgE3cFnF1P/OpenHands-Product-Designs--Paul-Bloch-?node-id=12406-22825&t=PmuQz8GAR7lFMz4x-0) ## Feedback (12/22/25) * Feature: Ability to show both 1) PRs assigned to me, and 2) PRs I created * Feature: Badge icon next to each PR that indicates any 'blocking' status from merging. Example: * Failed Tests (and ability to see which failed tests from the Conversation Dashboard) * Unresolved Comments * Waiting for Feedback * Feature: Button to start a conversation for PRs that 1) don't already have a conversation associated with it, and 2) address the Failing Test or Unresolved Comments

title: unit tests are failing on openhands cloud
body:
# Unit tests are failing on OpenHands cloud

## Summary

Unit tests that pass on GitHub CI are failing when run locally in the OpenHands cloud environment. The failures are due to environment-specific differences between the CI environment and the cloud runtime environment.

## Test Execution Results

When running the full `py-unit-tests.yml` workflow locally:

### Unit Tests (`poetry run pytest --forked -n auto -svv ./tests/unit`)
- **Results**: 1231 passed, 22 failed, 22 skipped, 5 errors
- **Main failure categories**:
  - JSON logging tests (5 failures)
  - Secrets API tests (13 failures) 
  - Runtime build tests (4 failures)
  - Settings API tests (1 failure)

### Runtime Tests (`TEST_RUNTIME=cli poetry run pytest -svv tests/runtime/test_bash.py`)
- **Results**: 24 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped
- **Failure**: User permission assertion in `test_cmd_run[CLIRuntime-True]`

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. Authentication Failures (Secrets/Settings API Tests)

**Issue**: The `SESSION_API_KEY` environment variable is set in the OpenHands cloud environment (`SESSION_API_KEY=xxx`), but test clients don't include the required `X-Session-API-Key` header.

**Code Location**: `openhands/server/dependencies.py`
```python
def check_session_api_key(
    session_api_key: str | None = Depends(_SESSION_API_KEY_HEADER),
):
    if session_api_key != _SESSION_API_KEY:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)
```

**Failing Tests**:
- `test_load_custom_secrets_names`
- `test_add_custom_secret`
- `test_store_provider_tokens_*`
- All other secrets/settings API tests

**Error**: `fastapi.exceptions.HTTPException: 401: Unauthorized`

### 2. User Permission Assertion Failure

**Issue**: Runtime test expects non-root user output but cloud environment runs as root.

**Code Location**: `tests/runtime/test_bash.py:457`
```python
elif runtime_cls == LocalRuntime or runtime_cls == CLIRuntime:
    assert 'root' not in obs.content and 'openhands' not in obs.content
```

**Actual Output**: `drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Jun 27 23:57 test`
**Expected**: Output without 'root' or 'openhands' strings

### 3. Environment Differences

| Environment | GitHub CI | OpenHands Cloud |
|-------------|-----------|------------------|
| `SESSION_API_KEY` | Not set | Set (causes auth dependency activation) |
| User | Non-root | root |
| Docker | Available | Not available |

## Impact

- Developers cannot reliably run unit tests in the OpenHands cloud environment
- Test failures mask real issues since environment-specific failures create noise
- CI/CD confidence is reduced when local testing doesn't match CI results

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Environment-Aware Test Configuration
- Modify test fixtures to detect cloud environment and adjust behavior
- Mock `SESSION_API_KEY` in test environments or provide proper headers
- Skip or modify user permission tests when running as root

### Option 2: Test Environment Isolation
- Create test-specific environment variable overrides
- Use pytest fixtures to temporarily unset `SESSION_API_KEY` during API tests
- Add environment detection utilities for tests

### Option 3: Consistent Test Client Setup
- Modify test client fixtures to automatically include required headers when `SESSION_API_KEY` is set
- Create environment-aware test client factory

## Reproduction Steps

1. Run in OpenHands cloud environment (where `SESSION_API_KEY` is set)
2. Execute: `poetry run pytest --forked -n auto -svv ./tests/unit`
3. Observe authentication failures in secrets/settings API tests
4. Execute: `TEST_RUNTIME=cli poetry run pytest -svv tests/runtime/test_bash.py`
5. Observe user permission assertion failure

## Additional Context

- Tests pass completely on GitHub CI where `SESSION_API_KEY` is not set
- The issue affects development workflow in cloud environments
- Similar issues may exist in other deployment environments with different configurations

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

The /init command, intended for repository initialization and documented as a CLI feature, is currently inaccessible when OpenHands is running in CLIRunetime. The command erroneously prompts that it is "only supported for local runtime," despite its presence in cli/commands.py and its logical applicability to CLI-based operations. This behavior contradicts the documentation and creates an unnecessary limitation for users who prefer or require CLIRunetime.

## Steps to Reproduce:

    Ensure OpenHands is configured to use the CLIRunetime. 

    Start OpenHands from your terminal.

    Attempt to execute the /init command within the OpenHands CLI.

The /init command should execute successfully when OpenHands is in CLIRunetime, creating or updating the .openhands/microagents/repo.md file with project details and structure as described in the CLI documentation.

Actual Behavior:
Upon attempting to run /init in CLIRunetime, the system returns the error message: "Repository initialization through the CLI is only supported for local runtime."

Impact:
This issue forces users to switch to local runtime specifically to utilize the /init command, which can be inconvenient

## Relevant Information:

    The /init command is defined in cli/commands.py.

    The current limitation appears to stem from an older runtime check in the codebase (as noted in discussion, potentially similar to logic found in https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/8017/files), which was likely intended to exclude non-local runtimes (like Docker) but inadvertently excludes CLIRunetime.

title: Feature: Implement Claude Code Hooks for OpenHands
body:
# Feature Request: Implement Claude Code Hooks for OpenHands

## Description

This issue proposes implementing Claude Code hooks functionality in OpenHands. Claude Code hooks are user-defined shell commands that execute at various points in an agent's lifecycle, providing deterministic control over the agent's behavior.

## Background

[Claude Code hooks](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks) allow users to define shell commands that execute at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. These hooks provide deterministic control over Claude's behavior, ensuring certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them.

Example use cases include:
- **Notifications**: Customize how users get notified when OpenHands is awaiting input
- **Automatic formatting**: Run `prettier` on .ts files, `gofmt` on .go files, etc. after every file edit
- **Logging**: Track and count all executed commands for compliance or debugging
- **Feedback**: Provide automated feedback when OpenHands produces code that does not follow codebase conventions
- **Custom permissions**: Block modifications to production files or sensitive directories

## Proposed Implementation

### Key Components

1. **Hook System Architecture**:
   - Create a new `hooks` module in the OpenHands codebase
   - Define hook events and matchers
   - Implement hook configuration and execution
   - Integrate with the existing event system

2. **Hook Events**:
   - **PreToolUse**: Runs before an action is executed
   - **PostToolUse**: Runs after an action completes
   - **Notification**: Runs when notifications are sent
   - **Stop**: Runs when the agent has finished responding

3. **Hook Configuration**:
   - User settings: `~/.openhands/settings.json`
   - Project settings: `.openhands/settings.json`
   - Local project settings: `.openhands/settings.local.json`

4. **Integration Points**:
   - Agent Controller
   - Event Stream
   - Runtime

## User Experience

1. Users can configure hooks via:
   - Configuration files
   - UI in the OpenHands frontend
   - Slash commands (similar to Claude Code)

2. Example hook configuration:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "echo 'Running bash command: $COMMAND' >> ~/openhands-hooks.log"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "prettier --write \"$FILE_PATH\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Implementation Plan

1. **Phase 1**: Core Hook System
2. **Phase 2**: Integration with Event System
3. **Phase 3**: Advanced Features
4. **Phase 4**: User Interface and Documentation

## Security Considerations

1. Hooks execute arbitrary shell commands and should be treated with caution
2. Implement validation and sanitization of hook input
3. Add timeout limits for hook execution
4. Provide clear warnings about security implications
5. Consider sandboxing hook execution in the runtime environment

## Related Work

- Claude Code hooks: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks
- OpenHands event system
- OpenHands runtime architecture

title: Rate limiting message "Retrying..." appears too late in UI
body:
## Issue Description

The rate limiting message "Agent is Rate Limited. Retrying..." only appears in the UI after approximately 8 minutes, even though the system starts retrying much earlier (every minute).

## Expected Behavior

The message "Agent is Rate Limited. Retrying..." should appear as soon as the agent encounters a rate limit error and begins retrying.

## Current Behavior

- The system retries every minute as expected
- However, the UI message only updates to "Agent is Rate Limited. Retrying..." after 8 minutes
- This is misleading since users might think the system is not retrying when it actually is

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be in the agent controller logic where the `AgentState.RATE_LIMITED` state is only set when a retry attempt fails, not immediately when the first rate limit error occurs.

## Test Setup Used

- Created a fake server that always returns 429 rate limit errors
- Configured OpenHands to use the fake server
- Triggered rate limiting by sending a message to the agent
- Observed that retries happen every minute but UI message appears much later

## Related PR

This issue was discovered while testing PR #9281 which updated the rate limiting messages.

title: [Bug]: Application ignores the `SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE` environment variable
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

Hello,

I am unable to get the Open Hands agent running in a standard Docker environment on a clean Ubuntu VPS. The application consistently ignores all sandbox configurations (both environment variables and `config.toml`) and forces a runtime build process (`runtime_build.py`).

This build process then fails with a GPG signature error from `apt-get update`.

**Environment:**
* VPS with Ubuntu 22.04
* Docker & Portainer
* Image: `allhandsai/openhands:latest`

**Problem:**
1.  The application ignores the `SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE` environment variable.
2.  The application also ignores the `base_container_image` key set in a volume-mounted `config.toml` file, even when the file is structured correctly with `[core]` and `[sandbox]` sections.
3.  Because the configuration is ignored, it always triggers a new image build.
4.  This build process consistently fails with the error: `W: GPG error: http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm InRelease: At least one invalid signature was encountered.`

**Troubleshooting Steps Taken:**
We have tried exhaustively to fix this for many hours, including:
* Using the `SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE` environment variable.
* Mounting a `config.toml` file to specify a pre-built sandbox (`nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.12-nodejs22`).
* Mounting a `config.toml` to build from a clean base (`debian:bookworm-slim`) and installing dependencies via `runtime_extra_deps`.
* Fixing the host's Docker daemon DNS to use `8.8.8.8`.
* Verifying all file/folder permissions and paths on the host.
* Stopping/restarting services and even rebooting the host.

None of these steps prevent the application from attempting to build the image, which subsequently fails. This suggests the configuration logic in the application is currently broken.

Please see attached logs for the GPG/apt-get failure.

Thank you.

title: Documentation: Agent Configuration section is missing many configuration options
body:
The Agent Configuration section in `docs/usage/configuration-options.mdx` is incomplete and missing many configuration options that are actually defined in the `AgentConfig` class.

## Missing Configuration Options

After comparing `openhands/core/config/agent_config.py` with the current documentation, the following options are missing:

### Missing from Documentation:
- `system_prompt_filename` (str, default: 'system_prompt.j2') - Filename of the system prompt template
- `enable_editor` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable the standard editor tool
- `enable_cmd` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable bash tool
- `enable_think` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable think tool
- `enable_finish` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable finish tool
- `enable_condensation_request` (bool, default: false) - Whether to enable condensation request tool
- `enable_mcp` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable MCP tools
- `disabled_microagents` (list[str]) - A list of microagents to disable
- `enable_som_visual_browsing` (bool, default: true) - Whether to enable SoM visual browsing
- `condenser` (CondenserConfig) - Condenser configuration
- `extended` (ExtendedConfig) - Extended configuration for the agent

### Incorrect Defaults in Documentation:
- `enable_browsing` - docs show `false`, code shows `true`
- `enable_jupyter` - docs show `false`, code shows `true`

### Incorrectly Documented:
- `function_calling` is documented but doesn't exist in `AgentConfig`

## Proposed Solution
Update the Agent Configuration section in `docs/usage/configuration-options.mdx` to include all missing configuration options with their correct types, defaults, and descriptions as defined in the `AgentConfig` class.

## Files to Update
- `docs/usage/configuration-options.mdx` - Add missing agent configuration options

title: Unify dual configuration systems (config.toml + settings.json)
body:
OpenHands currently maintains two separate configuration systems that create confusion, duplication, and bugs:

1. **`config.toml`** - Used by CLI, contains system-level settings including agent configuration
2. **`settings.json`** - Used by web server, contains user-level preferences with overlapping fields

This dual system causes:
- **Configuration bugs**: Agent settings in `config.toml` don't consistently propagate to runtime components
- **User confusion**: Users don't understand which file controls what behavior
- **Maintenance overhead**: Same settings exist in different formats across multiple files
- **Development friction**: Adding new configuration requires touching multiple systems

### **Current Architecture Analysis**

**CLI Mode:**
```
config.toml → OpenHandsConfig → settings.json (user overrides) → Runtime
```

**Web Server Mode:**
```
config.toml → shared.config + settings.json (per user) → ConversationInitData → Runtime
```

**Key Files:**
- [`openhands/core/config/`](openhands/core/config/) - TOML-based configuration
- [`openhands/storage/settings/`](openhands/storage/settings/) - JSON-based user settings
- [`ConversationInitData`](openhands/server/session/conversation_init_data.py) - Bridge class that inherits from `Settings`

### **Evidence of Duplication**

Both systems contain overlapping fields:
- LLM configuration (model, API key, base URL)
- Agent selection and parameters
- Security and confirmation settings
- Runtime resource allocation

### **Proposed Solution: Unified Configuration Architecture**

**Phase 1: Create Unified Interface**
- Create `UnifiedConfig` class that combines both systems
- Implement configuration inheritance: `System → User → Session`
- Add format flexibility (TOML, JSON, environment variables)
- Maintain backward compatibility

**Phase 2: Migrate Services**
- Update CLI and web server to use unified interface
- Migrate all configuration loading points
- Ensure consistent configuration propagation to all components

**Phase 3: Deprecate Dual System**
- Remove duplicate code paths
- Update documentation
- Migration guide for users

### **Benefits**

- **Single source of truth** for configuration schema
- **Proper inheritance** chain for settings override
- **Reduced bugs** from configuration inconsistencies  
- **Better developer experience** when adding new settings
- **Clearer user experience** with unified configuration approach

### **Breaking Changes**

- Configuration loading API changes (internal)
- Possible `settings.json` format updates
- Documentation updates required

### **Implementation Considerations**

- Maintain backward compatibility during transition
- Comprehensive test coverage for configuration edge cases
- Clear migration documentation for users
- Consider impact on existing deployments

title: Bug: Jupyter tab not showing input commands
body:
## Summary

The Jupyter tab in OpenHands was not displaying input commands, only showing outputs. This made the Jupyter experience appear broken or incomplete, as users could see the results of IPython commands but not the commands themselves.

## Environment

- **OpenHands Version**: Latest (main branch)
- **Runtime**: All runtimes with Jupyter support
- **Browser**: All browsers
- **Affected Component**: Frontend Jupyter tab

## Bug Description

### Expected Behavior
The Jupyter tab should display both:
1. Input commands (the Python code being executed)
2. Output results (the execution results)

### Actual Behavior
The Jupyter tab only displayed:
1. ❌ Input commands: Missing
2. ✅ Output results: Working correctly

### Impact
- Users couldn't see what commands were being executed
- Jupyter tab appeared broken or non-functional
- Poor user experience for data analysis workflows
- Made it difficult to understand the agent's Python code execution

## Root Cause

The issue was in the frontend action handling logic in `frontend/src/services/actions.ts`. The system was missing handling for `RUN_IPYTHON` actions to add input to the Jupyter state.

**Missing Code:**
```typescript
if (message.action === ActionType.RUN_IPYTHON) {
  store.dispatch(appendJupyterInput(message.args.code));
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start OpenHands with Jupyter enabled
2. Ask an agent to run Python code (e.g., "Create a simple plot using matplotlib")
3. Navigate to the Jupyter tab
4. Observe that only outputs are shown, not the input commands

## Fix

Fixed in PR #9533

## Labels

- bug
- frontend
- jupyter
- good first issue

The `openhands-app` logs show repeated "ConnectTimeout" errors while "Waiting for client to become ready at `http://host.docker.internal:<port>`. > 
>     [llm]
>     model="openai/mistral-gptq"
>     api_key="local"

>     ```

> ### Steps to Reproduce
> 
> 1.  **Ensure a clean Docker environment:**
>     ```bash

>     ```
> 2.  **Verify `docker-compose.yml` configuration** for the `openhands` service, including the `HOST_DOCKER_INTERNAL_IP` environment variable set to the Docker bridge gateway IP (`172.17.0.1` in my environment):

>           - WORKSPACE_MOUNT_PATH=${WORKSPACE_BASE:-$PWD/workspace}
>         ports:
>           - "3000:3000"

>           - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
>         volumes:
>           - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
>           - ~/.openhands-state:/.openhands-state
>           - ${WORKSPACE_BASE:-$PWD/workspace}:/opt/workspace_base
>         pull_policy: build
>         stdin_open: true
>         tty: true
>     ```
> 3.  **Start OpenHands:**
>     ```bash

title: [Bug] OpenHands ignores custom context window size for Ollama models, displays hardcoded limit instead of configured value
body:
### Summary
OpenHands ignores custom context window configurations for Ollama models and displays hardcoded limits instead. When using a custom Ollama model configured with a 90,000 token context window, OpenHands UI and backend continue to report and enforce a lower limit (65,336 tokens), despite correct configuration via both environment variables (`LLM_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=90000`) and config.toml settings. This prevents full utilization of custom LLM capabilities.

---

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Ollama with a custom model supporting a 90,000 token context window.
2. Start OpenHands in Docker with the following configuration:
   - Environment variables: `-e LLM_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=90000 -e LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192`
   - Mount a config.toml containing:
     ```toml
     [llm]
     model = "ollama/devstral:24b-MAX"
     api_key = "dummy"
     base_url = "http://ollama.lan:11434"
     max_input_tokens = 90000
     max_output_tokens = 8192
     ```
   - Mount settings.json
     ```json
        {
          "language": "en",
          "agent": "CodeActAgent",
          "max_iterations": null,
          "security_analyzer": null,
          "confirmation_mode": false,
          "llm_model": "ollama/devstral:24b-MAX",
          "llm_api_key": "tvly-dev-DUMMY",
          "llm_base_url": "http://ollama.lan:11434",
          "remote_runtime_resource_factor": 1,
          "secrets_store": {
            "provider_tokens": {}
          },
          "enable_default_condenser": true,
          "enable_sound_notifications": true,
          "enable_proactive_conversation_starters": false,
          "user_consents_to_analytics": false,
          "sandbox_base_container_image": null,
          "sandbox_runtime_container_image": null,
          "mcp_config": {
            "sse_servers": [],
            "stdio_servers": [],
            "shttp_servers": []
          },
          "search_api_key": "",
          "sandbox_api_key": null,
          "max_budget_per_task": null,
          "email": null,
          "email_verified": null
        }
     ```

   - Docker image: `docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.48`
   - Model: `ollama/devstral:24b-MAX` with confirmed 90,000 token context
   - Docker command used:
     ```sh
     docker run -it --rm --pull=always \
          -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.48-nikolaik \
          -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
          -e LLM_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=90000 \
          -e LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192 \
          -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
          -v ~/openhands-configs/devstral.local.config.toml:/app/config.toml \
          -v ~/openhands-configs/devstral.local.settings.json:/.openhands/settings.json
          -p 3000:3000 --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
          --name openhands-app \
         docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.48
     ```
3. Navigate to the Display Cost feature in the UI (Settings > LLM Model Details).
4. Observe that the context window shows 65,336 tokens instead of 90,000.

---

### Verification of Ollama Configuration
- Confirmed Ollama model context size: `ollama run devstral:24b-MAX` → `/show parameters` → `num_ctx: 90000`
- Tested direct API call to Ollama with 90k tokens: [success]
- OpenHands logs show nothing that helps

---

### Impact
This limitation prevents users from fully utilizing custom LLM configurations and may lead to:
- Unnecessary context truncation
- Reduced agent performance on complex tasks
- Misleading cost estimates in the UI

---

### Technical Details
- OpenHands appears to use hardcoded context limits, possibly from LiteLLM model mappings
- The `max_input_tokens` configuration is ignored for UI display and possibly backend enforcement
- This affects both Docker environment variables and config.toml settings
- OpenHands version: 0.48
- Ollama version: 0.9.3
- Model: ollama/devstral:24b
- Host OS: debian12
- docker: 28.3.1

---

### Additional Notes
- Please provide a way to override or dynamically detect the context window for custom models.
- Document any special requirements for custom LLM setups.

title: [Bug]: Jupyter tab requires page refresh to display content
body:
## Summary

While PR #9533 fixed the issue of Jupyter tab not showing input commands, there remains a problem where the Jupyter tab does not display any content (input or output) until the user manually refreshes the page.

## Environment

- OpenHands version: Latest main branch
- Browser: All major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)
- Deployment: Both local and cloud deployments

## Bug Description

### Expected Behavior

When a user executes IPython commands through OpenHands, the Jupyter tab should immediately display both the input commands and their outputs without requiring any manual intervention.

### Actual Behavior

Currently, when IPython commands are executed, the Jupyter tab remains blank until the user manually refreshes the page. Only after refreshing does the tab display the input commands and their outputs.

### Impact

This issue significantly disrupts the user experience when working with Jupyter notebooks in OpenHands:
- Users might think the Jupyter functionality is broken when they do not see any content
- The need for manual refreshing breaks the flow of interactive data analysis
- It creates confusion about whether commands were actually executed

## Root Cause

The root cause appears to be related to state management or component rendering in the frontend. PR #9114 attempted to debug this issue by adding console logs to track when actions are dispatched and when the component updates, but it was closed without resolving the problem.

Potential areas to investigate:
1. State updates not triggering component re-renders
2. Event handling for Jupyter actions
3. Redux state management for Jupyter cells
4. Component lifecycle issues in the Jupyter tab

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a new conversation with OpenHands
2. Ask it to execute a Python command using IPython, e.g., "Run `print("Hello, World!")` in IPython"
3. Navigate to the Jupyter tab
4. Observe that the tab is empty
5. Refresh the page
6. Navigate to the Jupyter tab again
7. Observe that now the input and output are visible

## Related Issues

- PR #9533 fixed the related issue of Jupyter tab not showing input commands
- PR #9114 was an attempt to debug this issue by adding console logs

## Additional Context

As noted by Muhammad in a comment on PR #9533:
> In process, Jupyter tab does not show the content until we refresh the page, I see there is a PR for it as well but marked as closed, yet issue remains unresolved.

title: Unify Configuration Architecture: Eliminate Parallel Systems
body:
Update (2025-08-14): Scope clarification and plan for incremental delivery

This issue will be delivered in phases. Phase 1 focuses exclusively on adding a robust TOML write API that mirrors our read path. Runtime hot-switch of LLM configs and Web UI wiring will be handled in later phases.

Scope (Phase 1)
- Implement and validate a TOML write API that persists OpenHands configuration sections to config.toml, mirroring the existing read-from-TOML behavior.
- Keep user_secrets persisted via the existing SecretsStore to secrets.json (not TOML).
- Extend writer coverage beyond [core], [llm], [agent] to additional sections (security, sandbox, kubernetes, cli, extended, condenser, mcp), with focused tests.
- Do not implement runtime hot-reload/hot-swap now.

Out of scope for Phase 1 (tracked for later)
- [Future] Hot-reloadable configs and runtime hot-swap of LLM instances.
- [Future] Web UI settings integration to the unified config chain.
- [Future] Format/comment preservation in TOML (may require tomlkit).

API direction for the write path
- Central Writer (recommended now): Keep a single TOMLConfigWriter responsible for merging and writing to config.toml. Leverage Pydantic model serialization (including unions, nested models, lists, dicts, SecretStr) and strip None/unset values.
- Class-level serialization (consider): Each config model exposes to_toml_data()/from_toml_data() helpers that return/consume dicts. The central writer orchestrates file I/O and merging; models remain decoupled from storage.
- Avoid per-class direct file writes to prevent merge conflicts and duplicated I/O logic.

Secrets
- Persist user_secrets via the existing FileSecretsStore (secrets.json). CLI/headless/web can access UserSecrets through SecretsStore; no change for Phase 1.

Status snapshot (current PR #10305)
- Writer extended to persist: [security], [sandbox], [kubernetes], [cli], [extended], [condenser] (union-safe w/ type), [mcp].
- Serializer enhanced for nested models/lists/dicts/secrets; strips None/unset values.
- Focused tests added for new sections (all passing locally); pre-commit clean; Windows import cycle fixed.

Next steps
- Validate full test suite in CI; address any regressions.
- Decide if/when to add format preservation with tomlkit (follow-up issue).
- Track runtime hot-switch and Web UI wiring in separate PRs under this issue.

----
Original write-up (for context)
(Claude write-up)

## Problem

OpenHands has **disconnected configuration systems**:

### Core Issues

1. **Web UI operates independently**: Uses `settings.json` instead of application configuration (`config.toml` + env vars)
1. **No write API for application config**: Can only read from TOML, no way to persist changes back
1. **Entry points can’t access secrets**: CLI/headless have no access to user credentials stored separately
1. **Fragmented override hierarchies**: Web settings don’t participate in the standard config chain

### Current Disconnected Architecture

```python
# Application config (read-only)
OpenHandsConfig → config.toml + env vars + defaults

# Web UI config (separate system)  
Settings → settings.json (completely isolated)

# User secrets (separate system)
UserSecrets → secrets.json (only web has access)
```

**Problems:**

- Web form changes don’t update application config
- Application config options that don’t exist in the web form are not applied
- CLI can’t access user secrets for agent operations
- No unified configuration API across entry points
- Manual sync required between parallel systems

## Current State

**Application config** (used by core system):

```python
class OpenHandsConfig:         # Read-only from TOML/env
    llms: dict[str, LLMConfig]
    agents: dict[str, AgentConfig]
    # No user_secrets, no write API
```

**Web settings** (completely separate):

```python
class Settings:                # JSON-based, isolated
    llm_model: str | None
    secrets_store: UserSecrets
    # Doesn't use OpenHandsConfig at all
```

**Access patterns:**

- Web: Uses Settings + dependency injection, no fallback to application configuration
- CLI/Headless: Uses OpenHandsConfig, no secrets access ✗
- No unified API ✗

## Proposed Solution

### Unified Configuration with Write API

1. **Web UI uses application config**: Settings become overrides in the standard config hierarchy
1. **TOML write API**: Bidirectional TOML serialization with format preservation
1. **Secrets in main config**: All entry points access user credentials consistently
1. **Hot-reloadable configs**: Runtime updates without restart

### Target Unified Architecture

```python
# Single configuration system
class OpenHandsConfig:
    llms: dict[str, LLMConfig] 
    agents: dict[str, AgentConfig]
    user_secrets: UserSecrets        # All entry points get secrets
    
    # Write API
    def update_llm_config(name, config)    # Persists to TOML
    def update_user_secrets(secrets)       # Persists to storage

# Unified config chain: defaults → TOML → env → web overrides
config = load_openhands_config()
web_config = apply_web_overrides(config, user_settings)
```

## Technical Changes

### 1. Add Write API to Application Config

```python
# openhands/core/config/toml_writer.py (new)
class TOMLConfigWriter:
    def update_section(self, section_path: str, data: dict)
    def write(self)  # Preserves comments and formatting

# openhands/core/config/openhands_config.py  
class OpenHandsConfig:
    user_secrets: UserSecrets = Field(default_factory=UserSecrets)
    
    def update_llm_config(self, name: str, config: LLMConfig):
        # Update in-memory + persist to TOML
```

### 2. Web UI Uses Application Config

```python
# Replace separate Settings system
class WebConfigProcessor:
    def apply_overrides(self, base_config: OpenHandsConfig, user_input) -> OpenHandsConfig:
        # Web forms become config overrides, not separate system

# openhands/server/routes/settings.py
config = load_openhands_config()           # Use app config
web_config = apply_web_overrides(config)   # Apply web form data
config.update_llm_config(name, llm_config) # Persist via write API
```

### 3. Unified Secrets Access

```python
# All entry points get same interface
config = load_openhands_config()
github_token = config.user_secrets.provider_tokens.get(ProviderType.GITHUB)

# CLI can now access secrets
# Web uses same config.user_secrets instead of dependency injection
```

### 4. Hot-Reloadable LLM Instances

```python
# Runtime config updates
config.update_llm_config('gpt-4', new_llm_config)  # Persists to TOML
llm_instance.hot_swap_config(new_llm_config)       # Updates runtime
```

## Migration Plan

### Phase 1: Add Write API

- [ ] Implement TOMLConfigWriter with format preservation
- [ ] Add `user_secrets` to OpenHandsConfig
- [ ] Add write methods: `update_llm_config()`, `update_user_secrets()`

### Phase 2: Connect Web UI

- [ ] Implement WebConfigProcessor (web forms → config overrides)
- [ ] Replace Settings JSON with TOML-backed web settings
- [ ] Web routes use application config instead of separate Settings

### Phase 3: Unify Access

- [ ] CLI/headless access secrets via `config.user_secrets`
- [ ] Remove Settings.secrets_store duplication
- [ ] Single configuration API across all entry points

## Benefits

- **Connected systems**: Web UI participates in standard configuration hierarchy
- **Bidirectional config**: Read from TOML/env, write back to TOML
- **Unified secrets**: All entry points access user credentials consistently
- **Hot reloading**: Runtime configuration updates
- **Single source of truth**: One configuration system to maintain

## Files to Change

**Write API:**

- `openhands/core/config/toml_writer.py` (new)
- `openhands/core/config/openhands_config.py`

**Web UI connection:**

- `openhands/server/routes/settings.py`
- `openhands/storage/settings/` (replace JSON with TOML)

**Unified access:**

- `openhands/cli/main.py`
- `openhands/storage/data_models/settings.py`

body:

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

### **Description**
The **Suggested Tasks** section currently filters tasks based solely on the repository’s title. This causes incorrect behavior when multiple repositories share the same title but come from different Git providers—filtering becomes unreliable or incorrect in such cases.

---

### ✅ Expected Behavior
- Filtering should correctly consider **both** the repository title **and** its Git provider to uniquely identify repositories.

---

### ❌ Current Behavior

The error message explicitly states that the `stop` parameter is not supported by the target model. The xAI API documentation confirms this for Grok-4.

The issue stems from the `CodeActAgent`'s implementation, which appears to hardcode the addition of a `stop` sequence (e.g., `["</execute_bash>"]`) to every LLM API call. While this is a valid parameter for many models (like those from OpenAI and Anthropic), it causes a fatal API error when used with Grok-4, making the model unusable.

#### **Steps to Reproduce**

1.  Navigate to the OpenHands **Settings** page.
2.  Enable **Advanced** options and configure the LLM as follows:
    *   **Custom Model:** `xai/grok-4-0709`
    *   **Base URL:** `https://api.x.ai/v1`
    *   **API Key:** `[A valid xAI API key]`
3.  Save the settings and start a new agent session.
4.  Enter any initial prompt (e.g., "hello world").
5.  Observe that the agent immediately transitions to an `ERROR` state and the logs show the `BadRequestError` detailed above.

#### **Suggested Solution**

To resolve this and enable support for Grok-4, the agent code should be modified to conditionally add the `stop` parameter. It should only be included in the API call for models that are known to support it.

A simple and effective fix would be to check the model identifier before adding the parameter.

**Example (pseudo-code for `openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/codeact_agent.py`):**

```python
# In the agent's step method, where the LLM call is prepared...
params = {
    "messages": messages,
    "temperature": 0.0,
    # other parameters...
}

# Conditionally add the 'stop' parameter
# self.llm.model should contain the model name, e.g., 'xai/grok-4-0709'
if "grok" not in self.llm.model:
    params["stop"] = self.stop_sequences # Or the hardcoded list

# Make the LLM call
response = self.llm.completion(**params)

title: Instrument OpenTelemetry
body: **What problem or use case are you trying to solve?** We want better observability (the ability to answer new questions about the behavior of the system) while staying vendor neutral. We should be able to visualize log entries as associated with the larger events they are associated with, like conversations and agent actions. **Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind** https://opentelemetry.io/ Create a `monitoring` config section with an option to enable OpenTelemetry (aka OTel). When enabled, log statements go through that (in addition to current places) and there are "spans" annotated throughout the app to give them structure. People will configure the collector primarily through the standard OpenTelemetry environment variables. **Additional context** Observability #9579 Visualize Agent Loop #8916 ^ also included a nice graphic of what tracing enables. ## Alternatives## **JSON Logs**: A previous stop-gap solution was JSON Logs with metadata included in a useful subset. While non-standard this at least allowed custom scripts to get better picture of what's going on. To take this to the next level we would need to make it's presence in the codebase a lot more obtrusive and **LiteLLM Proxy**: We have recommended people use **LiteLLM Proxy** to serve their LLM-requests, which has several vendor integrations. This keeps does a good job at raw LLM requests but does not tie well to what the agent itself is doing. Again, to go further with it requires crossing into our codebase. **LogFire** is an opinionated OTel wrapper for Python by makers of Pydantic. It can ship to any backend, so one can argue that even though they are an O11y vendor, the SDK is still a vendor-neutral option. However, while trying it out in OpenHands I was prompted in the logs to sign-in to the LogFire website, and this is not what want to show our users. ### If you find this feature request or enhancement useful, make sure to add a 👍 to the issue
