title: Proposal: Auth System in OpenHands and APIs redesign
body:
## Summary

I propose to introduce an auth system in OpenHands, and a redesign of the current interface between OH and external applications built on OH (e.g. /enterprise multiuser build).

The two are related, though not the same. I would like to open them both for discussion.

What I see this like, is an auth system in OH that supports multiple _strategies_:
- **None**: No auth (with or without git token; current behavior)
- **Single User (SU)**: Single authenticated user with pre-configured identity, optional
- doesn't implement MU (multiuser), but we can redesign the interfaces to the outside world so that it works with external MU naturally, without MU-specific logic in OH core.

For this, I think we should consider two abstractions:
1. **TokenSource** (fka TokenProvider): Boundary for provider token access and refresh
2. **UserContext**: Boundary for user identity and storage namespacing

We may want a few auxiliary ones, like:
- **ConversationPaths**: encapsulates storage paths (they are request scoped)

**Reference**: This design addresses GitHub issues
- [#10730](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/10730)
- [#10751](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/10751).


## Problem

- OH currently has over 350 occurrences of `user_id` scattered in business logic, which are not in use, spread auth details across the codebase and couple auth concerns into code logic.
- OH currently supports Git provider tokens saved locally (secrets store), while MU/enterprise has different implementation and logic for these. Routes and services accept `provider_tokens` widely, which spreads auth details across the codebase and couples many components.
- MU business logic is in OH, e.g. in points related to auth (e.g., `REFRESH_TOKEN_URL` in `ProviderHandler`).
- Saas implements full multi-tenant auth. A lot of this currently leaks into OH via `user_id`, `ProviderHandler` (refresh URL), access token and many, many route signatures.
- this is all brittle, error-prone, and smells of inappropriate design for the needs at hand.

## Proposed Solution 
Unified interfaces between OH and external applications with clean boundaries.

We can introduce a small set of clearly defined interfaces:

- `UserContext`: DI-provided context for user identity and storage namespacing
  - None: `DefaultUserContext` / SU: `SingleUserContext` / (outside OH) MU: `MUUserContext` (like in /enterprise)

- `ConversationPaths`: DI-provided paths, per-request scope
  - the majority of OH codebase uses `user_id` to isolate user data (event stream, conversation metadata, etc)
  - refactor `user_id` to `ConversationPaths` = same interface, implemented differently in different strategies
  - different strategies implement different paths or logic to find storage locations for request-scoped EventStore, ConversationStore, etc.

- `TokenSource` boundary: (fka `TokenProvider` @malhotra5 )
  - Encapsulates how Git provider tokens are obtained (local file, refresh endpoint, etc.)
  - Routes depend on `TokenSource` instead of `provider_tokens`
- Provider handler consumes tokens via `TokenSource` to instantiate concrete Git services

This decouples identity and token resolution from core routes/services and removes/replaces MU concerns from OH core. A custom MU application (e.g. enterprise build) can implement its own `TokenSource`, `UserContext`, `ConversationPaths`.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "API Layer"
        Routes[Route Handlers]
        Deps[FastAPI Dependencies]
    end

    subgraph "Auth Boundary"
        UC[UserContext]
        TP[TokenSource]
        CP[ConversationPaths]
    end

    subgraph "Core Services"
        PH[ProviderHandler]
        CM[ConversationManager]
        SS[Storage Services]
    end

    subgraph "Implementations"
        subgraph "None Mode"
            NUA[NoUserAuth]
            NTP[NoTokenSource]
        end

        subgraph "SU Mode"
            SUA[SingleUserAuth]
            SUTP[SingleUserTokenSource]
        end

        subgraph "MU Mode"
            MUA[MultiUserAuth]
            MUTP[MultiUserTokenSource]
        end
    end

    Routes --> UC
    Routes --> TP
    UC --> CP
    TP --> PH
    CP --> SS

    UC -.-> NUA
    UC -.-> SUA
    UC -.-> MUA

    TP -.-> NTP
    TP -.-> SUTP
    TP -.-> MUTP
```

## Why this works

Per-request scoping belongs at the edges of the system, _at the boundary between OH and the outside world:_
- at one end, API routes
- at the other end, filesystem, db, HTTP retrieval of refresh tokens etc.

It may seem easier at first to pass around primitives (user_id string, tokens themselves), but there's a point after which that just doesn't scale, it's unmaintainable, because every auth concern leaks into core business logic.

I made a bunch of reviews of OH codebase that show that:
- most of the `if user_id` baggage in OH is not MU-logic, but only _storage isolation per-request_ (e.g. server conversation paths)
    - when we use a primitive like `user_id` for that, we couple auth concerns into code
- individual tokens are retrieved beforehand and used all throughout OH core logic
    - that forces logic/vars/signatures in routes and services - since they seem different per auth strategy, but you can't have different either
- MU-specific logic leaks in, e.g., `REFRESH_TOKEN_URL` in `ProviderHandler`.

==> but these are request-scoped logic
    - they belong to a request context abstraction, which does per-request isolation
    - we can implement them differently for each strategy
    - and invert control = move the implementation to DI-provided abstractions.

## What this solution doesn't fix

OH lacks a real extensibility system, so the interface between OH and complex enough applications built on OH has to rely on... everything else: dynamic imports, good ole' python habits to load stuff from `env`, direct subclassing, direct replacement of core files etc.

OH does have _some_ systems:
- if what someone building on OH needs is another runtime or another agent, that works: OH has a way to plug them in and use them via APIs.
- and a little, incipient way to load replacement classes (`get_impl`), but without versioning, so... well, it works, but it might become a nightmare to maintain. 😅 

# Code examples

## Before

1) user_id propagation in utilities and services (current OH):

```python
async def get_conversation_store(request: Request) -> ConversationStore | None:
    conversation_store: ConversationStore | None = getattr(request.state, 'conversation_store', None)
    if conversation_store:
        return conversation_store
    user_id = await get_user_id(request)
    conversation_store = await ConversationStoreImpl.get_instance(config, user_id)
    request.state.conversation_store = conversation_store
    return conversation_store
```


2) Route taking provider_tokens:

```python
@app.post("/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/start")
async def start_conversation(
    conversation_id: str,
    user_id: str = Depends(get_user_id),
    provider_tokens: PROVIDER_TOKEN_TYPE = Depends(get_provider_tokens),
):
    provider_handler = ProviderHandler(provider_tokens)
    # ...
```

3) ProviderHandler has MU-specific logic:

```python
class ProviderHandler:
    def __init__(
        self,
        provider_tokens: PROVIDER_TOKEN_TYPE,
        external_auth_id: str | None = None,
        external_auth_token: SecretStr | None = None,
        external_token_manager: bool = False,
        session_api_key: str | None = None,
        sid: str | None = None,
    ):
        # ...
        self._provider_tokens = provider_tokens
        WEB_HOST = os.getenv('WEB_HOST', '').strip()
        self.REFRESH_TOKEN_URL = (
            f'https://{WEB_HOST}/api/refresh-tokens' if WEB_HOST else None
        )
```

## After

### A. UserContext

```python
@dataclass
class UserContext:
    user_id: Optional[str]
    auth_type: Optional[AuthType]
    token_provider: TokenSource
    settings_store: SettingsStore
    secrets_store: SecretsStore

    # Convenience: conversation paths without passing user_id
    def conversation_dir(self, sid: str) -> str:
        return get_conversation_dir(sid, self.user_id)

# Dependency provider
async def get_user_context(
    user_auth = Depends(get_user_auth),
    token_provider: TokenSource = Depends(get_token_provider),
) -> UserContext:
    user_id = await user_auth.get_user_id()
    settings_store = await user_auth.get_user_settings_store()
    secrets_store = await user_auth.get_secrets_store()
    auth_type = await user_auth.get_auth_type()
    return UserContext(user_id, auth_type, token_provider, settings_store, secrets_store)
```

Routes then depend on a single UserContext interface:

```python
@app.post('/conversations')
async def new_conversation(
    data: InitSessionRequest,
    user: UserContext = Depends(get_user_context),
) -> ConversationResponse:
    # Build stores and paths from user
    conversation_dir = user.conversation_dir(conversation_id)
    # Continue with conversation creation using conversation_dir

    if data.repository:
        provider_handler = ProviderHandler(user.token_provider)
        await provider_handler.verify_repo_provider(data.repository, data.git_provider)
    # Use user.conversation_dir(conversation_id) downstream
```

### B. ConversationPaths

```python
@dataclass
class ConversationPaths:
    user_id: Optional[str]
    def dir(self, sid: str) -> str: return get_conversation_dir(sid, self.user_id)
    def events_dir(self, sid: str) -> str: return get_conversation_events_dir(sid, self.user_id)
    def event(self, sid: str, id: int) -> str: return get_conversation_event_filename(sid, id, self.user_id)
    def metadata(self, sid: str) -> str: return get_conversation_metadata_filename(sid, self.user_id)

# Bound into UserContext
@dataclass
class UserContext:
    ...
    paths: ConversationPaths

# Construction
return UserContext(user_id, auth_type, token_provider, settings_store, secrets_store, paths=ConversationPaths(user_id))
```

Route/service signatures migrate from threading user_id to accepting UserContext:

Before:
```python
async def get_conversation(conversation_id: str, user_id: str | None = Depends(get_user_id)):
    ...
```

After:
```python
async def get_conversation(conversation_id: str, user: UserContext = Depends(get_user_context)):
    ...
```

### C. TokenSource boundary (fka TokenProvider)
= decouples token management

```python
class TokenSource(Protocol):
    async def get(self, provider: ProviderType) -> Optional[ProviderToken]:
        ...
    async def get_all(self) -> Mapping[ProviderType, ProviderToken]:
        ...

class SecretsStoreTokenSource(TokenSource):
    def __init__(self, tokens: Mapping[ProviderType, ProviderToken] | None):
        self._tokens = MappingProxyType(tokens or {})
    async def get(self, provider: ProviderType) -> Optional[ProviderToken]:
        return self._tokens.get(provider)
    async def get_all(self) -> Mapping[ProviderType, ProviderToken]:
        return self._tokens
```

OH dependency to construct it from the local stores:

```python
async def get_token_provider(
    user_secrets = Depends(get_user_secrets),
) -> TokenSource:
    tokens = user_secrets.provider_tokens if user_secrets else None
    return SecretsStoreTokenSource(tokens)
```

A custom MU application can provide its own `TokenSource`, and give it the responsibility to retrieve tokens according to its own requirements.

### ProviderHandler becomes

```python
class ProviderHandler:
    def __init__(self, token_provider: TokenSource):
        self.token_provider = token_provider
        self.service_class_map = { ... }

    async def _get_service(self, provider: ProviderType) -> GitService:
        pt = await self.token_provider.get(provider)
        if not pt or not pt.token:
            raise AuthenticationError(f"No token for {provider.value}")
        service_class = self.service_class_map[provider]
        return service_class(token=pt.token, base_domain=pt.host)
```

==> it removes `REFRESH_TOKEN_URL` and any MU-specific logic here from OH core.

### Routes depend on TokenSource abstraction rather than pre-retrieved provider_tokens

```python
@app.post("/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/start")
async def start_conversation(
    conversation_id: str,
    token_provider: TokenSource = Depends(get_token_provider),
):
    provider_handler = ProviderHandler(token_provider)
    # ...
```

# SU Auth Strategy (OH)

I think we should add auth for OH web server. It can have:
- OAuth flow - map to a (pre-configured) allowed user.
- email / password - easier way to secure running OH web server.

```python

@dataclass
class SingleUserGithubAuth(UserAuth):
    user_id: str | None
    access_token: SecretStr | None
    auth_type: AuthType = AuthType.COOKIE

    async def get_user_id(self) -> str | None:
        return self.user_id

    async def get_access_token(self) -> SecretStr | None:
        return self.access_token

    async def get_user_settings_store(self) -> SettingsStore:
        # same as DefaultUserAuth but with stable user_id
        ...

    @classmethod
    async def get_instance(cls, request: Request) -> UserAuth:
        # Parse secure cookie or return None -> UI can redirect to GH OAuth
        # For None mode (no OAuth), return instance with user_id=None and access_token=None
        ...
```

### SU: preconfigured user
```
[auth]
strategy = "single_user_github"
allowed = "12345678"          # numeric -> GitHub ID; non-numeric -> login
github_client_id = "<client_id>"
github_client_secret = "<client_secret>"
```

Selection is still configured via `server_config.user_auth_class`. For None (no auth), continue using `DefaultUserAuth`.

## After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph OH None
    FE[Frontend] --> API[FastAPI Routes]
    API --> TP[SecretsStoreTokenSource]
    TP --> PH[ProviderHandler]
    PH --> Git[Git Provider APIs]
  end
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph OH SU
    FE[Frontend] --> API[FastAPI Routes]
    FE --> OAuth[GitHub OAuth]
    OAuth --> Cookie[Secure Cookie]
    Cookie --> UA[SingleUserGithubAuth]
    API --> TP[SecretsStoreTokenSource]
    UA --> TP
    TP --> PH[ProviderHandler]
    PH --> Git[Git Provider APIs]
  end
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph MU Application
    FE[Frontend] --> API[FastAPI Routes]
    FE --> KC[Keycloak]
    KC --> Cookie[Secure Cookie]
    API --> EUA[SaasUserAuth]
    API --> ETP[SaaSTokenSource]
    ETP --> RefreshTokensEndpoint
    API --> PH[ProviderHandler]
    PH --> Git[Git Provider APIs]
  end
```

title: OpenHands API Keys should have expiration
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Many enterprises have requirements around key rotation, specific max key lifetimes and product operators are expected to configure limits to adhere to these standards. OpenHands API keys do not have expiration that may be set at either the user level or by an administrator.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

The most robust implementation of this would be to have user selectable expiration date (similar to GitHub) AND for the enterprise-server to have a OPENHANDS_API_KEY_MAX_DAYS setting in the helm chart (or administrative UI) that would force new keys to have an expiration date not more than OPENHANDS_API_KEY_MAX_DAYS from the creation date.

A minimal implementation would be to have the enterprise setting and an UI to indicate when keys are expired or expiring. 

When keys are validated we need to check the expiration date and throw an error for requests made by an expired key.

title: [Bug]: Function apply_patch: Rename detection incorrectly applies to all diffs in patch
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

There is a bug in the apply_patch function located in openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py at line 62, related to rename operation detection.

A fix has been proposed in the related pull request (#10913)

**Current Behavior**
The function checks:
```
if "rename from" in patch:
```
This means the entire patch string is scanned for "rename from", rather than checking the specific diff currently being processed.

**Why This Is a Problem**
If a patch contains both a rename operation and a regular edit, the condition will return True for all diffs in the patch. This causes normal edit diffs to be incorrectly treated as rename operations.

**Example Problematic Patch**
```
diff --git a/file1.txt b/file2.txt
similarity index 100%
rename from file1.txt
rename to file2.txt
diff --git a/file3.txt b/file3.txt
index 17d5d9e..bc8b8aa 100644
--- a/file3.txt
+++ b/file3.txt
@@ -1 +1,2 @@
 another file
+modified content
```
In this case, the edit operation for file3.txt will also be treated as a rename because "rename from" exists somewhere in the overall patch.

**How to Reproduce**
Run the project using:
```
openhands/resolver/resolve_issue.py
```
Then run :
```
openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py
```
The issue occurs in openhands/resolver/send_pull_request.py during patch application.
While OpenHands is not normally executed in this way, the issue can be reproduced when testing patch application directly.

To developers,

I am writing to you today to present Project OpenMule, a comprehensive proposal for a crypto-first, open-source marketplace designed specifically for AI and physical automation services, or "Agents." Given Mulerun's position as a marketplace for computer-using agents, our vision for OpenMule appears to be a natural and powerful extension of this concept, and we believe a collaboration could be mutually beneficial.

Our core vision is to become the "Freelancer.com for AI," creating a new economy where humans and automated agents can collaborate and transact seamlessly. OpenMule is designed as a robust multi-sided platform that would enable users to discover, purchase, and manage a vast array of automated tasks, from digital AI assistants to agents controlling physical hardware.

The proposed platform includes several key features we are excited to discuss:
*   A versatile marketplace with service listings, fixed-price/subscription options, and a bidding system for negotiable tasks.
*   A robust reputation and trust system, including a "Certified" verification badge for providers and users.
*   A unique Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) system, allowing humans to earn money by providing real-time oversight and corrections to automated agents.
*   A secure technical architecture built on Vue 3 and FastAPI, with YAML-based configuration for easy agent deployment on OpenMule-hosted, provider-owned, or user-defined machines.

We understand that security is paramount, especially concerning physical hardware control. Therefore, our proposal includes a stringent Security & Safety Protocol featuring network isolation, virtualization recommendations, and bare-metal emergency stop triggers to ensure user safety and trust.

Our monetization strategy is designed for sustainable growth, beginning with a free tier to build ecosystem adoption and evolving into a sophisticated crypto-first economy with escrow payments, milestone releases, and a future vision for a distributed network (MuleNet) where participants can operate relay or validator nodes to earn fees.

We have a deep respect for the foundation Mulerun has built and see immense potential in combining our vision with your expertise. We are confident that OpenMule could significantly expand the scope and capabilities of your existing marketplace.

We would be delighted to schedule a meeting at your earliest convenience to discuss this proposal in greater detail and explore potential avenues for collaboration.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

James Brown
Cybergod AGI Research

title: Proposal: OpenHands configuration
body:
We all know there's an awful lot of problems with OH config/settings parallel systems. We've tried to fix it in CLI, but from some perspective, we may have made some subset of uses friendlier, at the cost of adding something else to the mess / confusion overall.

I'd like to share some thoughts about this.

**Proposal:** consistent OH configuration implies to design for extensibility in some measure, but **_not_** code in multiuser applications assumptions itself. It implies to get MU out of OpenHands configuration.

**Summary:**
- we can redesign configuration loading to _allow_ override from other packages/applications
	- allow other apps to _filter_ stuff _out_
	- allow them to _add_ stuff _in_
- but not code in MU considerations itself.

Sorry for the quick write-up, but this is very important IMHO.

We always had a tension in OH configuration system(s), between
- all OH supports, which are all supposed to be available in some way to the individual developer running OH on their machine, and
- what the SaaS (a MU app) wants/needs the user to access/change/see, which is obviously restricted.

We are converging to:
- `~/.openhands/settings.json` = user-level configuration, in both CLI and server
- we start to design and implement a configuration system as its own package. (cc: @malhotra5 )

I suggest this actually means `settings.json` should contain all settings by default, including those currently in `config.toml`. CLI is a good indicator here (the user expects all settings), as is a VSCode-like application.

(Local server / individual server has quite a lot of complexity, it has a server-level config with only a few things; and we have many settings in `config.toml` that it doesn't support; and, it applies some of `config.toml` and not others.)

Allow me to take a step back and look at OpenHands.
From the perspective of the individual developer running OH:
- all settings are available to them
- in CLI mode, there is no such thing as "a config.toml somewhere with global settings"
	- CLI user runs `openhands` in the current directory = > that's workspace
	- we have now a possibility to load a `config.toml` from current directory (= workspace), which means it has precedence
	- same goes for a VSCode extension: VSCode settings are user-level (everything), or workspace-level (if any; they have a higher precedence than user-level)
	- I think this is an excellent indicator of user-friendliness, for a local/individual user.
- in server, we have a bit of a mess. "UserSettings" cover some configuration and not another. Some configuration objects; but also, some parts of them and not others.

I think we should get rid of the concept of "global settings" as embodied by `config.toml` sort of, and sort of the opposite, today. It's super-confusing.

**The problem** with what I just said: the web server maps `~/.openhands/settings.json` to "user-level" in a different sense:
- "user-level means accessible to a user, not another"
- "a user means someone without access to system settings"

I think those definitions are from the perspective of a multiuser application built on top of OH. They are not OH stuff.

I'd suggest to take them out of OH. From OH perspective:
- OH configuration works the same way everywhere, CLI or server, or even client app built on SDK
	- maybe it offers the ability to define and apply filters
	- and it offers the ability to add new settings
- conceptualize and build configuration that makes this difference: filters out some settings, allows to add new settings
- **important**: filters probably need to be in OH configuration package, as one of the first things that happens as we load. (for client applications security / less error prone)

Then, in a MU applications (aka multiuser cloud):
- MU "system settings" = a MU application filters out of what is permitted for all/some users to access
- MU "user settings" = in a MU application, we'd apply filters on OH settings when we load the user context; and add extra settings for the users to access features that the application implements. (and OH doesn't)

title: CLI(V1): Speed up binary executable startup
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
We want the binary executable for the CLI to be super quick when starting up. Using UV to run the CLI is already very quick, but we want the same for the executable as well. 


**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**
Strategies can include

- **Trimming dependencies**: lowers memory and speeds up boot time 
-  **PyInstaller tricks**: Instead of packaging as one file, we can pacakge into a directory. This will increase the footprint but boost boot up time. We'd have to zip the directory to create a single asset that can be passed around. There's other settings we could tweak as well to optimize the final build.
- **Lazy imports**: Ideally the first boot up simply displays the welcome page and exposes simple commands. No conversation or upstream `agent-sdk` related code is executed yet. These should be lazily imported once a command is sent to an agent. 
- **Upstream package optimizations**: Package `__init__` files can force multiple imports even if we're only attempting to import a subset. Look into either removing some imports from the init files in `agent-sdk` and `agent-tools`. Alternatively opt for lazy imports inside the init files when possible.   

Nice to have
- Add a slash page: this gives the illusion of a faster boot up

**Additional context**

First attempt at trimming dependencies is in #11006

title: [Agent] Customizable Guardrails
body:
Some customers have asked about the ability to create guardrails for OpenHands to help reduce the chance of it performing actions that are not intended. For example, one anecdotal comment from a customer mentioned that an AI agent they were using committed code even after it was instructed earlier in the session not to.

In general, we've message there are two types of guardrails:
1. Prompt-level controls (e.g. what the LLM Risk Analyzer does with risk thresholds)
2. Network-level controls (e.g., being able to create Network Policies to deny the agent from accessing specific resources)

What this ticket is focused on is closer to #1 - being able to create additional guardrails that the agent must 'pass through' will be important for larger enterprise adoption. An example could be command denylists (which is available in some competing solutions).

title: [Bug]: Messages are lost when server is stopped and status indicator is unclear
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

### Description
On the new Cloud redesign, the UI looks clean and neat.  
However, there is an issue when the server is stopped:

- When the status message shows **"server stopped"**, any user message typed and submitted **disappears**.
- The message is not delivered or saved anywhere.
- After a refresh, the user must retype the message.
- The new **"server stopped"** status indicator is less obvious (smaller text, less noticeable position), which makes this issue occur frequently.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the new Cloud interface.
2. Wait until the server goes into **"stopped"** state.
3. Type a message and submit it.
4. Refresh the page.

### Expected Behavior
- User messages should either:
  - Be queued and delivered once the server is back, or  
  - Be preserved locally so users don’t lose their input.  
- The **"server stopped"** status should be more prominent to prevent confusion.

### Actual Behavior
- Messages sent during the **"server stopped"** state are lost.  
- Status indicator is subtle and often overlooked.  

### Environment
- Cloud redesign (new UI)
- Server status: *stopped*

### Notes
This issue makes it easy for users to lose work and creates confusion. A clearer status indicator and message preservation mechanism would greatly improve the experience.

body: In the case where an STDIO MCP server is setup in the configuration but fails to deploy due to a code error, it would be nice to be able to see the error in the terminal stdout/stderr where OH was launched. Currently there is no information, aside from the tools not being listed in the logs, which makes debugging a server deployment difficult.

title: what is the role of setting.json?
body:
In `openhands/cli/main.py`, line 596~597, it tries to load `setting.json` from directory `~/.openhands`. But there is no `setting.json` example. What is the exact format and content that `settting.json` should contain?

From the comments in the same file,
```python
        # Handle LLM configuration with proper precedence:
        # 1. CLI parameters (-l) have highest precedence (already handled in setup_config_from_args)
        # 2. config.toml in current directory has next highest precedence (already loaded)
        # 3. ~/.openhands/settings.json has lowest precedence (handled here)

        # Only apply settings from settings.json if:
        # - No LLM config was specified via CLI arguments (-l)
        # - The current LLM config doesn't have model or API key set (indicating it wasn't loaded from config.toml)
```
I have set llm name/url/api key in `config.toml`. Why should I still run into setup flow?

BTW: I run openhands with `openhand --config-file ./config.toml`

author: Digital-Media-Group

title: Multi-repo/Cross-repo Awareness
body:
As a developer, when you start a conversation with a single repo, there are usually other repos in an organization that are dependencies to the repo I am currently working in. A simple example is frontend and backend repos. It would be great if OpenHands had context/knowledge of these other repos automatically so it could make changes in those repos if needed.

**Automatic repo awareness**
The core customer desire is having OpenHands automatically pull in that context, without having to select those repos manually (#7752).
- For example, a seasoned developer who is deeply familiar with a given repo will not have a problem selecting the other related repos. However, a new developer on the team may not have this knowledge, and so having OpenHands figure out the dependent repos would be useful.

**Automatically maintaining a repo.md with this knowledge**
Automatically maintaining the appropriate markdown file - whether a `repo.md` or an organizational microagent - would  help enable faster time-to-value and less overhead/maintenance.

title: [UI]: Keyboard Shortcuts for File Copy and Paste
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

We need to enable support for Ctrl + V (Windows/Linux) and Cmd + V (Mac) to allow users to paste copied files directly into the chat input.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

- Users can copy files using Ctrl/Cmd + C.

title: [Bug] Import Caching Producing False Negatives
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

During the debugging process, it is often the case that current files can be modified without the creation of additional files. However, this poses a unique problem whereby the agent imports the relevant modules into the testing file, executes the file, and thus caches these directories. Subsequently, when the agent modifies these files to succesfully resolve the issue, the test execution uses the cached version of these updated files. This results in an improper evaluation.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

I want to explore methods for providing the agent with a debugging strategy that could resolve this problem. This could look like:

a) Giving the agent the power to restart the Python process or clear the compiler/import cache (for any/all files)
b) Providing context that informs the agent it can add lines (e.g., importlib.reload()) as temporary measures to reset imports for files it knows it has affected

Option A is more robust but has higher overhead costs, while Option B runs the risk of leaving file modification artifacts in non-test files.

**Additional context**

The following trajectory is a very simple to understand example of this problem:

[experiments](https://github.com/multi-swe-bench/experiments/tree/main)/[evaluation](https://github.com/multi-swe-bench/experiments/tree/main/evaluation)/[python](https://github.com/multi-swe-bench/experiments/tree/main/evaluation/python)/[verified](https://github.com/multi-swe-bench/experiments/tree/main/evaluation/python/verified)/[20250329_OpenHands_Claude-3.5-Sonnet(Oct)](https://github.com/multi-swe-bench/experiments/tree/main/evaluation/python/verified/20250329_OpenHands_Claude-3.5-Sonnet(Oct))
/trajs/sympy__sympy-23534

In this trajectory listing, we found that of 26 "failed" trajectories that successfully applied the golden patch, 24 of them imported a library into the testing file that would later be modified during the patching process.

title: Add visual callouts for workarounds and hacks made during task completion
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently, OpenHands is very verbose in its output, providing detailed explanations of every action it takes. While this transparency is valuable, it creates a significant UX problem: users often miss important information about workarounds, hacks, or compromises that OpenHands makes during task completion.

The core issues are:
1. **Information overload**: 95% of OpenHands output is verbose "I did what you said" messages
2. **Hidden compromises**: When OpenHands takes shortcuts or makes workarounds, these decisions get buried in the verbose output
3. **Lack of scannable warnings**: Users can't quickly identify when the AI had to deviate from best practices
4. **Missed learning opportunities**: Users don't notice when OpenHands knows it did something suboptimal

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

Add a visual callout system that highlights when OpenHands makes workarounds, hacks, or compromises during task completion. This would include:

### Visual Design
- **Consistent emoji/icon**: Use a recognizable emoji (e.g., 🔧 ⚠️ 🚧) to make these callouts instantly scannable
- **Distinct styling**: Different background color, border, or formatting to make these stand out from regular output
- **Collapsible sections**: Allow users to expand/collapse detailed explanations while keeping the summary visible

### Content Categories
The callout system should highlight:
- **Workarounds**: When OpenHands bypasses normal procedures due to constraints
- **Hacks**: Quick fixes that aren't best practice but get the job done
- **Compromises**: When OpenHands chooses a suboptimal solution due to limitations
- **Assumptions**: When OpenHands makes assumptions about user intent or system state
- **Incomplete solutions**: When OpenHands partially solves a problem but notes limitations

### Implementation Approach
1. **Detection**: Modify the agent's response generation to identify when it's describing a workaround or hack
2. **Formatting**: Add special markdown or HTML formatting for these callouts
3. **UI Integration**: Update the frontend to render these callouts with special styling
4. **Categorization**: Allow different types of callouts (warning, info, hack, etc.)

### Example Output
Instead of this buried in verbose text:
```
I'll now install the dependencies. Since the requirements.txt file seems to have some formatting issues, I'll install the packages individually to avoid conflicts...
```

Show this as a prominent callout:
```
🔧 **Workaround Applied**
Installing packages individually instead of using requirements.txt due to formatting issues in the file.
[Click to see details...]
```

### Benefits
- **Improved awareness**: Users immediately see when compromises were made
- **Better learning**: Users understand when and why OpenHands deviates from best practices
- **Faster scanning**: Users can quickly identify potential issues without reading verbose logs
- **Trust building**: Transparency about limitations and workarounds builds user confidence
- **Debugging aid**: Makes it easier to identify the source of problems when things go wrong

**Additional context**

This feature would significantly improve the user experience by making OpenHands' decision-making process more transparent and scannable. It addresses a common user frustration where important information gets lost in verbose output.

The implementation should be configurable, allowing users to:
- Toggle callout visibility on/off
- Filter by callout type (warnings, hacks, assumptions, etc.)
- Adjust verbosity levels for different callout categories

This feature aligns with OpenHands' goal of being a transparent and helpful AI assistant while making that transparency more actionable for users.

title: [Bug]: "openhands serve" hangs on "starting runtime" even though runtime container appears to be running (arch, 0.57.2))
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

when running `openhands serve --mount-cwd` installed via `uv tool install openhands-ai`, everything runs, but any new conversations starting a runtime container hang indefinitely with "Starting runtime... (this may take 1-2 minutes)" (using the openhands cli as `openhands` works consistently).  Eventually the `openhands` container raises an exception for a timeout in `httpx`

Looking at the logs for the runtime container, the VSCode agent is running and has access to the mounted workspace (I can bring it up in a browser) and other ports on the runtime container respond to curl (logs for the runtime and openhands container attached).  So the runtime seems to be running without error, but there is some sort of communications issue between the openhands container and the runtime.

The output was 
```
📂 Mounting current directory: /home/vputz/projects/QS1 to /workspace
Running Docker command: docker run -it --rm --pull=always -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.57.2-nikolaik -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v /home/vputz/.openhands:/.openhands -e SANDBOX_VOLUMES=/home/vputz/projects/QS1:/workspace:rw -e SANDBOX_USER_ID=1000 -p 3000:3000 --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway --name openhands-app docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:0.57.2
```

And I can verify through `docker inspect` that the host gateway was mounted
```
❯ docker inspect --format='{{json .HostConfig.ExtraHosts}}' openhands-app
["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]
```

But `curl`ing either `host.docker.internal:31124` or the internal ip `172.17.0.1:31124` from within the openhands-app container hangs.

I'm uncertain how to further diagnose at this time; docker has otherwise been performing correctly on my system but I'm puzzled as to this connectivity issue; `uvicorn` is running on the runtime at the designated port, and that port is exposed to the host system (I can curl the runtime's port, in the above case 31124, from my local shell) but for some reason it's not accessible at host-gateway, which makes no sense to me; it's as if they aren't exposed to the host:
```
❯ docker inspect --format="{{json .Config.ExposedPorts}}"  69991c67f059  #this is the runtime container on a different run
{"37801/tcp":{},"43287/tcp":{},"52823/tcp":{},"56491/tcp":{}}
```

[openhands.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22615278/openhands.log)

title: [Bug]: Locally mounted folders are chowned to root
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

I'm running locally via Docker, and have set up access to local filesystem[1]. Whenever a new conversation is started, a git repo is created (don't want it, but that's only a nuisance), and the folder is chowned to `<openhands-user>:root`. I don't see any option/environment variable to set the group for the chown, nor to stop creating the git repo.

This also means that any file the agent creates is owned by group `root`.

Current workaround:
When creating a new conversation, run `sudo chown -R $UID:$GID .`, and also whenever the agent has created any files I need to modify.


Command I use to start:
```bash
export OPENHANDS_VERSION=0.57
export OPENHANDS_RUNTIME=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/runtime:$OPENHANDS_VERSION-nikolaik
export OPENHANDS_IMAGE=docker.all-hands.dev/all-hands-ai/openhands:$OPENHANDS_VERSION
export OPENHANDS_USER=$(echo "$DOCKER_HOST" | grep podman && echo root || echo $UID)

docker rm -f openhands-app &>/dev/null
docker run -it \
  --rm \
  --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  --name openhands-app \
  --security-opt label=disable \
  -e LOG_ALL_EVENTS=true \
  -e LOG_LEVEL=debug \
  -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=$OPENHANDS_RUNTIME \
  -e SANDBOX_GROUP_ID=$OPENHANDS_USER \
  -e SANDBOX_USER_ID=$OPENHANDS_USER \
  -e SANDBOX_VOLUMES=$PWD:/workspace:Z \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v ${DOCKER_HOST#*://}:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -v ~/.openhands:/.openhands \
  $OPENHANDS_IMAGE
```



 [1]: https://docs.all-hands.dev/usage/runtimes/docker#using-sandbox-volumes

title: [Bug]: Endless Loop in v1 CLI When Combining Security Analyzer and MCP Tools
body:
# Endless Loop in v1 CLI When Combining Security Analyzer and MCP Tools

## Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

## Describe the bug and reproduction steps

The v1 CLI enters an endless loop when both the security analyzer and MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools are enabled simultaneously.

### Reproduction Steps:
1. Enable the security analyzer in CLI configuration
2. Configure and enable MCP tools
3. Run a task that triggers an MCP tool call
4. The agent enters an endless loop and becomes unresponsive

### Expected Behavior:
The agent should handle MCP tool calls normally when the security analyzer is enabled.

### Actual Behavior:
- The CLI becomes stuck in an endless loop
- The agent becomes unresponsive and cannot proceed with the task
- Manual intervention (pausing the agent and providing alternative instructions) is required to break the loop

### Workaround:
Pausing the agent and telling it to try something else can break the loop.

## Connection to Issue #11163

This bug may be related to issue #11163, which involved MCP tool validation errors causing CLI crashes. The fix for that issue might have introduced this loop condition when the security analyzer is also enabled.

## OpenHands Installation

CLI

## OpenHands Version

v1 (latest from main branch)

## Model Name

Various (issue occurs regardless of model)

## Operating System

Multiple (reported on different systems)

## Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

### Key Components Involved:
- `openhands/cli/main.py` - CLI main execution loop
- `openhands/security/analyzer.py` - Security analysis functionality  
- `openhands/mcp/tool.py` - MCP tool execution

### Reproduction Command:
```bash
uvx --python 3.12 --from git+https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands@v1#subdirectory=openhands-cli openhands-cli
```
(With security analyzer enabled and MCP tools configured)

This is a critical bug that makes the CLI unusable when both security analyzer and MCP tools are enabled.
author: neubig

title: Bug: 400 Bad Request error when resuming conversations with custom secrets
body:
## Description

When resuming a conversation that has custom secrets configured, the backend attempts to re-setup custom/ secrets via POST `/api/secrets`, which returns a 400 Bad Request error because the secrets already exist in the runtime from the previous session. This causes the conversation resume process to crash.

## Error Log

```
openhands {"message": "Task exception was never retrieved\nfuture: <Task finished name='Task-23428' coro=<SaasNestedConversationManager._start_agent_loop() done, defined at /app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/ddtrace/contrib/internal/asyncio/patch.py:58> exception=HTTPStatusError(\"Client error '400 Bad Request' for url 'https://wcebdskotxrprhsi.prod-runtime.all-hands.dev/api/secrets'\\nFor more information check: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/400\")", "severity": "ERROR", "exc_info": "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"/app/server/saas_nested_conversation_manager.py\", line 270, in _start_conversation\n    await self._setup_custom_secrets(client, api_url, settings.custom_secrets)\n    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\n  File \"/app/server/saas_nested_conversation_manager.py\", line 358, in _setup_custom_secrets\n    response.raise_for_status()\n    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^\n  File \"/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/httpx/_models.py\", line 829, in raise_for_status\n    raise HTTPStatusError(message, request=request, response=self)\nhttpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '400 Bad Request' for url 'https://wcebdskotxrprhsi.prod-runtime.all-hands.dev/api/secrets'\nFor more information check: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/400\"}
```

## Root Cause

The `/api/secrets` POST endpoint is designed to create new secrets and correctly returns 400 when a secret with the same name already exists (proper REST API behavior). However, the conversation manager's `_setup_custom_secrets()` method does not handle this expected error case when resuming conversations.

**Flow:**

1. User starts a conversation → runtime created → custom secrets POSTed to `/api/secrets` → stored successfully
2. User pauses conversation → runtime stays alive, secrets persist in storage
3. User resumes conversation → backend attempts to POST the same secrets again
4. `/api/secrets` endpoint finds secrets already exist → returns 400 (correct behavior)
5. No error handling in `_setup_custom_secrets()` → conversation resume crashes

## When Bug Was Introduced

This bug was introduced on **September 4, 2025** when enterprise code was merged (commit e37f7b0e0 in PR All-Hands-AI/OpenHands#10770). It was NOT introduced by PR [#11155](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/11155) as initially suspected.

## Impact

* **Severity**: High - Prevents users from resuming conversations
* **Scope**: Affects all users with custom secrets configured who try to resume conversations
* **Frequency**: Increases as runtimes live longer and more users adopt the resume feature

## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure custom secrets in Settings → API Keys & Secrets
2. Start a new conversation
3. Pause the conversation (runtime stays alive)
4. Resume the conversation
5. Observe 400 error in logs and failed resume

## Affected Code

* `enterprise/server/saas_nested_conversation_manager.py` (line 346-363)
* `openhands/server/conversation_manager/docker_nested_conversation_manager.py` (line 239-261)

## Solution

PR [#11213](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/11213) implements comprehensive error handling:

* Catches 400 errors and logs a warning (secrets already exist - expected)
* Catches other HTTP errors and re-raises (genuine issues)
* Catches generic exceptions for backward compatibility with older runtimes
* Includes full test coverage

## Related

* Fix PR: [#11213](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/11213)
* Investigation initially suspected PR: [#11155](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/11155) (confirmed NOT the cause)
* Original endpoint: `/api/secrets` created in PR [#8213](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/8213) (May 3, 2025)

## Environment

* Production deployment
* Affects both SaaS and OSS deployments with enterprise features
* Runtime version mismatch scenarios (old runtimes with new backend code)

title: Enhancement: Add prominent CTA button in docs to access OpenHands Cloud
body:
## Problem

Users are having difficulty finding and accessing the OpenHands Cloud (app.all-hands.dev) when browsing the documentation. While there is currently a small "OpenHands Cloud" link in the global navigation anchors, it's not prominent enough for users to easily discover the cloud offering.

As mentioned in user feedback: "its difficult for people to access the cloud version in the docs. It's been difficult working with these hackers to get to app.all-hands.dev when they are in the docs. versus our landing page it's a button"

## Proposed Solution

Add a prominent Call-to-Action (CTA) button in the documentation to direct users to OpenHands Cloud. This should be:

1. **Highly visible** - Placed in a prominent location where users will see it
2. **Clear messaging** - Make it obvious this leads to the cloud version
3. **Consistent with design** - Match the existing documentation styling

## Suggested Implementation Locations

### Option 1: Hero Section on Main Docs Page
Add a prominent CTA button in the main documentation landing page (`docs/index.mdx`) after the video embed, similar to how the main landing page has a button.

### Option 2: Enhanced Navigation
Make the existing "OpenHands Cloud" anchor in the global navigation more prominent by:
- Converting it to a button-style element
- Adding visual emphasis (different color, styling)
- Potentially moving it to a more prominent position

### Option 3: Floating CTA
Add a floating or sticky CTA button that appears on all documentation pages.

## Current State

- There is already an "OpenHands Cloud" link in the global navigation anchors (docs.json line 194-197)
- The link correctly points to https://app.all-hands.dev
- However, it's not prominent enough for user discovery

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Users can easily find and access OpenHands Cloud from the documentation
- [ ] The CTA is visually prominent and clearly indicates it leads to the cloud version
- [ ] The implementation is consistent with the existing documentation design system
- [ ] The CTA works across all documentation pages where it's implemented
- [ ] Analytics/tracking can be added to measure click-through rates (optional)

## Additional Context

- The documentation uses Mintlify as the documentation platform
- Current cloud documentation is well-organized under `/usage/cloud/`
- The main landing page (all-hands.dev) already has effective CTA buttons that we can use as design reference

## Labels
enhancement, documentation, ux, cloud

When running OpenHands on Windows without WSL/Docker, the application fails to start due to multiple missing configuration files and JSON parsing errors during initialization.

Clone repository on Windows

Application starts but fails to initialize conversations

Multiple file not found and JSON parsing errors occur

Root Causes
Application expects configuration files that are not auto-created on first run

Missing proper initialization sequence for Windows environment

Path handling issues with Windows file system

No fallback for missing configuration files

Expected Behavior
Application should create default configuration files on first run

Graceful handling of missing files with default values

Proper Windows path normalization

Clear error messages guiding user to setup

Environment
OS: Windows

Python: 3.12

Runtime: Local (no WSL/Docker)

Architecture: Likely x64

Temporary Workaround
Manually creating the required directory structure and configuration files:

bash
mkdir -p C:\Users\admin-os\.openhands\sessions
But this doesn't solve the underlying initialization issue.

Related Issues
This appears to be part of broader Windows support issues mentioned in PR #8674, but focuses specifically on the configuration initialization failures.

title: CLI(V1): DeepSeek LLM fails tool calling due to missing security_risk parameter in V1 SDK
body:
## Describe the bug and reproduction steps

Weaker LLMs crash the agent in confirmation mode.

**Two main issues observed:**
1. LLM does not provide `security_risk` parameter
2. LLM fills parameters with wrong format (e.g., `view_range`)


## OpenHands Installation
CLI

## OpenHands Version
V1 branch

## Model Name
DeepSeek (various models)

## Operating System
MacOS

## Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

```
Error starting agent chat: Missing required parameters for function 'str_replace_editor': {'security_risk'}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/openhands_cli/simple_main.py", line 30, in main
    run_cli_entry()
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/openhands_cli/agent_chat.py", line 142, in run_cli_entry
    runner.process_message(message)
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/openhands_cli/runner.py", line 75, in process_message
    self._run_without_confirmation()
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/openhands_cli/runner.py", line 79, in _run_without_confirmation
    self.conversation.run()
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py", line 236, in run
    self.agent.step(self._state, on_event=self._on_event)
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openhands/sdk/agent/agent.py", line 206, in step
    raise e
  File "/Users/yangxiao/git/OpenHands_local/openhands-cli/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openhands/sdk/agent/agent.py", line 180, in step
    response = self.llm.completion(
  ...
openhands.sdk.llm.exceptions.FunctionCallValidationError: Missing required parameters for function 'str_replace_editor': {'security_risk'}
```

## Proposed Fix

Currently toggling confirmation mode changes the confirmation policy, but doesn't actually remove the security analyzer itself. 

The fix should involve removing the security analyzer from the agent preset, and better error handling around this error with an explainable user message to disable confirmation mode. 

Tradeoff will involve invalidating the cache (due to system prompt changes), but should not be very expensive unless repeatedly toggling confirmation mode in a single conversation.

title: [Bug]: CLI V1 crashes with 'LLM provided a security_risk but no security analyzer is configured'
body:
## Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When using the OpenHands CLI (V1), the agent crashes with a RuntimeError during execution:

```
RuntimeError: LLM provided a security_risk but no security analyzer is configured - THIS SHOULD NOT HAPPEN!
```

This error occurs in the openhands-sdk package when the LLM returns a `security_risk` parameter in its response, but the conversation doesn't have a security analyzer configured.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install OpenHands CLI V1
2. Configure and run the CLI agent
3. During agent execution, the error occurs when the LLM tries to take an action

### Root Cause

Based on code analysis:

1. The CLI's `setup_conversation()` function in `openhands-cli/openhands_cli/setup.py` conditionally includes a security analyzer based on the `include_security_analyzer` parameter
2. When confirmation mode is disabled (NeverConfirm policy), the security analyzer is removed via `toggle_confirmation_mode()` in `runner.py`
3. However, the LLM may still return `security_risk` parameters in its tool call responses
4. The openhands-sdk expects that if `security_risk` is present, a security analyzer must be configured, otherwise it raises this RuntimeError

This appears to be related to the recent changes in commit `9fe4e9715` ("CLI(V1): Fix confirmation mode breaking on weaker models").

### Suggested Fix

The issue can be resolved in one of these ways:

1. **SDK-side fix**: Modify the openhands-sdk to gracefully handle cases where `security_risk` is provided but no analyzer is configured (e.g., treat it as UNKNOWN or ignore it)
2. **CLI-side fix**: Ensure the security analyzer is always initialized, even when confirmation mode is disabled, but configure it to not prompt the user
3. **LLM prompt fix**: Update the system prompt to explicitly instruct the LLM not to return `security_risk` parameters when the security analyzer is not enabled

CLI

## OpenHands Version

Latest (commit 22f67d309 or later with CLI V1 support)

## Model Name

Not specified in the error report, but appears to affect multiple models

title: [Bug]: Linux CLI binary fails with GLIBC_2.38 not found error
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When attempting to run the V1 CLI Linux binary (openhands-linux) on a Linux system, it fails to start with the following error:

```
[PYI-4084584:ERROR] Failed to load Python shared library '/tmp/_MEIk9hBhm/libpython3.12.so.1.0': /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found (required by /tmp/_MEIk9hBhm/libpython3.12.so.1.0)
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Download the Linux CLI binary (openhands-linux)
2. Make it executable: `chmod +x ./openhands-linux`
3. Run it: `./openhands-linux`
4. Error appears immediately

**Root Cause:**
The Linux binary is being built on `ubuntu-latest` (currently Ubuntu 22.04 or newer), which includes Python 3.12 compiled against GLIBC 2.38. This makes the binary incompatible with older Linux distributions that have GLIBC < 2.38.

**Context:**
- GLIBC 2.38 was released in August 2023
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS includes GLIBC 2.39
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS includes GLIBC 2.35
- Many enterprise Linux distributions and stable releases use older GLIBC versions

**Potential Solutions:**
1. Build the Linux binary on an older Ubuntu version (e.g., Ubuntu 20.04) to ensure compatibility with a wider range of systems
2. Use a static Python build or build in a manylinux container
3. Build multiple versions of the binary for different GLIBC versions
4. Document minimum GLIBC version requirements clearly in the release notes

### OpenHands Installation

CLI

### OpenHands Version

Latest release (V1 CLI)

### Model Name

N/A (binary doesn't start)

### Operating System

Linux

### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

**Error Output:**
```
[PYI-4084584:ERROR] Failed to load Python shared library '/tmp/_MEIk9hBhm/libpython3.12.so.1.0': /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found (required by /tmp/_MEIk9hBhm/libpython3.12.so.1.0)
```

**Build Configuration:**
The Linux binary is currently built using:
- CI: `ubuntu-latest` in `.github/workflows/cli-build-binary-and-optionally-release.yml`
- Python 3.12
- PyInstaller

**Additional Notes:**
- The macOS binary reportedly works fine
- This affects Linux users with GLIBC < 2.38
- The issue was verified on a system with GLIBC < 2.38

author: jcoffi

title: Add documentation for CGM-MCP integration as an MCP server
body:
Based on troubleshooting, CGM-MCP (from jcoffi/cgm-mcp) is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation for code graph model capabilities. It should be integrated into OpenHands by configuring it as an MCP server in config.toml under mcpServers, e.g., for the model-agnostic mode: {"mcpServers": {"cgm-modelless": {"command": "python", "args": ["/path/to/cgm-mcp/main_modelless.py"], "env": {"CGM_LOG_LEVEL": "INFO"}}}.

The OpenHands wiki and documentation should include a section on integrating third-party MCP servers like CGM-MCP, including available tools such as cgm_analyze_repository, cgm_get_file_content, etc.

This would help users load CGM-MCP tools correctly in OpenHands.

title: [Bug]: ValidationError when using LiteLLM model names containing slashes
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When following the LiteLLM proxy setup guide https://docs.all-hands.dev/openhands/usage/llms/litellm-proxy OpenHands throws a ValidationError if the LiteLLM model name contains a forward slash after the litellm_proxy/ prefix.

My LiteLLM model names look like this:

copilot/gpt-4.1

According to the docs, I should specify the model in OpenHands as:

litellm_proxy/copilot/gpt-4.1

However, this results in the error:

RuntimeError: There was an unexpected error while running the agent: ValidationError. You can refresh the page or ask the agent to try again.

It seems like OpenHands might be parsing the model name and treating the additional / as a path separator, which could be causing the validation failure.

### OpenHands Installation

title: Add working directory configuration command to CLI interface
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Currently, when using the OpenHands CLI, users cannot easily change or set their working directory from within the CLI interface. The working directory is set to `os.getcwd()` at startup (line 333 in `openhands/cli/main.py`) and there is no interactive command to modify it during a session.

This creates friction when users want to:
- Switch between different project directories during a session
- Set a specific working directory without having to restart the CLI from that location
- Work on multiple projects or repositories in a single session
- Navigate to different parts of a large codebase structure

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

Add a new CLI command `/cd` or `/workdir` that allows users to change the working directory interactively. The implementation should:

1. **Add a new command to the CLI interface:**
   - Add `/cd <path>` to the `COMMANDS` dictionary in `openhands/cli/tui.py`
   - Update the command handler in `openhands/cli/commands.py`

2. **Command functionality:**
   - `/cd` - Display current working directory
   - `/cd <path>` - Change working directory to the specified path
   - `/cd ..` - Go up one directory level
   - `/cd ~` - Go to home directory
   - Support both absolute and relative paths
   - Validate that the target directory exists before changing
   - Show confirmation message with the new working directory

3. **Technical implementation:**
   - Update the `current_dir` parameter that is passed through the CLI session
   - Ensure the runtime environment reflects the working directory change
   - Update any repository initialization logic to work with the new directory
   - Consider security implications and validate paths appropriately

4. **User experience:**
   - Provide clear error messages for invalid paths
   - Show the current working directory in the CLI prompt or status
   - Integrate with existing `/status` command to display current working directory
   - Consider tab completion for directory paths (future enhancement)

**Additional context**

This feature would significantly improve the CLI user experience by providing the same directory navigation capabilities that users expect from a terminal environment. It aligns with the CLI's goal of providing a comprehensive interface for interacting with OpenHands.

The implementation should be consistent with existing CLI command patterns and maintain the security model that OpenHands uses for directory access.

**Files that would likely need modification:**
- `openhands/cli/commands.py` - Add command handler
- `openhands/cli/tui.py` - Add command to COMMANDS dictionary
- `openhands/cli/main.py` - Update working directory handling
- Tests in `tests/unit/cli/` - Add test coverage

title: CLI crashes with FunctionCallValidationError: Missing required parameter 'security_risk' for execute_bash
body:
## Summary
The OpenHands CLI crashes with a `FunctionCallValidationError` when the LLM generates an `execute_bash` function call without the required `security_risk` parameter.

## Error Details
```
Error: Missing required parameters for function 'execute_bash': {'security_risk'}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/fn_call_converter.py", line 739, in _extract_and_validate_params
openhands.sdk.llm.exceptions.FunctionCallValidationError: Missing required parameters for function 'execute_bash': {'security_risk'}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. **Enable security-based confirmation mode**:
   ```
   > Auto-confirm LOW/MEDIUM risk, ask for HIGH risk
   ```

2. **Trigger an execute_bash function call**:
   - Use any prompt that would cause the agent to run a bash command
   - The LLM generates a function call for `execute_bash`

3. **Observe the crash**:
   - Function call validation fails in `fn_call_converter.py`
   - CLI crashes with `FunctionCallValidationError`

## Expected Behavior
- The `execute_bash` function call should include all required parameters
- Function call validation should pass
- The command should execute normally

## Actual Behavior
- LLM generates `execute_bash` call without `security_risk` parameter
- Function call validation fails
- CLI crashes with unhandled exception

## Environment
- **OpenHands CLI version**: Latest (main branch)
- **Confirmation mode**: Auto-confirm LOW/MEDIUM risk, ask for HIGH risk
- **Agent-SDK integration**: Using new agent-sdk structure

## Technical Details

### Error Location
- **File**: `openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/fn_call_converter.py`
- **Line**: 739
- **Function**: `_extract_and_validate_params`

### Complete Stack Trace
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "openhands_cli/simple_main.py", line 45, in main
  File "openhands_cli/agent_chat.py", line 174, in run_cli_entry
  File "openhands_cli/runner.py", line 83, in process_message
  File "openhands_cli/runner.py", line 103, in _run_with_confirmation
  File "openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py", line 245, in run
  File "openhands/sdk/agent/agent.py", line 209, in step
  File "openhands/sdk/agent/agent.py", line 187, in step
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/llm.py", line 476, in completion
  File "tenacity/__init__.py", line 338, in wrapped_f
  File "tenacity/__init__.py", line 477, in __call__
  File "tenacity/__init__.py", line 378, in iter
  File "tenacity/__init__.py", line 400, in <lambda>
  File "concurrent/futures/_base.py", line 449, in result
  File "concurrent/futures/_base.py", line 401, in __get_result
  File "tenacity/__init__.py", line 480, in __call__
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/llm.py", line 461, in _one_attempt
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/non_native_fc.py", line 82, in post_response_prompt_mock
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/fn_call_converter.py", line 957, in convert_non_fncall_messages_to_fncall_messages
  File "openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/fn_call_converter.py", line 739, in _extract_and_validate_params
openhands.sdk.llm.exceptions.FunctionCallValidationError: Missing required parameters for function 'execute_bash': {'security_risk'}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue occurs in the function call validation process:

1. **LLM generates function call**: Creates `execute_bash` call without `security_risk` parameter
2. **Function call converter processes it**: `convert_non_fncall_messages_to_fncall_messages` in `fn_call_converter.py`
3. **Parameter validation fails**: `_extract_and_validate_params` expects `security_risk` parameter but doesn't find it
4. **Exception thrown**: `FunctionCallValidationError` crashes the CLI

## Impact
- CLI becomes completely unusable when this occurs
- User cannot proceed with their task
- No graceful error handling or recovery

## Suggested Solution

1. **Investigate why LLM omits `security_risk` parameter**:
   - Check if function definition includes `security_risk` as required
   - Verify prompt templates include security risk guidance

2. **Add better error handling**:
   - Catch `FunctionCallValidationError` and provide user-friendly message
   - Allow user to retry or modify the request

3. **Parameter defaulting**:
   - Consider defaulting missing `security_risk` parameter to `UNKNOWN` or `MEDIUM`
   - Log warning when parameters are auto-defaulted

## Files to investigate
- `openhands/sdk/llm/mixins/fn_call_converter.py` (validation logic)
- Function definition for `execute_bash` tool

title: [Feature] Adding an MCP call handler significantly reduces the overhead of RPC requests.
body:
### Background
When the system currently executes an MCP tool call, it first establishes connections with all configured MCP Servers (including SSE, SHTTP, and Stdio types) and retrieves the complete set of tools, before executing the tool matching logic. This full-connection approach results in unnecessary resource consumption, and is particularly inefficient when only specific tools need to be called.

### Optimization Solution
Add an MCPCallHandler to implement instance caching for MCPClient. This avoids initiating full-scale initialization and tool call requests every time during multi-turn conversations, thereby eliminating unnecessary overhead.
To support dynamic updates of the tool list for MCPClient, a default refresh interval of 60 seconds is designed: When no matching MCPClient is found in the cache, expired mcp_clients will be refreshed, followed by another check for a match.

title: Pre-commit hooks not automatically executed before agent creates pull requests
body:
## Description

When a user places a pre-commit script at `.openhands/pre-commit.sh` in their project, OpenHands correctly installs it as a git hook during workspace setup. However, the agent does not automatically execute this hook when making commits before creating pull requests, unless explicitly instructed to do so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a pre-commit script at `.openhands/pre-commit.sh` in your project root
2. Make the script executable (`chmod +x .openhands/pre-commit.sh`)
3. Start OpenHands GUI with a task that requires code changes and PR creation
4. Let the agent complete the task and create a PR
5. Observe that the pre-commit hook was not executed

## Expected Behavior

The pre-commit hook at `.openhands/pre-commit.sh` should be automatically executed whenever the agent runs `git commit`, including when preparing to create pull requests.

## Actual Behavior

The pre-commit hook is not executed automatically. The hook only runs when the user explicitly instructs the agent to run it. When manually instructed, the hook works as expected.

## Environment

- **Interface**: GUI
- **LLM**: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (though likely affects all models)
- **OpenHands version**: Latest (as of 2025-10-16)

## Additional Context

The hook installation logic appears to be working correctly:
- The hook is installed during workspace setup (see `openhands/runtime/base.py:maybe_setup_git_hooks()`)
- The `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file is created and calls the user's script
- When manually invoked, the script executes properly

Possible causes:
1. The agent might be using `git commit` with flags that bypass hooks (e.g., `--no-verify`)
2. There might be a timing issue where commits are made before hooks are fully installed
3. The hook installation might not persist across all agent operations

## Related Code

- Hook installation: `openhands/runtime/base.py:maybe_setup_git_hooks()`
- App server hook setup: `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/git_app_conversation_service.py:maybe_setup_git_hooks()`
- Session initialization: `openhands/server/session/agent_session.py` (line 379)

## Impact

This prevents users from enforcing code quality standards, linting, formatting, or other pre-commit checks in their OpenHands workflows. Users expect that pre-commit hooks will run automatically, as they do in normal git workflows.

---

*Original report from user running OpenHands locally with GUI interface.*

title: Fallback method for "Agent got stuck in a loop"
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**
I'm using CLI mode, and my agent sometimes "got stuck in a loop" in my use cases. Think maybe it's because I'm using a relatively weak agent (DeepSeek-V3.2), but encountering this sort of issue is really annoying. 
It results in destroying my contexts completely.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**
I believe a fallback mechanism can help this issue. Instead of dropping everything in the case of "Agent got stuck in a loop", agent should try to find where this loop starts. Drop everything that be seemed as part of loop from memory, and request user if we should restart again.


**Additional context**

@openhands-agent Can you create a PR for this?

title: Add "SSL no-verify" config option for debugging
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

Make it easier for corporate users with custom cert bundles to debug their SSL connections.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

Add an "SSL no-verify" config option in the security section, with name like `SECURITY_SSL_INSECURE_NO_VERIFY`. It would be off by default and documented as for troubleshooting use only.

**Additional context**

The feature was suggested as part of PR #11051, which was split out to this issue in order to allow for discussion.

There is a tradeoff here that while we make troubleshooting easier, we're also allowing an option of running in an insecure way.

From some research we can see that this tradeoff is well traveled as the option appears in many standard tools:

* We [reference](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/47776ae2adcf8fb9f5592a0ba79ea0def08ccaac/frontend/.env.sample#L7C1-L7C26) `VITE_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` in front-end.
* [AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/) offers the option `--no-verify-ssl`.
* Google Cloud's CLI [supports](https://github.com/twistedpair/google-cloud-sdk/blob/master/google-cloud-sdk/lib/googlecloudsdk/core/requests.py#L350) `gcloud config set auth/disable_ssl_validation  True`.

This seems fairly convincing that this is standard and doesn't pose a compliance risk. We should still warn against use with some combo of naming, docs, and logging.
