title: Consolidate duplicate `Settings` type definitions
body:
## Problem

We currently maintain two parallel sets of `Settings` interfaces that represent the same data with different casing conventions:

https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/1a983d29781149187fb46a437da8e26dc02ac983/frontend/src/types/settings.ts#L40-L67

https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/1a983d29781149187fb46a437da8e26dc02ac983/frontend/src/settings-service/settings.types.ts#L3-L39

This requires **manual transformation** between the two in [`use-settings.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/hooks/query/use-settings.ts) and [`use-save-settings.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/hooks/mutation/use-save-settings.ts)

### Issues with the current approach

- **Maintenance burden**: Adding a new setting requires updating about 4 places (both type definitions + both transformation functions)
- **No type safety**: Nothing ensures the transformations stay in sync with the types
- **Error-prone**: Easy to miss a field or introduce bugs during refactoring
- **Unnecessary code**: ~60 lines of boilerplate transformation logic

## Proposed Solution

Consolidate to a single type using the `ApiSettings` snake_case format (the format returned directly from the API)

title: Avatar context menu closes when moving cursor diagonally to menu (hover zone gap)
body:
## Problem

When a user hovers over their avatar in the sidebar, a context menu appears to the right of the avatar. To interact with the menu, the user must move their cursor from the avatar to the menu items. However, if the user moves their cursor diagonally or takes a direct path from the avatar to the menu, they may accidentally leave the hover zone, causing the menu to close unexpectedly. This is a classic "hover intent" UX problem where the hover zone doesn't account for the natural diagonal cursor path users take when moving between a trigger element and its associated menu. Current Behavior:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f979366-5bd8-4b65-8be7-415dc4ffdacd

## Expected Behaviour

The user should be able to move their cursor from the avatar to the menu without the menu closing. The hover zone should include:

- The avatar itself
- The menu itself
- **The area above the avatar that runs parallel to the menu** (forming a safe "corridor" for diagonal cursor movement)

### Relevant files

[`user-actions.tsx`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/sidebar/user-actions.tsx)
[`account-settings-context-menu.tsx`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/context-menu/account-settings-context-menu.tsx)

title: Consolidate frontend theme colors
body:
## Problem Our frontend has inconsistent color usage - the same semantic colors (danger, warning, success, etc.) are defined in multiple ways across the codebase. This makes theming difficult and creates visual inconsistencies. We have a `@theme` block in `tailwind.css` that defines semantic colors: [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/1a983d29781149187fb46a437da8e26dc02ac983/frontend/src/tailwind.css#L13-L25]() But many components bypass this and use: * Tailwind's default palette (`text-red-500`, `bg-blue-400`, etc.) * Hardcoded hex values (`bg-[#4A0709]`, `text-[#9099AC]`) **Example: "Danger" Red Used 4 Different Ways** 1. Theme definition 2. `risk-alert.tsx` 3. `brand-button.tsx` 4. `error-message.tsx` ## How to All Instances Run these commands from the frontend/ directory: 1. Find Tailwind default color classes (red, blue, green, etc.) ``` grep -rE "(text|bg|border|fill|stroke|ring)-(red|blue|green|yellow|orange|purple|pink|gray|slate|zinc|neutral|amber|lime|emerald|teal|cyan|sky|indigo|violet|fuchsia|rose)-[0-9]+" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts” src/ ``` 2. Find hardcoded hex colors in className/style attributes
`grep -rE "(#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}|#[0-9A-Fa-f]{3})" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" src/` 3. Find specific color categories
Danger/Error colors:
`grep -rE "(red-[0-9]+|#[Ff]{2}0|#[Ee]7|#[Dd]55|#[Bb]91)" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" src/` Gray/Neutral colors:
`grep -rE "(gray-[0-9]+|neutral-[0-9]+|slate-[0-9]+|zinc-[0-9]+)" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" src/` ## Acceptance Criteria * No direct usage of Tailwind color palette classes (`red-*`, `blue-*`, `gray-*`, etc.) for semantic colors * All hardcoded hex colors in components replaced with theme tokens * `@theme` block contains all necessary color variants * Visual appearance remains unchanged after migration

title: OpenHands Hooks System Design
body:
This is a small proposal to replace the `ExperimentManager` with a more extensible hooks system inspired by Claude Code hooks.

It's here for us to look at, and think about it. I'm not sure this would work with immutability (experiments change the Agent), or whether it belongs in OH or SDK. But let's see how it looks like, if it was in OH:

### Problem

The current `ExperimentManager` runs hardcoded experiments at session start. It's a bit, not much, but a bit more tightly coupled to specific experiment implementations than it could be (they're in the same files), so it needs code modification to add/remove experiments.

But these are easily solvable. In reality, it's a hook: it's not named that, it requires env vars, and it's undocumented AFAIK. But it's practically a hook, so how about we make it one? 😅 

```python
# Hardcoded in SaaSExperimentManager
class SaaSExperimentManager(ExperimentManager):
    @staticmethod
    def run_agent_variant_tests__v1(user_id, conversation_id, agent) -> Agent:
        agent = handle_condenser_max_step_experiment__v1(user_id, conversation_id, agent)
        if EXPERIMENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_EXPERIMENT:
            agent = agent.model_copy(update={'system_prompt_filename': '...'})
        return agent
```

### Proposal: Make them into Hooks

```python
# Extensible via registered hooks
agent = hooks.run_session_start_hooks(user_id, conversation_id, agent)
```

The hook system makes _the extensibility_ cleaner and more discoverable: a "hook" implies there's an extension point, like `sessionStart`, when the user can add code to see or modify the behavior of the system.
- decoupled, composable hooks
- users register their own
- each hook is independently testable
- same pattern extends to other lifecycle events
- a bit cleaner extension point than hunting through the codebase to find where to inject logic
- engineers can add experiments without modifying core service code

## Terminology

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Hook** | A callback registered to run at a specific lifecycle point |
| **Hook Type** | The interface/protocol a hook must implement (e.g., `SessionStartHook`) |
| **Hooks** | Collection of hooks for a specific type, with priority ordering |
| **HookRegistry** | Central coordinator that holds all hook collections and runs them |

## Comparison with Claude Code Hooks

| Aspect | Claude Code Hooks | OpenHands Hooks (Proposed) |
|--------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| **Trigger points** | `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, etc. | `SessionStart` initially, expandable |
| **Implementation** | Shell commands (stdin/stdout JSON) | Python classes implementing protocols |
| **Configuration** | JSON settings files | JSON settings files, Python registration at startup |
| **Scope** | Per-user, per-project | Per-user, per-project, per-deployment, per-tenant |

Claude hooks use shell scripts. This proposal for OpenHands hooks has them registered in python or config.

---

## Implementation

### Hook Type Definitions

```python
# openhands/hooks/types.py

class SessionStartHook(Protocol):
    """Called when a new conversation session begins."""
    
    def on_session_start(
        self,
        user_id: str | None,
        conversation_id: UUID,
        agent: Agent,
    ) -> Agent:
        """Transform or inspect the agent before the session starts.
        
        Args:
            user_id: The user starting the session (None for anonymous)
            conversation_id: Unique ID for this conversation
            agent: The agent configuration
            
        Returns:
            The agent (potentially modified via model_copy)
        """
        ...


class SessionEndHook(Protocol):
    """Called when a conversation session ends."""
    
    def on_session_end(
        self,
        user_id: str | None,
        conversation_id: UUID,
        agent: Agent,
        summary: 'SessionSummary',
    ) -> None:
        """React to session completion (analytics, cleanup, etc.)."""
        ...
```

### Hooks Collection

```python
# openhands/hooks/hooks.py

H = TypeVar('H')  # Hook type

class Hooks(Generic[H]):
    """Collection of hooks for a specific type, with priority ordering."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self._hooks: list[tuple[int, H]] = []  # (priority, hook)
    
    def register(self, hook: H, priority: int = 100) -> None:
        """Register a hook. Lower priority = runs first."""
        self._hooks.append((priority, hook))
        self._hooks.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
        logger.debug('hook:registered', extra={
            'hook': hook.__class__.__name__,
            'priority': priority,
        })
    
    @property
    def all(self) -> list[H]:
        """Return hooks in priority order."""
        return [h for _, h in self._hooks]
    
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._hooks)
```

### HookRegistry

```python
# openhands/hooks/registry.py

class HookRegistry:
    """Central registry for all hook types."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.session_start = Hooks[SessionStartHook]()
        self.session_end = Hooks[SessionEndHook]()
    
    def run_session_start_hooks(
        self,
        user_id: str | None,
        conversation_id: UUID,
        agent: Agent,
    ) -> Agent:
        """Run all session start hooks in priority order."""
        for hook in self.session_start.all:
            hook_name = hook.__class__.__name__
            try:
                logger.debug('hook:session_start:running', extra={
                    'hook': hook_name,
                    'user_id': user_id,
                    'conversation_id': str(conversation_id),
                })
                agent = hook.on_session_start(user_id, conversation_id, agent)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error('hook:session_start:error', extra={
                    'hook': hook_name,
                    'user_id': user_id,
                    'conversation_id': str(conversation_id),
                    'error': str(e),
                })
                # Policy: continue with other hooks on error
        return agent

# Global instance - or use dependency injection
hooks = HookRegistry()
```

---

## Redesign Experiments as Hooks

### Condenser Experiment Hook

```python
# enterprise/experiments/hooks/condenser_experiment.py

class CondenserExperimentHook(SessionStartHook):
    """A/B test for condenser max_size parameter.
    
    Variants:
        - control: max_size=120
        - treatment: max_size=80
    """
    
    def __init__(self, get_variant_fn):
        """
        Args:
            get_variant_fn: Callable(user_id, conversation_id) -> variant string or None
        """
        self._get_variant = get_variant_fn
    
    def on_session_start(
        self,
        user_id: str | None,
        conversation_id: UUID,
        agent: Agent,
    ) -> Agent:
        variant = self._get_variant(user_id, str(conversation_id))
        
        if variant is None:
            logger.debug('condenser_experiment:skipped', extra={
                'reason': 'no_variant_assigned',
                'user_id': user_id,
            })
            return agent
        
        variant_config = {
            'control': 120,
            'treatment': 80,
        }
        
        max_size = variant_config.get(variant)
        if max_size is None:
            logger.error('condenser_experiment:unknown_variant', extra={
                'variant': variant,
                'user_id': user_id,
                'conversation_id': str(conversation_id),
            })
            return agent
        
        logger.info('condenser_experiment:applied', extra={
            'variant': variant,
            'max_size': max_size,
            'user_id': user_id,
            'conversation_id': str(conversation_id),
        })
        
        condenser_llm = agent.llm.model_copy(update={'usage_id': 'condenser'})
        condenser = LLMSummarizingCondenser(
            llm=condenser_llm,
            max_size=max_size,
            keep_first=4,
        )
        
        return agent.model_copy(update={'condenser': condenser})
```

### System Prompt Experiment Hook

```python
# enterprise/experiments/hooks/system_prompt_experiment.py

class SystemPromptExperimentHook(SessionStartHook):
    """Swap system prompt for long-horizon task handling."""
    
    def __init__(self, enabled: bool = False, prompt_filename: str = 'system_prompt_long_horizon.j2'):
        self._enabled = enabled
        self._prompt_filename = prompt_filename
    
    def on_session_start(
        self,
        user_id: str | None,
        conversation_id: UUID,
        agent: Agent,
    ) -> Agent:
        if not self._enabled:
            return agent
        
        logger.info('system_prompt_experiment:applied', extra={
            'prompt_filename': self._prompt_filename,
            'user_id': user_id,
            'conversation_id': str(conversation_id),
        })
        
        return agent.model_copy(
            update={'system_prompt_filename': self._prompt_filename}
        )
```

### Hook Registration at Startup

```python
# enterprise/experiments/setup.py

def register_experiment_hooks() -> None:
    """Register all experiment hooks. Called once at app startup."""
    if not ENABLE_EXPERIMENT_MANAGER:
        logger.info('hooks:experiments:disabled')
        return
    
    # Priority determines order: lower = runs first
    hooks.session_start.register(
        CondenserExperimentHook(_get_condenser_max_step_variant),
        priority=10,
    )
    
    hooks.session_start.register(
        SystemPromptExperimentHook(enabled=EXPERIMENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_EXPERIMENT),
        priority=20,
    )
    
    logger.info('hooks:experiments:registered', extra={
        'count': len(hooks.session_start),
    })
```

### Example Service Code

```python
# openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py
# ... in _build_start_conversation_request_for_user

async def _build_start_conversation_request_for_user(self, ...):
    llm = LLM(
        ...
    )
    agent = get_default_agent(llm=llm)
    
    conversation_id = uuid4()
    
    # Run all registered session start hooks
    agent = hooks.run_session_start_hooks(user.id, conversation_id, agent)
    
    start_conversation_request = StartConversationRequest(
        conversation_id=conversation_id,
        agent=agent,
        workspace=workspace,
        confirmation_policy=AlwaysConfirm(),
    )
    # ...
```

---

## Example: Custom Hooks

```python
# acme_corp/hooks.py

class ComplianceLoggingHook(SessionStartHook):
    """Log all session starts to compliance system."""
    
    def __init__(self, compliance_client):
        self._client = compliance_client
    
    def on_session_start(self, user_id, conversation_id, agent):
        self._client.log_session_start(
            user_id=user_id,
            conversation_id=str(conversation_id),
            model=agent.llm.model,
        )
        return agent  # No modifications


def register_acme_hooks():
    hooks.session_start.register(ComplianceLoggingHook(compliance_client), priority=1)
```

title: Refactor tests to use Zustand's native state setting instead of `vi.mock` for stores
body:
## Problem

Several test files are using `vi.mock` to mock Zustand stores, which is unnecessary given our test setup. Our custom Zustand mock in `__mocks__/zustand.ts` automatically resets stores between tests, and Zustand's API allows direct state manipulation via `store.setState()` and `store.getState()`.

Some files that use full store mocking with `vi.mock`:

`__tests__/components/browser.test.tsx` https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ed7adb335ca7e65f19418ca1f337f88c7b7f9c24/frontend/__tests__/components/browser.test.tsx#L33-L44

`__tests__/components/interactive-chat-box.test.tsx` https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ed7adb335ca7e65f19418ca1f337f88c7b7f9c24/frontend/__tests__/components/interactive-chat-box.test.tsx#L16-L19

`__tests__/components/chat/chat-interface.test.tsx` https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ed7adb335ca7e65f19418ca1f337f88c7b7f9c24/frontend/__tests__/components/chat/chat-interface.test.tsx#L30-L31

`__tests__/services/actions.test.tsx` https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ed7adb335ca7e65f19418ca1f337f88c7b7f9c24/frontend/__tests__/services/actions.test.tsx#L15-L21

### Why this is bad practice

1. Mock objects replicate store shape, which can drift from actual implementation
2. Doesn't test actual store behavior, reducers, or derived state
3. Requires manual reset in `afterEach` and recreating mock objects
4. Changes to store interface require updating both store and mock

## Preferred Patterns

**Pattern A: Direct state setting before render**

```ts
useBrowserStore.setState({ url: "https://example.com", screenshotSrc: "" });
renderWithProviders(<BrowserPanel />);
```

**Pattern B: Calling actions via `getState()` wrapped in `act()`**

```ts
act(() => {
  useCommandStore.getState().appendInput("echo hello");
});
```

**Pattern C: Using `renderHook` for testing store hooks directly**

```ts
const { result } = renderHook(() => useEventStore());
act(() => result.current.addEvent(mockEvent));
expect(result.current.events).toContain(mockEvent);
```

### Examples of Correct Usage

[`__tests__/stores/use-event-store.test.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/__tests__/stores/use-event-store.test.ts) - uses `renderHook` + `act()`
[`__tests__/components/terminal/terminal.test.tsx`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/__tests__/components/terminal/terminal.test.tsx) - uses `setState()` before render
[`__tests__/components/features/microagent-management/`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/__tests__/components/features/microagent-management/microagent-management.test.tsx) - uses `setState()` with helper functions

## Acceptance Criteria

- Remove `vi.mock` for Zustand stores in the affected files
- Replace with `store.setState()` for initial state setup
- Use `act(() => store.getState().action())` for triggering actions
- Ensure tests still pass and maintain coverage

title: [PRD] LLM Profile Management
body:
## Overview

LLM Profile Management enables users and admins to define, persist, and switch between multiple LLM configurations (“profiles”) in OpenHands. A profile encapsulates provider connection info (base URL + API key) and a model identifier, allowing fast model switching per user or per org policy.

This feature is a prerequisite for [APP-542](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-542/feature-switching-models-within-a-conversation) and supports the growing need for multi-model workflows (e.g., using GPT-5 for planning and Sonnet for execution).

## In Scope

1. Let users create, edit, delete, and persist multiple LLM Profiles.
2. Allow users to choose a default profile for new conversations (personal workspaces).
3. Allow conversation-level model switching by selecting from available profiles.
4. Allow org admins to enforce which profiles members can use, and set an org default.

## Out of Scope

For now, we're keeping any CLI changes out of scope. We're focusing on the GUI needs only in this PRD. See this ticket for CLI work: [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/issues/68](<https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/issues/68>)

## Customer Problem

1. Users want to work with different models as choices expand, especially for coding tasks.
2. We currently don’t persist API keys across providers
3. Users want a fast way to switch models depending on the stage of work.
4. Orgs need governance: admins want members to use approved providers/models.

## Personas

* **Personal Workspace User (Local GUI / OpenHands Cloud Personal)**

  Wants flexibility to define and switch models quickly.
* **Org Admin (OpenHands Cloud Commercial Orgs / Self-hosted)**

  Wants control over available models and a compliant default.
* **Org Member**

  Wants access only to approved models, with easy switching among them if allowed.

## Key Concepts

**LLM Profile**: Stored configuration containing:

* **Name** (display name): “GPT-5”, “Sonnet Builder”
* **Base URL**: provider endpoint (e.g., `https://api.openai.com`)
* **Model Name**: provider-scoped model id (e.g., `openai/gpt-5-main`)
* **API Key**: secret credential for that provider
* **Memory condenser size** (e.g., 250)
* **Confirmation mode:** enabled/disabled, and LLM risk analyzer selection

**Default Profile**

* Personal workspaces: user-selected default for new conversations.
* Orgs: admin-selected default enforced for all members.

**Available Profiles**

* Personal workspaces: all profiles created by user + pre-generated LLM Profiles for `OpenHands LLM provider`
* Orgs: subset selected by admin.

## User Stories & Acceptance Criteria

### Creating an LLM Profile

Applies to: Local GUI, OpenHands Cloud - Personal Workspace

As a user with access to the LLM settings in OpenHands, I want the ability to define LLM Profiles. An LLM Profile contains:

* A base URL to an LLM provider - e.g., [https://api.openai.com](<https://api.openai.com>)
* A model name - e.g., openai/gpt-5-main
* An API key
* A display name - e.g., “GPT-5”
* Memory condenser size (e.g., 250)
* Confirmation mode enabled/disabled, and LLM risk analyzer selection

AC:

* Verify that SaaS users already have LLM Profiles created for each model under OpenHands LLM profile
* Verify users can create, edit, and delete LLM profiles
* Verify a user can create multiple LLM profiles that persist base URL, model name, API key settings
* Verify users can select the default LLM profile that new conversations start with

### Conversation-level Model Switching

Applies to: Local GUI, OpenHands Cloud - Personal Workspace, OpenHands Cloud - Commercial Orgs

As a user in OpenHands, I want to be able to switch to a different LLM at the end of a conversation turn. I want to do this by selecting an available LLM Profile from within the Conversation UI.

AC:

* Verify a user can switch to an available LLM Profile from the Conversation UI

### 

### Enforcing LLM profiles in OpenHands Cloud Orgs

Applies to: OpenHands Cloud - Commercial Orgs

As an Admin in an OpenHands SaaS or Self-hosted Org, I want to define the LLM Profiles my users can see. I also want to select the default LLM profile new conversations start with, as well as select the LLM Profiles that users can switch to.

AC:

* Verify an Admin can create, edit, delete LLM Profiles
* Verify an Admin can select an LLM Profile as ‘default’
* Verify an Admin can select the LLM profiles they wish to expose to Members
* Verify a Member in an Org can only start a conversation using the LLM Profile that an Admin set as ‘default’
* Verify a Member in an Org only sees the LLM Profiles they are permitted to use

title: Task tracking loading indicator is static instead of animated spinner
body:
## Problem

In the task tracking UI that displays plan items in the chat, the "in progress" status shows a static loading icon instead of an animated spinner.

When a task has status: `”in_progress"`, the [`TaskItem`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/task-tracking/task-item.tsx) component renders a static SVG icon (`loading.svg`) that looks like a partial arc/circle. There is no animation applied, making it indistinguishable from a static icon at a glance.

## Expected Behaviour

The loading icon should animate (spin) to clearly indicate that the task is actively in progress, providing better visual feedback to users.

body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

### Summary
When installing OpenHands with ***no docker build*** and a ***local*** runtime:

`make run` / `uvicorn openhands.server.listen:app` fails during tmux dependency check with `TmuxSessionExists: Session named test-session exists`, which is then surfaced as "tmux is not properly installed". The self-check uses a fixed session name (`test-session`), so any leftover, unnatural interuption of the deployment(which spawn the test-session but fails to close it cleanly), or user-created session with that name causes a false failure.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a tmux session named `test-session` (e.g., `tmux new -s test-session` and detach).
2. Run `INSTALL_DOCKER=0 RUNTIME=local make run` (or start the server directly).
3. Startup fails with the tmux error.

### Expected
Dependency check should use a unique session name and clean up, not collide with existing sessions.

### Actual
If `test-session` exists, `libtmux` raises `TmuxSessionExists`, startup aborts, and the error message claims tmux is not installed.

title: [Bug]: Local runtime should avoid /workspace defaults and use writable host paths
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps


In `runtime=local`, the workspace and browser cache/download paths fall back to `/workspace` or a temp dir. On host machines `/workspace` is often missing or unwritable, leading to errors or files landing in a hidden temp. Playwright/BrowserGym can also throw `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspace'` when using that default. We need local-friendly defaults while keeping Docker behavior unchanged.





Reproduction steps:

1) Set `RUNTIME=local` (no docker) with no `workspace_base`.
2) Start the server (e.g., INSTALL_DOCKER=0 RUNTIME=local make run / uvicorn …).
3) Workspace is `/workspace` or a temp dir; on host it may be unwritable or unclear.
4) Playwright launch may fail with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspace'`.

**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

The microagent-management-service directory is currently located in frontend/src/ui, but it should be consolidated with the other API services under frontend/src/api.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Relocate the microagent-management-service directory to frontend/src/api.
- Update all relevant import paths in affected files.
- Ensure that all tests pass successfully.
- Confirm that there are no broken imports by running npm run typecheck.

## Problem

We have a well-established pattern for TanStack Query (https://tanstack.com/query/docs) hooks in the frontend:

- Mutations go in [`frontend/src/hooks/mutation/`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/tree/main/frontend/src/hooks/mutation)

title: Action panel shows loading state when pausing agent
body: ## Problem When a user clicks the pause button in the chat input area (bottom right), the action panel on the right side of the screen incorrectly displays a loading spinner. This happens because the `isPausing` state was included in the `shouldShownAgentLoading` condition, which is shared globally via the conversation store. ### Root Cause The `shouldShownAgentLoading` variable in [`agent-status.tsx`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/d772dd65a5e09ea4696d15ad4877c3f642236f79/frontend/src/components/features/controls/agent-status.tsx#L61) serves two purposes: - Local: Controls the loading indicator in the `AgentStatus` component (chat input area) - Global: Synced to `conversation-store` and used by `ConversationTabContent` to show/hide the action panel loading state The `isPausing` flag was included in this shared condition, causing both the local chat UI and the global action panel to show loading states during a pause action. ## Acceptance Criteria - Pause button shows loading indicator in chat input area - Pause button does NOT trigger loading state on action panel - Other loading conditions (`INIT`, `LOADING`, `CONNECTING`, task polling) still work for both areas

title: [Bug]: Excessive Time Spent on `chown` Operations During SWE-bench Evaluation
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

# Performance Issue: Excessive Time Spent on `chown` Operations During SWE-bench Evaluation

## Summary

During SWE-bench evaluation, Docker image building step `#17 [13/22]` takes an excessive amount of time (approximately 41 minutes / 2482.8 seconds) due to multiple `chown -R` operations on large directories.

## Environment

- **OpenHands Version**: v0.62.0
- **Evaluation**: SWE-bench (princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
- **Agent**: CodeActAgent
- **Docker Build Step**: `#17 [13/22]`

## Problem Description

The Docker build step `#17 [13/22]` in `Dockerfile.j2` contains multiple recursive `chown` operations that take an extremely long time to complete:

```dockerfile
chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/poetry && \
chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/workspace && \
chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/micromamba
```

### Observed Performance

From the build logs:
- **Start Time**: `12:27:11`
- **End Time**: `13:08:34`
- **Duration**: `2482.8s` (approximately **41 minutes**)

This step is significantly slower than other build steps, which typically complete in seconds.

## Expected Behavior

The `chown` operations should complete much faster, ideally within seconds rather than tens of minutes.

## Actual Behavior

The `chown` operations on `/openhands/poetry`, `/openhands/workspace`, and `/openhands/micromamba` take approximately 41 minutes to complete.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run SWE-bench evaluation:
   ```bash
   ./evaluation/benchmarks/swe_bench/scripts/run_infer.sh \
     llm.eval_qwen3_8b HEAD CodeActAgent 500 100 1 \
     princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified test
   ```

2. Monitor Docker build logs for step `#17 [13/22]`
3. Observe the excessive time spent on `chown` operations

## Logs

### Relevant Log Entries

```
[92m12:27:11 - openhands:INFO[0m: docker.py:317 - #17 [13/22] RUN ... chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/poetry && ... chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/workspace && chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/micromamba ...
[92m13:08:34 - openhands:INFO[0m: docker.py:317 - #17 DONE 2482.8s
```

### Full Command in Step #17

```bash
RUN /openhands/micromamba/bin/micromamba run -n openhands poetry run python -c "import sys; print('OH_INTERPRETER_PATH=' + sys.executable)" >> /etc/environment && \
    chmod -R 755 /openhands/poetry && \
    chmod -R 755 /openhands/micromamba && \
    chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/poetry && \
    mkdir -p /openhands/workspace && chmod -R g+rws,o+rw /openhands/workspace && \
    chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/workspace && \
    chown -R openhands:openhands /openhands/micromamba && \
    ...
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue likely stems from:

1. **Large Directory Trees**: The `/openhands/micromamba` and `/openhands/poetry` directories contain many files (Python packages, conda environments, etc.), making recursive `chown` operations slow.

2. **Filesystem Performance**: The underlying filesystem (possibly overlay2 in Docker) may have performance issues with metadata operations on large directory trees.

3. **Redundant Operations**: Multiple `chown` operations are performed on the same directories at different build steps, which may be unnecessary.

## Suggested Solutions

1. **Use `COPY --chown` instead of `chown`**: When copying files, use Docker's `--chown` flag to set ownership during copy, avoiding post-copy `chown` operations.

2. **Optimize chown operations**: 
   - Only chown directories that actually need it
   - Consider using `find` with `-exec chown` for better performance
   - Use `--no-dereference` flag where appropriate

3. **Reduce chown scope**: 
   - Set ownership at the directory level where possible
   - Avoid recursive chown on entire large directory trees if only specific subdirectories need it

4. **Cache optimization**: Ensure chown operations don't invalidate Docker layer cache unnecessarily

## Related Files

- `openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_templates/Dockerfile.j2` (lines 225-231)
- Multiple `chown` operations throughout the Dockerfile

## Additional Context

- This issue significantly impacts evaluation time, as each instance requires building a new runtime image
- The problem is reproducible across multiple evaluation runs
- Similar performance issues may exist in other build steps with `chown` operations

## Questions

1. Is it necessary to recursively chown all files in `/openhands/micromamba` and `/openhands/poetry`?
2. Could we set ownership during file creation/copy instead of post-processing?
3. Are there any filesystem-specific optimizations we could apply?

(If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead). - [x] I have checked the existing issues. ### Describe the bug and reproduction steps An OpenHands agent crashed with a 502 Bad Gateway error from the LiteLLM proxy server instead of automatically retrying. ## Root Cause **`BadGatewayError` is missing from the retry exception list** in `openhands/llm/llm.py` ## The Problem ```python # Current code in openhands/llm/llm.py:44 LLM_RETRY_EXCEPTIONS: tuple[type[Exception], ...] = ( APIConnectionError, RateLimitError, ServiceUnavailableError, litellm.Timeout, litellm.InternalServerError, LLMNoResponseError, ) # ❌ Missing: BadGatewayError ``` ## The Solution ```python # Add to imports (line 22) from litellm.exceptions import ( APIConnectionError, BadGatewayError, # ADD THIS RateLimitError, ServiceUnavailableError, ) # Add to retry exceptions (line 44) LLM_RETRY_EXCEPTIONS: tuple[type[Exception], ...] = ( APIConnectionError, RateLimitError, ServiceUnavailableError, BadGatewayError, # ADD THIS litellm.Timeout, litellm.InternalServerError, LLMNoResponseError, ) ``` ## Technical Details ### Error Flow 1. **LiteLLM Proxy** returns HTML 502 Bad Gateway 2. **OpenAI SDK** raises `openai.InternalServerError` 3. **LiteLLM** converts to `litellm.APIError` (should be `BadGatewayError`) 4. **OpenHands retry logic** doesn't recognize it → no retry 5. **Agent Controller** catches it → agent crashes ```python Traceback (most recent call last): File "/openhands/poetry/.../tenacity/__init__.py", line 400, in _add_action_func self._add_action_func(lambda rs: rs.outcome.result()) File "/openhands/code/openhands/controller/agent_controller.py", line 878, in _step action = self.agent.step(self.state) File "/openhands/code/openhands/agenthub/codeact_agent/codeact_agent.py", line 219, in step response = self.llm.completion(**params) File "/openhands/code/openhands/llm/llm.py", line 340, in wrapper resp = self._completion_unwrapped(...) 502 Bad Gateway

", llm_provider="litellm_proxy", model=model, response=original_exception.response, ) File "/openhands/poetry/.../litellm/llms/openai/openai.py", line 756, in completion raise OpenAIError(...) File "/openhands/poetry/.../openai/_base_client.py", line 1047, in _request raise self._make_status_error_from_response(err.response) from None litellm.exceptions.APIError: APIError: Litellm_proxyException - 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/openhands/code/openhands/controller/agent_controller.py", line 373, in _step_with_exception_handling await self._step() File "/openhands/code/openhands/controller/agent_controller.py", line 901, in _step action = self.agent.step(self.state) Exception: Error while running the agent (session ID: {session_id}): APIError: Litellm_proxyException - 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

``` ### Why 502 Errors Should Be Retried 502 Bad Gateway is a **transient error** indicating: - Proxy server overload - Backend temporarily unavailable - Network congestion - Load balancer issues

title: [Bug]: V0 + V1 coexistence (and `RUNTIME` confusion) in OpenHands
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

## Summary
- Even when `ENABLE_V1 != 0`, the server still **starts the V0 conversation manager** at startup and still **mounts V0 routes**. V1 is currently *added*, not *replacing* V0.
- The env var `RUNTIME` is used in **two different places with two different meanings**:
    - **V0**: selects the runtime backend (`docker`/`local`/etc).
    - **V1**: selects the sandbox backend (`docker`/`process`/`remote`) via a legacy fallback.
- When running without Docker and setting `RUNTIME=local`, V0 `LocalRuntime.setup()` initializes BrowserGym/Playwright with a hardcoded downloads path under `/workspace`, causing:
    - `playwright._impl._errors.Error: BrowserType.launch: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspace'`

## Evidence from code (current `main`)

### 1) V0 is always started at server startup
- FastAPI lifespan always enters `conversation_manager`:
  - `openhands/server/app.py:54` (`_lifespan`) and `openhands/server/app.py:56`
- V0 routes are always mounted (independent of `ENABLE_V1`):
  - `openhands/server/app.py:87` (`app.include_router(conversation_api_router)`)
- The conversation manager unconditionally initializes the selected V0 runtime:
  - `openhands/server/conversation_manager/standalone_conversation_manager.py:82`
    - `get_runtime_cls(self.config.runtime).setup(self.config)`

### 2) V1 is conditionally added, not replacing V0
- V1 router is only *additionally* included:
  - `openhands/server/app.py:93` (`if server_config.enable_v1: ...`)
- V1 API prefix:
  - `openhands/app_server/v1_router.py:12` (`APIRouter(prefix='/api/v1')`)

### 3) `RUNTIME` is read both by V0 and V1 (different semantics)
- V1 sandbox “legacy fallback” checks `os.getenv('RUNTIME')`:
  - `openhands/app_server/config.py:168` (sandbox injector)
  - `openhands/app_server/config.py:180` (sandbox_spec injector)
- V0 `LocalRuntime` dependency check initializes `BrowserEnv()`:
  - `openhands/runtime/impl/local/local_runtime.py:118` → `BrowserEnv()` at `openhands/runtime/impl/local/local_runtime.py:122`

### 4) `/workspace` hardcoded in BrowserGym/Playwright path
- BrowserGym openended env passes a hardcoded downloads path:
  - `openhands/runtime/browser/browser_env.py:90` (see `downloads_path: '/workspace/.downloads/'`)
- Action execution server also assumes `/workspace/.downloads` exists:
  - `openhands/runtime/action_execution_server.py:208` (`self.downloads_directory = '/workspace/.downloads'`)

### 5) Frontend still chooses between V0 and V1 APIs
- Frontend explicitly falls back to “legacy API” depending on `settings.v1_enabled`:
  - `frontend/src/hooks/mutation/use-create-conversation.ts:54` (`useV1 = ...`)
  - `frontend/src/hooks/mutation/use-create-conversation.ts:81` (`// Use legacy API`)

## Repro (local machine, no Docker)

### A) Trigger V0 LocalRuntime + `/workspace` crash
1. `export INSTALL_DOCKER=0`
2. `export RUNTIME=local`
3. `make run ...`
4. Observe Playwright trying to `mkdir '/workspace'` and failing with `EACCES`.

### B) Try to use V1 without `RUNTIME`, still see docker sandbox selection
1. `unset RUNTIME`
2. `export INSTALL_DOCKER=0`
3. `make run ...`
4. When creating a V1 conversation, backend logs show docker sandbox checks like:
   - `openhands.app_server.sandbox.docker_sandbox_service ... Sandbox server not running ...`
   - This happens because the V1 sandbox fallback defaults to docker when not explicitly configured.

## Why this matters
- Users can believe they are “using V1 only” but still hit V0 initialization at startup.
- `RUNTIME` naming collision causes configuration surprises (V0 runtime vs V1 sandbox backend).
- Local development without Docker is currently fragile due to `/workspace` assumptions.

title: [PRD] OpenHands Plugins
body:
# Problem Statement

## **Background**

* Organizations want an easy way to **publish, discover, and run pre-built agents** (sometimes called “Recipes” or “Plugins”) that include *everything needed* for a specific use case.
* Today, enterprises are attempting to build agents around recurring software engineer tasks, such as:
  * CVE remediation agents
  * Dependency upgrade agents
  * FinOps optimization tools
  * Cobol migration agents

## **Pain Points**

* **Lack of packaging and extensibility:** The current system mainly supports **single-file Skills**, which are easy to get started — BUT, too limited compared to emerging standards like **Claude Code Plugins**. For example, they lack extended functionality like:
  * Defining MCP servers
  * Defining runtime environments requirements, like custom images that need to be included
  * Bundling and linking additional Skills needed for more complex scenarios
  * Defining what an “initial prompt” is, including any parameterized inputs required by the user to execute that initial prompt
* **Fragmentation:** In large enterprises (e.g., 1000s of developers and repos), there is typically a lot of fragmentation:
  * Multiple Git providers
  * No org-level Git repo standard to universally share Skills
  * No reliable way to ensure all repos have `.openhands/skills` setup

## **Negative Consequences**

* **High friction for developers** to run or reuse agents. They must manually assemble skills, configs, prompts, and tools.
* **Poor reusability and scalability**: Skills are duplicated or bloated instead of being composed from smaller parts.
* **Fragmentation across teams**: Multiple repos, patterns, and Git providers with no single source of truth.
* **Not “future proof”:** Single-skill-only approaches won’t support agents that require MCP configs, runtime configs, scripts, or multiple skills over time.
  * **Complexity:** Massive monolithic Skills files that evolve over time
  * **Inefficiency:** No established “packaging” or “distribution” mechanism, leading to ad-hoc repo structures and no cross-team sharing
  * **Redundant work:** Teams end up re-creating the same Skills over-and-over, due to lack of distribution, discovery, and awareness of pre-built agents.

## **Desired Future State**

* **A packaging standard (again, exactly like Claude Code Plugins), that:**
  * Bundles skills, initial prompts, MCP definitions, runtime configs, scripts, and other assets.
  * Is extensible over time (“batteries included”).
* **A central, private, org-level marketplace**
  * Acts as the canonical distribution point across the enterprise.
  * Used by Agent Builders for publishing agents, and Agent Consumers and discovering reusable agents.
  * Encourages forking and cloning to help with extending agents
* **One-click, “batteries included” experience**:
  * A developer who is new to AI should be able to:
    * Navigate the marketplace and discover an agent for their problem
    * Click a button to start a conversation with that agent
    * Enter parameterized values needed for the agent to perform work. For example, a CVE Remediation agent may ask for:
      * repo location
      * package name with vulnerabilities that need to be fixed
      * package version to upgrade to
    * Have the conversation start with an initial prompt
* **Industry-aligned design**: Compatibility with Claude Code Plugins to reduce friction and enable reuse.

# Goals

## In Scope

* A packaging standard for distributing “batteries included” agents (which we will call “Plugins”)
* A way for Agent Builders to publish those Plugins, and a way for Agent Consumers users to discover and use those Plugins easily
* Features in OpenHands Cloud that allow for Plugin discovery, distribution, and execution

## Out of Scope

* A public-facing, OpenHands maintained Plugin Marketplace of open source/public Plugins that anyone in the ecosystem can use. This will come later and likely reuse parts of this epic.

# Personas

* **Agent Builders:** These are engineers who create repeatable, reusable agents for recurring engineering tasks such as CVE remediation, code reviews, expanding unit test coverage, upgrading dependencies, and more. They build agents, test them, run evals to test effectiveness, and share them with the rest of the organization.
* **Agent Consumers:** These are typically engineers on an application development team who are looking to solve recurring software engineering tasks, like CVE Remediation, and would like to use an AI Agent to be more productive with that task.

# Use Cases

**Plugin Definition** ([#12086](<https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12086>))

1. Converting Skill to Plugin for distribution: Existing Skill file that needs to be packaged into a Plugin for distribution
2. Building and Testing a New Agent
   1. Skills may still be built and tested independently
   2. Integration Testing: Skills may then be packaged into a Plugin and tested locally for integration purposes

Dependencies: [Support AgentSkills Standard](<https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/1473>)

**OpenHands Cloud - REST API** ([APP-629](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-629/openhands-cloud-rest-api))

1. Using a Plugin to start a Conversation via a REST API in OpenHands Cloud

**OpenHands Cloud - Organizational Marketplace GUI** ([APP-628](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-628/plugin-marketplace-gui))

1. Publishing a Plugin
2. Discovering a Plugin
3. Using a Plugin to start a Conversation (user clicks a button on Marketplace GUI)

# Sequencing

1. [AGE-285](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/AGE-285/plugin-10-definition)
2. [APP-629](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-629/openhands-cloud-rest-api)
3. [APP-628](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-628/plugin-marketplace-gui)

title: OpenHands Cloud - REST API
body:
## Goals

- Provide a way to start a conversation in OpenHands Cloud using a Plugin by executing a single REST API call

## Requirements

- REST API accepts a URL to a plugin (this can be a URL to a git repo, or a URL a plugin directory within a git repo)
- Can optionally accept parameterized inputs needed to start the conversation. For example, a CVE Remediation agent may ask for:
    - repo location
    - package name with vulnerabilities that need to be fixed
    - package version to upgrade to
- Results in a Conversation started with the initial prompt, plus any parameterized inputs filled in by the user

## Example REST API

**High level example**

```yaml
curl -X POST https://openhands-cloud.acmeco.com/v1/start_conversation \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {{ API KEY HERE }} " \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "plugin_url=https://github.com/acmeco/plugin-marketplace/cve-remediation/" \
  -d 'plugin_params={
		    "package-name": "nginx-ingress:1.0"
		    "upgrade-to": "2.0"
		  }'
```

title: Plugin Marketplace GUI
body:
## Problem Statement

**Typical Customer Profile:** Enterprises (100s of devs, 1000s of employees)

Today, enterprise customers struggle with distributing the agents they create for recurring engineering tasks (like CVE remediation, dependency upgrades) to different teams. There is no "discoverability" layer in OpenHands that facilitates this, and therefore other teams are unable to reap the efficiency/productivity benefits of executing agents built by others.

Example current state:

* Platform team creates a Skill that proactively refactors Angular 1.2 --> React.
* Platform team publishes this to their `acmeco/.openhands` repo for others to use
* Frontend team is tasked with refactoring their app, but decidely builds their own Skill to do this.
* Result? Redundant work: Frontend team spends effort creating a Skill that was already built by Platform team

Future state:

* Frontend team is able to browse a directory of "Plugins" developed by the organization to solve recurring
* Frontend team is able to search for Plugins related to React and immediately use it
* Bonus: OpenHands can recommend specific Plugins based on the context/codebase of their repo

## What is a Plugin, and how does it compare to a Skill?

See: [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12085](<https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12085>)

## Goals

**Goals**

* **Enable publishing** of Plugins to a shared, org-accessible repository.
* **Enable discovery** of Plugins through a dedicated in-product page.
* **Enable feedback loops** via comments and effectiveness ratings.

**Non-Goals**

* Public marketplace across multiple organizations (this is org-scoped).
* Complex workflow approvals beyond a simple publish/review flow (future).

## Key questions

* **Redundancy with Microagent Management UI:** Today we have a UI for sharing Organization-level microagents (stored in a `.openhands` repo within the Git organization). Do we remove this functionality in favor of this Organization-level Plugin Directory
  * No, this is separate. In general, we need to update the Microagent Management functionality to be more in-line with AgentSkills. Additionally, the current UX is not intuitive and needs to be re-evaluated.
* Would a Plugin be executed at the start of a conversation?
  * Yes it should support being able to execute the Plugin at the start of the conversation.
* Do you need to package MCP with the Plugin?
  * Not for initial scope, but in the future
* Do you need to package Secrets with the Plugin?
  * Not for initial scope, but in the future
* Should we prompt for specific input variables before the conversation starts (rather than have OpenHands interview the user for additional info)?
* Does this override the system prompt?
  * For MVP, I think we keep the system prompt

## Users and Use Cases

### Primary Users

* **Agent Publishers (Builders):** create and publish Plugins.
* **Agent Consumers (End Users):** browse and use existing Plugins. Agent Consumers could be users with or without an account on OpenHands Cloud.
* **Org Admins / Leads:** manage access and moderate content.

### MVP - Key Use Cases

1. **Publish a Plugin to org repo**
   * An author finishes a Plugin and wants it available to teammates.
2. **Browse/search Plugins in a Marketplace UI**
   * A consumer visits a directory to find a Plugin for the desired task.
3. **Rate + comment on Plugin effectiveness**
   * After using a Plugin, a consumer leaves a rating and a short comment.
4. **Ownership + edits**
   * A consumer finds a bug and pings the owner; owner can update/publish new versions.
5. **Executing Plugins**
   1. Ability to execute a Plugin as the initial prompt at the start of an OpenHands conversation
6. **Marketplace Administration**

## Assumptions

**1. A private Marketplace may initially be available to customers using Self-hosted OpenHands Cloud**
Given our initial target customer profile for this feature is enterprises, and enterprises typically prefer Self-hosted OpenHands Cloud, we may make this functionality initially available to those cohorts. We will consider expanding to OpenHands Cloud SaaS Organizations later, once [Organizations Support](<https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-Cloud/issues/18>) is released.

**2. A large enterprise (1000s of developers) may want all developers to be able to browse the Marketplace (to help with discoverability), but only users with an account on OpenHands Cloud can start a conversation with those Plugins**

**3. Implementation wise, the Marketplace UI may be a separate application - TBD for additional engineering discussion.** 
Pros:

* Allows us to execute on this work without being blocked by [Organizations Support](<https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-Cloud/issues/18>)
* Separates the user bases between 1) Marketplace users who are simply browsing, and 2) OpenHands Cloud users who can start conversation
  * Enterprises may want to have tight control over user licenses cohort `#2` above, while allowing users in cohort `#1` to browse/discover plugins and eventually 'request' a license
* Allows for scenarios where a Self-hosted OpenHands Cloud customer may have *multiple Organizations* configured, but wants a *single, company-wide* Plugin Marketplace available
* Aligns with the initial desire to make this a feature of Self-hosted OpenHands Cloud - e.g., customers can choose to optionally offer the Marketplace UI to employees

Cons:

* Separate code base to maintain
* Doesn't support OpenHands Cloud SaaS immediately

## 5\. Requirements

### 5.1 Plugin Publishing

**User story:** As an agent publisher, I want to publish a Plugin to a git repo, and then make it available via a centralized 'marketplace' UI, so others can discover and reuse it.

**AC:**

* For new plugins, Agent Publishers should have a way to submit a Plugin (which is the path to a git repo) to the Marketplace UI
* The Marketplace UI should read the contents of that Git repo, determine the unique Plugins in that repo, and let the user select the specific Plugins they would like to publish to the Marketplace
* A Marketplace Admin should have ability to accept/reject new Plugins being submitted.

### 5.2 Marketplace UI

**User story:** As a developer interested in AI agents within my company, I want to discover Plugins from a dedicated 'marketplace' UI made available to me internally.

**AC:**

* Add a new navigation item - Plugin Marketplace - from OpenHands
* Marketplace
* Within Marketplace, have the ability to search for Plugins
* Clicking a card opens a **Plugin Detail Page**.

### 5.3 Ratings & Comments

**User story:** As an agent consumer, I want to rate and comment on a Plugin's effectiveness, so authors and others know what works.

**AC:**

* Plugin detail page includes:
  * **Star rating** (1–5)
  * Optional short comment text
* Only authenticated marketplace users can rate/comment.
* A user can:
  * leave one rating per Plugin
    * comment multiple times if needed
* Display:
  * Average rating
  * Recent comments (with timestamps and author)

**Acceptance criteria**

* Rating updates average rating immediately.
* Comments are visible to org members in chronological order.
* Users can edit/delete their own comments.

### 5.4 Ownership & Edit Rights

**User story:** As an agent consumer, I want to see who owns a Plugin so I know who to contact for fixes

**AC:**

* Every Plugin has a single **Owner** (user or team entity).
* Owner is displayed prominently on Plugin cards and detail page.
* Marketplace Admins can delete plugins

### 5.5 Plugin execution

**User story:** As an agent consumer, I want to start a conversation with a specific plugin

**AC:**

* Within the Marketplace UI, have a button to start a conversation with that Plugin
* User should be redirected to the OpenHands Cloud app to start the conversation

### 5.6 Marketplace Administration

As a Marketplace Admin, I want the ability to customize the marketplace experience.

**AC:**

* Upload/change the logo
* Add footer text

title: Support for bare git repository plugin marketplaces
body:
## Description

Add support for distributing OpenHands plugins via bare git repository marketplaces. This is the approach used by Claude.

## Goals

Implement basic support for loading plugins from git repository marketplaces, enabling teams to easily share and discover plugins without packaging overhead. The implementation follows the [Claude Code plugin marketplace format](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces>) for cross-platform compatibility.

## Relevance

The marketplace is relevant to:

* [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12088](<https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12088>)
* Possibly CLI, with idea of installing / activating plugins

## Proposed Implementation

### Marketplace Descriptor Location

For compatibility with [Claude Code marketplaces](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins>), we will support reading from:

* `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude Code compatibility)
* `.plugin/marketplace.json` (vendor-neutral alternative)

Both locations will be supported, with `.plugin/marketplace.json` taking precedence if both exist.

### Basic Marketplace Schema

Following the [Claude Code marketplace schema](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#marketplace-schema>):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json",
  "name": "marketplace-name",
  "description": "Optional marketplace description",
  "owner": {
    "name": "Team Name",
    "email": "team@example.com"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "plugin-name",
      "source": "./plugins/my-plugin",
      "description": "Plugin description",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "category": "development"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Required Fields

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200 -->
| Field | Type | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `name` | string | Marketplace identifier (kebab-case, no spaces) |
| `owner` | object | Marketplace maintainer information |
| `owner.name` | string | Name of the maintainer or team |
| `plugins` | array | List of available plugins |

#### Optional Metadata

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200 -->
| Field | Type | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `$schema` | string | JSON schema URL for validation |
| `description` | string | Brief marketplace description |
| `owner.email` | string | Contact email for the maintainer |
| `metadata.pluginRoot` | string | Base directory prepended to relative plugin source paths |

### Plugin Entry Schema

Each plugin entry in the `plugins` array supports these fields per the [Claude Code plugin entries spec](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#plugin-entries>):

#### Required Fields

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200 -->
| Field | Type | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `name` | string | Plugin identifier (kebab-case, no spaces) |
| `source` | string | object |

#### Optional Fields

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:200,200,200 -->
| Field | Type | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `description` | string | Brief plugin description |
| `version` | string | Plugin version |
| `author` | object | Plugin author (`name` required, `email` optional) |
| `category` | string | Plugin category (e.g., "development", "productivity") |
| `tags` | array | Tags for searchability |
| `homepage` | string | Plugin homepage or documentation URL |
| `strict` | boolean | If `false`, plugin doesn't need its own `plugin.json` |

### Plugin Source Support (Initial)

Following the [Claude Code plugin sources spec](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#plugin-sources>):

* **Relative paths**: Plugins within the same repository

  ```json
  {
    "name": "my-plugin",
    "source": "./plugins/my-plugin"
  }
  ```
* **GitHub repositories**:

  ```json
  {
    "name": "github-plugin",
    "source": {
      "source": "github",
      "repo": "owner/plugin-repo"
    }
  }
  ```
* **URL sources** (any Git URL):

  ```json
  {
    "name": "external-plugin",
    "source": {
      "source": "url",
      "url": "https://gitlab.com/team/plugin.git"
    }
  }
  ```

### Core Functionality

* Read and parse marketplace.json from git repositories
* Support basic plugin metadata (name, description, version, author, category)
* Load plugins from relative paths within marketplace repo
* Load plugins from external GitHub repos
* Load plugins from arbitrary git URLs via `url` source type
* Basic validation of marketplace schema

## Out of Scope (Initial Implementation)

The following features are intentionally excluded from the initial implementation and can be added in future iterations:

* **Auto-update functionality**: Automatic marketplace and plugin updates at startup
* **Version pinning and constraints**: Specific version requirements or ranges (`ref` field for GitHub/git sources)
* **Enterprise restrictions**: `strictKnownMarketplaces` and allowlisting
* **Team configuration**: `.openhands/settings.json` integration for `extraKnownMarketplaces`
* **Advanced plugin sources**: npm packages, local absolute paths
* **Marketplace metadata refresh**: `/plugin marketplace update` command
* **Custom component paths**: Override locations for commands, agents, hooks, mcpServers, lspServers
* **Inline component definitions**: Defining mcpServers/lspServers directly in marketplace.json
* **Marketplace versioning**: Marketplace-level version tracking via `metadata.version`
* **Dependency resolution**: Plugin dependencies on other plugins
* **Conflict detection**: Handling duplicate plugin names across marketplaces
* **Caching and performance optimization**: Marketplace metadata caching
* **Plugin validation tools**: CLI validation commands for marketplace creators
* **Marketplace hosting guidelines**: Documentation for best practices
* **Private repository authentication**: Handling private git repos with credentials
* **Webhook integrations**: Automatic notifications on plugin updates
* **Plugin ratings and reviews**: Community feedback mechanisms
* **Usage analytics**: Tracking plugin installation and usage stats

## References

### Claude Code Documentation

* [Create and distribute a plugin marketplace](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces>) - Official guide for creating marketplaces
* [Discover and install prebuilt plugins](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins>) - User guide for marketplace usage
* [Plugins reference](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference>) - Complete technical specifications

### Example Marketplaces

* [anthropics/claude-plugins-official](<https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official>) - Anthropic's official plugin marketplace
* [anthropics/claude-code/plugins](<https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins>) - Demo marketplace with example plugins

## Related Issues

* OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1440 - Plugin 1.0 Definition
* OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1452 - AgentSkills Compatibility
* OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1473 - Support AgentSkills standard (skills/SKILL.md format)
* OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1399 - POC: support for Python package-based plugin loading
* OpenHands/OpenHands#12085 - Plugin Packaging & Marketplace Vision
* This complements the Python package-based distribution (see OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1399) by providing an easier setup method that doesn't require formal build processes or SDLC overhead.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Can read marketplace.json from both `.claude-plugin/` and `.plugin/` directories
- [ ] Can parse and validate basic marketplace schema (name, owner, plugins)
- [ ] Can load plugins from relative paths within marketplace repository
- [ ] Can load plugins from external GitHub repositories (`{"source": "github", "repo": "..."}`)
- [ ] Can load plugins from arbitrary git URLs (`{"source": "url", "url": "..."}`)
- [ ] Basic error handling for invalid marketplace configurations
- [ ] Documentation for creating and using marketplace repositories
- [ ] Tests covering core marketplace loading functionality

**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

The SaaS UI is currently not displaying the "Reasoning:" field from LLM responses. When using reasoning models (like o1, o3, or Claude with extended thinking), the reasoning/thinking content is available in the response but not shown to users in the chat interface.

Display the reasoning content in a collapsible UI element, similar to how ChatGPT handles it:

- This would apply to both `reasoning_content` (from reasoning models) and `thinking_blocks` (from Anthropic extended thinking)

The frontend already has the data structures in place:
- `reasoning_content?: string | null` - Intermediate reasoning/thinking content from reasoning models
- `thinking_blocks: (ThinkingBlock | RedactedThinkingBlock)[]` - Anthropic thinking blocks from the LLM response

These fields are defined in `frontend/src/types/v1/core/events/action-event.ts` but are not currently rendered in the UI.

title: [Bug]: Flaky test test_tool_call_validation_error_handling due to feedback loop in EventStream
body:
## Summary

The test `test_tool_call_validation_error_handling` in `tests/unit/controller/test_agent_controller.py` is flaky and fails when run with pytest-xdist (parallel test execution). The test expects 1 `ErrorObservation` but gets multiple (4-10 depending on timing).

## Root Cause Analysis

The test creates an `AgentController` which subscribes to the `EventStream` in its constructor:

```python
if not self.is_delegate:
    self.event_stream.subscribe(
        EventStreamSubscriber.AGENT_CONTROLLER, self.on_event, self.id
    )
```

When `_step()` is called and catches a `BadRequestError` with tool validation failure, it adds an `ErrorObservation` to the event stream:

```python
self.event_stream.add_event(
    ErrorObservation(
        content=f'Tool call validation failed: {str(e)}. Please check the tool parameters and try again.',
    ),
    EventSource.AGENT,
)
```

The `EventStream` has a background thread that processes events and notifies subscribers. When the `ErrorObservation` is added, the background thread calls the controller's `on_event` callback, which then calls `should_step()`. Since `should_step()` returns `True` for `ErrorObservation` events, it triggers another `_step()` call.

This creates a **feedback loop**:
1. Test calls `controller._step()`
2. `_step()` catches `BadRequestError` and adds `ErrorObservation` to event stream
3. Background thread picks up the event and calls `on_event`
4. `on_event` calls `should_step(ErrorObservation)` which returns `True`
5. `on_event` calls `_step_with_exception_handling()`
6. `_step()` catches `BadRequestError` again (mock always raises the same error)
7. Repeat until iteration limit is reached

The test passes without pytest-xdist because the background thread doesn't have time to process events before the assertion runs. With pytest-xdist, the timing is different and the feedback loop executes.

## Proposed Fix

Change the mock in the test to only raise the error once, then return a valid action (like `NullAction`). This makes the test deterministic and correctly tests the error handling logic:

```python
call_count = 0

def mock_step(state):
    nonlocal call_count
    call_count += 1
    if call_count == 1:
        raise BadRequestError(
            message='litellm.BadRequestError: GroqException - {"error":{"message":"tool call validation failed: parameters for tool str_replace_editor did not match schema: errors: [missing properties: \'path\']","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"tool_use_failed"}}',
            model='groq/llama3-8b-8192',
            llm_provider='groq',
        )
    return NullAction()
```

## Related

- Commit that introduced the test: ec9daf3bc "Fix tool call validation error handling for Groq LLM provider (#10927)"
- PR #12107 skips this test as a workaround
- CI failure: https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/actions/runs/20380478897/job/58569463227

In the `ALL-2596/org-support` branch, we introduced hooks that use TanStack Query for client-side state management. This approach is not inherently an anti-pattern; however, it is inconsistent from our established state management practices in the frontend app.

- Is already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., [`error-message-store.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ALL-2596/org-support/frontend/src/stores/error-message-store.ts), [`optimistic-user-message-store.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ALL-2596/org-support/frontend/src/stores/optimistic-user-message-store.ts))

    - `setOrgId` should update the state
    - State should persist across hook calls
    - Route revalidation should trigger on state change
2. **Run tests (they will fail)** - Confirm the tests fail with the expected errors

title: Fix nested button accessibility issue in `TooltipButton` component
body:
## Problem

The `TooltipButton` component creates nested interactive elements when used as a wrapper around existing buttons (e.g., `ConversationTabNav`). This results in invalid HTML where a `<button>` is rendered inside another `<button>`:

```tsx
<ChatActionTooltip>
  <ConversationTabNav />  {/* This is a <button> */}
</ChatActionTooltip>
```

Expands to:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <button>              {/* TooltipButton creates this */}
    <button>...</button> {/* ConversationTabNav creates this */}
  </button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Symptoms

- Invalid HTML: Buttons cannot contain other buttons per HTML spec
- Broken keyboard navigation: Tab focuses the outer button (which has no action), not the inner one
- Enter key doesn't work: The outer button receives the keypress but has no `onClick` handler
- Double Tab required: Users must `{Tab}` twice to reach the actual actionable button
- Screen reader confusion: Announces nested buttons, which is semantically meaningless

### Why this is bad practice

- `TooltipButton` is overloaded, it conflates two separate concerns:
    - `Tooltip` wrapper: Just show a tooltip on hover
    - Interactive element: A button/link that performs an action
- When a component needs both, `TooltipButton` creates its own interactive element and wraps the child's interactive element, causing the nesting issue.

## Proposed Change

1. Separate the concerns:
    - Create a simple `StyledTooltip` wrapper - Only handles tooltip display with consistent styling (`tooltipClassName`, `closeDelay`, etc.). Does not create any interactive elements.
    - Let components manage their own interactive elements - Each component (button, link, etc.) handles its own click behavior and accessibility attributes.
2. Refactor existing usages:
    - Where `TooltipButton` wraps an existing button -> use `StyledTooltip instead`
    - Where `TooltipButton` creates a button with tooltip -> use `StyledTooltip` + explicit button

## Acceptance Criteria

- No nested `<button>` elements in the DOM
- Keyboard navigation works correctly (single Tab to focus, Enter to activate)
- Screen readers announce elements correctly without nested button confusion
- All existing tooltip functionality preserved (hover, placement, styling)
- Accessibility attributes (`aria-label`, etc.) properly applied to the correct element

## Relevant Files

- [`tooltip-button.tsx`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/shared/buttons/tooltip-button.tsx)

title: Remote setup: CORS errors prevent file uploads in v1.0 (agent-server missing CORS support)
body:
## Problem

When running OpenHands v1.0 in a remote setup, **file uploads from the web UI fail with CORS errors**. This affects all remote deployments where the browser and server are on different machines.

## Environment

- **OpenHands Version**: v1.0
- **Setup**: Remote (server at 192.168.1.171, browser on different machine)
- **Runtime**: agent-server (Rust binary, not Python runtime)
- **Architecture**: V1.0 with agent-server containers

## Root Cause

The `openhands-agent-server` binary does not send CORS headers. When the browser tries to upload files or make API calls to the runtime container (which uses random high ports), it fails the preflight OPTIONS check.

The issue occurs because:
1. Browser is on a different origin than the agent-server
2. Agent-server binary doesn't handle CORS headers
3. Preflight OPTIONS requests return 400 without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`

## Browser Console Errors

```
XHR OPTIONS http://192.168.1.171:51579/api/file/upload/...
CORS Missing Allow Origin

Cross-Origin Request Blocked: The Same Origin Policy disallows reading the remote resource at http://192.168.1.171:51579/api/file/upload/...
(Reason: CORS header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing). Status code: 400.
```

## Impact

- **File uploads completely broken** in remote setups
- **Affects all v1.0 remote deployments**
- Not documented in remote setup guide
- Users cannot upload files to the agent for processing

## Current Workaround

We created a custom Docker image with a Python CORS proxy wrapper:

**Wrapper Script** (`agent-server-cors-wrapper.py`):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import asyncio
import subprocess
from aiohttp import web, ClientSession, WSMsgType

async def websocket_proxy(request):
    ws_client = web.WebSocketResponse()
    await ws_client.prepare(request)
    backend_url = f'ws://127.0.0.1:18000{request.path_qs}'
    
    async with ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.ws_connect(backend_url) as ws_backend:
            # Bidirectional WebSocket forwarding
            # ... (full code omitted for brevity)
    return ws_client

async def http_proxy(request):
    target_url = f'http://127.0.0.1:18000{request.path_qs}'
    
    if request.method == 'OPTIONS':
        return web.Response(headers={
            'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
            'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': '*',
            'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': '*',
            'Access-Control-Max-Age': '86400',
        })
    
    async with ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.request(
            method=request.method,
            url=target_url,
            headers={k: v for k, v in request.headers.items() if k.lower() != 'host'},
            data=await request.read()
        ) as resp:
            headers = dict(resp.headers)
            headers.update({
                'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
                'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': '*',
                'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': '*',
            })
            return web.Response(body=await resp.read(), status=resp.status, headers=headers)

@web.middleware
async def cors_middleware(request, handler):
    if request.headers.get('Upgrade', '').lower() == 'websocket':
        return await handler(request)
    response = await handler(request)
    response.headers['Access-Control-Allow-Origin'] = '*'
    return response

async def handle_request(request):
    if request.headers.get('Upgrade', '').lower() == 'websocket':
        return await websocket_proxy(request)
    else:
        return await http_proxy(request)

def start_agent_server():
    subprocess.run(['/usr/local/bin/openhands-agent-server', '--port', '18000'])

async def main():
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    loop.run_in_executor(None, start_agent_server)
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    
    app = web.Application(middlewares=[cors_middleware])
    app.router.add_route('*', '/{tail:.*}', handle_request)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, '0.0.0.0', 8000)
    await site.start()
    
    print("CORS proxy running on port 8000 -> 18000")
    await asyncio.Event().wait()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())
```

**Dockerfile**:
```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:97652be-python

USER root
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir aiohttp
COPY agent-server-cors-wrapper.py /usr/local/bin/cors-wrapper.py
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cors-wrapper.py

USER openhands
ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/usr/local/bin/cors-wrapper.py"]
```

**Configuration**:
- Set `SANDBOX_AGENT_SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:cors-enabled` in docker-compose
- Proxy only port 8000 (main API), let other services (VSCode on 8001, etc.) run directly

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Add CORS Support to Agent-Server Binary (Preferred)
Add a `--cors-origin` flag to the Rust agent-server binary:
```bash
openhands-agent-server --port 8000 --cors-origin="*"
```
Or allow comma-separated origins:
```bash
openhands-agent-server --cors-origin="http://192.168.1.171:3000,http://localhost:3000"
```

### Option 2: Auto-Enable CORS for Remote Setups
Detect when `SANDBOX_LOCAL_RUNTIME_URL` or `DOCKER_HOST_ADDR` is set and automatically enable CORS.

### Option 3: Official CORS Proxy Container
Provide an official sidecar container that wraps the agent-server with CORS support.

### Option 4: Update Documentation
Document the CORS issue and provide the workaround in the remote setup guide.

## Related Issues

- #12072 - Remote setup issues in v1.0
- #12081 - V0/V1 runtime architecture changes

## Testing

After implementing CORS support:
1. Deploy OpenHands remotely (server != browser machine)
2. Start a conversation
3. Try uploading a file via the web UI
4. Verify no CORS errors in browser console
5. Verify file is successfully uploaded and accessible to the agent

## Additional Context

This issue affects the v1.0 architecture specifically because:
- V1.0 uses compiled Rust `agent-server` binary (not editable Python runtime)
- Can't modify response headers in the binary
- V0.x used Python runtime which could be patched

The workaround works but requires:
- Custom Docker image build
- Additional Python dependencies (aiohttp)
- Maintenance overhead for users

A proper fix in the agent-server binary would benefit all remote deployment users.

title: Replace loading spinner with skeleton cards in conversation panel
body:
## Problem

The [conversation panel](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation-panel/conversation-panel.tsx) currently displays a loading spinner while fetching conversations. This creates a jarring user experience because the spinner doesn't reflect the actual layout of the content that will appear, making the transition from loading to loaded state feel abrupt.

## Expected Behavior

The conversation panel should display skeleton cards that match the exact layout of [`ConversationCard`](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation-panel/conversation-card/conversation-card.tsx) components during the loading state. This provides users with a visual preview of the content structure and creates a smoother perceived loading experience.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `ConversationCardSkeleton` component is created that mirrors the structure of `ConversationCard`.
- The skeleton includes placeholder elements for the status indicator, version badge, title, repository link, and timestamp.
- The skeleton uses the existing `.skeleton` and `.skeleton-round` CSS classes defined in [tailwind.css](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/tailwind.css).
- The `ConversationPanel` component renders multiple skeleton cards instead of a `LoadingSpinner` during initial data fetch.
- The number of skeleton cards displayed should provide adequate visual feedback without excessive rendering.
- The skeleton cards maintain the same dimensions and spacing as actual conversation cards to prevent layout shift.

## Relevant Files
