title: Add loading feedback to git changes refresh button
body:
## Problem

When clicking the refresh button in the Changes tab, there is no visual feedback indicating that the git changes API is being called. Users have no way to know if their click was registered or if data is being fetched, which can lead to confusion and repeated clicks.

## Expected Behavior

The refresh button should provide clear visual feedback when a refresh is in progress. The button should appear in a loading state and prevent additional clicks until the current fetch completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refresh icon should spin while the git changes API request is in progress.
- The button should be disabled during loading to prevent multiple simultaneous requests.
- The button should have a visually distinct appearance when disabled, such as reduced opacity.
- Consider using `isFetching` from TanStack Query rather than `isLoading`, since `isLoading` only applies to the initial load while `isFetching` covers refetch scenarios. (see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75401477/reasons-for-using-isloading-or-isfetching-in-react-query)

## Relevant Files

- [frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tab-title.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tab-title.tsx) contains the refresh button component that needs the loading state.
- [frontend/src/hooks/query/use-unified-get-git-changes.ts](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/hooks/query/use-unified-get-git-changes.ts) contains the hook that fetches git changes and will need to expose isFetching.

title: Replace chat loading spinner with skeleton messages
body: ## Problem When returning to an existing conversation, the current loading state displays a `LoadingSpinner` inside the scroll container while the `ChatSuggestions` component remains visible behind it. This creates an awkward visual overlap where users see both the "Build it with AI" suggestions and a loading spinner simultaneously. The `ChatSuggestions` component uses absolute positioning and only hides when `userEventsExist` becomes true, but during the loading phase this condition is `false` because events haven't loaded yet. ## Expected Behavior When loading an existing conversation, the UI should display skeleton placeholder messages that mimic the actual message structure. These skeletons should replace both the loading spinner and the chat suggestions, providing a near-seamless loading experience that accurately represents the content that will appear. ## Acceptance Criteria > [!IMPORTANT] > The PR implementing this change should include sufficient test coverage. A test-driven development approach is preferred. - The loading spinner in the chat interface should be replaced with skeleton message components when loading existing conversations. - The chat suggestions component should be hidden when skeleton loading states are displayed. - Skeleton components should visually match the structure of actual messages, including user messages, assistant messages, and event cards. - The skeleton loading state should only appear when returning to existing conversations, not for new conversations. - Tests should be added for the new skeleton components to verify correct rendering and visibility conditions. ## Relevant Files ### Current loading implementation - [chat-interface.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/chat-interface.tsx) contain the current `LoadingSpinner` implementation. - [chat-suggestions.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/chat-suggestions.tsx) is the component that overlaps with the loading spinner. ### Message components to create skeletons for > [!NOTE] > We do not need individual skeleton components for every message type. Instead, we should create a single composite `ChatMessagesSkeleton` component that renders a realistic-looking mix of placeholder elements, for example one user message skeleton followed by one assistant message skeleton followed by two or three event card skeletons. - [chat-message.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/chat-message.tsx) defines the user and assistant message structure. - [generic-event-message.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/generic-event-message.tsx) defines the event card structure with left border. - [error-message.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/chat/error-message.tsx) defines the error event structure. ### Existing skeleton patterns for reference - [tailwind.css](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/tailwind.css), lines 31-37 define the `.skeleton` and `.skeleton-round` CSS classes. - [recent-conversations-skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/home/recent-conversations/recent-conversations-skeleton.tsx) is an example of a list skeleton component. - [task-suggestions-skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/home/tasks/task-suggestions-skeleton.tsx) is an example of a card skeleton component.

title: Agent-server containers cannot resolve host.docker.internal in Docker runtime deployment
body:
## Problem

When deploying OpenHands 1.1 as a LAN-accessible server using Docker runtime, agent-server containers fail to start because they cannot resolve `host.docker.internal`, causing conversations to remain stuck at `WAITING_FOR_SANDBOX`.

## Environment

- **OpenHands Version**: 1.1
- **Deployment**: Docker Compose on Ubuntu 22.04
- **Runtime**: Docker
- **Network**: LAN deployment (accessing from remote machines)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy OpenHands 1.1 with Docker runtime:
   ```yaml
   services:
     openhands:
       image: docker.openhands.dev/openhands/openhands:1.1
       ports:
         - "3000:3000"
       volumes:
         - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
       extra_hosts:
         - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
   ```

2. Start a conversation via UI or API
3. Observe agent-server containers fail with DNS errors

## Error Logs

```
openhands.app_server.sandbox.docker_sandbox_service:INFO: docker_sandbox_service.py:202 - 
Sandbox server not running: http://host.docker.internal:50555 : [Errno -2] Name or service not known
```

Agent-server logs show:
```
httpx.ConnectError: [Errno -2] Name or service not known
RuntimeError: Client failed to connect: [Errno -2] Name or service not known
  at fastmcp/client/client.py:419 in _connect
  at openhands/sdk/mcp/utils.py:39 in _list_tools
```

## Root Cause

In `openhands/app_server/sandbox/docker_sandbox_service.py` (line ~363), when creating agent-server containers, the `extra_hosts` parameter is not passed to `docker_client.containers.run()`:

```python
container = self.docker_client.containers.run(
    image=sandbox_spec.id,
    command=sandbox_spec.command,
    name=container_name,
    environment=env_vars,
    ports=port_mappings,
    volumes=volumes,
    # ❌ MISSING: extra_hosts parameter
    detach=True,
    init=True,
)
```

This means:
- ✅ Main `openhands-app` container can resolve `host.docker.internal` (via docker-compose `extra_hosts`)
- ❌ Dynamically-created `oh-agent-server-*` containers **cannot** resolve it
- ❌ MCP client in agent-server tries to connect to `http://host.docker.internal:3000/mcp/mcp` and fails

## Attempted Workarounds

- ❌ `SANDBOX_RUNTIME_EXTRA_HOSTS` - Only applies to runtime containers, not agent-servers
- ❌ Custom Docker networks - Agent-servers still created on default bridge
- ❌ `network_mode: host` - Breaks health checks and port mapping
- ❌ Docker daemon configuration - Conflicts with existing setup

## Proposed Solution

### Option 1: Add environment variable support (Recommended)

Add a new environment variable `AGENT_SERVER_EXTRA_HOSTS` that allows users to configure extra hosts for agent-server containers:

```python
# In docker_sandbox_service.py
extra_hosts_config = os.environ.get('AGENT_SERVER_EXTRA_HOSTS', '')
extra_hosts = {}
if extra_hosts_config:
    # Format: "hostname1:ip1,hostname2:ip2"
    for entry in extra_hosts_config.split(','):
        if ':' in entry:
            hostname, ip = entry.split(':', 1)
            extra_hosts[hostname.strip()] = ip.strip()

container = self.docker_client.containers.run(
    ...
    extra_hosts=extra_hosts if extra_hosts else None,
    ...
)
```

Usage:
```yaml
environment:
  - AGENT_SERVER_EXTRA_HOSTS=host.docker.internal:host-gateway
```

### Option 2: Inherit from parent config

Add `extra_hosts` to `DockerSandboxServiceInjector` configuration and pass it through to agent-server containers.

## Impact

This bug **blocks LAN deployment** of OpenHands as a team server. Users cannot:
- Deploy OpenHands on a local server for team access
- Access OpenHands UI from remote machines on the same network
- Use Docker runtime in multi-user scenarios

## Workaround

Currently requires patching the OpenHands source code manually, which is difficult to maintain across updates.

## Additional Context

- Docker version: 29.1.3
- Tested on clean Ubuntu 22.04 installation
- Issue does not occur when accessing from localhost (127.0.0.1)
- Only affects remote LAN access where browser and server are different machines

title: [Bug]: GitHub token export fails when bash session is busy (race condition)
body:
## Summary

The runtime fails to export refreshed GitHub tokens when the bash session is busy executing another command. This causes a `RuntimeError: Failed to add env vars [dict_keys(['GITHUB_TOKEN'])] to environment` error.

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Problem

When `_export_latest_git_provider_tokens()` attempts to refresh the GitHub token while the bash session is occupied with a long-running command:

1. Token refresh triggers `add_env_vars()` which creates a `CmdRunAction('export GITHUB_TOKEN=...')`
2. The bash session is busy → no PS1 prompt is visible (0 PS1 metadata blocks detected)
3. After 10 seconds (`NO_CHANGE_TIMEOUT`), `_handle_nochange_timeout_command()` returns `CmdOutputMetadata()` with `exit_code=-1`
4. `add_env_vars()` checks `obs.exit_code != 0` and raises `RuntimeError`

### Code Path

- **base.py:311-315**: `add_env_vars()` creates `CmdRunAction(cmd)` without special timeout handling
- **bash.py:385-400**: `_handle_nochange_timeout_command()` sets `metadata = CmdOutputMetadata()` (default exit_code=-1)
- **action_execution_server.py:274-275,283-284**: `NO_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 10 seconds

### Evidence from Production Logs

Multiple production runtimes show the exact same pattern:

**Runtime 8263dbca**:
- `16:12:42.071` - Token fetched
- `16:12:52.246` - PS1 warning: "Expected exactly one PS1 metadata block BEFORE the execution of a command, but got 0 PS1 metadata blocks"
- `16:12:52.248` - Error raised

**Runtime c394f209**:
- `00:48:16.121` - Token fetched  
- `00:48:26.684` - Error (exact 10s NO_CHANGE_TIMEOUT gap)

All failures show "0 PS1 metadata blocks" indicating the bash session was occupied when the export command was attempted.

## Proposed Fixes

1. **Use `/env` endpoint instead of `CmdRunAction`**: The action execution server has an `/env` endpoint that can set environment variables without using the bash session. This would avoid the race condition entirely.

2. **Add retry logic with backoff**: In `add_env_vars()`, detect the timeout condition and retry after a delay when the bash session becomes available.

3. **Use a separate bash session for env var export**: Create a dedicated bash session for system operations that won't conflict with user commands.

4. **Queue token refresh**: Only attempt token refresh when the bash session is confirmed idle (e.g., check for PS1 prompt availability before executing).

## Affected Code

- `openhands/runtime/base.py` - `add_env_vars()` and `_export_latest_git_provider_tokens()`
- `openhands/runtime/action_execution_server.py` - `NO_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
- `openhands/runtime/impl/action_execution/bash.py` - `_handle_nochange_timeout_command()`

## Labels

bug, runtime

title: [Bug]: `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS=true` does not prevent "AI Provider Configuration" modal from appearing
body:
## Description

When deploying OpenHands with `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS=true` environment variable, the "AI Provider Configuration" modal still appears for users who haven't saved their settings yet.

## Current Behavior

1. Server is configured with `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS=true` in environment variables
2. `/api/options/config` correctly returns `FEATURE_FLAGS.HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS: true`
3. For a new user (or user without saved settings), `/api/settings` returns 404
4. The Sidebar component shows the "AI Provider Configuration" modal despite the feature flag

## Expected Behavior

When `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS=true`, the settings modal should NOT appear, regardless of whether the user has saved settings. The server-side LLM configuration should be used automatically.

## Root Cause

In `frontend/src/components/features/sidebar/sidebar.tsx` (around lines 46-49), the modal display logic does not check the `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS` flag:

```javascript
} else if (config?.APP_MODE === "oss" && settingsError?.status === 404) {
  setSettingsModalIsOpen(true);
}
```

## Suggested Fix

Add a check for `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS` before showing the modal:

```javascript
} else if (
  config?.APP_MODE === "oss" && 
  settingsError?.status === 404 && 
  !config?.FEATURE_FLAGS?.HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS
) {
  setSettingsModalIsOpen(true);
}
```

## Environment

- OpenHands version: 0.41 (Docker image)
- Deployment: Docker Compose with AWS Bedrock backend (server-side LLM configuration)
- `HIDE_LLM_SETTINGS=true` set in docker-compose environment

## Workaround

Manually POST to `/api/settings` to save default settings, which prevents the 404 and thus the modal. However, this workaround must be applied per-user.

## Use Case

This issue affects deployments where administrators want to:
- Pre-configure LLM settings server-side (e.g., using AWS Bedrock with IAM roles)
- Prevent users from seeing or modifying LLM configuration
- Provide a seamless experience without requiring users to configure anything

title: Extend frontend permission guards
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Make sure you’ve read the description on the parent issue before working on this ticket: https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12136

## Problem

The [`ALL-2596/org-support`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/tree/ALL-2596/org-support/frontend) branch has a permission system defined in [`permissions.ts`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ALL-2596/org-support/frontend/src/utils/org/permissions.ts) with three roles (owner, admin, member), but it is only enforced in two routes: Organization settings and Organization Members. All other settings routes (Secrets, MCP, LLM, Billing, etc.) have no role-based access control, allowing any authenticated user to access and modify settings regardless of their role.

## Expected Behavior

The permission matrix defines the following access controls:

| Feature | Member | Admin | Owner | Permission key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Settings > Secrets | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `manage_secrets` |
| Settings > MCP | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `manage_mcp` |
| Settings > Integrations | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `manage_integrations` |
| Settings > Application | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `manage_application_settings` |
| Settings > API Keys | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `manage_api_keys` |
| Settings > LLM | 👁️ View | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `view_llm_settings`, `edit_llm_settings` |
| Settings > Billing | ❌ None | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `view_billing` |
| Invite members | ❌ None | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `invite_user_to_organization` |
| Assign member/admin roles | ❌ None | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `change_user_role:member`, `change_user_role:admin` |
| Change org name | ❌ None | ❌ None | ✅ Full | `change_organization_name` |
| Delete organization | ❌ None | ❌ None | ✅ Full | `delete_organization` |
| Assign owner role | ❌ None | ❌ None | ✅ Full | `change_user_role:owner` |
| Add credits | ❌ None | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | `add_credits` |



## Current Behavior

- LLM settings allow all roles to edit (should be view-only for members).
- Billing route has no role check and is accessible to members.
- Navigation items are shown to all users regardless of permissions, causing redirects after clicking.
- Settings routes for Secrets, MCP, Application, Integrations, and API Keys have no permission guards at all, even though they currently allow all roles.

## Acceptance Criteria

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This work should follow TDD. Write failing tests first for each permission scenario (member accessing billing, member editing LLM settings, etc.), then implement the guards to make them pass. The existing tests in manage-organization-members.test.tsx demonstrate the pattern of mocking useMe with different roles and asserting on UI visibility.

- **All new permission logic has corresponding unit tests covering each role's access to each feature.**
- The permission types in `permissions.ts` are extended to cover all settings features (e.g., `manage_secrets`, `manage_mcp`, `view_llm_settings`, `edit_llm_settings`, `view_billing`).
- Each role's permission array is updated to match the matrix, with members receiving view-only LLM access and no billing access.
- All settings routes check the user's role against `rolePermissions` before rendering.
- The LLM settings page disables the save button and form inputs for members.
- The billing route redirects members to an accessible page.
- The navigation hook filters out menu items the user does not have permission to access.
- **BONUS (but not required for this issue)**: A reusable `usePermission` hook is created for consistent permission checking across components.
- Existing tests in `manage-organization-members.test.tsx` and `manage-org.test.tsx` continue to pass.

## Relevant Files

[frontend/src/utils/org/permissions.ts](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/ALL-2596/org-support/frontend/src/utils/org/permissions.ts) defines the permission types and role mappings.

title: Add message queue support for V1 conversations during WebSocket connection
body:
## Problem V1 conversations do not queue user messages when the WebSocket connection is not yet established. A user is unable to submit a message before the WebSocket is fully connected (e.g., during runtime startup), instead of being queued and sent automatically once the connection is ready. ## Background PR [#11687]() added message queuing support for V0 conversations in the [Socket.IO]() WebSocket provider. However, this functionality was never implemented for V1 conversations which use a native WebSocket via `ConversationWebSocketProvider`. ## Current Behavior The chat input is disabled when the WebSocket is not connected ## Expected Behavior Messages submitted before the WebSocket connection is established should be queued and automatically sent once the connection is ready, matching the V0 behavior. ## Acceptance Criteria > \[!IMPORTANT\]
The PR implementing this change should include sufficient test coverage. A test-driven development approach is preferred. * The V1 WebSocket provider should maintain a queue of pending messages when the connection is not yet open. * Queued messages should be automatically flushed in order when the WebSocket connection opens. * The pending message queue should be cleared when the conversation changes or is intentionally stopped. * Unit tests should be added to verify the message queuing and flushing behavior. ## Relevant Files [frontend/src/contexts/conversation-websocket-context.tsx lines 722-741]() contains the V1 `sendMessage` function that might be relevant for queuing support.
[frontend/src/context/ws-client-provider.tsx]() contains the V0 implementation with `pendingEventsRef` and `flushPendingEvents` that might serve as a reference. Feel free to implement a different strategy if you feel it would be better.
[frontend/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts]() is the unified hook that routes messages to V0 or V1 providers.
[frontend/**tests**/conversation-websocket-handler.test.tsx]() should be extended with tests for the new queuing behavior.

title: Tab pin/unpin functionality not working in conversation panel dropdown
body: ## Summary The ellipsis dropdown menu in the conversation panel allows users to pin/unpin tabs (Changes, Code, Terminal, App, Browser), but the functionality is broken. Clicking pin/unpin in the dropdown menu has no visible effect on which tabs are displayed. ## Current Behavior There is a `localStorage` key mismatch between the two components that manage tab visibility: - Clicking the ellipsis button opens the dropdown menu correctly. - Clicking pin/unpin on any tab in the dropdown menu has no visible effect. - The tab bar remains unchanged regardless of pin/unpin actions. ### Possible cause The context menu component writes to a hardcoded global localStorage key, while the tabs component reads from a conversation-specific `localStorage` key that includes the `conversationId`. ## Expected Behavior - When a user clicks the ellipsis menu and unpins a tab, that tab should immediately disappear from the visible tabs. - When a user pins a previously unpinned tab, it should reappear in the tab bar. - Pin/unpin preferences should persist correctly per conversation. ## Acceptance Criteria - The context menu and tabs component should use the same `localStorage` key for tracking unpinned tabs. - Pin/unpin actions in the dropdown should immediately reflect in the visible tabs. - Tab visibility preferences should persist across page refreshes. - Unit tests should be added to verify that both components read and write to the same `localStorage` key. - Integration tests should cover the full pin/unpin workflow to prevent regression. ## Relevant Files [conversation-tabs.tsx (lines 48-51)](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tabs.tsx#L48-L51) [conversation-tabs-context-menu.tsx (lines 28-31)](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tabs-context-menu.tsx#L28-L31)

title: Fix localStorage leak: conversation tab preferences are never cleaned up
body:
## Problem

The frontend stores per-conversation tab preferences in localStorage using conversation-specific keys, but these entries are never removed when conversations are deleted. Over time, this causes unbounded growth of localStorage entries, potentially accumulating hundreds of orphaned entries for active users. Each conversation creates 3 localStorage entries:

- `conversation-selected-tab-${conversationId}`
- `conversation-right-panel-shown-${conversationId}`
- `conversation-unpinned-tabs-${conversationId}`

## Current Behavior

- User opens a conversation → 3 localStorage entries are created
- User deletes the conversation → localStorage entries remain
- Repeat over weeks/months → localStorage accumulates 100s of orphaned entries
- The deletion flow in `useDeleteConversation` only updates TanStack Query cache and calls the backend API. It never cleans up the associated `localStorage` entries.

## Expected Behavior

When a conversation is deleted, the corresponding `localStorage` entries should be removed. Additionally, a one-time migration should clean up existing orphaned entries for users who already have accumulated stale data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a conversation is deleted via `useDeleteConversation`, the 3 associated `localStorage` keys should be removed
- A migration utility should clean up orphaned `localStorage` entries (keys where the conversation no longer exists)
- The cleanup should handle edge cases (conversation ID not found, `localStorage` errors)
- No regressions in tab persistence for active conversations

## Relevant Files

[conversation-tabs.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tabs.tsx#L36-L51) - Creates the localStorage entries (lines 36-51)
[use-delete-conversation.ts](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/hooks/mutation/use-delete-conversation.ts) - Needs cleanup logic added to onSuccess or onSettled
[conversation-tabs-context-menu.tsx](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/main/frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tabs-context-menu.tsx) - Also uses the unpinned tabs key

> [!NOTE]
> Consider creating a utility function (e.g., `clearConversationLocalStorage(conversationId)`) that can be reused and ensures all conversation-related keys are cleaned up in one place.

> [!TIP]
> For the migration cleanup, you could compare `localStorage` keys matching the `conversation-*-${id}` pattern against the user's actual conversation list from the API.

title: feat(app_server): Support starting conversations with remote plugins
body:
## Summary

Extend the app-conversations API to accept a plugin specification and pass it to the agent server, which will fetch/load the plugin and start a conversation with the plugin's skills, hooks, and MCP configuration.

## Context

This is part of the Plugin Directory feature ([#12088](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12088)), more specifically a [REST API (issue #12087)](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/12087) that allows one to start conversations with a particular plugin. When a user clicks "Launch" in the Plugin Directory and fills out the parameter form, the frontend calls this API to start the conversation with the selected plugin.

### Architecture Note

Plugin fetching and loading happens **in the agent server** (which runs inside the sandbox), not in the app server. This is because:
- Plugins may contain scripts or hooks that need to execute in the sandbox
- Plugin MCP servers need to run inside the sandbox  
- Skills may reference files that need to exist in the sandbox filesystem

The app server's role is to accept the plugin specification from the frontend and pass it through to the agent server via `StartConversationRequest`.

**Dependencies:**
- [software-agent-sdk#1645](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/1645) - SDK `Plugin.fetch()`
- [software-agent-sdk#1650](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/1650) - Agent Server plugin loading support

## Proposed Implementation

### 1. Extend Request Model

In `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_models.py`:

```python
class PluginSpec(BaseModel):
    """Specification for loading a plugin into a conversation."""
    
    source: str = Field(
        description="Plugin source: 'github:owner/repo', git URL, or local path"
    )
    ref: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Optional branch, tag, or commit"
    )
    parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="User-provided values for plugin input parameters"
    )


class AppConversationStartRequest(OpenHandsModel):
    # ... existing fields ...
    
    plugin: PluginSpec | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Optional plugin to load for this conversation"
    )
```

### 2. Pass Plugin Spec to Agent Server

In `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py`:

When building `StartConversationRequest`, pass the plugin source to the agent server:

```python
async def _build_start_conversation_request_for_user(
    self,
    # ... existing params ...
    plugin_spec: PluginSpec | None = None,
) -> StartConversationRequest:
    # ... existing code ...
    
    return StartConversationRequest(
        conversation_id=conversation_id,
        agent=agent,
        workspace=workspace,
        # ... existing fields ...
        
        # NEW: Pass plugin source to agent server
        plugin_source=plugin_spec.source if plugin_spec else None,
        plugin_ref=plugin_spec.ref if plugin_spec else None,
    )
```

### 3. Handle Plugin Parameters → Initial Prompt

Plugin parameters from the user should be incorporated into the initial message:

```python
def _construct_initial_message_with_plugin_params(
    initial_message: SendMessageRequest | None,
    plugin_spec: PluginSpec | None,
) -> SendMessageRequest | None:
    """Incorporate plugin parameters into initial message if specified."""
    if not plugin_spec or not plugin_spec.parameters:
        return initial_message
    
    # Format parameters as part of the initial prompt
    params_text = "\n".join(
        f"- {key}: {value}" 
        for key, value in plugin_spec.parameters.items()
    )
    
    # Prepend or append to existing message
    # ...
```

## Files to Modify

- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_models.py` - Add `PluginSpec` to `AppConversationStartRequest`
- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py` - Pass plugin source to agent server
- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_router.py` - Accept plugin in API endpoint

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `POST /app-conversations` accepts `plugin` field with source, ref, and parameters
- [ ] Plugin source and ref are passed to agent server in `StartConversationRequest`
- [ ] Plugin parameters are incorporated into the initial conversation message
- [ ] Errors from agent server (plugin fetch failures) are propagated appropriately
- [ ] Works with existing conversation start flow (plugin is optional)

## Related Issues

- #12085 - [PRD] OpenHands Plugins
- #12088 - Plugin Marketplace GUI  
- #12322 - Frontend: Plugin Launch Dialog
- [software-agent-sdk#1645](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/1645) - SDK `Plugin.fetch()`
- [software-agent-sdk#1650](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/1650) - Agent Server plugin loading

title: [Bug]: --mount-cwd flag does not mount directory in agent-server container
body:
### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

When using `openhands serve --mount-cwd`, the current working directory is not mounted into the agent-server container. The CLI correctly sets the `SANDBOX_VOLUMES` environment variable, but the new agent-server architecture does not read this variable when creating Docker containers.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Navigate to a directory with files: `cd /path/to/my/project`
2. Run: `openhands serve --mount-cwd`
3. Start a new conversation in the UI
4. Ask the agent to list files in the current directory
5. The agent will not see the files from your local directory

**Expected behavior:**
The files from the current working directory should be visible at `/workspace` inside the agent-server container.

**Actual behavior:**
The `/workspace` directory in the agent-server container is empty or contains default files, not the mounted directory.

### Root Cause

The migration from the old runtime architecture (V0) to the new agent-server architecture (V1) did not include handling for the `SANDBOX_VOLUMES` environment variable.

In `openhands/app_server/config.py`, the `config_from_env()` function creates a `DockerSandboxServiceInjector` but does not parse `SANDBOX_VOLUMES` to create `VolumeMount` objects.

The CLI sets:
```
-e SANDBOX_VOLUMES=/your/cwd:/workspace:rw
```

But this is never read by the app server when creating agent-server containers.

### OpenHands Installation

CLI (`openhands serve`)

### OpenHands Version

latest

### Operating System

Linux

### Logs, Errors, Screenshots, and Additional Context

You can verify the issue by:
1. Running `docker exec openhands-app env | grep SANDBOX` - shows `SANDBOX_VOLUMES` is set
2. Running `docker inspect <agent-server-container> | grep -A 20 Mounts` - shows no mount for the user's directory

title: [Bug] V1 Conversation fails to restore due to secret serialization/deserialization mismatch
body:
## Bug Description

V1 conversations fail to restore from persistence with a Pydantic validation error when the conversation state contains secrets in the `secret_registry`. The error occurs because secrets are serialized as redacted values (`**********`) but the `StaticSecret` model requires a non-null `value` field.

## Error Message

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 6 validation errors for ConversationState
secret_registry.secret_sources.LLM_API_KEY.value
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'description': 'This is ...oxy.app.all-hands.dev/'}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.12/v/missing
secret_registry.secret_sources.DD_API_KEY.value
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'description': 'Datadog API Key'}, input_type=dict]
...
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in the `openhands-sdk` package, specifically in how secrets are serialized and deserialized:

1. **Serialization** (`state.py` line 161-162):
   ```python
   def _save_base_state(self, fs: FileStore) -> None:
       payload = self.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True)
   ```
   This calls `model_dump_json()` without providing a `cipher` or `expose_secrets=True` in the context.

2. **Secret Serialization** (`pydantic_secrets.py` line 6-28):
   ```python
   def serialize_secret(v: SecretStr | None, info):
       if info.context and info.context.get("cipher"):
           return cipher.encrypt(v)
       if info.context and info.context.get("expose_secrets"):
           return v.get_secret_value()
       return v  # Returns SecretStr, which Pydantic serializes as "**********"
   ```

3. **Secret Deserialization** (`pydantic_secrets.py` line 31-64):
   ```python
   def validate_secret(v: str | SecretStr | None, info) -> SecretStr | None:
       if not secret_value or not secret_value.strip() or secret_value == "**********":
           return None  # Redacted secrets become None
   ```

4. **StaticSecret Model** (`secrets.py` line 25-28):
   ```python
   class StaticSecret(SecretSource):
       value: SecretStr  # REQUIRED field, not Optional
   ```

When the conversation is restored, the redacted `"**********"` value is converted to `None`, but `StaticSecret.value` is a required field, causing validation to fail.

## Timeline from Datadog Logs

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 15:57:20 | Conversation `eb4d72fc-37c2-4316-a3e7-90421ba22e0a` created successfully |
| 16:38:07 | Conversation working normally (API calls returning 200) |
| **17:03:58** | **ERROR**: `error_loading_event_service` - Pydantic validation failed |
| 17:04:04+ | All subsequent requests return 404 "Conversation not found" |

## Affected Versions

- `openhands-sdk` 1.7.4 (confirmed)
- `openhands-sdk` 1.8.1 (confirmed - same code)

## Suggested Fix

Option 1: Make `StaticSecret.value` optional with a default of `None`:
```python
class StaticSecret(SecretSource):
    value: SecretStr | None = None
```

Option 2: Always use a cipher when serializing conversation state to preserve secrets.

Option 3: Skip serializing secrets entirely and require them to be re-provided on conversation restore.

## Impact

- Users lose access to V1 conversations after server restarts or reconnections
- The conversation data is still on disk but cannot be loaded
- Error message "Connection lost: Conversation not found" is shown to users

## Related

- Conversation ID: `eb4d72fc-37c2-4316-a3e7-90421ba22e0a`
- URL: https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/eb4d72fc37c24316a3e790421ba22e0a

title: Feature Request: Context Offloading for Large Tool Outputs
body:
## Problem

Large tool outputs are currently truncated (lossy), causing permanent information loss:
- Command outputs > 30KB lose middle content (`_maybe_truncate()` in `commands.py`)
- Browser screenshots/DOM consume massive tokens
- No way to recover full content after truncation

## Proposed Solution

Add context offloading: save full content to filesystem, return preview + reference.

**Key points:**
1. Trigger **before** `_maybe_truncate()` in `CmdOutputObservation.__init__`
2. Save to `.openhands/context_offload/{session_id}/` (configurable)
3. Return head/tail preview with file path
4. Agent retrieves via `cat`/`grep` when needed

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Threshold | 25K chars | Below current 30K truncation limit |
| Browser screenshots | Keep thumbnail in context | LLM vision needs image data |
| Cleanup | Session-end default | Configurable retention for debugging |
| Default state | Disabled (opt-in) | Backward compatible |

## Security & Cleanup

- Offloaded files inherit workspace permissions
- Cleanup triggered on session close; optional `retention_hours` config
- Filesystem write failure falls back to truncation

## Files to Modify

- `openhands/core/config/offload_config.py` (new)
- `openhands/memory/offloader.py` (new)
- `openhands/events/observation/commands.py`
- `openhands/events/observation/browse.py`

## References

- LangChain DeepAgents: [filesystem.py](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/master/libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/filesystem.py)
- Manus: [Context Engineering Blog](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)

title: [Bug]: 500 Internal Server Error with self-hosted Gitea (HTTP) - Sandbox forces HTTPS causing GnuTLS handshake failure
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug? (If one exists, thumbs up or comment on the issue instead).

- [x] I have checked the existing issues.

### Describe the bug and reproduction steps

### Description

I am encountering a persistent `500 Internal Server Error` when trying to start a conversation/task using a repository from a self-hosted Gitea instance (configured via the Forgejo provider).

While the OpenHands UI successfully connects to the Gitea API (listing repositories and branches works perfectly), the **Sandbox Container** fails immediately upon initialization. The logs indicate that the internal Git client inside the sandbox is forcing an **HTTPS** connection for the `git clone` operation, even though the provider is explicitly configured for **HTTP**.

Because the Gitea server is running on plain HTTP, the Sandbox's attempt to initiate a TLS handshake results in a crash, which bubbles up as a 500 error in the API.

### Environment

* **Host OS:** Linux Mint Debian Edition (virtualized in Proxmox)
* **Deployment:** Docker (Standard `docker run` command)
* **OpenHands Version:** 1.1 (Image: `docker.openhands.dev/openhands/openhands:1.1`)
* **Git Provider:** Self-hosted Gitea (accessed via local IP `192.168.178.120:3000`)
* **Provider Setting:** Using "Forgejo" (since Gitea is compatible) - Note: The UI successfully lists all Gitea repositories and allows selection before the crash occurs during project creation.
* **Protocol:** HTTP (No SSL/TLS configured on Gitea)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a self-hosted Gitea instance on HTTP (e.g., `http://192.168.x.x:3000`).
2. Start OpenHands via Docker with `--add-host` to ensure connectivity.
3. In OpenHands UI -> Settings, configure the **Forgejo** provider with the Base URL `http://192.168.x.x:3000` and a valid token.
4. Select a repository from the dropdown (successfully lists repos).
5. Start a new conversation/task.

### Expected Behavior

The Sandbox container should respect the protocol defined in the Git Provider settings (HTTP) and successfully clone the repository via `http://...`.

### Actual Behavior

The UI prepares the task, but the Sandbox container immediately crashes. The `openhands-app` logs show a `500 Internal Server Error` on `/api/conversations`. Deep diving into the logs reveals a `GnuTLS handshake failed` error, indicating an HTTPS request was sent to an HTTP port.

### Logs

**1. The 500 API Error:**

```text
httpx.HTTPStatusError: Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url 'http://host.docker.internal:xxxxx/api/conversations'
...
openhands.app_server.sandbox.docker_sandbox_service:INFO: docker_sandbox_service.py:202 - Sandbox server not running: http://host.docker.internal:xxxxx : Server disconnected without sending a response.

```

**2. The Root Cause (Git Protocol Mismatch):**

```text
openhands.app_server.app_conversation.app_conversation_service_base:WARNING: app_conversation_service_base.py:291 - Git clone failed:
Cloning into 'deepwiki-open-fixxed'...

### Attempted Solutions (All Failed)

We have tried extensive troubleshooting to rule out environment issues:

1. **UI Configuration:** Explicitly set the Forgejo URL to `http://...`. **Result:** Ignored by the Sandbox Git client.
2. **Environment Variables:**
* `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=true`: **Result:** Failed. (The issue is a protocol mismatch/handshake failure, not an invalid certificate, so skipping verification doesn't help).


3. **Config.toml:**
* Mounted a `config.toml` with `[git] force_http = true`.
* **Result:** Failed. The logs show `Unknown section [git] in config.toml`, suggesting this configuration method is deprecated or not working in version 1.1.


4. **Global Git Config Injection:**
* Attempted to run `git config --system url."http://...".insteadOf "https://..."` inside the running container.
* **Result:** Failed to persist or apply to the spawned sandbox environment.



### Analysis

The issue appears to be that the **Sandbox Runtime** does not inherit or respect the `http` protocol defined in the OpenHands provider settings. It defaults to `https` for the `git clone` operation. Since the target server is strictly HTTP, the TLS handshake fails, causing the git process to exit with a fatal error, which in turn causes the Sandbox server to crash, resulting in the generic 500 error in the main application.

title: Repo skills in .openhands/skills without triggers not reliably injected (remote workspace parsing)
body:
### Expected
Markdown skills in `.openhands/skills/` with no `triggers` frontmatter should be treated as repo context (always active) and injected into `<REPO_CONTEXT>`.

### Actual
In OpenHands app-server, repo skills are loaded by reading file contents via `AsyncRemoteWorkspace` (remote agent-server) and then constructing SDK `Skill` objects. The loader was calling an outdated SDK API: `Skill.load(..., file_content=...)`. Current `openhands-sdk` `Skill.load()` reads from local disk and does not accept `file_content`, so repo skills from remote workspaces were not reliably parsed/loaded, and therefore not consistently injected.

### Why this happens
The workspace repo is frequently **remote relative to the app-server**, so the app-server cannot assume local filesystem access to `{working_dir}`. Repo skills must be parsed from remote file content fetched through the workspace API.

### Fix
Parse remote markdown content locally (YAML frontmatter via `python-frontmatter`) and construct SDK `Skill` objects directly, mapping:
- no `triggers` -> `trigger=None`
- `triggers` -> `KeywordTrigger`
- `inputs` -> `TaskTrigger` (ensuring `/{name}` trigger exists, matching SDK behavior)

title: Improve UX for runtime disconnect/timeout message
body:
## Summary

When a user leaves the OpenHands window open for a while and returns, they see a disconnect/timeout message. While this is expected behavior, the current UX could be improved.

## Current Behavior

- The disconnect message appears with what seems like an error-style background (red/scary)
- Users need to manually refresh the page to reconnect

## Suggested Improvements

Several ideas were discussed:

1. **Add a "Resume" button** (preferred solution) - Instead of requiring a page refresh, provide a button that allows users to reconnect/resume their session directly.

2. **Make "refresh the page" a clickable link** - If keeping the current text, at least make it actionable.

3. **Change the visual styling** - Use a less alarming background color (pale yellow or grey) since this is not really an error condition but rather a common, expected state.

4. **Auto-reconnect when page becomes active** - Automatically try to reconnect when the page regains focus. However, this could restart the runtime without explicit user action, which might be wasteful.

## Related Issues

There are similar non-critical "errors" that could benefit from the same UX treatment, such as when the agent sends a multi-line bash command.

## Recommendation

The consensus is that adding a **"Resume" button** would be the best option - it gives users explicit control without requiring a full page refresh.

title: [PRD] Re-thinking Skills Management
body:
Currently, OpenHands GUI offers a 'Microagent Management' interface that does not get the job done. It is sorely behind when you consider all of the recent changes to OpenHands, such as the use of [AGENTS.md](), Agent Skills, and additional jobs to be done. We should re-think what it means to manage Skills via both GUI and CLI. I am sharing some initial use cases that come to mind - open to feedback on 1) which ones are most important, 2) which ones are missing, 3) missing/unclear requirements. **How does this compare to the Marketplace?** * For now, we're referring to this as a "Skills Manager" interface. But really, it we could think of it as a "Personal Context Manager". We could make it a "home" for storing *personal* Skills and [Plugins]() that you may want available at anytime in a GUI or CLI based conversation. * This is different from Marketplace, which is more of an organization-wide or public directory of Plugins that are meant to be distributed. # Use cases ## MVP ### Browse Skills from Personal Repo Users should be able to view Skills stored in their personal repo (e.g., `username/.openhands/skills`). ### Launch Conversation with Skill When users are browsing Skills from their Personal Repo, they should have the option to launch a conversation with that Skill as the initial prompt. ### Save Skill to Personal Repo Users should be able to add a Skill to their personal repo from within a conversation: **Option 1 (recommended): Via a** `/save-skill` Slash command
*Dependency:* [APP-612](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-612/prd-gui-slash-command-menu) * User enters `/save-skill ` into CLI or GUI conversation input * Example: `/save-skill code-review` * OpenHands uses Git to commit that skill to the user's personal repo (e.g., `username/.openhands/skills`). **Option 2: Via 'Show Available Skills' menu** * User navigates to a conversation in the GUI * User selects "Show Available Skills" * User selects a "Save" button next to the Skill name * OpenHands creates a conversation in the background that copies that Skill into their personal repo ## Later ### Enable/disable Skills within a Conversation Users should be able to enable/disable skills that are available within a conversation. * Related: [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/13034]() ### Repo Context Management (e.g., [AGENTS.md]()) * Offer to automatically create an [AGENTS.md]() if repo does not have an [AGENTS.md]() (or `.openhands/skills/repo.md`) * Related: [https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-Cloud/issues/206]() * Automatically updating an [AGENTS.md]() with new context on-demand ### Using Skills during a Conversation * **Using Trigger-based Skills and Commands:** Make trigger-based Skills, as well as any slash commands defined in a `commands/` directory, via the conversation input textarea * Related: [https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/issues/343]() ### Importing Skills * Ability to import a one-off Skill and store it in your OpenHands Cloud account ### Creating Skills * First-class "Skill Builder" workflow for creating new skills * Related: [https://github.com/OpenHands/skills/tree/main/skills/skill-creator]() * Publishing Skills as Plugins ### Syncing Skills between CLI<>Cloud * Ability to download Skills stored in your OpenHands Cloud account (dependency: Importing Skills)

title: UI should display the LLM model used for each conversation
body:
Summary
There’s currently no clear way in the UI to tell which LLM a particular conversation is using. While we display the selected model in the general model selector, it isn’t shown per-conversation. This makes it harder to audit, reproduce, and debug results—especially as we work toward model switching on the fly. Motivation * Reproducibility: Users and developers need to know which model generated a conversation’s outputs. * Debugging/Support: Easier to trace differences when multiple models are used across conversations. * Future-proofing: Prepares the UI for per-conversation model switching without reworking the same component later. Proposed UX * Conversation list: Show a small model badge or subtitle for each conversation item (provider/model). * Chat header: Display the current model for the active conversation. When model switching ships, this can become a dropdown. * Conversation stream (future): If the model changes mid-conversation, insert a lightweight “Model changed to …” system entry. * Tooltip: Show full provider+model identifier on hover. Technical Notes * Frontend * Add model info to conversation metadata types (e.g., frontend/src/types and any related hooks in frontend/src/hooks/query). * Render in ConversationListItem and chat header components. * Add i18n strings where appropriate. * Backend * Ensure conversation objects include the selected model (and provider) on creation and retrieval. * Persist on the conversation, and optionally support an event marker for mid-stream changes later. * Enterprise: consider persistence/migrations if needed. Acceptance Criteria * The model used by each conversation is visible in the conversation list and in the active chat header. * Model info persists across reloads and is accurate to that conversation. * Prepares for future “switch model on the fly” without major UI refactor. * Lint/build/tests pass. Related * Conceptual alignment: [https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/781]() * WIP: “switching model on the fly” PR mentioned internally

title: [Feature] Support kubeconfig file for Kubernetes runtime
body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

  Currently, the Kubernetes runtime only supports in-cluster configuration via config.load_incluster_config() (see openhands/runtime/impl/kubernetes/kubernetes_runtime.py:330). This means OpenHands must be running inside a Kubernetes cluster (or via mirrord) to use the Kubernetes runtime.

  This limitation prevents several important use cases:

  1. Local Development: Developers working on their laptops who want to test against a remote Kubernetes cluster (e.g., GKE, EKS, AKS) cannot use the Kubernetes runtime without setting up mirrord.
  2. CI/CD Pipelines: Running OpenHands in CI/CD environments (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, etc.) that need to deploy runtime pods to a remote Kubernetes cluster is not possible.
  3. Remote Management: Users who want to run the OpenHands Web UI on their local machine or a VM while having the runtime execute on a separate Kubernetes cluster cannot do so.
  4. Multi-cluster Management: Organizations managing multiple Kubernetes clusters cannot easily switch between clusters without redeploying OpenHands.

**Describe the UX or technical implementation you have in mind**

  Add support for loading Kubernetes configuration from a kubeconfig file, similar to how kubectl works.

  Configuration Changes:

  Add a new optional field to KubernetesConfig in openhands/core/config/kubernetes_config.py:

```
  kubeconfig_path: str | None = Field(
      default=None,
      description='Path to kubeconfig file. If not specified, uses in-cluster config.'
  )
```

  Example config.toml:

```
  [core]
  runtime = "kubernetes"

  [kubernetes]
  namespace = "openhands"
  ingress_domain = "openhands.example.com"
  # New option: path to kubeconfig file
  kubeconfig_path = "~/.kube/config"
  # Or use environment variable
  # kubeconfig_path = "${KUBECONFIG}"
```

  Implementation Changes:

  Update _init_kubernetes_client() in openhands/runtime/impl/kubernetes/kubernetes_runtime.py:

```
  @staticmethod
  @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
  def _init_kubernetes_client(kubeconfig_path: str | None = None) -> tuple[client.CoreV1Api, client.NetworkingV1Api]:
      """Initialize the Kubernetes client."""
      try:
          if kubeconfig_path:
              # Load from kubeconfig file
              config.load_kube_config(config_file=kubeconfig_path)
          else:
              # Fall back to in-cluster config
              config.load_incluster_config()
          return client.CoreV1Api(), client.NetworkingV1Api()
      except Exception as ex:
          logger.error(
              'Failed to initialize Kubernetes client. Make sure you have a valid '
              'kubeconfig file or are running in a Kubernetes cluster.'
          )
          raise ex
```

  Behavior:

  1. If kubeconfig_path is specified, use config.load_kube_config(config_file=kubeconfig_path)
  2. If not specified, fall back to current behavior: config.load_incluster_config()
  3. Support environment variable expansion (e.g., ${KUBECONFIG}, ${HOME}/.kube/config)

  This maintains backward compatibility while enabling new use cases.

**Additional context**

  - The Python Kubernetes client already supports both load_incluster_config() and load_kube_config(), so the implementation is straightforward.
  - This feature would align OpenHands with standard Kubernetes tooling practices (kubectl, helm, etc. all support kubeconfig files).
  - Related to the original Kubernetes runtime implementation in PR #8814

  ---

title: Changes tab refresh button doesn't update the displayed changes
body:
## Bug Description

The refresh button on the Changes tab doesn't appear to update the displayed git changes when clicked. The button exists and is clickable, but the UI doesn't reflect any updates even when files have been modified in the repository.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open OpenHands with a git repository
2. Navigate to the Changes tab
3. Make some changes to files in the repository (e.g., modify a file or add a new file)
4. Click the refresh button in the Changes tab header
5. Observe that the changes list doesn't update to show the new modifications

## Expected Behavior

When clicking the refresh button, the Changes tab should:
- Fetch the latest git changes from the repository
- Update the displayed list of changed files
- Show newly modified files
- Remove files that are no longer changed
- Update the status of existing files if their change type has changed

## Actual Behavior

The refresh button is clicked but the displayed changes don't update. The list remains static even when new changes have been made to the repository.

## Root Cause Analysis

After investigating the code, the issue appears to be in the `useUnifiedGetGitChanges` hook (`frontend/src/hooks/query/use-unified-get-git-changes.ts`):

1. **Data reference comparison**: The hook uses a `previousDataRef` to check if data has changed (line 72):
   ```typescript
   if (currentData !== previousDataRef.current) {
   ```
   If TanStack Query returns the same object reference (due to caching), this condition fails and the UI doesn't update.

2. **Ordering preservation logic**: The hook maintains a custom ordering of changes that only adds NEW items to the top (lines 76-91). This means:
   - If a file is modified (not a new file), it won't move to the top
   - The ordering might not be reset even after a refetch
   - Changes to existing files might not be reflected in the UI

3. **Stale time**: The query has a `staleTime` of 5 minutes (line 58), which might prevent immediate refetching in some cases, though `refetch()` should bypass this.

## Suggested Fix

There are several potential approaches to fix this:

1. **Reset ordering on manual refetch**: When `refetch()` is called explicitly, reset the `orderedChanges` state completely instead of trying to preserve order:
   ```typescript
   const { refetch: originalRefetch, ...rest } = useQuery(...);
   
   const refetch = () => {
     setOrderedChanges([]); // Clear current state
     previousDataRef.current = null; // Reset reference
     return originalRefetch();
   };
   ```

2. **Deep comparison instead of reference comparison**: Use a deep comparison of the data to detect changes:
   ```typescript
   if (JSON.stringify(currentData) !== JSON.stringify(previousDataRef.current)) {
   ```

3. **Force update on refetch**: Add a flag to track manual refetches and always update the UI when it's a manual refresh.

4. **Simplify the ordering logic**: Instead of trying to maintain order across fetches, simply use the order returned by the API and let the API handle sorting.

## Related Code

- Refresh button: `frontend/src/components/features/conversation/conversation-tabs/conversation-tab-title.tsx` (line 15-17)
- Hook with issue: `frontend/src/hooks/query/use-unified-get-git-changes.ts` (line 67-98)
- Changes tab component: `frontend/src/routes/changes-tab.tsx`

## Additional Context

The refresh button was added in PR #12036 (commit 060761437). The functionality exists but the data flow has an issue preventing the UI from updating properly.

## Environment

- OpenHands version: main branch (latest)
- Frontend framework: React with TanStack Query
- Affected component: Changes tab / Git changes viewer

## Labels

`bug`, `frontend`, `ui`, `git`

title: Use agent-server/SDK as source of truth for skills loading (incl. OpenHands/skills repo) and expose resolved skills via app-server API
body:
## Background There is confusion and inconsistent behavior around “Available Skills” in the OpenHands UI: * Users expect “global/public skills” to be loaded from the dedicated repository: [https://github.com/OpenHands/skills/tree/main/skills]() * Current SaaS UI/app-server behavior for v1 conversations loads skills from: * `OpenHands/skills/` inside the OpenHands monorepo (treated as “global skills”) * org-level config repo (`.openhands` / `openhands-config`) * repo-level `.openhands/skills` (and `.openhands/microagents` for v0/back-compat) * user `~/.openhands/skills` Per discussion, the agent-server / SDK already supports loading “public/global skills” from the new repository, but OpenHands app-server does not consistently rely on that and instead re-implements loading/merge logic. This results in cases like the Notion skill existing in `OpenHands/skills` repo but not appearing in UI “Available Skills”. ## Problem Statement 1. The OpenHands app-server currently loads/merges skills itself rather than delegating to agent-server/SDK. 2. “Global skills” in app-server are assumed to come from `OpenHands/skills/` (monorepo) rather than the dedicated `OpenHands/skills` repo. 3. Frontend “Available Skills” can diverge from CLI/SDK behavior (`load_public_skills`/`load_user_skills` expectations). ## Goals * Make the SDK/agent-server the canonical resolver for the full skills set (including public/global skills from the `OpenHands/skills` repo). * Make the OpenHands app-server a thin layer that: 1. requests resolved skills from agent-server/SDK and 2. exposes them to frontend via REST. * Ensure the UI “Tools → show available skills” reflects the same skill set the agent actually uses. ## Non-goals * Reworking skill formats/triggers unless required for compatibility. * Copying public skills into the OpenHands monorepo as a workaround. ## Current Implementation Notes (OpenHands repo) * App-server endpoint exists: `GET /{conversation_id}/skills` in `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_router.py`. * It calls `AppConversationServiceBase.load_and_merge_all_skills(...)`. * The loader currently treats “global skills” as local monorepo `OpenHands/skills/` (not `OpenHands/skills` GitHub repo). ## Proposed Implementation ### A) Standardize a resolved skills API in agent-server (preferred) Add or standardize an agent-server endpoint (illustrative): * `GET /skills` or `GET /v1/skills` It should return resolved skills plus metadata (source: public/global/user/org/repo/sandbox), triggers, content, etc. Agent-server should: * load public/global skills from `OpenHands/skills` repo (cached with refresh semantics) * load user/org/repo skills as currently supported * merge with deterministic precedence rules * return the final resolved list ### B) Update OpenHands app-server to call agent-server for skills In OpenHands app-server: * Replace direct loading/merge logic in: * `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_service_base.py` (`load_and_merge_all_skills`) * `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/skill_loader.py`
with a client call to agent-server’s resolved-skills endpoint. Keep `GET /{conversation_id}/skills` but make it proxy/translate the agent-server response into the UI response model. ### C) Backward compatibility * Continue supporting `.openhands/microagents` and `.openhands/skills` (repo-level) as agent-server already does. * Keep v0 conversation behavior unchanged; v1 uses unified agent-server resolver. ### D) Caching / “Sync” semantics Clarify behavior in code + UI: * whether “Sync” triggers cache refresh in agent-server * expected TTL/refresh behavior for public skills repo fetch * ensure UI updates after sync ## Acceptance Criteria * A skill added to `OpenHands/skills` repo (e.g., `skills/notion/...`) appears in OpenHands UI “Available Skills” without copying into `OpenHands/OpenHands` monorepo. * Skills returned to UI match skills available to the agent during execution. * Only one component (agent-server/SDK) owns merge logic and precedence rules. * Refresh/sync behavior is documented and predictable.

title: Jira Cloud Integration: read:me scope error even after customer adds scope
body:
## Summary

Customer reports receiving a "read:me scope is required" error when setting up Jira Cloud integration, even after adding the scope to their Atlassian app configuration.

**Screenshot from customer:**
The error message states: "This app has requested Jira API & User identity API scopes that have not been added to the app. Configure the app at https://developer.atlassian.com/apps and add the following scopes to the Jira API & User identity API: read:me."

## Analysis

After investigating the codebase and Atlassian OAuth documentation, I identified **two potential issues** that may be causing this problem:

### 1. Most Likely: App Configuration Issue on Atlassian Side

The `read:me` scope belongs to the **User Identity API**, not the **Jira API**. In the Atlassian Developer Console, these are configured in **separate sections**:

- **User Identity API** → requires `read:me` scope
- **Jira API** → requires `read:jira-user`, `read:jira-work`, etc.

**Evidence:**
- According to [Commvault documentation on Atlassian OAuth scopes](https://documentation.commvault.com/11.42/software/creating_oauth_app_for_atlassian_jira_with_required_scopes.html), the `read:me` scope must be added specifically under "User Identity API" in Permissions.
- The error message explicitly mentions "Jira API & User identity API" - indicating the customer may have only added scopes to the Jira API section.

**Customer troubleshooting steps:**
1. Go to https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/
2. Select the OAuth app
3. Navigate to **Permissions**
4. Under **User identity API**, verify that "View active user profile" (`read:me`) is enabled
5. Under **Jira API**, verify classic scopes `read:jira-user` and `read:jira-work` are enabled
6. After making changes, users who previously authorized the app may need to **revoke and re-authorize** to pick up the new scopes

### 2. Secondary Concern: Missing URL Encoding in OAuth Authorization URL

I noticed that the OAuth authorization URL construction does not properly URL-encode the query parameters:

**Current code** (enterprise/server/routes/integration/jira.py, lines 301-313):
```python
auth_params = {
    'audience': 'api.atlassian.com',
    'client_id': JIRA_CLIENT_ID,
    'scope': JIRA_SCOPES,  # 'read:me read:jira-user read:jira-work'
    'redirect_uri': JIRA_REDIRECT_URI,
    'state': state,
    'response_type': 'code',
    'prompt': 'consent',
}

auth_url = (
    f"{JIRA_AUTH_URL}?{'&'.join([f'{k}={v}' for k, v in auth_params.items()])}"
)
```

This produces a URL with **unencoded spaces** in the scope parameter:
```
https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize?...&scope=read:me read:jira-user read:jira-work&...
```

According to [Atlassian's OAuth 3LO documentation](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/oauth/getting-started/implementing-oauth-3lo/), the scopes should be URL-encoded with `%20` between them:
```
scope=REQUESTED_SCOPE_ONE%20REQUESTED_SCOPE_TWO
```

While browsers may handle unencoded spaces, this could cause parsing issues where only `read:me` is recognized as the scope (truncated at the first space).

**Recommended fix:**
```python
from urllib.parse import urlencode
auth_url = f'{JIRA_AUTH_URL}?{urlencode(auth_params)}'
```

## Why `read:me` is Required

The `read:me` scope is used in the OAuth callback flow to retrieve the Jira user's account ID:

**enterprise/server/routes/integration/jira.py:457-465:**
```python
jira_user_response = requests.get(JIRA_USER_INFO_URL, headers=headers)  # https://api.atlassian.com/me
if jira_user_response.status_code != 200:
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=400,
        detail=f'Error fetching user info: {jira_user_response.text}',
    )

jira_user_info = jira_user_response.json()
jira_user_id = jira_user_info.get('account_id')
```

The `account_id` is then stored to link the Jira user to their OpenHands account. Without this scope, the `/me` endpoint call will fail.

## Relevant Code

- **Scopes defined:** enterprise/server/routes/integration/jira.py:28
- **Authorization URL construction:** enterprise/server/routes/integration/jira.py:301-313 and 363-373
- **User info endpoint usage:** enterprise/server/routes/integration/jira.py:457-465

**Git blame:** All code authored by Ray Myers in commit e37f7b0e0 ("Enterprise code and docker build (#10770)", 2025-09-04)

## Recommended Actions

1. **Immediate customer guidance:** Share troubleshooting steps for verifying the User Identity API scope configuration in Atlassian Developer Console
2. **Code fix consideration:** Add proper URL encoding using `urllib.parse.urlencode()` for the authorization URL construction (both in jira.py and jira_dc.py)
3. **Documentation:** Consider adding setup documentation for Jira Cloud integration that explicitly mentions the need to configure scopes in both User Identity API and Jira API sections

## References

- [Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) Implementation Guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/oauth/getting-started/implementing-oauth-3lo/)
- [Jira scopes for OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and Forge apps](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/scopes-for-oauth-2-3LO-and-forge-apps/)
- [Example: Creating OAuth App with Required Scopes](https://documentation.commvault.com/11.42/software/creating_oauth_app_for_atlassian_jira_with_required_scopes.html)

title: [Feature Request] V1 DockerSandboxService: Support for host networking and additional exposed ports
body:
## Summary

When deploying OpenHands behind a reverse proxy (nginx/CloudFront), accessing user-launched applications (e.g., Flask apps on port 5000) via `/runtime/{port}/` URLs results in 502 Bad Gateway errors. This is due to V1's `DockerSandboxService` architecture limitations.

## Problem Description

### Current V1 Architecture Limitations

1. **Fixed exposed ports**: V1 only exposes 4 hardcoded ports (8000, 8001, 8011, 8012) in `sandbox_models.py`
2. **No `network_mode` support**: `DockerSandboxService` doesn't support host networking
3. **Dynamic port mapping**: Bridge network uses dynamic host ports, making it incompatible with proxy patterns like `localhost:{container_port}`

### How this affects users

When a user asks the agent to "Create a Flask app and run it on port 5000":
1. The Flask app starts inside the sandbox container on port 5000
2. Port 5000 is NOT in the exposed ports list (`ExposedPortName`)
3. The port is never mapped to the host
4. The reverse proxy (`/runtime/5000/` → `localhost:5000`) fails with 502

### V0 vs V1 Comparison

| Feature | V0 (DockerRuntime) | V1 (DockerSandboxService) |
|---------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| Network Mode | ✅ Configurable via `SANDBOX_DOCKER_RUNTIME_KWARGS` | ❌ Hardcoded bridge |
| Exposed Ports | ✅ Dynamic based on app | ❌ Fixed (8000, 8001, 8011, 8012) |
| Runtime URL Access | ✅ Works with host networking | ❌ 502 errors |

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Add `network_mode` support (Recommended)

Allow `DockerSandboxService` to use host networking via configuration:

```python
# In docker_sandbox_service.py
network_mode = sandbox_config.use_host_network and 'host' or 'bridge'
container = self.docker_client.containers.run(
    ...,
    network_mode=network_mode,
    ...
)
```

**Note**: The `use_host_network` field already exists in `sandbox_config.py` but isn't used.

### Option 2: Add configurable extra ports

Allow users to specify additional ports to expose:

```toml
# config.toml
[sandbox]
extra_exposed_ports = [5000, 8080]
```

### Option 3: Add common development ports to ExposedPortName

```python
class ExposedPortName(StrEnum):
    AGENT_SERVER = 'agent_server'  # 8000
    VSCODE = 'vscode'              # 8001
    WORKER_1 = 'worker_1'          # 8011
    WORKER_2 = 'worker_2'          # 8012
    # Add common development ports
    FLASK_DEFAULT = 'flask_default'  # 5000
    DJANGO_DEFAULT = 'django_default'  # 8000 (already covered)
    NODE_DEFAULT = 'node_default'  # 3000
```

## Environment

- OpenHands Version: Latest main branch (V1 app server)
- Deployment: AWS EC2 with CloudFront + nginx reverse proxy
- Sandbox Type: Docker

## Related Code

- `openhands/app_server/sandbox/docker_sandbox_service.py` - Container creation (no `network_mode` param)
- `openhands/app_server/sandbox/sandbox_models.py` - `ExposedPortName` enum (fixed ports)
- `openhands/core/config/sandbox_config.py` - Has `use_host_network` field but unused

## Workaround

Currently, users can instruct the agent to run apps on port 8011 (WORKER_1) or 8012 (WORKER_2) instead of the default Flask port 5000. However, this is not intuitive and breaks common development patterns.

## Additional Context

This issue was discovered while deploying OpenHands with a CDK-based infrastructure that uses CloudFront → ALB → nginx → Docker architecture. The nginx runtime proxy pattern (`/runtime/{port}/` → `localhost:{port}`) works correctly for V0 with `SANDBOX_DOCKER_RUNTIME_KWARGS={"network_mode":"host"}`, but V1 ignores this environment variable.

title: Improve Browser and App tab empty state instructions for better user guidance
body:
## Problem

Users working on web applications are confused about how to get their apps to display in the **Browser** and **App** tabs in the OpenHands UI. The current empty state messages are minimal and do not provide enough guidance:

- **App tab**: Shows "start a web server to run the application" which is vague
- **Browser tab**: Shows "no page loaded" without any helpful instructions

## User Feedback

> "The UI is great that it lets us use the browser and view the app with webserver but there arent really any instructions on how to get OpenHands to render/run either/or respective to the given project. Im working on a web app, not really sure how to get it to display the browser."
>
> "Also stating app might be confusing for someone working on a web app, what does this actually render? Like phone apps?"
>
> "Possibly including some more info on the unloaded app/web tabs that explains how to get them to run in OpenHands would benefit others."

## Proposed Solution

### Browser Tab
- Improve the empty state to include actionable instructions like:
  - "Ask OpenHands to navigate to a URL or start browsing"
  - "The agent can browse websites to research information or test web applications"
  - Example prompts users can try

### App Tab
This overlaps with #12049 which proposes excellent improvements including:
- Renaming "App" to "Web App" for clarity
- Providing clear empty-state messaging
- Adding troubleshooting hints

### General Improvements
- Add brief explanations of what each tab is for (tooltip or in empty state)
- Include example prompts or quick-start instructions
- Link to documentation for detailed setup instructions

## Related Issues
- #12049 - [App tab] Improve ability for Agent to use the App tab

## Additional Context
This would particularly help new users who are trying OpenHands for web development projects and are not sure how to leverage these features.

title: [Project] V0 API Deprecation
body:
As we move all end-users (SaaS, Local GUI, and Self-hosted deployments) to V1, we need a plan to EOL the V0 APIs.  We want to do this in a way that's fair to our end-users and customers, so we can manage expectations (and not suddenly change APIs that break any downstream dependencies our users/customers have setup).

IIUC, there is no formal documentation for V0 APIs. We want to make sure we document appropriate changes to:
- Cloud REST APIs
- AgentServer APIs

The All Hands AI team has been starting to discuss this, so we've decided to create a public issue to communicate what we think are next steps at this time. We also have a channel in our community slack: `#project-v0-api-deprecation`

Current next steps:

1. Do some gap analysis:
- Research: Which APIs have had material changes that could be disruptive? (for example, Trajectory API has had big changes, especially around JSON structure)
- Research: Using SaaS data, determine which APIs are most heavily used

2. Create a migration guide:
- Based on gap analysis, create a V0 --> V1 migration guide. Use the migration guide to get feedback from community. Following this, we'd want to communicate an EOL date. 

3. Decide: Potentially release a client library

title: Migrate from Poetry to UV for Python dependency management
body:
## Overview

Migrate the OpenHands project from Poetry to UV for Python dependency management. UV offers significantly faster dependency resolution and installation times, which will improve developer experience and CI/CD performance.

## Why UV?

- **10-100x faster** dependency resolution and installation
- **Better CI/CD performance** - faster builds and tests
- **Modern PEP 621 compliance** - uses standard `[project]` metadata
- **Drop-in replacement** - supports similar workflows to Poetry

## Migration Plan

### Phase 1: Non-Breaking Changes (Add UV Support)

Add UV scaffolding while keeping Poetry fully functional:

- [x] Step 1.1: Add PEP 621 `[project]` section - #12414
- [x] Step 1.2: Add `[dependency-groups]` section - #12415
- [x] Steps 1.3-1.6: Add `[project.dependencies]`, `[project.optional-dependencies]`, generate `uv.lock` - #12416
- [ ] Step 2: Add UV support to Makefile (alongside Poetry)
- [ ] Step 3: Add UV support to Docker files (alongside Poetry)
- [ ] Step 4: Add UV support to GitHub Actions (alongside Poetry)
- [ ] Step 5: Update runtime build code to support both lock files
- [ ] Step 6: Update evaluation scripts to support both tools
- [ ] Step 7: Update documentation
- [ ] Step 8: Apply same changes to `enterprise/pyproject.toml`

### Phase 2: Breaking Changes (Switch to UV as Primary)

- [ ] Change build-system from `poetry.core.masonry.api` to `hatchling`
- [ ] Update `build.sh` to use `uv build`
- [ ] Switch Makefile to use UV by default
- [ ] Switch Docker files to use UV by default
- [ ] Switch GitHub Actions to use UV by default
- [ ] Update all scripts from `poetry run` to `uv run`

### Phase 3: Cleanup

- [ ] Remove `[tool.poetry]` sections from pyproject.toml
- [ ] Remove `poetry.lock`
- [ ] Remove Poetry installation from Docker/CI
- [ ] Update all documentation to remove Poetry references

## Files Requiring Updates

### Core Configuration
- `pyproject.toml` (root)
- `enterprise/pyproject.toml`
- `poetry.lock` → `uv.lock`

### Build Scripts
- `build.sh`
- `Makefile`

### Docker/Container Files
- `containers/app/Dockerfile`
- `containers/dev/Dockerfile`
- `openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_templates/Dockerfile.j2`

### GitHub Actions
- `.github/workflows/pypi-release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/py-tests.yml`
- `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ghcr-build.yml`
- `.github/workflows/check-package-versions.yml`

### Runtime Build Code
- `openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py`

### Evaluation Scripts
- Multiple `evaluation/benchmarks/*/scripts/*.sh` files
- `evaluation/utils/version_control.sh`

### Documentation
- `Development.md`
- Various benchmark README files

### Tests
- `tests/unit/runtime/builder/test_runtime_build.py`

### Skills/Templates
- `skills/add_repo_inst.md`

## Reference Implementation

The `openhands-cli` subdirectory already uses UV (`uv.lock` exists), which serves as a reference implementation.

## Related Links

- [UV Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
- [PEP 621 - Project Metadata](https://peps.python.org/pep-0621/)
- [PEP 735 - Dependency Groups](https://peps.python.org/pep-0735/)
- Linear Issue: APP-315
