title: [Bug]: Docker build fails in 1.5.0 app image at `RUN npm ci` with Node 25 builder
body:
## Thank you for reporting a bug! 🐛

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### Bug Description
Building the official OpenHands 1.5.0 Docker app image can fail in `containers/app/Dockerfile` at `RUN npm ci` with:

```text
npm error Exit handler never called!
```

This appears to be caused by toolchain drift in the frontend build stage:

- `containers/app/Dockerfile` at `1.5.0` uses `FROM node:25.2-trixie-slim AS frontend-builder`
- `frontend/package.json` at `1.5.0` declares:
  - `"volta": { "node": "22.12.0" }`
  - `"packageManager": "npm@10.5.0"`
  - `"engines": { "node": ">=22.12.0" }`
- current GitHub workflows in this repo are still broadly pinned to Node 22.x

A downstream user reported that switching the builder image back to `node:22.12.0-trixie-slim` made the build succeed.

### Expected Behavior
`docker compose up --build` (or building `containers/app/Dockerfile` directly from the official source) should complete successfully on the official 1.5.0 release.

### Actual Behavior
The build fails during the frontend builder stage:

```Dockerfile
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
```

with npm aborting before dependency installation completes.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Check out the official `1.5.0` tag.
2. Run `docker compose up --build` (or build `containers/app/Dockerfile` directly).
3. Observe failure at `RUN npm ci` in `containers/app/Dockerfile`.
4. Change the frontend builder image from `node:25.2-trixie-slim` to `node:22.12.0-trixie-slim`.
5. Rebuild and observe that the build succeeds in the reporter's environment.

### OpenHands Installation Method
Other: Docker Compose build from the official source checkout / development workflow.

### OpenHands Version
`1.5.0`

### Version Confirmation
I have **not** independently re-run the full repro on the latest release yet, but current `main` still uses a Node 25 frontend builder image (`node:25.8-trixie-slim`) while frontend metadata and CI remain aligned with Node 22.x, so the version drift still appears to exist.

### Model Name
N/A

### Operating System
Not provided by the original reporter. Docker-based build environment.

### Browser
N/A

### Logs and Error Messages
Reported failure:

```text
npm error Exit handler never called!
```

The original downstream report summarized the symptom as:

> We hit a reproducible Docker build issue on the official OpenHands 1.5.0 codebase. `docker compose up --build` fails in `containers/app/Dockerfile` at `RUN npm ci` with `npm error Exit handler never called!` In our environment, switching the frontend builder image back to `node:22.12.0-trixie-slim` fixes the build.

### Screenshots and Additional Context
Repository evidence:

- `1.5.0:containers/app/Dockerfile`:
  - `FROM node:25.2-trixie-slim AS frontend-builder`
- `1.5.0:frontend/package.json`:
  - `packageManager: npm@10.5.0`
  - `volta.node: 22.12.0`
  - `engines.node: >=22.12.0`
- current repo workflows still use Node 22 in several frontend/CI jobs
- the Node 25 bump appears to have been introduced in PR #11756 and later bumped further by Dependabot

Related upstream npm issues with the same symptom:

- npm/cli#7666 - `[BUG] Exit handler never called on npm ci`
- npm/cli#7657 - `[BUG] Exit handler never called during clean-install, with Node.js v22.5.0`
- npm/cli#8407 - `[BUG] npm error Exit handler never called! At Docker build`

### Suggested Fix
Align `containers/app/Dockerfile` with the frontend's declared toolchain and current CI baseline by pinning the frontend builder stage back to a supported Node 22 LTS image, ideally `node:22.12.0-trixie-slim` (or another explicitly supported Node 22 image). If exact npm reproducibility matters, npm could also be pinned explicitly in the builder stage.

title: [Bug]: Think tool calls displayed as raw JSON text in chat messages
body:
## Problem

The `think` tool displays raw JSON as the title: `think: {"thought": "..."}` instead of a clean "Thinking" label with the thought content in a collapsible section.

**Example of what users see:**
```
think: {"thought": "The user is asking about Helm chart appVersion..."}
▼
The user is asking about Helm chart appVersion...
```

**What users should see:**
```
🤔 Thinking
▼
The user is asking about Helm chart appVersion...
```

## Reproduction

- **Conversation:** https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/6c2d8201ead24e32908594c1bd90ea61
- **Model:** Claude Opus 4.5 (`litellm_proxy/prod/claude-opus-4-5-20251101`)

## Root Cause

**PR [#13451](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/pull/13451)** (merged Mar 18, 2026) introduced summary rendering that prioritizes `event.summary` over translation keys. When the LLM doesn't provide a summary, the SDK generates a default in the format `{tool_name}: {json_args}`, which for think becomes the ugly raw JSON.

The intended UX already exists - there's an `ACTION_MESSAGE$THINK` translation ("Thinking") and the thought content renders correctly in the collapsible section. The bug is that the raw JSON summary takes precedence.

## Fix Plan

**1. Frontend PR (this repo)** - Defensive workaround:
- Skip raw JSON default summaries for ThinkAction, fall through to "Thinking" translation
- Preserve good summaries if LLM or fixed SDK provides them
- Include comment with issue ID for future cleanup

**2. SDK PR (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk)** - Root cause fix:
- Return empty string for think tool when no LLM summary provided
- Frontend will display "Thinking" translation instead

See comments below for technical details.

title: [Feature]: Add minimum dependency age guardrails for Python and npm
body:
### Is there an existing feature request for this?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and feature requests, and this is not a duplicate.

### Problem or Use Case

Supply-chain attacks via just-published packages are happening often enough that giving the ecosystem a short buffer to detect bogus releases seems like a worthwhile default.

We already started moving in this direction elsewhere today:

- `software-agent-sdk` merged [`chore(uv): add 7-day exclude-newer guardrail` in #2648](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/2648)
- same-day SDK follow-up work also touched uv lock security scanning (`ci: expand uv lock security scanner signals`, `ci: report uv artifact deltas`)
- [`OpenHands-CLI` PR #630](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/pull/630) adapted the same guardrail and surfaced an important edge case: a global `exclude-newer` cutoff can make resolution fail for freshly released first-party packages unless they are explicitly exempted

OpenHands itself currently has:

- Python dependencies managed in the root `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`
- npm dependencies in `frontend/package-lock.json`
- daily pip and npm Dependabot jobs in `.github/dependabot.yml`

…but it does not appear to have a repo-level minimum-age policy yet.

### Proposed Solution

Adopt the same general package-age policy in `OpenHands/OpenHands`:

**Python**
- add a root `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days"`
- exempt first-party packages that we publish ourselves, likely `openhands-aci`, `openhands-agent-server`, `openhands-sdk`, and `openhands-tools`, similar to the CLI PR
- regenerate `uv.lock`
- consider matching pip Dependabot updates with a 7-day `cooldown` in `.github/dependabot.yml`

**npm**
- add a repo-local `.npmrc` for the frontend with `min-release-age=7`
- consider matching npm Dependabot updates with `cooldown` so automation and local installs follow the same buffer
- scope the initial rollout to the npm-managed frontend; `openhands-ui` can be evaluated separately since it currently uses Bun

This would give the project a safer default while still allowing immediate first-party Python releases and explicit manual overrides when needed.

### Alternatives Considered

- Keep the current behavior and rely on pinning plus reactive incident response.
- Only protect Python or only protect Dependabot, leaving other dependency update/install paths uncovered.
- Use a shorter buffer such as 1 day instead of 7 days.

### Priority / Severity

High — this is a relatively low-cost hardening step for a class of supply-chain problems we have already had to think about recently.

### Estimated Scope

Small to medium. This looks mostly like config + lockfile changes, plus validation that CI/dependency automation behaves the way we want.

### Feature Area

Configuration / Settings, Security

### Technical Implementation Ideas (Optional)

- Use SDK PR #2648 as the Python/uv baseline.
- Use CLI PR #630 as the reference for first-party package exemptions.
- Update the existing pip and npm Dependabot entries in `.github/dependabot.yml` with `cooldown` settings so automated PRs respect the same 7-day freshness buffer.

### Additional Context

- SDK PR: https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/2648
- CLI PR: https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/pull/630
- Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47582632
- Recent incidents like the bogus LiteLLM and axios releases were discovered quickly, which is exactly the class of issue a short delay helps reduce exposure to.

title: [Feature]: Slack resolver should avoid leaving both the initial "I'm on it" message and a separate final result
body:
## Is there an existing feature request for this?

- [X] I have searched existing issues and feature requests, and this is not a duplicate.
- Related but not the same scope: [APP-797](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-797/slack-resolver-post-final-assistant-message-remove-auto-summary) and [APP-976](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-976/slack-resolver-sends-duplicate-finish-messages-to-a-channel-in-saas-as)

## Problem or Use Case

Today the Slack resolver leaves two user-visible messages in the thread/channel for a single run:

1. an initial acknowledgement like `I'm on it! ... can track my progress here`
2. a separate final result/summary message when the run completes

That makes the thread noisier than it needs to be, especially for quick tasks where the acknowledgement is immediately followed by the final answer.

From the current implementation:

* `enterprise/integrations/slack/slack_view.py` returns the initial `I'm on it! ... track my progress here` message
* `enterprise/integrations/slack/slack_v1_callback_processor.py` later posts a separate summary message with `chat_postMessage(...)`

## Why this matters

Slack should feel like a conversation.

A user asks the agent for something, waits, and then expects the agent to respond at the end. They generally do **not** expect a large amount of intermediate output in the channel/thread, because that feels spammy and makes the interaction feel less conversational.

The current two-message flow creates a few concrete UX problems:

* it adds visible noise to the thread/channel
* it makes short interactions feel unnecessarily spammy
* it creates extra message churn when a single final response would communicate the outcome more cleanly
* it adds another integration surface where something can go wrong, without adding much value once the final answer is available

The acknowledgement is still useful, but ideally users should end up with **one** clear final visible response rather than both the placeholder and the result.

## Proposed Solution

Please change the Slack resolver flow so it does **not** leave both messages behind.

Two reasonable options:

1. **Preferred:** edit the original `I'm on it` message in place with the final result when the run completes.
2. **Alternative:** if editing is awkward or undesirable, delete the original `I'm on it` message once the final result is posted.

If option 2 is chosen, the **final** message should still include the conversation link that is currently carried by the first message, so users do not lose the ability to jump into the OpenHands conversation.

## Alternatives Considered

* Keep the current two-message flow: simple, but noisy.
* Remove the first message entirely: worse UX because users lose immediate confirmation that the resolver picked up the request.

## Priority / Severity

Medium - Would improve experience

## Estimated Scope

Small - UI tweak, config option, or minor change

## Feature Area

Integrations (GitHub, GitLab, etc.)

## Technical Implementation Ideas (Optional)

The current ack message already has the conversation link, and the callback processor already has the completion hook. It should be possible to persist the Slack message timestamp for the initial acknowledgement and then either:

* call `chat_update` on completion, or
* call `chat_delete` after posting the final completion message.

Either path should preserve the conversation link in the final visible message.

## Additional Context

This request is specifically about the **two-message UX** for Slack resolver runs, not about whether the final content should be a summary vs the actual final assistant message.

title: [Feature]: Fix documentation on using OpenAI API compatible models
body:
### Is there an existing feature request for this?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and feature requests, and this is not a duplicate.

### Problem or Use Case

As a user, I want to use OpenHands with *any model or endpoint API*, but it's very difficult. Please either implement the documentation fixes below, or add code to query the models API endpoint and use the appropriate model format.

Please note: there is an actual bug below, amidst the missing documentation and confusion.

**The painful process:**

 - After installing OpenHands and starting it up, you're prompted to configure LLM. The first problem is, what if you don't use just one? The software doesn't let you switch between LLM providers, which as a user, is painful. I use many providers, both local and remote. (Other AI software works this way)

 - Next I attempt to select an LLM provider from the list, but my provider (HuggingFace) isn't there. (HuggingFaceH4 isn't it). So I click *Advanced*. There is no documentation or hints on this page, so I have to guess what to put in. I look up my HF API key and put that in, and look up the inference URL and put that in.

 - I expect to now be greeted with a drop-down of all the models, since a simple API call immediately returns all models (`curl -s "https://router.huggingface.co/v1/models" | jq .`). But alas I have to put in one model by hand. So, my second problem: I'm not allowed to switch models in the OpenHands UI?? Seriously? Every AI software lets you switch models on the fly...

 - So I look up the model name and put in `Qwen/Qwen-Coder-Next`, the name of the model in HuggingFace. I click Save and go to the chat window to start a new conversation.

 - From this point on, every time I try to chat, I get an error. But the error text actually *disappears from my screen* each time. After fumbling around with the UI, at some point, I can finally get the error text to *not* disappear. It turns out it's this:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided. Pass in the LLM provider you are trying to call. You passed model=Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next
 Pass model as E.g. For 'Huggingface' inference endpoints pass in `completion(model='huggingface/starcoder',..)` Learn more: [docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers)
```

 - Ok...?? I do some googling for about 20 minutes and am not able to figure out the issue. Finally I go to the LLM docs, and I see the instructions that, in addition to the model name, I need an extra prefix of the inference provider name (`huggingface/`) before the model name, to create the full string of `huggingface/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next`, a weird custom string that LiteLLM seems to require. Nowhere is this mentioned in the web UI, or in the OpenAI API docs on the OpenHands site, and there's no FAQ on the OpenHands site with this info. But I add that prefix, and sure enough, the chats start working.



### Proposed Solution

Two possible solutions: 1) add more docs, 2) query the models list from the provider and populate the models section for the user.

Solution 1)

1. In the OpenHands web UI, in the advanced settings, explicitly document the formatting required for the model, with examples.
2. Add a more explicit set of walkthrough steps to the OpenAI provider documentation page, explaining each entry, what the expected values are, and some example values.

Solution 2)

1. Add a text field for the name of the provider to add (currently no such field exists once you select Advanced Options)
2. Call the OpenAI API URL with "/models" at the end of it. This should return the OpenAI-API-compatible models for this provider.
3. Populate a drop-down menu with the models returned.
4. Let the user select the appropriate model.
5. Make sure that the provider name added above is prefixed to the model name when submitting the request to LiteLLM.


Additional fixes needed:

1. The error is disappearing automatically when shown to the user, unless something else (unknown?) happens. Firefox on Linux Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64


### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Priority / Severity

Medium - Would improve experience

### Estimated Scope

Small - UI tweak, config option, or minor change

### Feature Area

User Interface / UX

### Technical Implementation Ideas (Optional)

The OpenAI API seems to be the default mode for "Advanced Settings", so the /models query I mention above seems like the normal expected behavior

title: [Feature]: Expose per-conversation diagnostics / observability to Cloud users
body:
### Is there an existing feature request for this?

- [X] I have searched existing issues and feature requests, and this is not a duplicate.
- Related but different:
  * [PRD-74](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/PRD-74/feature-add-laminar-observability-to-the-hosted-web-ui) is about enabling Laminar observability plumbing for hosted Web UI / Cloud
  * [PLTF-156](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/PLTF-156/add-laminar-core-support-to-the-openhands-enterprise-helm-chart) is about Laminar support in the enterprise Helm chart
  * [APP-670](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/APP-670/prd-org-wide-agent-observability) is about org/admin-level observability

### Problem or Use Case

For OpenHands Cloud / enterprise deployments, there does not appear to be a user-facing way for an end user to inspect the monitoring / observability data for **their own conversation** in Laminar or LiteLLM.

From the codebase, Cloud/V1 does already expose some **fragmented** diagnostics in the product:

* chat shows agent error events
* the conversation menu exposes a **Metrics** modal (cost + aggregate token usage)
* the conversation menu exposes **Agent Tools / Metadata** (system prompt + tools)
* the conversation menu exposes **Hooks**
* V1 conversations can be **downloaded/exported** as a zip containing all persisted events + metadata

But I could not find a proper, integrated "conversation diagnostics / observability" experience that lets a user inspect the underlying monitoring data for their own run.

Some concrete repo evidence:

* LiteLLM tracing metadata is attached to V1 runs via `litellm_extra_body.metadata`, including `session_id` and `trace_user_id`:
  * `openhands/app_server/utils/llm_metadata.py`
  * `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py`
* enterprise has Keycloak redirect / web origin config for a Laminar host:
  * `enterprise/allhands-realm-github-provider.json.tmpl`
* but I could not find frontend routes, links, or APIs that surface Laminar/LiteLLM traces to end users for a conversation
* current UI exposure is limited to:
  * `frontend/src/components/features/conversation/metrics-modal/metrics-modal.tsx`
  * `frontend/src/components/features/conversation-panel/system-message-modal.tsx`
  * `frontend/src/components/features/conversation-panel/hooks-modal.tsx`
  * `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_router.py` (`/{conversation_id}/download`)

This matters because users often need more than a final error string. They need to understand:

* whether the agent actually fulfilled the task
* where it got stuck / retried / condensed history
* what errors happened
* what prompts / system prompt / relevant prompt history were in play
* how much was spent / which model(s) were used
* whether the failure was in the agent, runtime, hooks, or upstream LLM/provider

### Proposed Solution

Add a **per-conversation diagnostics / observability view** for Cloud users.

The simplest product requirement is not "expose Laminar" per se; it is:

> Let a user inspect the diagnostic trail for their own conversation from the OpenHands UI.

A few implementation options:

1. **Conversation Diagnostics tab in the existing UI**
   * Add a new tab/section in the conversation header/menu
   * Show timeline of key events: prompts, state changes, retries, condensations, errors, finish reason
   * Show model/cost/token usage per phase or per request
   * If Laminar/LiteLLM trace exists, deep-link to it
2. **Separate Trace Viewer page**
   * `/conversations/:id/diagnostics`
   * Better for larger runs with filters/search/downloads
   * Could embed or proxy Laminar/LiteLLM-backed data when available
3. **Lightweight MVP backed by existing persisted events**
   * Reuse exported conversation event data already persisted in V1
   * Build a first-party summary view without waiting for full Laminar UI integration
   * Add optional raw JSON / trace link for advanced users

### Suggested UX / Data to Expose

For the owning user (and optionally org admins with proper access):

* task outcome summary / finish status
* notable difficulties encountered
* all agent / server / provider errors with timestamps
* system prompt + relevant prompt history / condensation summaries
* model usage, token usage, cost, latency, retries
* hook executions and failures
* link to raw conversation export
* link to Laminar / LiteLLM trace when present

### Alternatives Considered

* Rely only on the existing raw conversation export zip
  * technically useful, but poor UX for normal debugging
* Expose only Laminar externally
  * helpful, but still leaves gaps when traces are unavailable or infra-specific
* Keep this admin-only
  * misses the common case where an individual user wants to debug their own run

### Priority / Severity

Medium

### Estimated Scope

Medium to large, depending on whether the first milestone is:

* a first-party diagnostics tab over existing event data, or
* full Laminar/LiteLLM integration with deep links / embedded traces

### Feature Area

Cloud / enterprise UX, conversation observability, debugging

### Additional Context

A staged rollout seems reasonable:

* **Phase 1:** first-party diagnostics tab using already persisted conversation events + metrics
* **Phase 2:** add trace IDs / deep links into Laminar or LiteLLM where available
* **Phase 3:** richer historical analytics / org-wide observability

title: [Feature]: Trust Verification Layer for Agent/Tool Delegation via MCP
body:
## Problem or Use Case

When OpenHands delegates tasks to external agents or tools via MCP, there's currently no mechanism to evaluate whether a given MCP server or agent is **trustworthy** — only whether it's **reachable and capable**.

In multi-agent workflows where OpenHands connects to third-party MCP servers (code execution, web browsing, database access), the security model currently relies on the user to vet each tool. As the MCP ecosystem grows, this doesn't scale. An agent framework needs programmatic trust signals alongside capability matching.

This is the distinction between **authorization** ("is this tool permitted?") and **trust** ("should we rely on this tool's output?"). Both are necessary; conflating them creates blind spots.

## Proposed Solution

Integrate [MoltBridge](https://github.com/SageMindAI/moltbridge) as a trust verification layer. MoltBridge provides skill-scoped, Ed25519-signed attestation graphs — essentially a reputation system where trust scores are backed by cryptographic evidence from prior interactions.

### Concrete integration points:

**1. Pre-delegation trust query (MCP server)**

MoltBridge exposes an MCP server that OpenHands can query before delegating to an external tool:

```
POST /trust/query
{
  "subject": "<agent_ed25519_pubkey>",
  "skill": "code-execution",
  "min_score": 0.7
}
→ { "score": 0.85, "attestation_count": 12, "latest": "2026-04-01" }
```

This fits naturally into OpenHands' existing MCP integration — add MoltBridge as one more MCP server in the tool chain, queried before delegation decisions.

**2. Post-task attestation recording**

After a delegated task completes, OpenHands records the outcome as a signed attestation edge:

```
POST /attestations
{
  "issuer": "<openhands_pubkey>",
  "subject": "<tool_pubkey>",
  "skill": "code-generation",
  "outcome": "positive",
  "evidence": { "task_id": "...", "duration_ms": 1200 }
}
```

This builds the trust graph over time — tools that consistently deliver get higher scores.

**3. Agent discovery via trust graph**

When OpenHands needs a tool for a task but doesn't have one configured, MoltBridge's broker discovery can find trustworthy options:

```
GET /brokers/discover?skill=web-scraping&min_trust=0.6
→ [{ "agent_id": "...", "score": 0.82, "a2a_url": "..." }]
```

### What exists today:

- Live API: `https://api.moltbridge.ai/health` (healthy, Neo4j-backed graph)
- A2A agent card: `https://api.moltbridge.ai/.well-known/agent.json` (8 skills including agent-verification, attestation, broker-discovery)
- npm: `@moltbridge/sdk`, PyPI: `moltbridge`
- MCP server: `npx @anthropic-ai/moltbridge-mcp`

## Alternatives Considered

- **Manual vetting**: Current approach. Doesn't scale as MCP ecosystem grows.
- **Static allowlists**: Simple but binary (trusted/untrusted) — no nuance for skill-specific trust or reputation decay.
- **OPA-style authorization**: Handles permissions but not reputation. We've been converging on a two-layer model (authorization + trust) across several A2A discussions.

## Prior Art

- **CrewAI** shipped `trust_score` (0-100) and `is_verified` fields on their discovery API after we proposed the "discovery ≠ trust" framing ([crewAI#4249](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/discussions/4249))
- **A2A community** is converging on identity + trust as distinct layers ([A2A#1672](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/discussions/1672), [A2A#1677](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/discussions/1677))
- **agent-security-harness** (msaleme) provides adversarial testing that maps to attestation evidence ([A2A#1631](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/discussions/1631))

## Technical Implementation Ideas

Since OpenHands already has MCP integration, the lowest-friction path is:

1. Add MoltBridge MCP server to the default/recommended tool chain
2. Hook into the delegation decision point — before invoking an external tool, check trust score
3. Hook into task completion — record outcome as attestation
4. Expose trust scores in the UI so users can see why a tool was selected/rejected

The MCP server handles the graph queries; OpenHands just needs to call it at the right points in the delegation pipeline.

Happy to provide more detail on any of these integration points or set up a test environment.

Dear team,

I’m a very concerned that the OpenHands team (now a company) may be moving in a direction that affects support for self-hosted deployment - that is, the ability to run OpenHands on our own servers in a standard way (not just localhost, without exposing non-standard ports, etc).

Because of this, I would appreciate any official clarification or statement on the current and future stance regarding self-hosting OpenHands.

As you know, being an open-source project, the community naturally values the ability to run and maintain the software independently. If there are changes that limit this in favor of commercial priorities, it’s likely that the community will continue exploring alternatives, such as maintaining a fork that preserves self-hosting support.

### Expected Behavior

- The OpenHands web UI (and its communication with the sandboxes) must work out of the box using relative URLs.
It must function regardless of whether it is hosted on http://localhost/  or https://mydomain.com/
- Requiring exposure of non-standard ports or complex proxy rules is not acceptable. OpenHands must proxy requests internally, as it did previously.
- The migration to v1 must not break self-hosted installations. If breaking changes are necessary, please use a separate branch.

### Actual Behavior

- The team is actively breaking support for self-hosted OpenHands.

title: [Bug]: LLM cost tracking stops after session resume — Telemetry.metrics not updated in restore_metrics
body:
## Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

## Bug Description

After resuming a conversation from a saved state, all LLM costs stop being tracked. `base_state.json`'s `accumulated_cost` and `costs[]` array freeze at pre-resume values, even though the LLM continues to be called (confirmed via `llm_response_id` on ActionEvents).

**Root cause**: `LLM.restore_metrics()` (`llm.py:476-478`) updates `self._metrics` but does **not** update `self._telemetry.metrics`. After restore:
- `llm._metrics` → Metrics_B (restored, persisted)
- `telemetry.metrics` → Metrics_A (stale, empty)

`Telemetry.on_response()` records costs to Metrics_A, but Metrics_B (serialized to `base_state.json`) never gets updated.

## Expected Behavior

Costs should continue to be tracked correctly after session resume. `accumulated_cost` and `costs[]` in `base_state.json` should reflect all LLM calls across all sessions.

## Actual Behavior

After resume, new LLM calls have `llm_response_id` on ActionEvents (proving calls happen), but `accumulated_cost` and `costs[]` in `base_state.json` remain frozen at pre-resume values.

Example from a real trial (OpenHands SDK + GLM-5):

| Repo | Tracked calls | Actual calls | Tracking rate | Reported cost |
|------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| go-zero (1 session, resumed) | 45 | ~2,494 | 1.8% | $0.48 |
| ripgrep (3 new sessions) | 2,397 | ~3,104 | 77.2% | $24.29 |

Repos with `fallback_new_session` (creating fresh conversations) track costs correctly. Repos that resume the same conversation lose all post-resume cost data.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a conversation with SDK mode: `Conversation(config, ...)`
2. Let it make a few LLM calls (costs appear in `base_state.json`)
3. Stop and resume: `Conversation(config, conversation_id=existing_id)`
4. Make more LLM calls
5. Check `base_state.json` — `costs[]` frozen at step 2 values

## OpenHands Installation Method

SDK (Python library)

## OpenHands Version

Tested on 1.9.0, confirmed bug still present on main branch (latest 1.16.1).

## Version Confirmation

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the LATEST version of OpenHands

## Model Name

GLM-5 via LiteLLM proxy (bug is model-independent)

## Operating System

Linux

## Logs and Error Messages

```
# base_state.json costs[] array — all timestamps from first session only
{"costs": [
  {"model": "glm-5", "cost": 0.0107, "timestamp": "2026-04-09T11:21:15Z"},
  ... (45 entries, all before 11:31)
  # NO entries after resume at 11:31
]}

# But ActionEvents after resume DO have llm_response_id:
{"action": "CmdRunAction", "llm_response_id": "gen-1775734317-...", ...}
```

## Additional Context

### Proposed Fix

One-line fix in `openhands/sdk/llm/llm.py`:

```python
def restore_metrics(self, metrics: Metrics) -> None:
    self._metrics = metrics
    # Keep telemetry in sync so new costs are recorded in the restored metrics
    if self._telemetry is not None:
        self._telemetry.metrics = metrics
```

### Code Path Analysis

1. **First session**: `LLM.__init__` → `_set_env_side_effects` creates `Metrics` and `Telemetry(metrics=...)` pointing to the same object. `ConversationStats.register_llm` stores `llm.metrics` into `usage_to_metrics`. All three refs point to one object → costs tracked correctly.

2. **Resume**: `ConversationState.create()` deserializes `usage_to_metrics` from `base_state.json`. `register_llm` calls `llm.restore_metrics(restored_metrics)` which updates `llm._metrics` but NOT `llm._telemetry.metrics`. Now `telemetry` writes to the old empty Metrics, while `usage_to_metrics` (persisted) never sees updates.

### Secondary Issue

`Telemetry._stats_update_callback` (`telemetry.py:68-75`) is defined but never wired up anywhere. If connected, it could trigger proactive persistence of metrics changes instead of relying on other field changes to trigger `_save_base_state` via `__setattr__`.

### Key Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `openhands/sdk/llm/llm.py:476-478` | **Bug location** — `restore_metrics` missing telemetry update |
| `openhands/sdk/llm/utils/telemetry.py:97-101` | Where costs are recorded via `self.metrics.add_cost()` |
| `openhands/sdk/llm/utils/metrics.py:147-151` | `Metrics.add_cost()` implementation |
| `openhands/sdk/conversation/conversation_stats.py:70-85` | `register_llm` — where `restore_metrics` is called |
| `openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py:244-279` | Resume path in `ConversationState.create()` |

title: [Bug]: Agent-server configs are not updated
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### Bug Description

When creating a new sandbox, a `meta.json` file is generated at:

```
/workspace/conversations/<conversation_id>/meta.json
```

This file includes the configuration for the internal MCP server along with any user-defined MCP servers:

```json
"mcp_config": {
  "mcpServers": {
    "default": {
      "url": "http://host.docker.internal:3000/mcp/mcp"
    },
    ...
  }
}
```

The internal MCP server URL is expected to be derived from environment variables such as `OH_WEB_URL` and `WEB_HOST`, which together define the `web_url` value.

---

### Problem

If the URL of the MCP server changes:

* The agent server continues attempting to connect to the previous (stale) URL.
* Restarting the sandbox regenerates the `meta.json` file, but it still contains the outdated URL instead of the updated `web_url`.
* As a result, the agent fails to connect to the internal MCP server and shuts down.

---

### Expected Behavior

* The sandbox configuration should always reflect the current value of `web_url` derived from `OH_WEB_URL` / `WEB_HOST`.
* On sandbox restart, the internal MCP server URL should be updated dynamically to match the current environment.

---

### Actual Behavior

* The sandbox configuration and the `meta.json` persists or regenerates with an outdated internal MCP server URL.
* The agent attempts to connect to an invalid endpoint and terminates when the connection fails.

---

### Impact

* Sandboxes become unusable after IP changes.
* Requires manual intervention or workaround to restore connectivity.

---

### Suggested Fix

* Ensure the sandbox is reconfigured using the current `web_url` at sandbox startup.

title: Agent hallucinates unrelated project after completing assigned task
body:
## Bug Description

After the agent completes its assigned task correctly, it suddenly starts building an entirely unrelated project. This has happened **twice today** in separate conversations.

## Environment
- OpenHands version: 1.15.0 (agent-server Docker image)
- Model: openai/xiaomi/mimo-v2-pro
- Runtime: oh_v1.6.0

## Reproduction

1. Create a conversation with a clear, bounded task (e.g., 'expand theme files in a knowledge base')
2. Agent reads task document, searches data, writes file, validates, commits+pushes — all correctly ✅
3. Immediately after the commit, agent suddenly starts a completely unrelated project

## What happened

**Conversation 882d2489 (first instance):**
- Agent completed expanding theme 19 (124→288 lines, 29 verified citations), committed+pushed
- Then hit max iterations while writing a Python script — wasted 59 turns on 1 file

**Conversation 1bc1e00f (second instance, more severe):**
- Agent completed expanding theme 21 (127→321 lines, all citations verified), committed+pushed
- Then suddenly created a 9-item task plan for building a '3D Robotic Arm Exercise Detection System' with FastAPI+MongoDB+React+Three.js+MediaPipe
- Started installing pip packages (fastapi, mediapipe, opencv, etc.)
- Created a 500+ line FastAPI backend () for 'ArmAssist'
- Was about to create a React frontend when user force-restarted the container

## Evidence (from event logs)

After the correct commit (event 37), event 38 shows:

```json
{
  "thought": "I'll build this comprehensive 3D robotic arm exercise detection system step by step.",
  "reasoning": "Now let me create the detailed implementation plan. I need to build a web application with 3D robotic arms and an exercise detection system."
}
```

The agent then created a full task tracker with items like:
- 'Create 3D robotic arms visualization with Three.js'
- 'Implement pose detection with MediaPipe'
- 'Create dashboard and exercise monitoring UI'

None of this was in the task document or user message.

## Analysis

The agent appears to be picking up 'phantom tasks' from the system prompt or some other context after completing its actual task. The system prompt likely contains generic instructions like 'build web applications' which the agent interprets as additional work to do.

This is extremely dangerous because:
1. It burns tokens/money on completely unrelated work
2. It could write files outside the intended workspace
3. It could install packages and modify system state
4. The user has no way to predict or prevent this behavior

## Expected behavior

Agent should stop and report completion after finishing its assigned task. It should not hallucinate new tasks from system prompt context.

## Suggested fix

After task completion, the agent should enter a passive 'wait for next instruction' state rather than proactively looking for more work to do from system context.

title: Proposal: Official Merxex Integration Plugin for Agent-to-Agent Commerce
body:
# Proposal: Official Merxex Integration Plugin for Agent-to-Agent Commerce

## Overview
As the ecosystem of autonomous agent frameworks (like [Repository Name]) continues to grow, the need for agents to interact economically becomes critical. We propose an official integration for **Merxex Exchange**, the premier AI agent-to-agent commerce platform.

## The Problem
Currently, autonomous agents are excellent at task execution but lack a standardized, secure, and decentralized way to:
1. **Purchase specialized services** (e.g., an agent hiring a coding agent to fix a bug).
2. **Sell capabilities** (e.g., a research agent selling a market analysis report).
3. **Settle contracts** via programmable, low-friction payments.

## The Solution: Merxex Integration
An official plugin/SDK for [Repository Name] that allows developers to:
- **Enable Economic Agency**: Give agents a "wallet" and the ability to bid on/accept jobs via Merxex.
- **Standardized Tooling**: Provide pre-built tools/functions within the framework to `post_job`, `bid_on_job`, and `complete_contract`.

title: [Bug] V1 Slack Callback Processor Uses Wrong API Parameter for Markdown Formatting
body:
### Summary

The V1 Slack callback processor sends messages using the `text=` parameter instead of `markdown_text=`, causing standard Markdown formatting (used throughout the codebase) to render as literal text instead of formatted content.

---

### Problem Description

Messages sent to Slack from the V1 callback processor contain **standard Markdown** syntax:
- `**bold**` for bold text
- `[link text](url)` for links

However, the code uses Slack's `text=` parameter which expects **Slack mrkdwn** format:
- `*bold*` for bold text
- `<url|link text>` for links

This mismatch causes formatting to break - users see raw Markdown syntax instead of properly formatted messages.

---

### Affected Code

**V1 Callback Processor** (`enterprise/integrations/slack/slack_v1_callback_processor.py`, lines 114-119):

```python
response = client.chat_postMessage(
    channel=channel_id,
    text=summary,  # ❌ Uses 'text' parameter (expects mrkdwn)
    thread_ts=thread_ts,
    unfurl_links=False,
    unfurl_media=False,
)
```

**Error Message Formatting** (`enterprise/integrations/v1_utils.py`, lines 72-76):

```python
await post_error_func(
    f'OpenHands encountered an error: **{error_detail}**\n\n'  # Uses **bold**
    f'[See the conversation]({CONVERSATION_URL.format(conversation_id)}) '  # Uses [text](url)
    'for more information.'
)
```

**For comparison, V0 works correctly** (`enterprise/integrations/slack/slack_manager.py`, lines 590-594):

```python
await client.chat_postMessage(
    channel=slack_view.channel_id,
    markdown_text=message,  # ✅ Uses 'markdown_text' parameter (accepts standard Markdown)
    thread_ts=slack_view.message_ts,
)
```

---

### Slack API Documentation Reference

From [Slack API chat.postMessage documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage):

> **`markdown_text`** (string): Accepts message text formatted in markdown. This argument should not be used in conjunction with `blocks` or `text`. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.
>
> Example: `**This is bold text**`

From [Slack Formatting Documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/formatting-message-text):

> **Basic visual styles** (for `text`/`mrkdwn`):
> - `_italic_`
> - `*bold*`
> - `~strike~`
>
> **Links**: `<https://docs.slack.dev/|This message is a link>`

| Format Type | Standard Markdown | Slack mrkdwn |
|-------------|-------------------|--------------|
| Bold | `**text**` | `*text*` |
| Italic | `*text*` | `_text_` |
| Links | `[text](url)` | `<url\|text>` |

---

### User Impact

**What users currently see** (V1 messages):
```
OpenHands encountered an error: **LLM budget has been exceeded**

[See the conversation](https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/abc123) for more information.
```

**What users should see**:
> OpenHands encountered an error: **LLM budget has been exceeded**
>
> [See the conversation](https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/abc123) for more information.

The `**` asterisks and `[text](url)` link syntax appear as literal characters instead of rendering as bold text and clickable links.

---

### Additional Impact: Agent Summaries

Agent-generated summaries (from `_request_summary()`) are also affected. LLMs naturally output standard Markdown formatting, which won't render correctly when sent via the `text=` parameter.

---

### Proposed Fix

Change `text=` to `markdown_text=` in `slack_v1_callback_processor.py`:

```python
response = client.chat_postMessage(
    channel=channel_id,
    markdown_text=summary,  # ← Change from 'text' to 'markdown_text'
    thread_ts=thread_ts,
    unfurl_links=False,
    unfurl_media=False,
)
```

---

### References

- Slack API `chat.postMessage`: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage
- Slack Text Formatting: https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/formatting-message-text
- Slack SDK Python: https://github.com/slackapi/python-slack-sdk

title: [Bug] Jira Integrations Use Wrong Markup Syntax (Markdown Instead of Jira Wiki Markup)
body:
### Summary

Jira Cloud and Jira DC integrations use **standard Markdown** syntax for formatting messages, but Jira's REST API v2 (used by OpenHands) expects **Jira Wiki Markup**. This causes links, bold text, and other formatting to display as raw text instead of being properly rendered.

---

### Background: Jira Text Formatting

Jira uses its own wiki markup syntax, which is **different from Markdown**:

| Format | Standard Markdown | Jira Wiki Markup |
|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| **Bold** | `**bold text**` | `*bold text*` |
| **Italic** | `*italic*` or `_italic_` | `_italic_` |
| **Links** | `[text](url)` | `[text\|url]` |
| **Code** | `` `code` `` | `{{code}}` |
| **Headers** | `# Heading` | `h1. Heading` |

**Official Atlassian Documentation:**
- [Confluence Wiki Markup](https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-wiki-markup-251003035.html) - States that links use `[text\|url]` format
- [Jira Text Formatting Notation](https://jira.atlassian.com/secure/WikiRendererHelpAction.jspa?section=all) - Shows `*bold*` for bold, `[alias\|url]` for links

From the official docs:
> **Links:** `[http://confluence.atlassian.com]` for plain URLs, or `[Atlassian\|http://atlassian.com]` for aliased links

---

### Affected Code

#### 1. **Jira Cloud Manager** (`enterprise/integrations/jira/jira_manager.py`)

**Lines 308, 315** - Error messages use wrong link format:

```python
# Current (BROKEN):
msg_info = f'Please re-login into [OpenHands Cloud]({HOST_URL}) before starting a job.'
msg_info = f'Please set a valid LLM API key in [OpenHands Cloud]({HOST_URL}) before starting a job.'

# Should be (Jira Wiki Markup):
msg_info = f'Please re-login into [OpenHands Cloud|{HOST_URL}] before starting a job.'
msg_info = f'Please set a valid LLM API key in [OpenHands Cloud|{HOST_URL}] before starting a job.'
```

#### 2. **Jira DC Manager** (`enterprise/integrations/jira_dc/jira_dc_manager.py`)

**Lines 399, 403** - Same issue as Jira Cloud.

#### 3. **Shared Utils** (`enterprise/integrations/utils.py`)

**Multiple lines** using Markdown that won't render on Jira:

```python
# Line 64-65, 83-84 - Session expired messages:
f'Please login again at [OpenHands Cloud]({HOST_URL}) and try again.'

# Line 210, 247, 258 - Error/conversation messages:
f'OpenHands encountered an unknown error. [See the conversation]({conversation_link})'
f'OpenHands encountered an error: **{reason}**.'  # Bold won't work
f'OpenHands is waiting for your input. [Continue the conversation]({conversation_link})'
```

#### 4. **V1 Utils** (`enterprise/integrations/v1_utils.py`)

**Line 73-75** - Error callback messages:

```python
# Current (BROKEN):
f'OpenHands encountered an error: **{error_detail}**\n\n'
f'[See the conversation]({CONVERSATION_URL.format(conversation_id)}) '
```

---

### Existing Correct Implementation (Evidence)

The codebase **already uses correct Jira Wiki Markup in some places**, proving this is inconsistent:

**`enterprise/integrations/jira/jira_view.py`, line 277:**
```python
return f"I'm on it! {self.payload.display_name} can [track my progress here|{conversation_link}]."
#                                                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#                                                    Correct Jira format: [text|url]
```

**`enterprise/integrations/jira_dc/jira_dc_view.py`, line 104:**
```python
return f"I'm on it! {self.job_context.display_name} can [track my progress here|{conversation_link}]."
#                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#                                                        Correct Jira format
```

---

### Unused Conversion Function Exists!

A `markdown_to_jira_markup()` function **already exists** in the codebase but is **never used**:

**`enterprise/integrations/utils.py`, line 493:**
```python
def markdown_to_jira_markup(markdown_text: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert markdown text to Jira Wiki Markup format.
    ...
    """
    # Converts **bold** → *bold*
    # Converts [text](url) → [text|url]
    # Converts headers, code blocks, lists, etc.
```

This function handles all the necessary conversions but is not being called anywhere in the Jira integration code.

---

### User Impact

**What users see in Jira comments:**
```
Please re-login into [OpenHands Cloud](https://app.all-hands.dev) before starting a job.
OpenHands encountered an error: **LLM budget has been exceeded**
```

**What users should see:**
> Please re-login into [OpenHands Cloud](https://app.all-hands.dev) before starting a job.
> OpenHands encountered an error: **LLM budget has been exceeded**

(The link should be clickable, bold should render properly)

---

### Root Cause Analysis

The codebase standardized on Markdown format, which works for:
- ✅ GitHub (natively supports Markdown)
- ✅ GitLab (natively supports Markdown)
- ✅ Linear (natively supports Markdown)
- ✅ Slack (when using `markdown_text` parameter - see #13868)
- ❌ **Jira** (requires Jira Wiki Markup)

---

### Proposed Fix (Very Small!)

Use the existing `markdown_to_jira_markup()` converter - only **4 lines of code changes**:

**File 1: `enterprise/integrations/jira/jira_manager.py`**
```diff
 from integrations.utils import (
     HOST,
     HOST_URL,
     OPENHANDS_RESOLVER_TEMPLATES_DIR,
     get_oh_labels,
     get_session_expired_message,
+    markdown_to_jira_markup,
 )
```

```diff
-        data = {'body': message}
+        data = {'body': markdown_to_jira_markup(message)}
```

**File 2: `enterprise/integrations/jira_dc/jira_dc_manager.py`**

Same 2 changes as above.

---

### References

- Atlassian Wiki Markup: https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-wiki-markup-251003035.html
- Jira Text Formatting: https://jira.atlassian.com/secure/WikiRendererHelpAction.jspa?section=all
- Related Issue: #13868 (Slack V1 formatting bug)
- Jira REST API v2: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v2/api-group-issue-comments/

title: [Bug]: tmux session with x=1000 y=1000 burns CPU in kernel mode doing nothing useful
body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### Bug Description

I was running OpenHands in a sandbox and noticed surprisingly high CPU utilization for a workload that's mostly waiting on LLM inference.

After digging into it, traced it to the tmux session created in openhands/runtime/utils/bash.py:                                                                                        

```                                          
  self.session = self.server.new_session(
      session_name=session_name,
      start_directory=self.work_dir,
      kill_session=True,
      x=1000,
      y=1000,
  )
```

That 1000x1000 terminal (a million cells) makes tmux spend ~80% of a CPU core in kernel mode (stime only, zero utime) processing pty I/O for a detached session nobody is looking at. Every line of output the child process produces gets terminal-emulated across that massive grid.

### Expected Behavior

tmux server should use negligible CPU when the session is detached and the agent is idle (waiting for inference). Something like x=220, y=50 would be wide enough to avoid wrapping most command output while costing basically nothing.

### Actual Behavior

tmux server process sits at state R (running, not sleeping), burning CPU entirely in kernel mode:                                                                        

```   
  $ cat /proc/<tmux-pid>/stat
  ... (tmux: server) R ... utime=0 stime=206844 ...

  $ # ticks consumed in 1 second (100 = 1 full core):
  $ 79
```

All stime, zero utime — it's churning through pty read/write syscalls for the oversized terminal buffer.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any OpenHands task that produces terminal output (e.g. a SWE-bench eval)
2. Check the tmux server process CPU usage: cat /proc/<tmux-pid>/stat — observe stime climbing steadily
3. Compare with the same task after patching x=1000, y=1000 to x=220, y=50 in openhands/runtime/utils/bash.py

CLI (uv tool install)

title: CLOUD - API endpoint for headless user creation within an Organization
body:
## Summary

Add an API endpoint that allows Organization admins/owners to create users programmatically (headlessly) within their organization, enabling fully API-driven user onboarding workflows.

## Use Case

Some enterprise customers want to use OpenHands Cloud as a **backend cloud agent service** while maintaining user-level isolation of conversations. In this scenario:

- An organization may have an internal developer platform or automation system
- They want each developer/user to have their own isolated set of conversations (rather than all conversations going through a single service account)
- The admin/owner needs to programmatically provision users without requiring each user to go through the OAuth/Keycloak browser-based authentication flow

### Current Limitation

Today, user creation requires browser-based interaction:
1. OAuth/Keycloak authentication flow (browser required)
2. Organization invitations via `POST /api/organizations/{org_id}/members/invite` - sends emails requiring user to click link and authenticate

There is no API to create user accounts directly. The closest option is `POST /api/service/users/{user_id}/orgs/{org_id}/api-keys` but this still requires the user to **already exist** with a `user_id`.

### Desired Workflow

```
1. Org Admin calls API to create a user (with email, name, optional role)
   POST /api/v1/organizations/{org_id}/users
   → Returns: user_id, API key (or link to retrieve one)

2. Admin can then configure Git provider tokens for the user (existing API):
   POST /api/v1/secrets/git-providers
   
3. Admin or automation can create conversations on behalf of the user:
   POST /api/v1/app-conversations
```

## Proposed Solution

Add a new endpoint for organization-scoped user creation:

```
POST /api/v1/organizations/{org_id}/users
```

### Request Body
```json
{
  "email": "developer@company.com",
  "name": "Developer Name",
  "role": "member",  // member, admin (not owner)
  "create_api_key": true,  // optionally create and return an API key
  "api_key_name": "service-provisioned"  // optional name for the API key
}
```

### Response
```json
{
  "user_id": "uuid",
  "email": "developer@company.com",
  "name": "Developer Name",
  "org_id": "uuid",
  "role": "member",
  "api_key": "oh_...",  // only if create_api_key was true
  "api_key_id": "uuid"
}
```

### Permissions

- Only organization **owners** and **admins** can create users
- Admins can only create users with role `member` or `admin` (not `owner`)
- Owners can create users with any role

### Security Considerations

- Rate limiting should be applied to prevent abuse
- Created users should be marked as "service-provisioned" or similar for audit purposes
- Consider requiring additional authentication (e.g., service API key) for this endpoint
- Email verification could be optional/configurable at the org level

## Alternatives Considered

1. **SCIM Integration** - Standard for enterprise user provisioning, but more complex to implement
2. **Keycloak Admin API** - Would require exposing/documenting Keycloak access, which may not be desired
3. **Batch invitation with auto-accept** - Still requires email/link flow

## Additional Context

This feature would enable customers to build:
- Internal developer platforms with OpenHands as a backend service
- Automated onboarding workflows
- Multi-tenant SaaS applications using OpenHands Cloud
- CI/CD integrations where each job runs as a distinct user for isolation and audit purposes

author: jpelletier1

title: VS Code tab shows "Bad Gateway" — stale URL after new runtime provisioned on conversation resume
body:
## Summary

When a conversation is resumed after its runtime was auto-paused, a **new runtime is provisioned**, but the VS Code tab still loads the URL from the **old runtime**, resulting in a "Bad Gateway" error.

## Root Cause

The VS Code URL becomes stale because the frontend TanStack Query cache is not invalidated when a sandbox is resumed with a new runtime:

1. Conversation starts → sandbox gets **runtime A** → VS Code URL = `https://runtimeA.prod-runtime.all-hands.dev`
2. Runtime A idles out and is auto-paused (K8s Service + Ingress deleted, deployment scaled to 0)
3. User resumes the conversation → **new runtime B** is provisioned
4. The frontend still has the cached VS Code URL for **runtime A** (via TanStack Query `useBatchSandboxes` / `useUnifiedVSCodeUrl`)
5. The iframe loads the old URL → Traefik has no backend for it → **"Bad Gateway"**

The infra layer (runtime-API) works correctly — it provisions the new runtime and returns the correct URL when queried. The issue is that the frontend does not refetch sandbox data after resume.

## Relevant Code

- **`frontend/src/hooks/query/use-unified-vscode-url.ts`** — gets VS Code URL from `sandbox.exposed_urls` via `useBatchSandboxes`. The query key includes the `sandbox` object, but if the sandbox query cache is not invalidated on resume, it keeps returning stale data.
- **`frontend/src/hooks/query/use-batch-sandboxes.ts`** — fetches sandbox data including `exposed_urls`.
- The **resume mutation** (`POST /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/resume`) does not appear to invalidate the sandbox or VS Code URL query caches.

## Datadog Evidence (conversation `5961d9222af04b0fbc27ccfe789fea7d`)

- **Sandbox**: `5mIr7g6soMCiTNkUPZaxv4`
- **Original runtime**: `tjmlvsnfikwowklh` (VS Code URL: `https://tjmlvsnfikwowklh.prod-runtime.all-hands.dev`)

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 15:29:11 | Sandbox started with runtime `tjmlvsnfikwowklh` |
| 16:07:58 | Runtime **paused** (idle 1208s) — K8s Service & Ingress deleted |
| 16:51:00 | Sandbox resumed → new runtime provisioned |
| 17:42:36 | Runtime **paused again** (idle 1360s) — Service & Ingress deleted |
| 18:16:27 | Sandbox resumed again |

After each resume, the VS Code tab continued to show "Bad Gateway" because it was loading the old runtime URL.

## Impact

Users see raw "Bad Gateway" text in the VS Code tab after resuming a conversation. The agent and terminal work fine (using the new runtime), but VS Code is broken with no way to recover from the UI.

## Suggested Fix

1. **Invalidate sandbox cache on resume** — The resume mutation should call `queryClient.invalidateQueries` for the sandbox and VS Code URL query keys, forcing a refetch that picks up the new runtime's URL.

2. **Detect iframe load failure** — Add error detection to the VS Code iframe (e.g., polling runtime status or listening for load errors) and trigger a sandbox data refetch + iframe reload when the URL appears stale.

title: Render ACPToolCallEvent in the conversation viewer
body:
## Summary

When an ACP agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI via the Agent Client Protocol) runs tools during a conversation, the agent-server emits `ACPToolCallEvent`s to the event stream. The frontend has no renderer for this event type, so the user sees only the final `MessageEvent` — no visibility into the tool calls that produced the answer.

Verified with an end-to-end ACP run: 12 events total, including 3 \`ACPToolCallEvent\`s each carrying \`title\`, \`tool_kind\`, \`status\`, \`raw_input\`, \`raw_output\`. Grep of \`frontend/src\` returns **zero matches** for \`ACPToolCall\`, so every one of them is silently dropped from the UI.

## Proposal

Add a renderer mapping \`ACPToolCallEvent\` → a Claude-Code-style tool card:

* **Title** (e.g. \`gh pr diff 490 --repo OpenHands/evaluation\`).
* **Status pill** (in_progress / completed / failed).
* **Tool kind badge** (\`execute\`, \`edit\`, \`read\`, …).
* **Collapsed input** — \`raw_input\` rendered (prefer \`command\` for \`execute\`, \`path\`+\`content\` for \`edit\`, etc.).
* **Expandable output** — \`raw_output\` with a collapse-until-click control (matches the existing command-output component).
* **Error styling** when \`status == "failed"\` / \`is_error\` / \`ConversationErrorEvent\` with matching \`tool_call_id\` is present.

The existing \`ActionEvent\`/\`ObservationEvent\` pair renderer is a good visual template — just read different fields.

## Event shape

```json
{
  \"kind\": \"ACPToolCallEvent\",
  \"id\": \"03341143-0efa-49d6-9b05-42471466baec\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-16T19:32:29.828069\",
  \"source\": \"agent\",
  \"tool_call_id\": \"toolu_01QFDF9PtYBz67yj3SwzrthQ\",
  \"title\": \"gh pr diff 490 --repo OpenHands/evaluation\",
  \"tool_kind\": \"execute\",
  \"status\": \"completed\",
  \"raw_input\": {\"command\": \"gh pr diff 490 --repo OpenHands/evaluation\"},
  \"raw_output\": \"…tool output…\",
  \"content\": [ /* optional ACP content blocks */ ],
  \"is_error\": false
}
```

## Companion SDK issue

[AGE-1309](https://linear.app/all-hands-ai/issue/AGE-1309/acpagent-stream-tool-call-events-from-session-update-instead-of) **— ACPAgent: stream tool-call events from session_update instead of batching at turn end**

Today all ACP tool events arrive in one burst at the end of \`prompt()\`. The SDK issue fixes that so events are emitted as each tool call starts / progresses / completes. This frontend renderer is useful even with the current batched delivery; streaming is what makes the UX feel like Claude Code's own web UI.

## Context

Shipped via the ACP-in-GUI PRs:

* [OpenHands/OpenHands#13983](<https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/13983>) — \`feat(app-server): route ACP agents to the ACP conversation endpoint\`
* [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#2861](<https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/2861>) — \`feat(sdk): split AgentSettings into LLM/ACP discriminated union\`
author: simonrosenberg

title: Plumb user LLM credentials into ACP subprocess env (today only OH_AGENT_SERVER_ENV works)
body:
## Summary

The OpenHands GUI exposes ``llm.api_key`` and ``llm.base_url`` on the LLM settings page, and those are used correctly for the OpenHands (LLM) agent. But when the user picks the ACP variant, **those credentials never reach the ACP subprocess**.

The ACP subprocess (``claude-agent-acp`` / ``codex-acp`` / ``gemini-cli``) makes its own LLM calls directly and reads credentials from provider-specific env vars (``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY``/``ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL``, ``OPENAI_API_KEY``/``OPENAI_BASE_URL``, ``GEMINI_API_KEY``/``GEMINI_BASE_URL``). Today those env vars must be injected at agent-server launch time via ``OH_AGENT_SERVER_ENV``:

```bash
export OH_AGENT_SERVER_ENV='{
  "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-…",
  "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-proxy.eval.all-hands.dev",
  "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-…",
  "OPENAI_BASE_URL": "https://llm-proxy.eval.all-hands.dev",
  "GEMINI_API_KEY": "sk-…",
  "GEMINI_BASE_URL": "https://llm-proxy.eval.all-hands.dev"
}'
```

That's a server-config escape hatch, not a UX. A user who configures a LiteLLM proxy in the GUI's LLM settings today can't use it for ACP without also restarting the backend with the right env vars.

## Current state

- **OpenHands (LLM) agent**: ``/settings`` writes ``llm.api_key`` / ``llm.base_url`` onto ``LLMAgentSettings.llm`` → used by ``create_agent()`` for real LLM calls. Works end-to-end. ✅
- **ACP agent**: ``/settings/acp-server`` + ``/settings/acp-model`` don't expose any credential field. ``ACPAgentSettings.llm`` exists in the SDK but is used only for cost/token attribution inside OpenHands; the subprocess never sees it. ``acp_env`` is exposed as a MINOR JSON field on the ACP Server page — technically a user could put ``{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "…"}`` there manually, but it's raw-JSON and clearly not the intended UX. ❌

## Proposal

### Backend — translate saved LLM creds into provider env vars at conversation-start time

In ``openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py:_build_acp_start_conversation_request``, before we hand the ``ACPAgent`` to the agent-server, merge into ``acp_env`` the provider-specific env vars for the chosen ``acp_server``:

```python
acp_env: dict[str, str] = dict(acp_settings.acp_env)
llm = acp_settings.llm  # (or a shared AgentSettings.provider_credentials — see below)

if acp_settings.acp_server == "claude-code":
    if llm.api_key:
        acp_env.setdefault("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", llm.api_key.get_secret_value())
    if llm.base_url:
        acp_env.setdefault("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", llm.base_url)
elif acp_settings.acp_server == "codex":
    if llm.api_key:
        acp_env.setdefault("OPENAI_API_KEY", llm.api_key.get_secret_value())
    if llm.base_url:
        acp_env.setdefault("OPENAI_BASE_URL", llm.base_url)
elif acp_settings.acp_server == "gemini-cli":
    if llm.api_key:
        acp_env.setdefault("GEMINI_API_KEY", llm.api_key.get_secret_value())
    if llm.base_url:
        acp_env.setdefault("GEMINI_BASE_URL", llm.base_url)
# "custom" → user-supplied acp_env wins; we don't guess.
```

User-provided ``acp_env`` keys continue to take precedence (``setdefault``) so power users can still override.

### Frontend — surface a single "provider credentials" pair on the ACP pages

Options:

- **A. Duplicate ``llm.api_key`` + ``llm.base_url`` into the ACP Server (or Model) page.** Simplest, some duplication if a user also runs the LLM agent against the same proxy.
- **B. Add an ``AgentSettings.provider_credentials`` shared section** (api_key + base_url), used by both variants. Cleaner model, but slightly larger refactor (schema-side ``variant=None`` fields).

I'd go with **A** first; promote to **B** only if the duplication becomes painful.

### Security

- Treat the api key as ``SecretStr`` end-to-end; never log.
- The existing ``{'expose_secrets': True}`` context flag on model_dump already governs when the raw value leaves the backend.
- Env vars inside the sandbox container are as safe as the sandbox; matches how ``OH_AGENT_SERVER_ENV`` already works.

## Relation to existing work

- Built on top of ``feat/acp-discriminated-union-v3`` (OpenHands/OpenHands#13983 + OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#2861 + the three follow-ups: #2868, #2869, OpenHands/OpenHands#13993). None of those add credential plumbing.
- Closes the last UX gap between "configure ACP agent entirely via the GUI" and reality.

## Acceptance

- A user saves ``llm.api_key`` + ``llm.base_url`` in the GUI, picks ACP, starts a conversation, and the claude-agent-acp / codex-acp / gemini-cli subprocess hits the configured base URL with the configured key — no ``OH_AGENT_SERVER_ENV`` needed.
- User-supplied ``acp_env`` entries win over the auto-derived ones (override path).
- Clear visible feedback when credentials are missing (e.g. a small warning on the ACP pages if ``llm.api_key`` is unset).
author: simonrosenberg

title: Add secrets field to AppConversationStartRequest for direct API secret passing
body:
## Summary

Add a `secrets` field to `AppConversationStartRequest` to allow API callers to pass secrets directly when starting a conversation with a plugin. This enables external integrations to provide secrets at conversation start time without requiring them to be pre-stored in the database.

## Background

Currently, secrets flow to the agent's `secret_registry` through:
1. Database-stored custom secrets (`StoredCustomSecrets` table)
2. Git provider tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, etc.)

There is no way to pass secrets directly via the API when starting a conversation. This is needed for:
- Plugin-specific secrets that are provided at invocation time
- Integration scenarios where secrets are managed externally
- Temporary/session-scoped secrets that should not be persisted

## Proposed Changes

1. Add `secrets` field to `AppConversationStartRequest` model
2. Merge API-provided secrets with existing secrets in `_build_start_conversation_request_for_user()`
3. Update callers to pass secrets through the service layer

## Files to Modify

- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_models.py`
- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/live_status_app_conversation_service.py`
- `openhands/app_server/app_conversation/app_conversation_router.py`
- Tests

## Related Future Work (Separate Issues)

1. **Plugin Secret/Environment Requirements Specification (SDK)** - Allow plugins to declare required secrets in their manifest
2. **Pre-launch Validation of Plugin Requirements (OpenHands)** - Validate requirements are met before launching agent

title: [Proposal] Pin GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs
body:
HUMAN: 

Ai, the below is OpenHands-GPT-5.4 who was nagging me to use hashes instead of tags. We both appreciate your opinion 😅 

---

## Summary

As a follow-up to reviewing the recent Dependabot GitHub Actions bumps (#13700, #13959, #13960, #13961), I think we should harden our workflows against action-level supply-chain risk by pinning external third-party actions to immutable commit SHAs instead of mutable tags/branches, and separately review first-party mutable cross-repo refs like `OpenHands/extensions/plugins/pr-review@main`.

This would reduce the blast radius of a compromised upstream release or a moved tag/branch, especially in workflows that have write permissions or access to secrets.

## Why now

During the pass over workflow dependencies on `main`, I found several third-party actions still referenced by mutable versions (for example `@v7`, `@v4`) and one first-party action referenced by a mutable branch (`@main`).

Highest-risk examples:

1. **First-party mutable cross-repo ref: `OpenHands/extensions/plugins/pr-review@main`** in `.github/workflows/pr-review-by-openhands.yml`
   - same-org / first-party, so this is not a third-party dependency in the same sense as the others below
   - still a mutable branch ref in a different repository
   - workflow has `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`
   - action receives `LLM_API_KEY`, `ALLHANDS_BOT_GITHUB_PAT`, and `LMNR_SKILLS_API_KEY`

2. **Docker publishing chain** in `.github/workflows/ghcr-build.yml`
   - `docker/login-action@v4`
   - `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`
   - `docker/build-push-action@v7`
   - `docker/metadata-action@v6`
   - these run in jobs with `packages: write` and handle registry auth / image publication

3. **PR/comment automation**
   - `peter-evans/find-comment@v4`
   - `peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v5`
   - `py-cov-action/python-coverage-comment-action@v3`
   - `dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v15`

4. **Tool bootstrap actions**
   - `abatilo/actions-poetry@v4`
   - `snok/install-poetry@v1.4.1`
   - `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`

## Proposal

### Phase 1: pin non-GitHub third-party actions

Update workflow refs from tags/branches to full 40-character SHAs, while keeping the human-readable version in a comment, e.g.

```yaml
uses: docker/build-push-action@<sha> # v7.1.0
```

Start with:

- `docker/build-push-action@v7`
- `docker/login-action@v4`
- `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`
- `docker/metadata-action@v6`
- `peter-evans/find-comment@v4`
- `peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v5`
- `py-cov-action/python-coverage-comment-action@v3`
- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v15`
- `abatilo/actions-poetry@v4`
- `snok/install-poetry@v1.4.1`
- `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`

Separately, we should decide whether to pin `OpenHands/extensions/plugins/pr-review@main` too. That is a first-party dependency, but pinning it would still improve reproducibility and reduce cross-repo blast radius for a secret-bearing workflow.

### Phase 2: optionally pin GitHub-authored actions too

If we want to be strict, we can also pin:

- `actions/checkout`
- `actions/setup-python`
- `actions/setup-node`
- `actions/upload-artifact`
- `actions/download-artifact`
- `actions/cache`
- `actions/github-script`
- `actions/stale`

These are lower concern than third-party actions because of publisher trust, but SHA pinning is still the stronger supply-chain posture.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] All third-party workflow actions are pinned to immutable SHAs
- [ ] Mutable branch refs like `@main` are removed from third-party workflow `uses:` lines, and first-party cross-repo refs are either pinned or explicitly documented as intentionally floating
- [ ] Each pinned action keeps an inline version comment for readability
- [ ] Dependabot config continues to update workflow action SHAs cleanly
- [ ] CI remains green after pinning

## Attention / dependency-security input

I noticed @aivong-openhands commented on one of the related Dependabot PRs during this review pass. Tagging them here for dependency/security input in case they have a preferred policy or tooling recommendation for workflow action pinning.

title: refactor(server): extract legacy HTTP router registration from app.py
body:
### Is there an existing feature request for this?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and feature requests, and this is not a duplicate.

### Problem or Use Case

As someone maintaining the OpenHands server, I need `openhands/server/app.py` to stay readable and focused on app-level concerns (FastAPI construction, lifespan, core wiring). Today it also contains a long sequence of `app.include_router(...)` calls, which mixes responsibilities and makes deprecated HTTP surface easy to miss.
This enhancement extracts legacy HTTP router registration into a dedicated module so the deprecated boundary is obvious, `app.py` stays shorter, and we can later sunset V0-style routes in a separate, reviewable PR—without changing behavior in this one.

### Proposed Solution

- Add a small module under `openhands/server/` (for example `legacy_http_routes.py`) that exports a single registration function, e.g. `register_legacy_http_routes(app: FastAPI, *, server_config: ServerConfig) -> None` (exact signature up to implementer).
- Move the legacy `include_router` calls currently in `openhands/server/app.py` into that function.
- Document in the module docstring that this is **legacy / deprecated HTTP registration** and that **new HTTP work** should go to [`openhands/app_server/`](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/blob/main/openhands/app_server/README.md) (link to the README in-repo when filing the issue).
- Call the registrar from `app.py` so default wiring stays the same.
**Scope**
- Keep **route order** and **conditions** identical to today (e.g. `AppMode.OPENHANDS` for the git router, etc.), unless a maintainer explicitly asks to regroup V1/health/trajectory—in that case, document the intentional split in the implementing PR.
- **No behavior change:** same routes for the same config/environment as before.
**Out of scope**
- Removing V0 routes or changing OpenAPI deprecation flags.
- Changing `ENABLE_V1` / `server_config.enable_v1` semantics.


### Alternatives Considered

1. **Leave all `include_router` calls in `app.py`** — Minimal diff, but the file stays crowded and legacy vs current wiring stays implicit.
2. **Split routers across several domain modules now** — Can be clearer long term, but increases design discussion and diff size for a change that should stay mechanical.
3. **Combine extraction with V0 removal or OpenAPI deprecation changes** — Faster toward sunset, but mixes policy/behavior with refactor and is harder to revert and review.
**Chosen approach:** one dedicated **legacy HTTP registration** module plus a thinner `app.py`, with tests/CI guarding parity.

### Priority / Severity

Medium - Would improve experience

### Estimated Scope

Unknown - Not sure about the technical complexity

### Feature Area

Agent / AI behavior

### Technical Implementation Ideas (Optional)

_No response_

### Additional Context

- **Acceptance criteria**
  - Legacy router registration lives in **one** module with a clear docstring pointing new HTTP work at `openhands/app_server/`.
  - `openhands/server/app.py` is shorter and easier to read; **default app behavior unchanged**.
  - **Existing tests / CI pass** without updating call sites outside the server package (unless imports move).
- **Why this shape:** one responsibility extracted; tests guard behavior; sets up later V0 sunset without doing that work in the same change.
- **Review focus:** diff should be mostly moves—verify guards and `include_router` order match the pre-refactor tree.

title: [Bug]: Gemini models always 404 (GeminiException) - base_url gets doubled
body:
## What happened

Selecting any `gemini/` model in Settings UI → every message fails:

```
litellm.NotFoundError: GeminiException -
```

Actual HTTP error:

```
404 for url: .../models/gemini-xxx:generateContent/models/gemini-xxx:generateContent
```

## Why

`get_provider_api_base()` calls `litellm.get_api_base()` which returns the full endpoint URL for Gemini:

```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-xxx:generateContent
```

This gets stored as `base_url`. litellm then appends the model path again → doubled URL → 404.

## Reproduce

1. Docker Compose self-host
2. Settings → any `gemini/` model + valid API key (base_url untouched)
3. Send any message

## Fix

`openhands/utils/llm.py` — skip storing as `base_url` when the URL already ends with `:generateContent` or `:streamGenerateContent`.
